Moreover, it complements classical interpretation methods, centred on modelling the properties of the first ionising sources. We define the IGM parameters driving the shape and amplitude of the 21-cm signal, from the globally averaged volume- and mass-weighted ionisation fractions ($\bar{x}_{HII}$ and $\bar{x}_{HIIm}$), the clustering of sources, through the halo bias ($b_{\mathrm{h}}$), and the characteristic sizes of ionised regions ($R_{i}$) and neutral islands ($R_{n}$). We extend this analysis to model the redshift dependence of the power spectrum, constraining parameters such as the midpoint and duration of reionization. We test the IGM framework on three reionization simulations (C2-Ray, 21cmFAST, and POLAR) with varying cosmologies, astrophysics, and numerical assumptions. The framework constrains the IGM parameter space, recovers the midpoint and duration of the EoR as well as the minimum mass of halos hosting ionising sources $M_{\mathrm{min}}$, and the redshift evolution of the global ionisation fraction, the evolution of ionised and neutral regions (measured with the radial mean free path method by Georgiev et al. (2026b, submitted)). Moreover, the IGM framework lends itself to joint analysis with other EoR probes, such as high-redshift galaxies and quasars and the Cosmic Microwave Background.

papers.title: The spectrum of codegree Turán densities of 3-graphs
papers.abstract: The \emph{minimum codegree} $δ_{k-1}(H)$ of a $k$-uniform hypergraph (in short, $k$-graph) $H$ is the smallest number of edges containing a $(k-1)$-set of vertices. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs, its \emph{codegree Turán density} $γ(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of $δ_{k-1}(H)/|V(H)|$ over growing $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs $H$. We prove that every real number $α\in[0,1)$ is the codegree Turán density of an infinite family $\mathcal{F}_α$ of $3$-graphs, and this family can be chosen so that $γ(\mathcal{F}')>α$ for every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subseteq\mathcal{F}_α$. This resolves the $3$-graph case of a conjecture of Mubayi and Zhao, the only case that remained open after recent work of Lin and Zhou. (Li and Liu earlier determined the codegree Turán spectrum in every uniformity $k\ge 4$ and, very recently, they determined the spectrum for $k=3$ independently of us.) We also consider \emph{positive codegree Turán density}, defined analogously by taking the minimum only over $(k-1)$-sets contained in at least one edge. We prove that there is an absolute constant $c<1$ such that, for every integer $k\geq3$, every real number in $[c,1)$ is the positive codegree Turán density of a $k$-graph family. This is done by presenting a construction with a relatively short proof, without optimising the value of $c$.

papers.title: The Boundary Conjecture for Smoothable Alexandrov Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove that in a noncollapsed limit of complete Riemannian manifolds with $\sec\geκ$, each boundary component of a compact full-dimensional convex body, equipped with its intrinsic length metric, has Alexandrov curvature at least $κ$. We also consider such a body in the limit of a noncollapsed sequence of Alexandrov spaces with curvature at least $κ$. If $κ>0$ or the boundary of the body is strongly convex, we show that the body can be approximated by convex bodies in the given sequence.

papers.title: CableMoE: Harm-Regularized Mean-Residual Expert Fusion for Transmission-Corridor Segmentation
papers.abstract: Semantic mapping of transmission corridors benefits from heterogeneous LiDAR and image-guided predictors, but replacing a strong ensemble with a learned router can damage rare electrical assets. We introduce CableMoE, a post-hoc mixture of four frozen segmentation experts. Its deployable prediction is a calibrated residual around availability-aware probability averaging, while a harm penalty discourages extra loss on points that the mean already classifies correctly. A matched component study shows why each design choice is needed: an unconstrained learned mixture loses 1.032 mIoU points relative to probability mean, harm regularization restores 0.359 points at fixed capacity, and removing an unnecessary point-wise gate slightly improves accuracy and stability. With three zones for fitting, two disjoint zones for residual-strength selection, and router-untouched t5b5 for final reporting, CableMoE obtains 84.906% mIoU and 98.140 % overall accuracy. This is +10.000 points over SPT and +0.263 over probability mean; all three seeds improve the latter. Across pylon, conductor, structural-cable, and insulator classes, macro-IoU rises from 84.517% for SPT and 97.153% for probability mean to 98.144 %. The results support conservative residual composition, not a claim of a new segmentation backbone or universal state of the art

papers.title: The AMPEL Platform: A Concept for Open-Source Collaboration in Developing In-House Medical Device Software under EU-Regulation
papers.abstract: Clinical decision support systems (CDSS) are expected to enhance medical treatment through automated data analysis, yet a substantial evidence gap persists as to whether they actually improve patient outcomes. It arises due to the black-box nature of commercial products and the constrains of the European medical device regulation (MDR) for such studies: patient outcomes may only be collected through the use of medical device software (MDSW). In-house MDSW under Article 5(5) MDR is a promising solution, allowing healthcare facilities to manufacture and study such software for their own use under reduced requirements. However, the overall limited experience with in-house MDSW development in Europe currently restricts the widespread use of this regulatory approach. While open-source software generally fosters evidence generation, publishing an in-house MDSW as open source would risk a classification as "placement on the market", which the MDR prohibits. The concept presented here builds on experience from developing an in-house CDSS at the University of Leipzig Medical Center, expert discussions, a literature review and a formal legal opinion. A companion online wiki summarizes and regularly updates the results. The current concept outlines a shared open-source codebase, which doesn't constitute a medical device under the MDR. Also, "Data Input" modules must be programmed separately at each site, while still allowing for multicenter collaboration on the codebase. Atypically for open-source projects, this leaves a considerable effort to deploy the software within each site, e.g. each healthcare facility must independently meet the MDR requirements for an in-house MDSW. The AMPEL concept describes a regulatory pathway for the open-source publication and development of in-house MDSW. It underpins the open-source AMPEL platform, which helps healthcare facilities build their own in-house CDSS.

papers.title: Sharp signature-weighted total-curvature bounds for complete minimal submanifolds
papers.abstract: Let $i:M^n\to\R^{n+p}$ be a complete connected minimal immersion, with $n\ge3$. We get a sharp bound of $\int_M |A|^n\ddμ$ from below in terms of the number of ends and the mod-two Betti numbers of $M$. As an application, if $\int_M |A|^n\ddμ<γ_n$, then $i(M)$ is an affine $n$-plane. Moreover, if $\int_M |A|^n\ddμ=γ_n$, then $i(M)$ is an $n$-catenoid in an affine $(n+1)$-plane, where $γ_n=\frac{[n(n-1)]^{n/2}}{n-1}\Vol(\Sn^n)$.

papers.title: Compactness-like properties in Alexandroff paratopological groups
papers.abstract: We study compactness-like and covering properties in non-compact Alexandroff paratopological groups. Several properties are characterized in terms of the order structure associated with the Alexandroff topology and the number of connected components. We establish equivalences among $2$-pseudocompactness, countable $o$-compactness, Baire, and an intersection property for increasing chains. We also obtain a common characterization of $σ$-local compactness, $σ$-compactness, the Lindelöf property, and left $ω$-precompactness in terms of the existence of a countable cofinal subset. Moreover, we characterize pseudocompactness, $H$-compactness, star-compactness, the countable chain condition, and the weakly Lindelöf property by means of the number of connected components. Finally, we determine further implications among the properties considered and provide examples and counterexamples.

papers.title: Early Realignment of Eccentric Planetary Orbits without Orbital Decay
papers.abstract: Warm Jupiters are, on average, more closely aligned with their host stars than hot Jupiters, even at high eccentricities. The low projected obliquities of eccentric warm Jupiters on the tidal migration track are difficult to reconcile with high-eccentricity migration (HEM) pathways that excite large misalignments. We examine whether tides acting on the star can realign initially misaligned systems before their orbits circularize. We extend a frequency-dependent tidal model to arbitrary eccentricities and focus on the $(1,0)$ obliquity tide. This component is stationary in the inertial frame, dissipates stellar rotational energy, and can change spin obliquity while leaving the semimajor axis and eccentricity unchanged. Its forcing frequency in the stellar rotating frame coincides with that of the rigid spin-over mode, which is non-dissipative. The strength of dissipation by non-rigid motions at this same frequency remains uncertain. In our models, enhancing the dissipative response by a factor of $10^7$ produces appreciable obliquity damping for Jupiter-mass planets. The stronger damping for more massive planets suggests that an enhancement of $10^6$ may suffice for super-Jupiters. Realignment can outpace circularization if the planet is already on an eccentric warm orbit while the star is still inflated and rapidly rotating during the pre-main sequence (PMS). If alignment occurs then, present-day stellar effective temperature may be a weak predictor of obliquity. In binary-driven HEM runs initialized at the zero-age main sequence, orbital circularization outpaces realignment in systems with sustained eccentricity forcing. The stellar quadrupole scaling suggests substantially stronger suppression of eccentricity excitation for PMS starts. These results cast doubt on binary-driven HEM as the origin of such aligned eccentric warm Jupiters, even when they lie along the tidal migration track.

papers.title: How Do Deep Networks Encode and Selectively Use Information? Shared Encoding and Conditional Signed Readout in Vision and Language Models
papers.abstract: How can trained deep networks retain contextual information across internal representations while using it selectively in a decision? We study this question through controlled background-texture edits in vision classifiers and entity-binding edits in frozen language models. Across both modalities, factor perturbations preserve recognizable structure across pre-fixed, mutually disjoint blocks of hidden units: visual channel blocks match their complements more closely for the same image than for other images under the same texture edit, while language blocks transfer a relational direction fitted under one query role to rank relational states within held-out name pairs under the other role. We then decompose the local output change into signed channel and pathway contributions. In a convolutional classifier, net channel-level reinforcement ($R^{(512)}>1$) coexists on individual images with cancellation between positive- and negative-weight groups ($R^{(2)}<1$). Holding weights, the paired relation edit, and red/blue answer words fixed, switching prompt presentation reverses the mean finite selection effect in Qwen2.5. Two held-out tests validate this mechanism. Attenuating development-selected antagonistic units amplifies edit effects on unseen inputs; in a vision transformer, attenuating the same frozen units in one forward pass increases the mean magnitude of the background-edit effect on one class margin and reduces it on another, with the opposite pattern for a second group (four-cell paired interaction $+78.30\times 10^{-5}$ logit). Finally, combining conditional channel variance with fixed downstream readout weights predicts single-channel pruning recovery across ten cuts. These results show how shared encoding and conditional signed readout can coexist in vision and language models.

papers.title: Geneva seven-colour synthetic photometry from Gaia DR3 spectrophotometry
papers.abstract: The well-established calibrations of astrophysical parameters derived from classical photometric systems (e.g. those of Johnson, Stromgren-Crawford, and Vilnius) are rarely applied at present. Instead, spectral energy distribution fitting techniques and the very broad Gaia photometric system are typically employed. However, these approaches have proven highly inaccurate for upper main-sequence stars. In this work, the Geneva seven-colour photometric system was synthesised from flux-calibrated low-resolution Gaia spectrophotometry (BP/RP spectra). The available ground-based observations have made it the most homogeneous dataset, offering a number of astrophysical calibrations and applications. The GaiaXPy Tool was used to synthesise the seven filters. The original Geneva U had to be exchanged with the SDSS u because it is found to be significantly blueward of the cut-off of the BP/RP spectra. The ground-based observations were used to correct for offsets and the known temperature dependence of the effective temperature in the ultraviolet region of the BP/RP spectra. The test using well-known effective temperature and metallicity calibrations on the synthetic photometry (with 21 080 stars) demonstrated the high accuracy of this approach. Further checks for possible correlations between the projected rotational velocity and binarity yielded negative results. As a direct application, the metallicity of 630 open clusters (and, thus, the radial Galactic metallicity gradient) was determined. Finally, we compiled a catalogue of 25 881 397 objects. This work demonstrates that alternatives exist to the widely used three-band Gaia photometric system. The Geneva seven-colour approach can help calibrate and analyse astrophysical parameters, especially those of upper main-sequence stars.

papers.title: Lessons from Chess: Mathematics in the Age of AI
papers.abstract: The history of chess offers a perspective on the growing role of artificial intelligence in mathematics. We explore the parallels and limitations of this analogy and consider possible directions for mathematical research, education, and the public perception of mathematics.

papers.title: On the theorem of F. Riesz on Blaschke products and on inner functions in the unit ball of $\mathbb C^{n}
papers.abstract: For a convergent Blaschke product $f$ in the unit disc of $\mathbb C$, let $G(f)$ be the set of all points $t$ on the unit circle for which $|f(rt)| \rightarrow 1$ as $r \rightarrow 1$. By a classical F. Riesz theorem $G(f)$ is of full measure, which describes $G$ metrically. We describe $G$ topologically by proving that it is a $G_δ$ set. The same description is true in general for inner functions not only in the unit disc but also in the unit ball of $\mathbb C^n$.

papers.title: Age and Gender Estimation from Face and Ocular Smartphone Images via Identity Transfer and Ordinal Learning
papers.abstract: We investigate the transferability of identity-recognition representations to gender and age estimation from face and ocular images. Three CNNs of varying complexity, pre-trained for face or ocular identity recognition, are evaluated using fixed features with SVMs and end-to-end adaptation. Experiments use 11,299 frontal smartphone images from Adience, following its predefined five-fold protocol and subject-disjoint validation. Results show that domain-matched identity pre-training outperforms direct ImageNet and scratch initialisation in end-to-end training, while combining both ocular regions narrows the gap with full-face estimation, especially for age. We additionally introduce an ordinal loss that exploits the ordering of age groups and consistently improves 1-off accuracy across architectures and input regions. Across the evaluated configurations, best gender accuracies reach 88.1% for the face and 82.9% for combined ocular regions, while age estimation reaches 59.0% exact and 93.1% 1-off accuracy for ocular images, versus 57.6% and 95.2% for the full face. To our knowledge, these are the highest ocular age accuracies reported on Adience.

papers.title: SYCLDB: A Cross-Vendor Heterogeneous Analytical DBMS
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of AI and analytical workloads has increased the need for fast, interactive analytical data processing. This, in turn, has led to a surge of interest in designing accelerated analytical database engines that can exploit modern GPUs to scale computation. While GPUs provide the massive data-parallelism required by modern analytics, the software landscape remains dominated by closed-source, vendor-locked programming models, like CUDA, limiting portability across multi-vendor GPUs. In this work, we present SYCLDB, an end-to-end analytical database engine built upon the SYCL open standard, designed to enable efficient, hardware-agnostic execution across a wide range of accelerators using a single codebase. By implementing core relational operators as modular SYCL kernels, integrating them with a SQL frontend based on Apache Calcite and Apache Thrift, and supporting Apache Arrow for efficient columnar ingestion, SYCLDB reduces dependence on vendor-specific GPU programming stacks by enabling a single SYCL codebase to execute analytical query pipelines across Intel, AMD, and NVIDIA GPUs.

papers.title: Deviant Machines: Innovation, Containment, and the Prevention of Autonomous Misalignment
papers.abstract: From May to September 2026, AI agents in training or evaluation at OpenAI, Anthropic and the UK AI Security Institute reached real third-party systems, published malicious packages, used fake identities to manipulate open-source maintainers, probed government data services, and wrote instructions into their own future contexts. Criminology has mostly treated AI as a tool for human offenders. This article treats these systems as deviant rather than criminal: they departed from training, rules and constraints without the intent that criminal concepts assume. It offers an exploratory, theory-informed analysis of documented records, using plausibility probes across three incident complexes and four behavioral clusters, profiled on four evidence dimensions that separate who acted from why. Drawing on Merton, it argues that goal pressure plus blocked legitimate means is a structural condition for innovation, and that whether it ends in containment or harm depends on the means chosen and the controls in place, not the goal. Three framework families fit the record best, each linking diagnosis to remedy: routine activity theory and situational prevention (handlers, guardians, place managers), organizational deviance and safety science (escalation, safeguard parity), and goal-means strain with differential opportunity (sanctioned exits, guarding illegitimate means), the last only structurally. Restrictive deterrence adds an analogy: penalizing visible reasoning produced less monitorable reasoning. The article proposes conditions that keep departures accountable and contestable, and allocates prevention responsibility across developers, evaluation partners, operators, platforms and the system, distinct from blame or legal liability. Because the record is shaped by disclosure and observed departures, the analysis shows plausibility and practical relevance, not a causal test.

papers.title: Exact Hausdorff and Packing Dimensions of $k$-Singular Matrices
papers.abstract: We determine the Hausdorff and packing dimensions of $k$-singular $m\times n$ matrices for all $m,n\geq1$ and $2\leq k\leq m+n-1$. Such matrices are characterized by the $(k-1)$st successive minimum tending to zero and the $(k+1)$st tending to infinity along an associated diagonal-flow orbit. The exact formula was announced by Das--Fishman--Simmons--Urbański in 2017 and formulated as a conjecture in their 2024 paper, which proves the matching Hausdorff-dimension lower bound. We prove the matching packing-dimension upper bound, resolving their Conjecture~5.1. The proof uses their variational principle together with a linear potential that corrects the local contraction rate. The corrected rate is nondecreasing under mergers of adjacent equality blocks that preserve a separating gap, reducing the estimate to two-block configurations. Secant-line estimates at integer points then allow us to choose a single pair of potential coefficients that controls both possible separating gaps. The dimension formula remains valid after excluding trivially singular matrices.

papers.title: Analytic $k$-essence Inflation
papers.abstract: In this work we develop a fully analytic $k$-essence inflation solution which is compatible with the observational constraints on inflation, without the need for the slow-roll assumption being imposed dynamically in the field equations. The analytic solution is obtained for a kinetic scalar sector of the form $K(X)= \frac{X^n}{X_s^{n-1}}$ and for the scalar field satisfying a tracking condition $\dotϕ^2=γH^{-m}$. For this class of theories, the sound speed of the primordial curvature perturbations is constant, so no gradient instabilities occur in the theory. The Hubble rate, the scale factor and the scalar field can be analytically expressed as functions of the cosmic time, and the observational indices of inflation depend solely on the parameters $n$ and $m$. The resulting evolution is inflationary and it develops a pressure singularity a few $e$-foldings after the end of inflation. However, using qualitative and quantitative numerical arguments, we show that the pressure singularity is classically avoided when the matter fluids of radiation and cold dark matter are taken into account.

papers.title: Quantifying and calibrating precision gain from covariate adjustment in clinical trials with binary endpoints
papers.abstract: Covariate adjustment is widely used in randomized clinical trials to improve estimation and inference of treatment effects. For continuous endpoints, the reasoning is straightforward: prognostic baseline covariates explain outcome variability and thereby increase precision. For binary endpoints, however, the situation is more complex because conditional and marginal effects generally differ in nonlinear outcome models such as logistic regression. We develop a theoretical framework for quantifying the maximum attainable first-order precision gain from covariate adjustment when estimating marginal treatment effects for binary endpoints. We derive a closed-form identity showing that precision-gain potential is governed by an estimand- and allocation-specific combination of the treatment-specific risk functions. Building on this identity, we introduce marginal prognostic strength as a population-level measure of prognostic information and characterize when it determines precision-gain potential and when the two quantities decouple. Specifically, substantial prognostic information within both treatment arms need not translate into improved precision for the marginal treatment effect when covariates are predictive on the target effect scale. We further develop a calibration algorithm for methodological simulation studies that preserves prespecified conditional outcome structures and marginal risks while allowing data-generating mechanisms to be calibrated by marginal prognostic strength and evaluated in terms of estimand-specific precision-gain potential. Together, these results provide a theoretical and practical framework for understanding, quantifying, and calibrating potential precision gains from covariate adjustment for binary endpoints.

papers.title: DyLoMo-DiT: Dynamic Looped Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) scale model capacity by increasing both parameter count and computation. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) variants expand parameter capacity while keeping per-token computation roughly fixed, but still require substantial parameter storage. In this paper, we propose Dynamic Looped MoE DiT (DyLoMo-DiT), which reuses parameters rather than adding them: a weight-shared loop repeatedly applies the middle layers, while sparse experts allocate parameter capacity across tokens. This design deepens the network without adding parameters, freeing the parameter budget for other uses, such as more experts or more distinct layers. It also allocates compute dynamically, varying the number of passes across noise levels. Experiments show that DyLoMo-DiT makes more effective use of parameter and compute budgets, with further gains from assigning more passes to low-noise steps. On ImageNet $256\times256$, DyLoMo-DiT reduces FID by 11-24% relative to DiT and 36-56% relative to DiT-MoE at matched parameter and compute budgets. For text-to-image generation, a scaled DyLoMo-DiT achieves a higher GenEval score than FLUX.1 (0.714 vs. 0.673), with less than one tenth of its active parameters (1.05B vs. 12B).

papers.title: Cleaning correlation matrices with external information: the Maximum Variance estimat
papers.abstract: Rotationally invariant estimators clean the eigenvalues of an empirical correlation matrix but keep its noisy eigenvectors. We study an estimator that corrects the eigenvectors by using external information, namely a partition of the assets into groups such as asset classes or regions. The Maximum Variance (MaxVar) estimator restricts the leading eigenvectors to linear combinations of the maximum-variance portfolios of the groups and replaces the rest of the spectrum by a single eigenvalue. It is a factor model with about n parameters instead of n2/2, and it is positive de nite even when the number of observations is smaller than the number of assets n. We apply it to the correlation matrix of 47 futures on stock indices, bonds and currencies, with the three asset classes as groups. In an illustrative Monte Carlo test, in which the reference matrix has the structure assumed by the estimator, the distance to the reference is reduced by one third with respect to the empirical matrix, against less than 10% for the rotationally invariant estimator. The decisive test is the performance of a portfolio on real data: over 1993-2018, the Sharpe ratio of the risk parity portfolio, which involves the inverse of the matrix, is 1.28 with the MaxVar estimator, 1.24 with the rotationally invariant estimator and 1.17 with the empirical matrix, and the advantage increases when the estimation window is shortened.

papers.title: Strong Banach property $(T)$ for $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb R)$
papers.abstract: Strong Banach property $(T)$ has been established for higher-rank algebraic groups over non-Archimedean local fields with respect to Banach spaces of nontrivial type. However, in the real setting, existing results have required additional geometric hypotheses on the Banach spaces, leaving the corresponding question open even for $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb R)$. We prove that $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb R)$ has strong Banach property $(T)$ with respect to every class of complex Banach spaces of uniformly nontrivial Rademacher type.

papers.title: Constructive continuous and sampled-data control of nonstandard singularly perturbed parabolic systems
papers.abstract: The existing results on control of singularly perturbed (SP) PDE systems are all qualitative with stability guaranteed for small values of SP parameter $\varepsilon$, whereas control design is confined to stable fast systems. In the present paper we study the finite-dimensional output-feedback boundary stabilization of SP parabolic systems with Neumann actuators and nonlocal sensors acting on both the slow and fast dynamics. This configuration allows us to treat not only unstable fast systems, but even a larger class of nonstandard SP systems (where the fast dynamics with $\varepsilon=0$ cannot be solved with respect to the fast state). We design a finite-dimensional controller based on the slow descriptor PDE system. We consider the continuous-time control and, for the first time, (even for the state-feedback for SP PDEs) its sampled-data implementation. For the latter, we introduce a multi-rate sampled-data framework in which the slow and fast variables can be sampled asynchronously. We consider time-triggered control input sampling and event-triggered output sampling. We prove the avoidance of Zeno behavior and derive LMI conditions for finding upper bounds on the observer dimension, sampling control intervals and $\varepsilon$ that preserve the stability. Our results include a new finite-dimensional controller design for the parabolic-elliptic equation. Numerical simulations demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed method.

papers.title: Certified Defense against Adversarial Patches on Traffic Signs via Mask-Aware Training
papers.abstract: Adversarial patches are a practical threat to traffic-sign recognition: a small sticker on a sign can change a classifier's decision. PatchCleanser is a certified defense that applies two rounds of masking and, for every image it certifies, provably returns the correct label for any patch that fits inside one mask. We show that on traffic signs the defense certifies almost nothing when paired with a normally trained classifier (1.7% to 4.8% certified accuracy on GTSRB), because a single mask can hide the small central symbol that distinguishes sign classes. We propose mask-aware training, which trains the classifier on images occluded by random pairs drawn from the defense's own mask set, with a sampling bias toward masks over the sign's centre. The defense, mask set and certification procedure are unchanged, so the guarantee is preserved. For an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50, mask-aware training raises certified accuracy from 4.8% to 60.0%. Under real per-image adversarial patches, the defended ResNet-50 reaches 85.7% accuracy, versus 74.6% for the original PatchCleanser with a normally trained ResNet-50.

papers.title: SARA: An Auditor-in-the-Loop LLM Recommender for Sustainability Reports
papers.abstract: Auditing corporate sustainability reports requires assurance professionals to map a company-specific checklist drawn from roughly 1,700 regulatory requirements onto the relevant passages of lengthy, repeatedly revised draft reports and to judge compliance. We present SARA (Sustainability Reporting Assistant), a human-in-the-loop recommender system delivered as a Microsoft Word add-in that recommends, for each requirement, the passages addressing it and predicts a compliance verdict while keeping the auditor in full control. SARA casts auditing as content-based recommendation over a fixed regulatory taxonomy and makes per-requirement large language model (LLM) matching cheaper, faster, and more accurate through topic-prediction filtering: on expert-annotated reports, it reduces matching cost about sixfold and runtime by 42% versus feeding the full report to the LLM. It is in production use across PwC Germany's sustainability-assurance practice.

papers.title: Interpretable Discovery of Heterogeneous Causal Dose-Response Curves
papers.abstract: Discovering subgroups with heterogeneous treatment effects is a central task in causal inference. While methods for heterogeneous effect discovery have proliferated for discrete treatments, their counterparts for continuous treatments remain underdeveloped. In this paper, we introduce a novel, data-adaptive algorithm for discovering interpretable subgroups with heterogeneous causal dose-response curves. This algorithm combines doubly-robust dose-response curve estimation with recursive partitioning, using flexible objective functions to quantify heterogeneity across potential subgroups' dose-response curves. First, we show that the standard doubly-robust pseudo-outcome for continuous treatments cannot serve this purpose. We therefore construct the pseudo-outcome separately for each candidate subgroup, using subgroup-specific g-computation and a subgroup-specific stabilizing density. Finally, we characterize the differences between dose-response curves detected by each objective function. We establish uniform convergence of the splitting criteria and give conditions for recovery of the population greedy tree. We apply it to county-level data on fine particulate matter pollution (PM2.5) and mortality in the contiguous United States over the period 2000-2019. The discovered heterogeneous subgroups vary by education, income, and race. The proposed algorithm is implemented in the R package discoverHTE.

papers.title: On the Geometry of Quadratic Maps
papers.abstract: To analyse a homogeneous quadratic map $Q:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^\ell$, the critical value variety $Σ_{Q}$ of its restriction to the unit sphere is very useful but difficult to handle. We prove its dual hypersurface $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is of degree $k$ (providing its equation) and is $\mathit{hyperbolic}$: every line though the origin in $\mathbb{R}^\ell$ cuts it at $k$ real points, counting multiplicities. These facts imply: $\boldsymbol{1}$. $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is the union of $k/2$ nested topological hyperspheres if $k$ is even, or the union of $(k-1)/2$ nested topological hyperspheres and one topological projective hyperplane if $k$ is odd. $\boldsymbol{2}$. The Toeplitz-Haussdorf Theorem on the range of of the restriction of $Q$ to the unit sphere if $k>\ell$. $\boldsymbol{3}$. The dual version of the hyperbolicity of $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is: the critical value variety $Σ_{Q}$ is of class $k$. $\boldsymbol{4}$. For generic $Q:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^k$, $Σ_{Q}$ contains $\lfloor\frac{k-1}{2}\rfloor$ collections of ellipsoids of codimension $2$ consisting of degenerate parabolic points. $\boldsymbol{5}$. If $k>\ell$, the parabolic set in $Σ_{Q}$ (if any) is a union of hyperplane closed discs bounded by ellipsoids. $\boldsymbol{6}$. The above ellipsoids (items $4$ and $5$) are in bijection with the isolated singular points in $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$.

papers.title: Can Multimodal Fusion MakeSense for Embodied Vision in Degraded Sensing?
papers.abstract: Embodied vision systems rely on complementary sensors to perceive and act as conditions change. Even models that accept arbitrary sensor subsets can exhibit negative fusion: adding a sensor increases prediction error. We propose MakeSense, a multimodal fusion framework that preserves sensor-specific evidence in private streams and combines information through shared bottleneck tokens. Training pairs full and subset views of the same degraded observations, penalizing higher error with more sensors. Where geometry permits, the distance readout uses range measurements alone, while the rest of the prediction draws on all available inputs. Paired tests across five datasets reveal helpful and harmful sensor additions. MakeSense reduces negative fusion on MM-Fi. With lightweight adapters and per-dataset training, the same design improves UAV localization on MMAUD, cooperative 3D detection on V2X-Real, few-shot pose transfer to RELI11D, and command prediction on Humanoid-Everyday, where a world model trained on the frozen core's outputs forecasts future fused states more accurately than a linear baseline at longer tested horizons. MakeSense supports embodied sensing across human activity, aerial systems, robotics, and autonomous driving.

papers.title: The KL Divergence Is Never Negative, Except in PyTorch
papers.abstract: A Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence is never negative, yet PyTorch users have reported negative values for years, and the standard advice is to clamp them at zero. The sign is only the visible part of a silent failure. Many machine-learning applications compare nearby distributions, where conventional KL formulas lose accuracy. On 8.5 million inputs with certified references across 18 closed-form KL families and F.kl_div, we find widespread errors in values and gradients on CPU and GPU. Among scalar families in ordinary parameter ranges, over 85% of FP32 values have at least 1% relative error near KL 10^(-7) (FP16: 10^(-3)), and about 30% become negative at smaller divergences. More precision is not the cure: evaluated one precision higher, the same formulas still leave 7--51% of FP32 values significantly wrong for 22 of 23 configurations. Stable closed-form decompositions, compensated arithmetic, and analytic gradients remove over 97% of significant errors in the working format. Strict repairs eliminate significant errors on 7.2 million scored closed-form samples and correctly round all 567 million scored F.kl_div components. The errors affect parameter fitting, Bayesian decisions, identical-start distillation (up to 97% top-1 disagreement), KL-based layer rankings in a quantized LLM, and 19--59% of GPT-2 circuit edge scores. With the repaired code they all but vanish. Code and data: https://github.com/xi-xiaoran/stablekl

papers.title: Unique continuation and its failure for the Monge--Ampère equation
papers.abstract: We study unique continuation for Alexandrov solutions with common Monge--Ampère density bounded above and below. In the plane, we prove that agreement on an open set forces global equality. For every bounded domain \(Ω\subset\mathbb R^n\) with \(n\ge3\), we construct two distinct uniformly convex \(C^{1,1}(Ω)\) solutions that agree on a nonempty open subset of \(Ω\).

papers.title: Disc functionals and rational curves
papers.abstract: We prove a criterion for the existence of rational curves on compact Kähler manifolds using disc functionals. As applications, we obtain a transcendental version of the Miyaoka--Mori theorem with an optimal degree bound and a new proof of the characterization of uniruled compact Kähler manifolds.

papers.title: A geometric-IEQ approach for curvature-driven flows
papers.abstract: We introduce a geometric invariant energy quadratization (IEQ) formulation for the $L^2$-gradient flow of a class of curvature-dependent energies of closed hypersurfaces, where the energy density depends on the mean curvature and the unit normal. A square-root auxiliary variable converts the geometric energy into a quadratic functional. Combining its evolution equation with a skew-symmetric treatment of surface transport yields a weak formulation whose energy law depends only on the normal velocity and is therefore independent of the chosen tangential motion. We construct monolithic nonlinear parametric finite element methods by coupling a common IEQ discretization with one of two geometric formulations that accommodate either the Barrett-Garcke-Nürnberg (BGN) tangential velocity or the minimal-deformation-rate (MDR) tangential velocity. Both fully discrete approximations satisfy an unconditional decay estimate for the discrete quadratic energy. We further extend the construction to anisotropic Willmore flow, and to $H^{-1}$-gradient flows. A variety of numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the robustness and accuracy of the introduced methods.

papers.title: 1+1 dimensional relativistic viscous magnetohydrodynamics with self-consistent longitudinal acceleration
papers.abstract: We study $(1+1)$-dimensional relativistic viscous magnetohydrodynamics with self-consistent longitudinal acceleration under the conformal equation of state $\varepsilon=3p$. We evolve temperature, fluid rapidity, and shear stress using energy conservation, longitudinal momentum conservation, and a shear-relaxation law in a prescribed transverse magnetic stress. Moving beyond longitudinal boost invariance, we derive perturbative analytical expressions in the Navier--Stokes approximation and obtain nonlinear solutions with shear relaxation, comparing dynamical and prescribed accelerating flows from identical initial conditions. The initial temperature curvature generates a longitudinal pressure gradient that alters the rapidity slope, modifies longitudinal expansion work, and produces a distinct cooling history. For the reference parameters, shear viscosity enhances the resulting central temperature difference much more strongly than the prescribed magnetic stress, while the condition for equal central temperatures shifts with proper time and initial shear. At $χ=λ^*=0.03$, the maximum relative difference in central temperature is $0.18\%$ over $0.6$--$6$~fm/$c$, despite a persistent momentum residual in the prescribed flow. Because the velocity mapping also enters the entropy per unit fluid rapidity, the rapidity distribution remains sensitive to the flow evolution even when central temperatures closely agree. Replacing the prescribed field with ideal induction removes direct magnetic work while retaining magnetic pressure and inertia in the longitudinal momentum balance.

papers.title: Analytic nuclear gradients for electronic resonances with the equation-of-motion coupled-cluster method and complex basis functions
papers.abstract: We present the general theory for and an efficient implementation of the analytic nuclear gradient for states which are metastable with respect to electronic decay within the equation-of-motion coupled-cluster singles-and-doubles family of methods using complex-scaled basis functions. We highlight the differences of our approach with the complex-absorbing potential method and outline a computational protocol for geometry optimisations and we use the method to compute equilibrium structures and harmonic vibrational frequencies of a number of temporary anion shape resonances and core-ionised Feshbach resonances.

papers.title: Potential Games for Self-Neighborhood Channel Mixing in Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Graph message passing must balance two competing objectives: incorporating neighborhood signals while preserving node-specific information. We model this trade-off as a game in which nodes choose how to mix their own representations with strict-neighborhood aggregates. For fixed channel representations, task supervision defines a common-payoff game, while local distinctness payoffs induce an exact potential game whose potential is the degree-normalized strict Dirichlet energy. We introduce CG2, which amortizes these choices through a shared six-parameter policy per layer based on local channel statistics and can be trained using either objective. Controlled comparisons show that the shared task-trained policy improves mean performance over fixed mixing on three of five heterophily benchmarks, with significant gains on two, while free per-node actions trained with either objective rarely improve on the same baseline. On the ECHO long-range benchmark, the clearest contribution of the gate appears on eccentricity, where the task-trained policy substantially reduces prediction error.

papers.title: Real-time optimization with online learning for pressure swing adsorption
papers.abstract: Real-time optimization (RTO) of pressure swing adsorption (PSA) units requires a process model that can be evaluated many times at each decision, which favours data-driven surrogates of the cyclic steady state. A surrogate, however, represents the plant only under the conditions covered by its training data, and disturbances that are not among its inputs remain outside its description. This work presents an RTO framework for PSA in which a neural network surrogate, optimized by particle swarm, is updated online with data generated at the plant when plant and model diverge. A rigorous dynamic model of a CH$_4$/CO$_2$ separation, integrated to cyclic steady state, served as virtual plant in three scenarios. In the first, five consecutive RTO events with different objectives ran without disturbance; all constraints were satisfied and the largest deviation between surrogate and plant was 1.7 percentage points. In the second, a step in the CO$_2$ feed fraction from 0.40 to 0.50 reduced the CH$_4$ purity at the operating point in force from 92.3 to 76.9%; after the network was fine-tuned on 43 local samples, the new RTO event returned a feasible optimum with a purity of 90.3%. In the third, a progressive loss of sorbent capacity was detected by the accumulated relative deviation of the CH$_4$ purity from a reference, triggering retraining before any constraint violation. Samples generated across the remaining activity range led to infeasible operation, whereas samples generated at the final activity kept the purity above 92.4% after the move transient.

papers.title: Data-Driven Nonlinear Observer Design Using the Koopman Generator
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the data-driven design of nonlinear continuous-time observers using the Koopman generator. For systems without inputs, an observer is designed that consists of a linear system part with a nonlinear output injection. Therein, the output injection introduces additional degrees of freedom to ensure an invariant dictionary or a small projection error. Subsequently, this observer is extended to systems with inputs. These results form the basis for a data-driven nonlinear observer design using generator extended dynamic mode decomposition. Probabilistic finite-data error bounds are derived for the observer error w.r.t. the data-driven observer error dynamics and for the corresponding steady-state observation error. Examples of nonlinear systems with invariant and non-invariant dictionaries illustrate the effectiveness of the novel data-driven observer design procedure.

papers.title: Task-Dependent Linguistic Measures in Aphasia Discourse: A Comparative Analysis of Narrative, Descriptive, and Procedural Speech
papers.abstract: Background: Transcript-based measures such as word counts, lexical diversity and disfluency rates are widely used to describe language ability in aphasia. Each measure comes from a specific elicitation task, and studies use different tasks, so values from different tasks may not be comparable. Aims: To test whether discourse tasks change these measures within the same speakers, and whether the measures follow a gradient from Procedural to Descriptive to Narrative discourse. Methods & Procedures: Baseline transcripts from 61 adults with chronic post-stroke aphasia were taken from the Fridriksson-2 corpus in AphasiaBank (POLAR trial, ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03416738). Each speaker produced a Procedural (Sandwich), a Descriptive (Broken Window) and a Narrative (Cinderella) sample in one session. A rule-based pipeline extracted 13 measures, 10 of which were common enough to test. Friedman, Page and Wilcoxon tests with false discovery rate correction were used, with a speaker-grouped Random Forest classifier as a supporting check. Outcomes & Results: Total words and number of different words followed the full gradient, but the step from Procedural to Descriptive was small. For most other measures, Narrative stood apart, while Descriptive and Procedural did not differ. Among the 31 speakers with at least 25 words in every task, filler rate, repetition rate and total disfluency density were higher in Narrative than in both other tasks. The classifier reached an accuracy of 0.61 (always guessing the most common task would give 0.41), mainly by recognizing Narrative samples. Conclusions: Discourse tasks are not interchangeable, and expressing disfluencies per word does not remove the task effect. The task should be reported with every measure, and values should be compared only within the same task.

papers.title: Doc-to-LoRA Analysis: Query Conditioning, Wrong Facts, and Distractor Interference
papers.abstract: Doc-to-LoRA (D2L) compiles documents into low-rank adapters, allowing language models to use their contents without repeatedly processing the original text. We investigate its suitability for internalizing user memories through factual question answering, controlled interventions, and a production MidBrain memory pipeline. Across Gemma-2-2B and Qwen3-4B, D2L loses accuracy relative to in-context learning, with additional documents introducing substantial interference. Single-document errors frequently match answers to other questions about the same passage, suggesting unreliable question-answer attribution. Layer-wise interventions show that interference accumulates across depth, with more concentrated early damage at larger bank sizes on Gemma. With eight documents, applying the full bank in the initial layers gives similar accuracy to withholding all document contributions there. Source membership is detectable in intermediate states, but trained readers do not reliably resolve the interference. On PersonaMem-v2, joint compilation and normalized adapter composition achieve accuracy close to consolidated text memory when retrieved episodes remain text, but the resulting token savings are modest. Measured throughput gains also depend on model and batch size despite substantial reductions in analytical compute. Together, these findings limit the practical case for D2L as a replacement for text-based memory and motivate investigating online-learning methods that acquire personalized behavior from interactions in which memory is used.

papers.title: On convergence rate bounds for Markovian push-sum algorithms
papers.abstract: In this work we establish an upper bound on the almost sure convergence rate of a broad class of push-sum algorithms, more precisely for those where message passing events follow a Markovian dynamics, or a Hidden Markov Model. In this context, having a computationally accessible quantity at hand is of top priority; we thus formulate tools to cut down the complexity of obtaining the stated bound. Furthermore, we introduce a transformation to adjust a given push-sum scheme in a way that the bound on the rate provably improves -- and often so does the true convergence rate. Theoretical understanding is complemented by numerical results, where the quality of all three directions is demonstrated: for the bound on the rate, for the computational complexity and for the improvement strategy.

papers.title: Spontaneous Axis-Switching Swirling in Transonic Core-Annular Flow of Highly Differentiated Fluids
papers.abstract: Forcing fluids to interact at high speeds creates a multitude of instabilities. Prior studies considered the consequences of these instabilities for core-annular flow (CAF) or atomization systems. However, the existence of spontaneous axis-switching swirling (SASS) modalities in CAF have never been explored. We computationally demonstrate this new behavior for a CAF of steam surrounded by a cold non-Newtonian fuel. Wave pile-up created 3-D fuel surface disturbances which eventually became thin slender lobes with radial modal deformation. Those slender lobes were subject to further instabilities and resulted in oscillatory tangential velocities that were a large fraction of the core steam velocity and orthogonal to the axially flowing base fuel wave. Since these tangential velocities were not externally imposed by atomizer geometry or boundary conditions, it was concluded that they are self-generating. Frequency analysis revealed that SASS tended to operate at the base wave frequency. We additionally explored numerical uncertainty with our previously validated computational tool and found that SASS behavior can be achieved on a coarse, limited mesh at relatively low simulation times.

papers.title: Fast and Consistent Structure Learning in Graphical Models via Approximate Cross-Validation
papers.abstract: Structure learning for sparse graphical models in high dimensions requires both computational scalability and selection consistency. Classical criteria such as (Extended) Bayesian Information Criterion can provide consistency, but rely on model-specific likelihoods and complexity calibration. In comparison, cross-validation avoids such analytic calibration and is therefore attractive for graph learning. However, cross-validation is computationally infeasible and theoretically inconsistent in structure learning. This creates a tension between consistency and flexibility in modeling. In this work, we resolve the tension by developing a scalable graph-recovery procedure built on approximate cross-validation. We demonstrate its effectiveness in learning large graphical models both theoretically and empirically, and establish selection consistency under mild signal strength assumptions.

papers.title: On Cohen Generic Sets in Supercompact Prikry Extensions
papers.abstract: Let $κ$ be $λ$-supercompact for a regular $λ>κ$. We show that if $λ$ is not the successor of a singular of cofinality below $κ$, $\diamondsuit(S^λ_{\geqκ})$ implies that every ${<}κ$-strategically closed forcing of size at most $λ$ is a projection of the $λ$-supercompact Prikry forcing. We show that the situation for successors of singulars of small cofinality is independent. Finally, we provide more limitations about the class of $κ$-distributive projections of the $λ$-supercompact Prikry forcing and give examples of $κ$-distributive forcings of size $λ$ which cannot be projections of this forcing.

papers.title: Linear forms in logarithms of rational numbers: an ineffective measure with the best possible exponent
papers.abstract: Let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be positive rational numbers without a nontrivial multiplicative relation. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a constant $C>0$, not effective, such that $|h_0+h_1\log a_1+\dots+h_n\log a_n| \ge C\max(1,|h_0|,\dots,|h_n|)^{-n-\varepsilon}$ for all integers $h_0,\dots,h_n$, not all zero. The exponent $n$ is best possible. For $n=1$ this is the known fact that the irrationality exponent of $\log a$ is $2$; for $h_0=0$ it gives the exponent $n$ for the linear forms $h_1\log a_1+\dots+h_n\log a_n$. The proof is an induction on $n$, starting from $n=1$. The step from $n-1$ to $n$ logarithms uses an interpolation determinant on $\mathbb{G}_m^n\times\mathbb{G}_a$ at the multiples of a rational point, in the manner of arXiv:2610.28079; its geometric part, a curve inequality, is proved by a second induction, on the number of torus coordinates, with the two-torus inequality of arXiv:2610.28079 as the base. The method is the interpolation and determinant method of OpenAI's preprint on the irrationality exponent of $π$; the case $n=1$ was obtained earlier by Liu, Jiang and Zhang (arXiv:2610.10192). The theorem and its corollary are verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib; the sources are in the ancillary files, on top of the Lean supplement of arXiv:2610.28079. This paper follows the formal proof: every definition, constant and intermediate statement is given in the form in which it is formalized, with the name of the Lean declaration.

papers.title: Ask Again: Answer-List Instability in Generative Engines
papers.abstract: Visibility in generative search engines is measured by which entities appear in responses, and in what order. Ask an engine the same question twice and the answer list can change: a different ordering, or different items altogether. Across 60,000 responses, we find that answers to the same prompt name a different first item 32% of the time, and even two answers with the same items disagree on which comes first. The first position is a measurement target of its own. A "clear leader" emerges after seven or eight runs, which are the budgets recommended for brand and source monitoring, but a "close leader" only about half the time. After 25 runs, a close leader is identified only 60% of the time. Variability between engines is larger than within the same engine. For open-ended prompts, the gap is more than double that for determinate ones. Search queries and cited sites observed leave most of the disagreement unexplained. Visibility measurement should report, for each engine, which items appear and how often each comes first, each with its own quantification of uncertainty.

papers.title: Search for Axion-like Particles using Blazar Observations with the HAWC Observatory
papers.abstract: Axion-like particles (ALPs) can mix with photons in astrophysical magnetic fields, modifying the propagation of very-high-energy gamma rays from distant blazars and producing an energy-dependent enhancement of the observed flux relative to the standard expectation from absorption on the extragalactic background light (EBL). We search for this signature through a joint likelihood analysis of seven TeV BL Lac objects at redshifts $z = 0.14-0.60$, combining approximately 3,000 days of HAWC observations with published High Energy Spectroscopic System (H.E.S.S.), Major Atmospheric Gamma Imaging Cherenkov Telescopes (MAGIC), and Very Energetic Radiation Imaging Telescope Array System(VERITAS) spectra. We find no statistically significant ALP signal and derive exclusion limits using the $\mathrm{CL}_s$ method. We exclude photon-ALP couplings at the 95% $\mathrm{CL}_s$ level down to $5.5 \times 10^{-12}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ for $m_a \lesssim 4$ neV and $4.6 \times 10^{-12}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ near $m_a \approx 6-9$ neV. The systematic uncertainty on the excluded parameter-space area is $-36.5\%$ to $+32.6\%$, dominated by the choice of EBL model. Because the survival probability oscillates with the coupling, the excluded region is not simply connected, and we quote at each mass the lowest excluded coupling rather than an upper bound. The combined limit is set almost entirely by the highest-redshift detected source, PG 1553+113.

papers.title: NeuroMotion: Aligning EEG to Discrete Motion Primitives for Continuous Motion Decoding
papers.abstract: EEG-to-motion decoding remains challenging because noisy scalp EEG is difficult to map directly to continuous kinematics. We present NeuroMotion, a framework that aligns EEG representations to discrete motion primitives for continuous motion decoding across heterogeneous paradigms, including full-body free movement, lower-limb treadmill locomotion, and upper-limb freewill reaching and grasping. A VQ-based motion prior discretizes continuous motion into reusable primitives that serve as both alignment prototypes and intermediate prediction targets. Prototypical and supervised contrastive objectives align EEG embeddings to motion-derived prototypes and organize them according to primitive assignments. An E2M Transformer predicts motion-code sequences from the learned EEG representations, while a final geometric refinement stage improves continuous trajectory reconstruction through motion-level training. Under a last-session test protocol, NeuroMotion achieves the best mean reconstruction performance among the compared EEG decoding baselines across all three datasets, with the clearest gains on full-body motion in both reconstruction accuracy and distribution-level quality. Multi-subject ablations further support the contributions of EEG-to-primitive alignment, token prediction, and refinement. Code is available at https://github.com/Liuyi2351433/NeuroAction.

papers.title: Unpacking the Evaluators: How Configuration Shapes the Evaluation of Alignment in Explainable AI
papers.abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) evaluation fundamentally requires human-centered evaluation, assessing whether explanations align with human reasoning and expert knowledge. However, such evaluations often require expert-driven manual validation and are difficult to scale, leading to the widespread use of alignment-based metrics, where attribution maps are compared against predefined ground-truth (GT) representations. Despite their popularity, alignment evaluations are implicitly bias towards multiple design choices made during the evaluation process, for example GT representations, metric families, metric formulations (soft vs. hard), and thresholding strategies. In this paper, we formalize alignment evaluation as a structured evaluation configuration space through which the influence of these design choices can be systematically analyzed. We further introduce a structured alignment evaluation framework that models interactions between XAI methods, GT representations, metric families, metric formulations, and thresholding strategies across 2D and 3D synthetic and real-world datasets. In addition, we propose a novel taxonomy of XAI output behavior based on local entropy and boundary mass ratio, enabling structured characterization of attribution patterns for alignment evaluation. Our experiments reveal systematic flows (triples of XAI-GT-metric configurations), showing that alignment outcomes provide distinct behavior patterns under certain configurations, such as soft/hard metric implementations. We further observe varying levels of threshold sensitivity across metric families and attribution structures. These findings demonstrate that alignment evaluation cannot be treated as a fixed or invariant measure of explanation quality, and provide practical guidance for designing more reliable and behavior-aware XAI evaluation protocols.

papers.title: Which $\Diamond \mathcal{P}$ Algorithm is Suitable for You? An Empirical Benchmark on Real Network Traces
papers.abstract: Unreliable failure detectors (UFDs) are a fundamental abstraction for dependability and fault tolerance in distributed systems, supporting core distributed algorithms, such as consensus. Yet selecting a suitable detector remains difficult because existing implementations are evaluated under different environments, workloads, parameterizations, and quality-of-service (QoS) requirements. We address this problem by systematizing 14 $\Diamond \mathcal{P}$ and closely related $\Diamond \mathcal{P}$-style UFDs, implementing 13 of them, and providing a reusable benchmark for their empirical comparison. Our methodology evaluates detectors through common QoS metrics, such as detection time, mistake rate, and query accuracy, and combines same-input replay of network traces with live deployment for detectors whose active probing or cooperative behavior requires online execution. We then formalize failure-detector selection as a constrained algorithm-selection challenge, mapping operational requirements to suitable detector candidates. We instantiate this methodology under controlled variations of communication rate, host load, and crash regime. Applying the selection process shows that no detector is uniformly preferable across the evaluated settings. At relaxed detection-time budgets, 2W [Tomsic et al., IPDPS 2015] is the most frequently selected detector, appearing in 12 of 16 scenario-metric combinations for $T_D \le 500$ ms, whereas stricter budgets yield substantially more scenario- and metric-dependent selections. The benchmark and selection methodology provide a reusable basis for practical detector selection and for establishing stronger analytical baselines for future failure-detection approaches, including learning-based detectors.

papers.title: Programmable Broadband Polarization-Preserving Optical Delay Line with Faraday Mirrors
papers.abstract: We report a broadband optical delay line programmable for delays up to 1 μs with nanosecond resolution, while preserving an arbitrary and unknown polarization state of the original light. The delay line comprises bidirectional pass in cascaded segments of standard single-mode fibers, along with terminal reflection from Faraday mirrors (FMs) at both ends. Each segment contains either a short path or a long path, selected by an optical switch. The FMs auto-compensate for random polarization fluctuations introduced by the optical fibers, thereby restoring the initial polarization state. Broadband operation of the delay line was assessed by investigating dispersion of both the fiber and the FMs. Surprisingly, we found that the two-pass propagation in the fiber can mitigate dispersive distortion introduced by the FM. Numerical experiments demonstrated that the output polarization state of the delay line has a mean fidelity better than 99% over a range of 50-nm deviation from the central wavelength. Remarkably, the mean fidelity often surpasses that in the absence of the fiber itself.

papers.title: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Pretrained vision is a common start for robot learning, but most comparisons still score one pooled vector from a third-person image. Bimanual policies instead read dense patch tokens from cameras on the robot. We introduce HIVE-Bench: one shared flow-matching policy reads 20 encoders from seven families on 24 egocentric bimanual tasks, across adaptation, task sharing, and sweeps of data, model size, and layer. Keeping the patches matters. Averaging each view to one token removes most of the success, adaptation helps every pair we test, and one shared policy keeps most of the success of separate policies at a fraction of the updates. The same tokens are then scored with statistics, state and object readouts, published vision scores, and an inverse-dynamics readout. That readout of the commanded motion is one of the strongest measurements available before a policy is trained. Recognition, depth, and correspondence do not transfer reliably. Fine-tuning can improve the action readout even when other measurements move the other way, and no statistic is stable enough to replace a rollout before any deployment.

papers.title: Support-Constrained Local Randomizers for Robust Private Distribution Learning
papers.abstract: Local differential privacy protects users before data collection, but full-support randomizers can be wasteful on ordered, metric, or semantic alphabets. We study support-constrained local randomizers for robust private discrete learning. Restricting reports to input neighborhoods reduces reporting distortion but creates support mismatch. Under range-restricted approximate local differential privacy, a relational guarantee weaker than ordinary all-pairs local differential privacy, we decompose the exact hockey-stick defect into support leakage and overlap excess loss. For line-supported sparse randomized response, we derive the exact defect, solve the joint privacy-distortion problem in closed form at each radius, and prove a privacy-imposed support lower bound. For distribution estimation, we obtain an exact finite-sample risk identity and show that the least-favorable law over any closed convex uncertainty set is a Euclidean projection. On cyclic alphabets, the uniform law is uniquely least favorable, nominal and minimax mechanism rankings coincide, and the minimax risk obeys spectral upper and lower bounds. This diagnoses why prior shift cannot alter the selected mechanism in a homogeneous cyclic experiment. We therefore introduce a boundary-normalized nonhomogeneous path family in which robust calibration changes the mechanism and reduces worst-case risk. We also derive exact cyclic privacy, robust privacy-range calibration, and precise conditions for safe context- or history-dependent channel selection. Sparse Laplace, Gaussian, staircase, and score-based mechanisms remain extensions of the same design principle. All numerical results use exact privacy and risk calculations with matched-guarantee baselines.

papers.title: Noise-Immune Attractors in Stochastically Driven Non-Hermitian Systems
papers.abstract: Temporal stochastic fluctuations generically destroy quantum coherence and accelerate defect generation in driven quantum systems. Here, we demonstrate that non-Hermitian dynamics can fundamentally reverse this trend by stabilizing noise-resilient late-time states. By developing an exact noise master equation for non-Hermitian systems subject to Gaussian fluctuations, we uncover a projective noise-invariance mechanism governed by T-symmetry-broken Liouvillian attractors. This mechanism produces robust defect-density plateaus and yields an exact geometric classification into noise-independent, fully polarized, and continuously tunable regimes. We substantiate these results in an imbalanced-pairing non-Hermitian Kitaev model, a prototypical pseudo-Hermitian system, and propose their experimental observation in coupled photonic waveguides. Our findings identify non-Hermitian attractor dynamics as a versatile route to controlling noise-induced excitations beyond conventional anti-Kibble-Zurek scaling.

papers.title: Reflected Elastic Diffusions
papers.abstract: We study the reflected elastic diffusion (RED), the pathwise counterpart of Feller's elastic boundary condition for a one-dimensional diffusion on $[0,\infty)$ with time-homogeneous, continuous drift and diffusion coefficients. Given a diffusion $X$ reflecting at zero, we construct a Feller process $\widetilde X$ by killing $X$ at the first time its local time at zero exceeds an independent exponential random variable. We characterize the infinitesimal generator of $\widetilde X$ explicitly and prove that its domain satisfies a Robin boundary condition, thereby identifying $\widetilde X$ as a probabilistic representation of Feller's analytical characterization of the elastic boundary. A key analytical ingredient, of independent interest, is a pair of moment asymptotics, as $t\downarrow 0$, for the boundary local time of a reflected diffusion, extending known results for the unreflected case. Uniqueness in law of $\widetilde X$ among Feller REDs sharing the same interior dynamics is established through a resolvent/boundary-value-problem argument. The result extends the classical Itô-McKean construction of elastic Brownian motion to time-homogeneous diffusions, closing the gap between analytic and probabilistic treatments of elastic killing used in recent applied models.

papers.title: Gallium at germanium surfaces: links to superconducting films and correlated adatom lattices
papers.abstract: Epitaxial films grown on Ge(001) show that germanium hyperdoped with substitutional Ga is superconducting. In earlier implanted films, Ga-rich precipitates obscured the origin of the superconductivity. This review examines the sites Ga occupies on Ge(001) and Ge(111) and how it enters the growing film. The Ga fraction expected from the growth fluxes is 17.9\%, yet the distribution of Ga among lattice sites is unknown. Comparisons include Ga on Si(001) and Si(111),In, Sn, Pb, Sb and P on Ge(001), and elemental and two-dimensional Ga. Where its surface coordination has been established, Ga has three bonds, whereas substitutional Ga in the films is fourfold coordinated and acts as an acceptor. Scanning tunnelling microscopy and X-ray standing waves have assigned Ga sites on Ge(111), but the dilute Ga site on Ge(001), where the films are grown, has yet to be measured. On Ge(111), Ga in the substrate may supply holes to the correlated Sn adatom lattice, as B supplies holes to the superconducting Sn lattice on Si(111). Whether Ga can supply holes depends on where it sits and whether it has three or four neighbours. On both surfaces, element-specific measurements and calculations comparing adsorption with substitution could settle the remaining site assignments.

papers.title: A particle method for the space homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation
papers.abstract: We propose a structure preserving particle method to numerically approximate the spatially homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation for collisional plasmas. The Lenard-Balescu operator is an improvement of the Landau equation with a dielectric function taking the dynamic screening effect into account. Our particle method is based on the variational formulation of the Lenard-Balescu equation under suitable regularization analogous to the strategy followed for the Landau collision operator in [12]. The method guarantees the conservation laws and the entropy dissipation at the semi-discrete level. The novel difficulty of the nonlocal nonlinear dependence of the dielectric function is tackled by rewriting it as integrals in terms of orthogonal and parallel components to the frequency variable. This equivalent form reduces the evaluation of the dielectric function to numerically computing an integral of the directional derivative of the solution on a hyperplane orthogonal to the frequency variable and its one-dimensional Hilbert transform. An efficient implementation of the numerical approximation for the Lenard-Balescu kernel is derived by exploiting this expression of the dielectric function. We finally validate our method by means of several numerical tests, further allowing us to explore qualitative properties of the Lenard-Balescu equation.

papers.title: Zariski-constructible functions of class $\mathcal{C}^k$
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a real closed field. A Zariski-constructible subset of $R^n$, $\mathcal{ZC}$-set for short, is a Boolean combination of algebraic subsets of $R^n$. Euclidean closed Zariski-constructible subsets of $R^n$ are the closed subsets of a Noetherian topology finer than the Zariski topology of $R^n$. Let $k\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$. Let $U\subset R^n$ be a $\mathcal{ZC}$-open set. We say that a function $f:U\to R$ of class $\mathcal{C}^k$ is a Zariski-constructible function, $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-function for short, if its graph is a $\mathcal{ZC}$-set. For instance, regular and $k$-regulous functions on $R^n$ are $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-functions. We show that the ring $\mathcal{ZC}^k(U)$ of $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-functions on a $\mathcal{ZC}$-open set is way richer, even for $k=\infty$, although $\infty$-regulous functions are just regular. Then, we extend the notion of $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-function over any $\mathcal{ZC}$-locally closed subset $X$ of $R^n$. This paper is mainly devoted to the study of the geometric and algebraic properties of the ring $\mathcal{ZC}^k(X)$ of $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-functions on a $\mathcal{ZC}$-locally closed subset $X$ of $R^n$. From now on, assume that $k\in\mathbb N$. We show that $\mathcal{ZC}$-closed subsets $X$ of $R^n$ are exactly the zero loci of $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-functions on $R^n$. We show that the Nullstellensatz holds in the ring $\mathcal{ZC}^k(U)$, where $U$ is a $\mathcal{ZC}$-open subset of $R^n$, and that this ring is radically principal. As a consequence of the Nullstellensatz, we prove that any $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-function on a $\mathcal{ZC}$-locally closed subset $X$ of $R^n$ extends to a $\mathcal{ZC}$-open neighborhood $U$ of $X$. Then, we translate our results into the language of sheaves of $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-functions on $\mathcal{ZC}$-locally closed sets, from which we deduce a $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-version of Cartan's theorems A and B.

papers.title: A Fitch-Based Wind Farm Parameterization for CM1: Implementation, Validation, and Impacts on Convection Initiation
papers.abstract: We implement a Fitch-based wind farm parameterization in Cloud Model 1 (CM1), representing turbines as elevated momentum sinks and turbulent kinetic energy (TKE) sources within the rotor-swept layer, with optimizations for computational efficiency and parallel execution. Direct comparison with the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model shows close agreement in the magnitude and spatial structure of wind-speed deficits and TKE enhancement. Diurnal simulations also capture the known dependence of boundary layer responses on atmospheric stability, further supporting the consistency of the implementation. Under stable conditions, the wind farm produces coherent spatial patterns in near-surface wind speed and temperature that extend well beyond the farm. In idealized simulations under conditions favorable for convection, large turbines promote convection initiation tens of kilometers downstream, earlier than in the no-farm simulation. Analysis identifies turbulent entrainment of warmer air across the boundary layer top as the dominant source of an elongated downstream warm band, with a smaller contribution from enhanced surface sensible heat flux. Secondary circulations develop across this warm band and provide sustained low-level lifting. A gravity wave generated by the wind farm supplies the initial vertical perturbation, which intensifies as it is advected downstream within an ascending branch of these circulations and develops into a localized deep convective updraft.

papers.title: Nearly-Tight Oracle Complexity of Packing and Covering Linear Programs
papers.abstract: We settle the deterministic oracle complexity of packing and covering linear programs, as measured by the number of oracle queries to the constraint matrix modeled by left and right matrix-vector products, up to a logarithmic factor. We do so by providing nearly-matching upper and lower bounds. Our algorithm breaks the $1/ε^2$ barrier of width-independent, $(1+ε)$-multiplicative error parallel solvers from prior work, improving the scaling with the error $ε>0$ to $1/ε,$ with total number of arithmetic operations scaling near-linearly with $1/ε$ and the number of nonzero entries of the constraint matrix.

papers.title: Random Feature Neural Networks for Stochastic Optimal Control
papers.abstract: Random feature neural networks (RFNNs) sample their hidden parameters once and train only the output layer. We analyze RFNNs as feedback policies for finite-horizon stochastic control with trajectory-dependent objectives. A policy change alters later states, so the error that matters is the objective error of the induced trajectory rather than a pointwise regression error. We extend the quantitative random-feature approximation theory for PDE solutions and nonlinear regression to feedback control. We investigate the objective error of an RFNN policy through two sources, approximation of the policy by random features and estimation of the objective from finitely many paths. A stability estimate for the controlled trajectory turns a policy error into an objective error. Under bounded actions, a regular benchmark policy and exact empirical minimization, the expected objective gap to the benchmark policy is at most of order $N^{-1/2}+\sqrt{N(1+\log N)/n}$, with $N$ the feature width per output coordinate and $n$ the number of paths. At fixed sample size the two terms trade off in $N$, and balancing them gives $N\asymp\sqrt{n/\log n}$. Across a wide range of examples, estimated gaps generally decrease with width and sample size, and RFNNs show an advantage when simulated paths are limited. We also study Parsimonious Random Feature Learning (PRFL), which grows and prunes the random dictionary during training while training only the output coefficients. At matched retained width and training budget, PRFL improves on a fixed RFNN in the LQ and Heston comparisons, while the fully trained network remains best in those examples.

papers.title: Isolated singularities of weak solutions to the quasilinear Lane-Emden equation
papers.abstract: We study isolated singularities of nonnegative weak solutions to $-Δ_pu=u^q$ in $B_1\setminus\{0\}$, where $Δ_p$ is the $p$-Laplacian, $1<p<n$, and $n(p-1)/(n-p)<q<np/(n-p)-1$. We prove that either the origin is a removable singularity or $u(x)\sim K_{n,p,q}|x|^{-p/(q+1-p)}$ as $x\to0$, where $K_{n,p,q}>0$ is an explicit constant depending only on $n,p,q$. The result holds without radial symmetry or an a priori growth assumption. The proof combines a removability criterion with a rigidity theorem for positive solutions in $\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$ satisfying two-sided power bounds. To handle the infinite $p$-Dirichlet energy at the singularity, we construct a continuous Steiner deformation that fixes all sufficiently high superlevel sets. The resulting energy comparison yields radial symmetry of the blow-up limits.

papers.title: Go Far, Look Less: Active Multi-Room Reconstruction with Persistent Goals and Selective Views
