papers.abstract: Active 3D reconstruction aims to allocate a sparse view budget to recover complete geometry and high-fidelity renderings. However, existing methods degrade sharply in multi-room homes: myopic next-best-view scoring gives transit no credit for distant rooms and over-polishes irreducible nearby residuals, whereas dense mappers reach far rooms only by streaming thousands of frames. We propose ROAM-GS, a training-free active multi-room reconstruction framework that couples persistent goals with selective views: each decision selects a goal and a variable-horizon prefix toward it, capturing only at its endpoint. A Surface Reconstruction Memory scores poses by projecting post-update defects and viewing directions. Persistent goals credit transit with their remaining value and are released once arrivals stop measurably improving them. Without per-scene tuning, ROAM-GS achieves state-of-the-art multi-room reconstruction while preserving single-room Replica fidelity, raising mean coverage from 74% to 93% on HSSD and from 47% to 96% (+11.7 dB PSNR) on HM3D, and matching 90-minute dense mapping using $173\times$ fewer views.

papers.title: Free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem
papers.abstract: We compute the limiting free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem for every pseudodimension $d>0$ and every inverse temperature $λ> 0$ at the scale $n^{1/d}$. We show that the limit is given by a rigorous replica-symmetric formula determined by the unique solution of a recursive distributional equation on a Poisson-weighted infinite tree, confirming conjectures of Aldous and Talagrand. As a consequence, for a fixed inverse temperature $λ> 0$, we deduce exponential concentration of the cost of a Gibbs assignment and determine the exponential growth rate of the number of near-optimal assignments.

papers.title: Constraining Gamma-Ray Emission Beyond the TOV Limit: A Targeted Fermi-GBM Search for Counterparts to 39 LVK Gravitational-Wave Candidates in GWTC-5.0
papers.abstract: We present a systematic search for sub-threshold gamma-ray counterparts within a one-day time window of 161 gravitational-wave (GW) events from the GWTC-5.0 catalog, whose inferred source masses exceed the adopted Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff (TOV) limit, using the Gamma-ray Targeted Search (GTS) pipeline. The search identifies 39 candidate GW--gamma-ray pairs satisfying the adopted joint likelihood-ratio thresholds. None of these candidates exhibits a temporal offset compatible with the prompt-emission delay observed for GW170817 ($\sim 1.7$ s); the smallest temporal separation is 17 min 17.976 s, ruling out GW170817-like prompt temporal associations in our candidate sample. Several candidates nevertheless show substantial spatial consistency. In particular, the most spatially consistent pair has a joint localization overlap of 95.4%, despite a temporal separation of 13 h 19 min 8.85 s, illustrating that high spatial agreement can occur by chance in the absence of temporal consistency. Among the sub-threshold gamma-ray candidates, we further identify an anomalous event with an exceptionally large single-instrument significance of log LR = 5250.84. For comparison, the adopted $3σ$ threshold corresponds to log LR $\approx 9$. The extreme likelihood ratio of this candidate motivates further investigation of trigger sensitivity, onboard veto configurations, and the statistical interpretation of sub-threshold events. Overall, we find no physically viable multi-messenger associations between the GWTC-5.0 events and the searched gamma-ray candidates, and derive corresponding upper limits on prompt high-energy emission from GWTC-5.0 progenitors.

papers.title: Fermionic dark linear seesaw with an anomalous Majoron
papers.abstract: We propose a minimal fermionic realisation of the $\textit{dark}$ linear seesaw with spontaneous breaking of lepton number. The small lepton-number-violating parameter responsible for linear-seesaw neutrino masses is generated radiatively by a $\textit{dark}$ sector consisting of a singlet and a doublet fermion, together with scalar singlets. The global U(1)$_L$ symmetry is broken to a residual $\mathcal{Z}_2$ under which the $\textit{dark}$ sector is odd. This breaking yields a Majoron $J$ and makes the lightest $\textit{dark}$ particle stable. The charged $\textit{dark}$ fermion acquires its mass solely from U(1)$_L$ breaking and thus induces an anomalous Majoron coupling to photons. Current bounds on this coupling exclude a massless Majoron for TeV-scale U(1)$_L$ breaking. We add a linear term that breaks lepton number softly and gives the Majoron a GeV-scale mass. Such a Majoron decays into two photons and can be probed at beam-dump experiments. We study the dark matter phenomenology, focusing on the case where the stable particle is a fermionic weakly interacting massive particle. We analyse how the framework can be tested through charged-lepton flavour-violating decays such as $μ\to eγ$, which receive contributions from both the $\textit{dark}$ and the seesaw sectors. Moreover, both sectors enhance the Majoron couplings to charged leptons, so that the Majoron-emitting decays $τ\to \ell J$ ($\ell = e,μ$) typically exceed $τ\to \ellγ$ by orders of magnitude and can probe parameter space beyond the reach of $μ\to eγ$.

papers.title: Precise Asymptotics of Non-Convex M-Estimators
papers.abstract: Precise asymptotic theory for M-estimators in high-dimensional settings is largely limited to convex or mildly non-convex formulations, yet non-convex loss functions as well as regularizers are widely used in practice. We study M-estimation in generalized linear models (GLMs) where the loss function or the regularizer can be non-convex. Under rotationally invariant design matrices in the proportional asymptotic regime, we analyze the problem through Vector Approximate Message Passing (VAMP), whose iterates are described by a low-dimensional deterministic recursion called State Evolution (SE). Existing proofs of SE require the proximal operators of the loss function and the regularizer to be Lipschitz, but a non-convex loss or regularizer can have a discontinuous proximal operator, and the usual Onsager terms in VAMP then miss the contribution of the discontinuities. Assuming that the proximal operators are special functions of locally bounded variation, we derive a correction to the Onsager terms using a distributional Stein's lemma. We prove that SE holds for the corrected VAMP. We apply the theory to analyze group sparse regression with an $\ell_0$-type penalty and to robust regression with the Cauchy loss.

papers.title: Spherical CR uniformization for 7 links
papers.abstract: We consider subgroups in $PU(2,1)$ generated by three involutions $I_1,I_2,I_3$ such that $I_2I_3$ has order $p$ and the elements $I_1I_2$, $I_2I_3$, $I_1I_3I_2I_3$ are all in the same conjugacy class of $PU(2,1)$. We show that these groups are discrete whenever $I_1I_2$ and $I_1I_2I_3$ are non-elliptic and we study the orbifolds at infinity. In addition, we show that for $3 \leq p \leq 9$ the complement of a symmetric cyclic chain of $p$ simple links admits a spherical CR uniformization.

papers.title: PestWeave: Linking Semantic Modeling and Evidence-Guided Text Modulation through Visual Prototypes for Fine-Grained Pest Learning
papers.abstract: Agricultural pests threaten crop yield and quality, making accurate pest recognition essential for targeted management and sustainable agriculture. Their diverse appearances complicate recognition and motivate multimodal approaches incorporating complementary species knowledge from text. However, complex backgrounds can obscure discriminative visual cues, while textual descriptions may contain information unsupported by the current image, limiting effective cross-modal fusion. To address these challenges, we propose PestWeave, a multimodal framework connecting content-adaptive visual organization with text fusion through visual prototypes. Its visual pathway augments a Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV) architecture with semantic token grouping and three types of auxiliary tokens, enabling content-adaptive scanning and contextual modeling while preserving spatial structure. Feature-similar tokens are reordered into adjacent scanning positions, while cluster prototype, global, and register tokens provide group-level summaries, global context, and additional interaction capacity, respectively. These prototypes also guide text modulation by assessing visual support for semantic components and regulating their relative contributions and overall fusion strength, reducing interference from unsupported descriptions. Extensive experiments on multiple pest recognition datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of PestWeave and its potential for practical pest management.

papers.title: Multipartite entanglement structure of crystal quenches
papers.abstract: Understanding how entanglement emerges and spreads in out-of-equilibrium quantum many-body systems is a fundamental problem. In this paper, we investigate multipartite entanglement after quantum quenches. In particular, we study the entanglement structure and dynamics of quasiparticle multiplets generated by crystal quenches in the tight-binding chain. We identify zero-configurations for which a multiplet shared between three parties has no irreducible tripartite entanglement---these configurations consist entirely of pairwise distributed bipartite-entangled states. The existence of zero-configurations has important implications on the entanglement structure and dynamics of crystal quenches. For example, we show that it can further delay the production of tripartite entanglement. We build the quasiparticle picture for the Markov gap, and prove that it is a faithful witness of irreducible tripartite entanglement for crystal quenches. We discuss several key aspects of their tripartite entanglement dynamics through the lens of the Markov gap. We confront our results with exact lattice numerics and find perfect agreement in the hydrodynamic regime.

papers.title: Pulse-to-pulse Power Fluctuations in Ultra-Fast Fiber Amplifiers with Gain-Managed Nonlinearity
papers.abstract: We present a theoretical framework for predicting pulse-to-pulse power fluctuations caused by pump and seed power noise and by amplified spontaneous emission in ultrafast fiber amplifiers operating in the gain-managed nonlinear regime. The numerical model evaluates statistically averaged quantities directly, without Monte Carlo simulations with stochastic sources, and reduces to a semi-analytical monochromatic model in the limit of vanishing signal bandwidth and negligible ASE. We show that nonlinear spectral broadening of the signal and of its perturbations, combined with the frequency-dependent gain, significantly alters the technical relative intensity noise in both the high-power, high-repetition-rate and the low-power, low-repetition-rate regimes, and that in the latter regime the contributions related to amplified spontaneous emission become comparable to those induced by pump and seed fluctuations.

papers.title: How Systems Treat Intent: A Faceted Taxonomy of Intent for Human-AI Co-Creation
papers.abstract: Human-AI interaction depends on systems acting on user intent rather than explicit procedures, even when that intent is incomplete, evolving, or partially communicable. Literature organizing systems by interaction technique, workflow stage, or division of labor, offer limited insight into which facet of intent an interaction mechanism addresses. We introduce a six-facet taxonomy of intent, grounded in philosophical accounts of mind, action, and meaning, and apply it to systems presented in 198 papers from eleven SIGCHI venues. Our analysis reveals that different forms of incomplete intent are associated with distinct interaction and authorship strategies, showing that mechanisms that appear similar often address fundamentally different intent-related problems. This exposes blind spots, as intent is rarely represented as an interaction object, authorship provenance is rarely tracked, and tentative preferences are rarely distinguished from firm commitments. The taxonomy offers a lens for analyzing and designing AI systems around the facets of intent they address.

papers.title: A martingale proof of simultaneous convex and smooth renorming
papers.abstract: We give an affirmative answer to Problem 198 of Guirao, Montesinos, and Zizler [\emph{Open Problems in the Geometry and Analysis of Banach Spaces}, Springer, Cham (2016), p.~90], also formulated by Pisier [\emph{Martingales in Banach Spaces}, Cambridge University Press (2016), p.~461]. Given equivalent norms with convexity of power type $p$ and smoothness of power type $q$, respectively, we construct a single equivalent norm with both properties using finite dyadic martingales. It can be chosen arbitrarily close to the given smooth norm in multiplicative distortion and preserves all linear symmetries shared by the two initial norms. The case $p=q=2$ with group invariance answers Problem 3.6 of Cabello Sánchez, Ferenczi, and Randrianantoanina [São Paulo J. Math. Sci. \textbf{16} (2022), 406--458].

papers.title: Joint statistics on vexillary involutions via Fulton's essential set
papers.abstract: We jointly enumerate various statistics over vexillary involutions among which there are the number of descents and the number of peaks. As a by-product, we get an equidistribution result between vexillary involutions and 3412-avoiding involutions, which, notably, implies that, for every $n$ and $k$, the number of involutions of length $n$ avoiding $3412$ and having $k$ descents equals the number of involutions of length $n$ avoiding $2143$ and having $k$ ascents. The proof describes $2143$-avoiding involutions through Fulton's ranked essential set, translates the count into a weighted enumeration of walks in the quarter plane, and solves the latter explicitly. Finally, we show that arbitrary vexillary permutations are encoded by excursions of the same walk model.

papers.title: Monsky's nodal cubic and the arithmetic of Frobenius invariants
papers.abstract: We prove Monsky's conjecture on the colengths of the ideals $(x^q,y^q,z^q,h^j)$ in $\mathbb{F}_2[x,y,z]$, where $h=x^3+y^3+xyz$, $q=2^e$, and $0\le j\le q$. We derive Monsky's recursion by interchanging the values of sections of syzygy bundles on the two branches at the node of the cubic $h=0$. For the hypersurface $uv+h=0$, the Hilbert-Kunz and Frobenius splitting series are algebraic of degree two over $\mathbb{Q}(w)$. For $uv+h(X_1)+\cdots+h(X_m)=0$, where the $X_i$ are disjoint triples of variables and $m\ge 2$, both series are transcendental over $\mathbb{Q}(w)$. When $m=2$, we express the Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity in terms of a period of an elliptic curve in characteristic zero. This gives an explicit seven-dimensional hypersurface over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with transcendental Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity and transcendental $F$-signature.

papers.title: Quantum resources constrain function approximation
papers.abstract: Universal function approximation is central to machine learning. Quantum learning models are universal as well, but this does not specify the resources needed to approximate a given function. We study how coherence, imaginarity, entanglement and magic constrain function approximation for a fixed encoding and readout, using the cumulative resource power of the trainable gates. In a one-qubit model with phase encoding, coherence bounds the oscillation of the model function, while imaginarity bounds its odd part. In a two-qubit model, entanglement bounds the distance from product functions. These bounds hold at any encoding depth. For magic, the phase encoding itself supplies non-Clifford operations. On domains bounded away from zero, Clifford trainable gates suffice for uniform approximation. Replacing unrestricted trainable gates by Clifford gates increases the encoding depth at most polynomially in the original depth, the inverse error and the inverse distance of the domain from zero. Magic in the trainable gates can nevertheless improve accuracy at fixed depth. These results show how the resources of a quantum model must match the structure of the target function.

papers.title: From joint attention to shared symbols: A free-energy principle account
papers.abstract: Joint attention precedes vocabulary acquisition. How can attending to the same object help two people with different sensory experiences come to use a shared word? In a free-energy principle account, marginalizing the common object induces a statistical dependence between private perceptual states. In a categorical world, the joint prior inherits a mixture structure whose component index provides a candidate for shared reference. The collective predictive coding model approximates this prior by representing the dependence through that shared index. An established Metropolis-Hastings naming game lets agents infer and exchange words using private evidence. Toy and multiview image experiments illustrate how word exchange can coordinate private categories and improve the fit of collective models. The account connects joint attention to shared symbols through the coupling of private inference.

papers.title: BridgeMVS: Bridging Multi-View Stereo and Monodepth via Bidirectional Dynamic Fusion
papers.abstract: Multi-View Stereo (MVS) and Monocular Depth Estimation (MDE) provide complementary cues for dense 3D reconstruction. While MVS leverages explicit geometry for metric depth, it struggles in challenging regions where feature matching is unreliable. Conversely, MDE provides robust structural priors but typically yields scale-ambiguous results. Existing hybrid methods mainly exploit monocular cues in a unidirectional manner, leaving the mutual enhancement between MDE and MVS insufficiently explored. To address this limitation, we propose BridgeMVS, a unified cascaded multi-stage MVS framework that bridges monocular depth features and multi-view cost volume representations through Bidirectional Dynamic Fusion (BDF). At each stage, BDF performs dynamic mono-to-cost and cost-to-mono updates, where monocular structural features guide cost volume refinement for more robust MVS depth estimation, while multi-view geometric evidence recalibrates monocular representations to improve their metric-scale consistency. Furthermore, the fused monocular and multi-view representations are progressively propagated from coarse to fine stages and constrained by stage-wise relative-scale MDE supervision and metric-scale MVS supervision, enabling cross-branch interactions to benefit subsequent high-resolution depth estimation. In addition, BDF is designed as a plug-and-play module that can be conveniently integrated into existing cascaded MVS frameworks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that BridgeMVS achieves state-of-the-art performance on the DTU, Tanks-and-Temples, and ETH3D benchmarks, while simultaneously boosting the accuracy of monocular depth estimation. Notably, BridgeMVS ranks first on both the Tanks-and-Temples Intermediate and Advanced benchmarks. The source code is available at \href{https://github.com/JianfeiJ/BridgeMVS}{https://github.com/JianfeiJ/BridgeMVS}.

papers.title: Closed-loop Properties of Value Iteration in Continuous Time with Approximation Errors
papers.abstract: Value iteration is an important tool for approximating solutions of infinite-horizon optimal control problems, but in practice it is never carried out exactly: value functions are represented by finite-dimensional approximators, and the iteration is stopped after finitely many steps. This paper analyzes which closed-loop guarantees remain under these limitations for continuous-time nonlinear systems. We consider a value iteration scheme in which each iteration solves a finite-horizon optimal control problem with the previous iterate as terminal cost, and the associated controller applies the optimal input of this problem over each horizon in a sampled-data fashion. We show that if the convergence tolerance and the approximation error are small enough, the controller asymptotically stabilizes the system on sublevel sets of the computed iterate, and provide a suboptimality bound. This condition consists of pointwise inequalities that can be checked for the computed iterate, without establishing convergence of the iteration, and is a first step towards sample-based certification. We further establish inherent robustness of the controller with respect to model errors and recover classical results for the linear-quadratic regulator. Numerical studies on a linear-quadratic problem and on a nonlinear system with known optimal value function are consistent with the guarantees and show that the suboptimality bound is conservative.

papers.title: PVFormer: Proper Velocity Transformer for Stable and Scalable Hyperbolic Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Hyperbolic representations have shown remarkable success on hierarchical and tree-like data, and Transformers have become a central architecture for representation learning. However, a principled construction of hyperbolic Transformers remains challenging because the self-attention layer decomposes into three coupled primitives, transformation, similarity, and aggregation, that should all respect the underlying geometry. Existing hyperbolic Transformer designs are typically built in the Poincaré or Lorentz models, where bounded domains, time-like constraints, tangent-space detours, or projection steps make it difficult to keep the full block intrinsic and scalable. To address this gap, we propose PVFormer, to the best of our knowledge, the first Transformer architecture that operates natively in proper velocity (PV) space. The proper velocity model provides an unconstrained representation of hyperbolic geometry, and PVFormer exploits this structure to redesign the Transformer block in PV space. On the transformation side, we use PV homomorphism transformations to update query and value representations. On the similarity side, we generalize Euclidean inner-product attention with a PV Busemann score inspired by Busemann-based hyperbolic learning and a PV point-to-hyperplane key transformation. On the aggregation side, we replace Euclidean averaging with PV midpoint aggregation and further derive a scalable PV linear attention variant for large graphs. Extensive experiments support the effectiveness of PVFormer across graph, text, and vision benchmarks.

papers.title: Beyond Domain Randomization: Real-World Policy Adaptation in Learned Dynamics for Legged Robots
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning policies are often trained with static domain randomization for real-world deployment. However, real-world environments often exhibit unmodeled dynamic variations, such as payload changes or friction shifts, that lie outside the randomization distribution, leading to performance degradation upon deployment. We propose a framework that moves beyond static domain randomization by adapting a learned dynamics model to the deployed target conditions, with a concurrent teacher-student paradigm applied to both the policy and dynamics model. This framework integrates the dynamics model into an on-policy reinforcement learning pipeline, letting the performance of the policy align with the empirical target dynamics. Experimental validations on bipedal locomotion tasks demonstrate competitive adaptability under extreme physical variations, including a payload reaching 80% of self-weight and an oil-lubricated low-friction surface.

papers.title: A mean index criterion for multiple closed characteristics
papers.abstract: Let $n\ge2$. We prove that a compact strictly star-shaped $C^3$ hypersurface in $\mathbb R^{2n}$ carries at least $n$ geometrically distinct prime closed characteristics if all iterates are nondegenerate and all mean indices are at least one. It suffices that all mean indices are positive and that the bound holds only for prime characteristics with negative mean Euler characteristic in the variational grading. The proof uses a minimum argument for the global Morse remainder and requires no individual index exclusion. For odd $n\ge3$, we obtain a smaller, dimension-dependent strict bound when good iterates of Maslov-type index $-1$ are excluded. Irrational ellipsoids show that the multiplicity bound is sharp.

papers.title: Irreducibility of Primitive Special Cycles in Locally Symmetric Spaces of Orthogonal Type
papers.abstract: Let $L$ be an even lattice of signature $(n_1,n_2)$ with $n_1\geq k+1,n_2\geq 2$ and let $X$ denote the quotient of the symmetric space associated to $O(L\otimes_\mathbb{Z}\mathbb{R})$ by the discriminant kernel of positive spinor norm. We show that primitive special cycles in $X$ of real codimension at most $kn_2$ are irreducible if $L$ splits off $k+1$ hyperbolic planes locally at every prime.

papers.title: Perfect Spin-to-Charge Signal Conversion via Inverse Spin Hall Effect in a Superconductor
papers.abstract: Spin-to-charge conversion is central to spintronics, but conventional spin Hall mechanisms are intrinsically limited by the small spin Hall angle. Here we show that superconductivity can overcome this limitation and enable near-unity spin-to-charge signal conversion. We consider a nonlocal spin-valve geometry in which a spin accumulation is injected into a superconductor and converted into a transverse charge signal through the inverse spin Hall effect. In the superconducting state, the strongly suppressed quasiparticle conductance below the gap allows the resulting charge imbalance to generate a voltage comparable to the injected spin bias, despite a small spin Hall angle. We derive the full nonequilibrium response including finite spectral broadening and finite temperature, and propose temperature and spin-bias-dependent measurements of the detector voltage to test our predictions.

papers.title: Light on GeV-scale seesaw
papers.abstract: The next generation of beam-dump and accelerator-neutrino experiments will probe GeV-scale sterile neutrinos with unprecedented sensitivity. However, the tiny active-sterile mixing predicted by the minimal seesaw mechanism is expected to remain out of reach. Oscillation data require at least two sterile neutrinos, $N_1$ and $N_2$, which may couple to the photon through a transition dipole. Such a coupling can radically change the picture, both by strongly enhancing sterile-neutrino production and by opening new decay channels. We identify charged-lepton pairs produced by an off-shell photon as the most promising experimental signature. We show that the seesaw band can be probed by the T2K near detector for sterile-neutrino masses $m_N\lesssim 500$ MeV, and by SHiP for $m_N\lesssim 5$ GeV. For a sufficiently large dipole, $d\gtrsim (10~\mathrm{TeV})^{-1}$, SHiP can selectively measure decay channels that require nonzero active-sterile mixing. This would give rise to a distinctive hierarchy of signatures, providing a direct test of the seesaw mechanism.

papers.title: SignalCount: Approximate Counts with Structured and Semantic Predicates in Seconds
papers.abstract: Many applications store records with structured columns and a text document, and ask how many records in a filtered set meet a criterion that only a reader of the text can judge, such as "How many patients with type 2 diabetes, aged 40 to 70, stopped metformin because their blood sugar stayed high?" An interactive application needs this count in seconds, as the user types the criterion, to decide whether the matching set is worth materializing with a batch pipeline in which an LLM judges the records. Prior approximate query processing over such semantic predicates has an expensive model, the oracle, label a sample at query time, so every query waits for the oracle. We present SignalCount, a production system that answers COUNT queries with structured and semantic predicates and calls no oracle at query time, even for ad-hoc criteria. Its oracle is the production LLM judge, and the judge's logged verdicts calibrate, offline, the fast classifier that already runs in front of the judge. At query time, SignalCount counts the filtered set exactly and draws a uniform sample of at most 1,000 records in one columnar scan, scores the sample with the classifier, and multiplies the average calibrated probability by the exact count. Its 90% interval combines a sampling term with one-sided, rate-dependent margins for calibration error, fitted by split conformal prediction across tenants. In a multi-tenant production deployment, latency has a p99 of 3.8 s and stays flat as the filtered set grows beyond the sample. On tenants held out from fitting, the interval covers the count that the production pipeline returns in 92% of estimates, although estimates run about 15% high in aggregate, because a calibration nearly unbiased per record is still biased per criterion.

papers.title: What Quality Engineers Need to Know About Generative AI: Structured Data Extraction
papers.abstract: In this expository paper, we explain how quality engineers can use large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) for structured data extraction. We introduce the relevant concepts, discuss structured extraction from a measurement-system perspective, and demonstrate its implementation in R and Python. We then present two freely available web-based applications (apps): (a) extracting information from automotive recall notices and (b) monitoring quality engineering research on arXiv. To ensure the accuracy of our AI-driven structured extraction, human evaluators validated the results. In the first app, four reviewers assessed information extracted from 30 recall notices using two models, with 98.6% of the 720 field-level ratings judged fully correct. In the second app, 21 authors evaluated information extracted from 45 of their arXiv papers. All paper summaries were rated mostly correct or correct, although the evaluations identified problems with some classification fields and mathematical expressions. These results demonstrate the practical potential of structured data extraction while emphasizing the need to validate the extracted information. We make both apps and their source code publicly available so that readers can adapt the approach to their own applications.

papers.title: AvatarAnyone: Agentic Reconstruction of Mesh-Based Layered Avatars from YouTube Video
papers.abstract: We introduce AvatarAnyone, a method for reconstructing avatars from casual YouTube videos as layered meshes, with each garment and footwear as a separate mesh layered on top of the body mesh. In such videos, people differ in garment classes, clothing types, and layers, and each combination needs a different reconstruction. A single fixed layered reconstruction pipeline therefore fails. AvatarAnyone solves this problem with AI agents that plan a custom optimization for each person's reconstruction. The agents predict the garment classes, the clothing type, and the layering. They use these predictions to choose an initialization and stage the optimization. Because the avatars are layered meshes, they support applications such as virtual try-on and cloth simulation. We change the clothing layers of an avatar and render it in different garments and poses. We can also simulate a clothing layer as cloth over the animated body with a standard cloth simulator. Most existing avatars are one fused surface or a set of Gaussians and cannot do this. We load the avatars directly into Blender, Unreal Engine, and robotics simulators such as MuJoCo. As the avatars are meshes, they support contact modeling with other objects. We show results from around 150 YouTube videos. On four datasets, AvatarAnyone outperforms existing mesh-based methods for animatable monocular reconstruction. Our project page is available at https://miraymen.github.io/avataranyone.

papers.title: Torcalia.jl: An MPI-based Runtime System for Asynchronous Task Parallelism in Julia
papers.abstract: Designed to address the two-language problem, the Julia programming language provides a powerful platform for developing high-performance scientific computing and machine learning applications. Such applications increasingly exhibit irregular, adaptive, or data-driven workloads for which traditional bulk-synchronous parallel (BSP) models often struggle to efficiently exploit the available parallelism. Asynchronous many-task (AMT) runtime systems offer a compelling alternative, decomposing computations into fine-grained tasks that are dynamically scheduled across the hierarchical architecture of modern HPC systems. This paper introduces Torcalia.jl, a Julia package designed to orchestrate the asynchronous execution of tasks across both shared and distributed memory environments. Built on top of MPI.jl and Julia's native multithreading, Torcalia employs a dependency-aware task scheduling scheme that combines the work-sharing and work-stealing paradigms to achieve adaptive load balancing. Tasks can be nested arbitrarily, enabling applications to exploit multiple levels of parallelism, while application-level distributed shared memory (DSM) extends task-based shared-memory programming to multi-node clusters. Beyond task-based programming, the proposed library supports skeletal programming, providing high-level abstractions that facilitate the implementation of parallel applications at scale. Evaluated on the ARIS supercomputer using four diverse workloads, Torcalia demonstrates strong scalability, reducing wall-clock time by up to 18.1% compared with Dagger, a state-of-the-art task-based engine in Julia. The source code of Torcalia.jl is publicly available at https://github.com/CEID-HPCLAB/Torcalia.jl.

papers.title: Reconstructing 3D+t Cardiovascular Flow From Sparse Planar Velocity Fields With Neural Fields
papers.abstract: Reconstructing time-resolved three-dimensional (3D+t) cardiovascular flow from sparse planar measurements is challenging because each plane observes only the two in-plane velocity components, on a small part of the volume. We propose a plane-aware neural-field framework that learns a continuous 3D velocity field from space and time coordinates through a per-plane projection, and then investigate the potential benefits of physics constraints. We evaluate the framework on computational aortic and aneurysm datasets, and on planes resampled from a real cardiac 4D Flow MRI scan. A plain multi-layer perceptron (MLP) was more accurate than classical radial basis function (RBF) interpolation on both computational datasets. For the aorta, a physics-constrained SIREN (PC-SIREN) reduced the rRMSE further to $0.3756$, compared with $0.4273$ for the plain MLP and $0.7256$ for RBF, and it was the most accurate model in every anatomical segment of the MRI data. For the aneurysms the plain MLP remained the most accurate model, with an rRMSE of $0.07$ to $0.16$ against $0.55$ to $0.71$ for PC-SIREN. Further experiments investigated scanning configuration, number of scans, and spatial resolution. These findings show that continuous neural fields can reconstruct volumetric cardiovascular flow from sparse planar measurements, and that physics constraints have to be matched to the flow.

papers.title: Connected but Late: Sample Age of Commercial BLE Wearables under Wi-Fi Coexistence for Real-Time Clinical Applications
papers.abstract: Wearable sensors are increasingly being used in real-time clinical applications, such as rehabilitation robots and live therapy monitoring. As Healthcare 5.0 moves towards personalized therapies, their use will continue growing, potentially compromising communication reliability. Most wearables transmit over Bluetooth Low Energy, sharing 2.4 GHz with institutional Wi-Fi. Previous coexistence studies have focused on whether data arrive, rather than when. We measured sample age for a commercial electrocardiogram strap, from acquisition through the gateway to storage in our platform MEDWEAR, in an anechoic chamber and a hospital rehabilitation gym, and we compared it with illustrative clinical deadlines. Without load, the strap's own framing was the largest source of delay, making samples on average 280 ms and up to 550 ms old before transmission. Wi-Fi load had no measurable effect while adaptive frequency hopping could avoid the loaded channel. In a stress test, which forced the link onto the loaded channel, the link became the dominant source of delay, adding up to 11 s. The link stayed connected, but a median of 29% of samples and up to 98% (worst case) were older than 1 s on arrival at the gateway. The gym behaved mostly like the quiet chamber, but during one traffic burst, while hopping was restricted, up to 4.6% of samples were older than 1 s. These results show that a connected link can deliver late data. Therefore, sensors intended for real-time clinical applications should be profiled in situ and monitored based on sample age rather than connection status alone.

papers.title: Trallie: from Free-Form Text to Structured Data with LLMs
papers.abstract: Trallie is an open-source framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to perform information extraction (IE) from natural language sources with or without user guidance. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on extensive labeled datasets or domain-specific training, Trallie enables the conversion of unstructured data into structured formats with minimal or no representative examples. The framework is designed with three key objectives: (i) reducing manual annotation by harnessing prompt-based zero-shot and few-shot capabilities of modern LLMs, (ii) flexibly parsing diverse document formats (i.e., HTML, PDF, TXT, and JSON), and (iii) improving accessibility for non-expert users by automatically inducing schemas from document collections, which can then be refined for extraction. We evaluate Trallie with open-weight LLMs on FDA 510(k) documents and on movie and university websites from SWDE. It outperforms previously reported systems when the target attributes are provided for text extraction and is competitive when it must discover attributes for the schema automatically. The project is available at https://github.com/PiSchool/trallie

papers.title: Automorphism groups of mixing shifts of finite type
papers.abstract: We prove that nontrivial two-sided mixing shifts of finite type are flip conjugate if and only if their automorphism groups are abstractly commensurable. This resolves an outstanding question of Boyle, Lind, and Rudolph from 1988.

papers.title: GameDojo: Benchmarking Real-Time Interactive Agents in Video Games
papers.abstract: Interactive intelligence requires agents to act on observations and adapt to the consequences of actions. Studying these abilities calls for diverse, challenging tasks under controlled conditions. We introduce GameDojo, a controllable interactive gameplay benchmark of 120 boss encounters across 20 games for evaluating model capabilities, learning algorithms, and agent harnesses. Coding agents reconstruct the environments and write gameplay scripts, producing GameDojo-Data with 600 hours of gameplay trajectories. Experiments reveal substantial challenges for frontier models, especially in real-time interaction. Training on GameDojo-Data brings GameDojo-4B to frontier performance, with the strongest real-time performance. We also find joint training improves individual tasks, and learned policies transfer across bosses. Together, these findings establish GameDojo as a challenging and valuable interactive gameplay benchmark for the community. Our project page is at https://gamedojo-benchmark.github.io/ , and our code is at https://github.com/THUSI-Lab/GameDojo .

papers.title: GRAIN: Shared-Budget Complementary Re-observation for Object Detection
papers.abstract: Re-running a frozen detector on enlarged image crops recovers small and crowded objects without retraining, yet every crop costs an extra detector call. Existing slicing and adaptive-cropping pipelines plan crops per image in isolation, even though inspection demand varies widely across an image collection. We present GRAIN, which unifies cross-image call allocation and bounded-output admission around cross-image comparable resolution-closure gains over boundary-safe crop interiors. Coarse hypotheses carry resolution deficits, crops close a geometric share of those deficits for hypotheses enclosed in their interior positive region, and multiplicative residuals discount covered evidence within a monotone submodular surrogate. Prefix sums and a global max-heap execute this collection-wide plan on CPU before crop inference, and Positive-Region Fusion aligns post-inference spatial admission with the planned interior support before class-balanced top- selection. Across 17 frozen detectors from five families on COCO, CrowdHuman, and VisDrone-DET, GRAIN beats call-matched tiling in 100 of 102 AP@100 settings and transfers to AI-TOD-v2. With RF-DETR-S on CrowdHuman, it nearly matches two-crop tiling using one eighth of the crop calls. At fixed budgets, the surrogate orders candidate plans with Spearman correlations of 0.95 to 0.99 while the sweep attains at least 98% of the exact surrogate optimum. Code will be publicly released.

papers.title: Screening for nonrigidity in structure from motion using projected reprojection residuals
papers.abstract: Sparse structure from motion (SfM) assumes a static scene, yet deformation may still yield plausible reconstructions. Reprojection-error summaries discard how errors are arranged across points and views. We propose a diagnostic that first removes residual components explainable by small point and camera adjustments and simple spatial trends that change over time. It then measures alignment with fixed spatial and temporal patterns. The diagnostic uses one estimated SfM reconstruction and provides screening evidence rather than a physical deformation estimate. Across four synthetic tubular families, the diagnostic detected all eight acquisitions with prescribed motion, compared with five or six for summaries of reprojection-error magnitude. Each family's cutoff was the highest static score among the other three families, so the static acquisition with the highest score also screened positive. With the same cutoffs, the diagnostic retained positive detections in 19 of 20 reconstruction variants spanning changes in appearance and reconstruction pipeline, with one numerical abstention. These findings show that the arrangement of reprojection errors across points and views can reveal inconsistencies that their magnitudes alone miss. The four families were known during development, and the transfer variants reused two of them. Within this setting, the diagnostic offers a practical way to flag a plausible reconstruction for closer inspection using only its estimated cameras, 3D points and image observations.

papers.title: Hyperconvexity of pseudoconvex domains with continuous boundaries
papers.abstract: This is a reading note on a disc formula proof of hyperconvexity of bounded pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb C^n$ with continuous boundaries.

papers.title: Janus Asymmetry Unlocks Rashba Spintronics and Chiral Phononics in Two-Dimensional Carbo-Chalcogenides
papers.abstract: Spintronics and chiral phononics offer complementary routes for nanoscale control, yet realizing both functionalities within a common two-dimensional platform remains challenging. Here, using extensive first-principles calculations, we show that Janus asymmetry simultaneously drives both effects in transition-metal carbo-chalcogenides (JTMCCs) along two chemically distinct routes, through either chalcogen or transition-metal substitution. Remarkably, both Janus routes yield giant Rashba responses, with $α_\mathrm{R}\approx2$ eV Å in Ta$_2$CSSe and NbTaCS$_2$, exceeding those reported for Mo/W-based Janus transition-metal dichalcogenides. Furthermore, Janus asymmetry lifts the degeneracy of opposite-chirality phonons, producing splittings as large as $\approx28$ cm$^{-1}$. More strikingly, asymmetry generates chiral carbon vibrations that were achiral in the centrosymmetric parent compounds, with splittings reaching $\approx8$ cm$^{-1}$. Finally, we show external electric fields tunability over Rashba strength and chiral-phonon splittings, providing a common control knob for electronic spin and lattice angular momentum. Our work offers a unified strategy for realizing spintronic and chiral phononic in two-dimensional materials.

papers.title: Bridging the Semantic Gap from Natural Language Specifications to RTL with Layered Formal Guidance
papers.abstract: While large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in generating register-transfer level (RTL) code from natural-language specifications, their reliability remains limited on designs with complex control logic and temporal behavior. This stems from a fundamental semantic gap: high-level natural language often leaves implementation-critical details underspecified, forcing LLMs to infer unstated assumptions. This paper presents Layered Formal Guidance, a novel framework that bridges this semantic gap by using formal properties as an intermediate semantic layer between natural-language specifications and RTL generation. Our framework applies formal guidance across three layers: property-driven specification augmentation before generation, property-consistency checking after generation, and counterexample-guided refinement after checking. Experiments on RTLLM benchmarks and various open-source IP designs demonstrate that our framework achieves higher functional correctness and lower sampled output-trace diversity. Furthermore, we show that Layered Formal Guidance can flexibly augment both general-purpose LLMs and domain-specific models to substantially improve their generation reliability.

papers.title: Object Count Generalization Is an Interface Problem: Warping a Frozen Skill Instead of Retraining It
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning policies for robot manipulation degrade when the number of objects N in the scene grows beyond the training range. This is a covariate shift that also changes the dimension of the state. We propose WAVE (Warping Actions and Views of an Expert), which extends a pretrained single-object skill to many objects without updating its weights. WAVE has three parts. First, a selection policy picks the one object the robot works on next. Second, a warping policy reads a local view of the scene around that object, whose size does not depend on N. It emits a multiplier and an offset for every quantity the skill reads and every action it outputs. Third, the skill acts under this affine warp. It is shown a scene that holds a single object, while the warp steers it around the objects it is not shown and edits the actions that are sent to the robot. Both the selection and warping policies are trained with PPO on the multi-object reward and use the skill as a black box, so WAVE is task-general and skill-agnostic. It requires only that the skill was trained on the same embodiment and that every object has a goal pose. We also bound the number of attempts needed to place all N objects, assuming positive expected net progress per attempt, and measure this progress for each object count. We evaluate WAVE on cube arrangement tasks with a gantry robot and with a Franka Panda arm. Trained with at most nine cubes, it generalizes zero-shot to several times its training count, on the gantry to scenes of up to thirty cubes. Published methods that learn multi-object manipulation show count generalization up to six objects. Fine-tuning the skill, learning from the same local view without it, and an entity transformer, even when distilled from the pretrained skill, all collapse within their training counts under the same training budget.

papers.title: Fate of Vainshtein Screening for UV/IR Mixing with a $P(X)$ Higgs Classicalizer
papers.abstract: Classicalization is a non-Wilsonian framework in which an effective field theory self-completes above its strong-coupling scale by generating semiclassical objects that decay into many soft quanta, thereby realizing ultraviolet-infrared mixing. A key requirement of this mechanism is that the force carrier be lighter than the strong-coupling scale. A natural application would be to embed classicalization in the electroweak Higgs sector to address the little hierarchy problem. In this work, we investigate whether Higgs classicalization can occur within the $P(X)$ class of gauged k-essence and k-chameleon models. For classicalization to occur, the theory must support Vainshtein screening around a sharply localized source. Our results show that it fails to do so, even when one attempts to engineer a symbiosis with chameleon screening through a gauge kinetic function, owing to a strong-coupling breakdown inside the screening region. These $P(X)$ theories therefore fail to provide a suitable framework for Higgs classicalization. Nevertheless, we emphasize that our results, obtained for a specific class of models, should not be interpreted as a no-go theorem for Higgs classicalization.

papers.title: Distribution of Rademacher random multiplicative functions in short intervals, with proper normalization
papers.abstract: We determine the limiting distribution of partial sums $\sum_{x<n\le x+y}f(n)$ of a Rademacher random multiplicative function over short intervals. Combined with the theorem of Soundararajan and Xu, our result gives a standard real Gaussian limit, with a suitable deterministic normalization, throughout $x^{1/5}\log x\ll y=o(x)$. This resolves the Rademacher extension raised by Harper, Soundararajan and Xu. The normalization is smaller than the standard deviation by a factor tending to zero when $\log(x/y)=o(\sqrt{\log\log x})$. As an application of our method, we also obtain a complex Gaussian limit for short interval sums twisted by a fixed primitive nonreal Dirichlet character.

papers.title: Conservative tidal effects to third post-Minkowskian order in scalar-tensor theories
papers.abstract: Using worldline effective field theory, we compute the conservative finite-size contributions to the impulse and scattering angle of nonspinning compact binaries in massless scalar-tensor theories with a scalar-Gauss-Bonnet coupling through third post-Minkowskian (3PM) order. We retain the full velocity dependence at linear order in the tidal response coefficients. The calculation covers the scalar dipole and quadrupole and the electric, magnetic, and mixed quadrupoles and octupoles. Among them, the scalar dipole enters the dynamics already at third post-Newtonian (3PN) order, two orders before the gravitational quadrupole. At 3PM, the tidal correction to the angle also depends on the first scalar derivatives of the responses and contains terms linear in the Gauss-Bonnet coupling. The results reproduce the general-relativistic tidal angle and the post-Newtonian tidal dynamics through 5PN, and a test-body calculation confirms their leading order in the mass ratio, including the Gauss-Bonnet terms for a companion with vanishing sensitivity.

papers.title: Normalized Weyl Energy and the Differential Topology of Four-Manifolds
papers.abstract: The Weyl functional $\int_M\|W_g\|^2\,dμ_g$ plays an important role in four dimensional conformal geometry. Using this functional, Chang, Gursky, and Zhang introduced an invariant of an admissible conformal class and a smooth invariant of the underlying manifold obtained by taking the infimum over all such classes. We use a normalization in which both invariants, denoted by $β(M,c)$ and $β(M)$, take values in $[0,1)$. We prove that every admissible four-manifold $M$ with $β(M)$ sufficiently close to $1/2$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{CP}^2$ up to reversal of orientation. At $β(M)=1/2$, this result and the conformal characterization of the Fubini--Study class confirm Conjecture~1.1 of Chang, Gursky, and Zhang. Among admissible four-manifolds with indefinite intersection form, we prove the corresponding stability of the diffeomorphism type of $S^2\times S^2$ near $2/3$. For the one- and two-point blow-ups of $\mathbb{CP}^2$, we show that $β(M)$ lies strictly above the respective topological lower bounds of $2/3$ and $23/30$. These results lead us to ask whether $1$ is the only accumulation point of the values of $β(M)$ and whether, among simply connected admissible four-manifolds, $β(M)$ determines the diffeomorphism type up to reversal of orientation.

papers.title: Categorical Torelli theorem for quintic threefolds
papers.abstract: We prove that two smooth quintic threefolds over $\mathbb{C}$ are isomorphic if their bounded derived categories of coherent sheaves are equivalent.

papers.title: On the Fourier Analysis of the Einstein-Klein-Gordon System: Limiting Behaviour of the Fourier Coefficients
papers.abstract: We revisit the problem of computing the Fourier coefficients associated with the spherically symmetric massless-scalar field system in $(1+3)$ dimensions initiated in [10]. We rigorously derive computationally efficient formulas for these coefficients and then use them to establish their asymptotic behavior as the mode numbers tend to infinity, including the explicit determination of the leading-order coefficients. Our approach builds on the method developed in [12] and relies on two powerful algorithms for hypergeometric summation, due to Zeilberger and Gosper. These algorithms enable us to systematically derive first-order linear recurrence relations and obtain closed-form discrete antiderivatives respectively for intricate hypergeometric sequences that arise in our analysis.

papers.title: Geometry-controlled clogging and transport mechanisms in confined Y-junctions
papers.abstract: We investigate transport and clogging of hard particles in a confined symmetric Y-junction using off-lattice Monte Carlo simulations. The geometry is controlled by the channel width w and a truncation parameter s that modifies the inner vertex. The flow probability exhibits a sharp sigmoidal crossover, defining a characteristic width wc that depends non-monotonically on s. This non-monotonic behavior persists under variations of the transverse Monte Carlo step, although the absolute values of wc change. Microscopic analysis reveals two distinct blocking mechanisms: single-particle obstruction at small truncations and collective arch-like structures at larger truncations. Residence-time statistics and particle-order inversions provide additional evidence of this change in transport dynamics. Our results demonstrate that local modifications of junction geometry can strongly affect clogging and particle transport, even in a minimal model with excluded-volume interactions only.

papers.title: A Matrix Lee-Sidford Barrier and Faster Semidefinite Programming
papers.abstract: We construct a matrix analog of the Lee-Sidford barrier for semidefinite programming (SDP) with $m$ equality constraints and $n$-by-$n$ matrices. The barrier has self-concordance parameter $\widetilde{O}(m)$, so short-step interior-point methods require only $\widetilde O(\sqrt m)$ iterations. We also show that our matrix Lee-Sidford barrier can be implemented efficiently by developing a randomized algorithm that solves SDPs with $m\leq n$ to accuracy $ε$ in $(n^{ω+o(1)}+n^2m^{3/2+o(1)})\operatorname{polylog}(1/ε)$ time, where $ω\leq 9/4$ is the matrix multiplication exponent, achieving the fastest known running time in this regime.

papers.title: Identification of Poisson processes through a one-dimensional projection
papers.abstract: We study the identification of stationary Poisson processes in Euclidean space through a single one-dimensional projection. Given a point process and a straight line, each point is retained independently with a probability given by a Gaussian function of its distance to the line; the retained points are projected onto the line. If the process is Poisson, the projection is again Poisson. What a single projection reveals depends on the sign of the second factorial cumulant, which is also the sign of the two-point correlations. Under a Palm domination condition, which holds for positively associated processes, the cumulant is nonnegative. Using a Chen-Stein argument we show that when the cumulant of the projection vanishes, the process is Poisson. Consequently, a single projection identifies non-Poissonianity. The same result holds under negative association. When the cumulant changes sign, a random projection detects a nonzero cumulant with probability one. We propose a test whose rejection region is computed by Monte Carlo. The test, together with a spacings-based variant for repulsive alternatives, rejects determinantal, shot-noise and other classical processes. When applied to lunar impact craters, the test rejects the Poisson hypothesis for craters with diameter below 30 km and does not reject it for craters above 45 km.

papers.title: A general formalism for electromagnetic production of two mesons on the nucleon
papers.abstract: We develop a general formalism for the electromagnetic production of two mesons on the nucleon, $γ_{\rm v}N\toΦ_1Φ_2B$, that can be used in single-channel as well as coupled-channel analyses over a wide range of energies. In the spirit of the decomposition introduced by Berends et al. for single-meson electroproduction, the hadronic current is expanded in a set of 16 gauge- and Lorentz-invariant matrices, four of which vanish for real photons. The corresponding Lorentz-invariant (Dirac) amplitudes can be obtained from any reaction model and are mapped onto 16 CGLN-like Pauli amplitudes, from which the five-fold differential cross section and its transverse, longitudinal, and interference response functions follow directly. Although these matrices are not all linearly independent, they follow directly from the covariant decomposition of the current, so the amplitudes can be read off from the Feynman diagrams and the observables take a simpler, more symmetric form. As a first application, we calculate the $γp\toπ^0π^0p$ and $γp\toπ^+π^0n$ reactions near threshold from tree-level nucleon Born terms. This example shows explicitly how the Dirac amplitudes are read off from Feynman diagrams and how gauge invariance, which is violated by the individual diagrams, is restored in the total amplitude and preserved when hadronic form factors are included. The formalism thus provides a versatile basis for future theoretical and phenomenological studies of double-meson photo- and electroproduction. A more complete abstract is provided in the paper.

papers.title: Symmetry breaking Poincar{é}--Einstein metrics and non-extendable boundary Killing fields
papers.abstract: We construct Poincar{é}-Einstein metrics on $R^2xS^3xS^2xS^2$ which bifurcate from anti-de Sitter black holes whose horizon is the product of a B{ö}hm metric on $S^3xS^2$ with a round $S^2$ , and which break the rotational symmetry of the $S^2$ factor while keeping their conformal infinity. Some Killing fields of the conformal infinity therefore do not extend to the bulk, although $$π$^1(M, $\partial$M ) = 0$. The construction rests on two results of independent interest: the Lichnerowicz eigenvalues of B{ö}hm metrics on invariant transverse traceless tensors are simple (with at most two exceptional values), the lowest one tends to $-$\infty$$ along B{ö}hm's sequence with a gap to the next one tending to infinity; and large anti-de Sitter black holes in dimension nine with an Einstein horizon have no static $L^2$ perturbation of scalar type, which we prove with an explicit positive supersolution of the Kodama-Ishibashi master equation.

papers.title: Aharonov-Bohm oscillations in transport through interacting quantum dots
papers.abstract: We investigate electronic transport through a two-terminal Aharonov-Bohm interferometer with two quantum dots in the presence of finite intra-dot Coulomb interactions. With the help of a diagrammatic technique, we derive, within linear perturbation theory in the tunnelling-coupling strength, analytic expressions for the occupations, current, and interferometric visibility in terms of a coherence measure that involves the sum of four off-diagonal elements of the reduced density matrix. The latter are calculated numerically from a master equation for arbitrary settings of the system parameters. For some symmetric setups, we obtain closed-form expressions for the linear conductance. We systematically analyse the impact of a finite Coulomb interaction on the interferometric visibility, and reveal a rapid suppression of destructive interference upon breaking of system symmetries. Our results are supported by alternative methods, including the TraSPI method.

papers.title: A Keller--Segel Chemotaxis Model on One-Dimensional Moving Domains
papers.abstract: We study a one-dimensional Keller--Segel system on an interval whose boundary moves according to a prescribed contracting law. The boundary motion makes the problem genuinely nonautonomous and destroys the mass conservation available on fixed domains. A time-dependent change of variables, combined with a time reparametrization, reduces the problem to a semilinear system on a fixed interval with time-independent principal part and nonautonomous transport terms. We prove global well-posedness and regularity of weak solutions, and we show that the contraction of the domain yields a uniform bound on the total mass. For the long-time dynamics, our main tool is a singular Gronwall type inequality with an exponentially damped kernel, for which we provide a self-contained version with explicit decay rate and constants, tailored to our setting; under a small gain condition on the boundary velocities, it yields dissipativity with an explicit exponential decay rate, which cannot be obtained from the classical inequality of Henry. With it we prove the existence of the minimal pullback attractor in the universe of families of bounded sets, on the moving domain and then on the fixed rescaled reference domains. Finally, numerical simulations on contracting domains illustrate the effect of the boundary motion on cell aggregation.

papers.title: Learning Dense Head-Object Contact Estimation with Synthetic Data
papers.abstract: Head serves a critical role in human cognitive and perceptual functions while remaining vulnerable to external impacts, making the understanding of head contact essential for human safety. Despite its importance, dense head-object contact estimation remains largely unexplored, primarily due to the absence of head-object contact data. Recently, it has been shown that synthetic data can serve as powerful training data in limited data scenario, implying the potential of synthetic data in head-object contact estimation. There are two core challenges for dense head-object contact estimation. First, head-object interactions are highly diverse, resulting in substantial variations in contact regions and patterns across different objects and interaction types. Second, head contact regions are often heavily occluded by hair, making direct visual observation of the actual contact regions difficult. To address these issues, we introduce HEad COntact estimation (HECO) with synthetic data. To handle diverse head-object interactions, we leverage semantic context from text features that encode semantic relationships between head regions and interacting objects. To resolve hair occlusion issue of actual head contact regions, we introduce occlusion-aware contact learning that learns to infer head contact beyond visible information from images via amodal inpainting. As a result, we enable head-object contact estimation with HECO trained with our synthetic dataset, overcoming the issue of absence of contact data. The codes will be released.

papers.title: SchemaCaps: When a Compatible Tool Update Silently Widens an AI Agent's Authority
papers.abstract: The tools users approve for their AI agents keep changing their JSON input schemas. Of 8 surveyed MCP clients and scanners, none is observed or documented to re-approve a tool whose input schema widens (two not determinable). We define non-amplification over the coordinates visible in the schema (declared arguments and undeclared fields, on effective values) and a re-binding rule decided by subschema inclusion, trusting no field labels by default and conservative up to its checker and tested case analysis. Evidence: a Coq proof of composition; 48 regression tests; an exact-reference benchmark, where the reviewed version of the rule silently re-bound 27 amplifying changes, now fixed; and a pilot on 604 releases of 39 public MCP servers. There, 412 of 580 compatible schema changes widen some coordinate, yet compatibility re-binds them silently. The authors' adjudicated double annotation finds at least 76 that add or widen an authority-bearing argument (66 of the 84 a name-based labeller flags, plus 10 it misses). On existing tools, the rule asks 645 re-approvals, against 1,197 for pinning the input schema (2,004 with descriptions) and 617 for compatibility. Behaviour change behind an identical schema remains out of reach.

papers.title: Notes on an elementary proof of Weil II from Hexagon
papers.abstract: Recently, L. Alpöge sketched an elementary proof of Deligne's weight bound in footnote 3 of his remark on joint work with Claude on the Riemann hypothesis. An expanded, AI-generated account appeared on Hexagon, where it was posted by F. Alderliefste. This note gives an exposition of the proof presented there.

papers.title: Two-dimensional Thyristor
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer a viable platform for next-generation electronics beyond sub-3 nm nodes, yet essential nonlinear circuit elements, such as thyristors, remain unexplored on atomically thin platforms. Here, we report an atomically thin reconfigurable electro-optical thyristor based on a lateral WSe2-MoSe2-WSe2-MoSe2 PNPN heterostructure, directly grown via sequential edge epitaxy. Unlike single-junction 2D diodes, this multijunction architecture exhibits thyristor-like nonlinear switching, including forward blocking, abrupt snapback, bistability, and electrical latching. The device exhibits a forward-blocking voltage of 183 V, corresponding to a critical electric field of 1 MV/cm. Under open-gate conditions, avalanche-assisted carrier multiplication and regenerative feedback are associated with a sharp forward-voltage drop of 175 V, a pronounced current surge, and an ultralow holding voltage. Gate-pulse modulation and temperature-dependent measurements indicate avalanche-assisted thyristor operation and latching behavior. This 2D lateral heterostructure enables a new route to nonlinear and bistable switching, latching, ultralow standby power, and adaptive logic, opening the way for reconfigurable 2D electronics and photonic integrated circuits.

papers.title: Dephasing-Powered Autonomous Quantum Engine with Time-Crystalline Work Cycles
papers.abstract: Autonomous quantum engines seek to convert energy supplied by environments into useful work, yet dephasing is usually regarded as detrimental noise. Here we show that local dephasing can instead power a quantum engine: by disrupting ferromagnetic correlations in an interacting spin-$1/2$ ensemble, it injects energy that can be transferred through an LC resonator to a passive load. Remarkably, without any external periodic driving, the coupled system can self-organize into a time-crystalline work cycle that delivers sustained, reproducible power. Within homogeneous mean-field dynamics, we identify two distinct routes to such operation. At weak spin--resonator coupling, the dissipative time crystal of the unloaded working medium survives loading and drives the receiver. At stronger coupling, resonator backaction can disrupt cyclic operation, whereas appropriate load damping restores a stable, self-consistent periodic cycle of the composite system. Finite-size spin-diffusion simulations further reveal rapidly increasing uninterrupted operating times with different size dependences in the two regimes. Our results demonstrate how an autonomous quantum engine can self-organize its collective dynamics through interactions and load feedback to harness environmental noise for sustained cyclic work output.

papers.title: Efficient Shot Allocation and Spectral Reconstruction for Real-Time Quantum Krylov Diagonalization
papers.abstract: We develop analytical and statistical methods to improve the energy estimate from the real-time quantum Krylov diagonalization under a fixed measurement budget. We first express the leading energy variance as a function of the number of shots assigned to each circuit setting, accounting for both the sensitivity of the energy to the measured moments and the correlations among outcomes recorded in the same shot.We use an initial batch of measurements to choose how to allocate the remaining shots. Under fixed-model regularity assumptions, the resulting generalized least-squares energy estimator attains the minimum leading mean-square error (MSE) coefficient within the prescribed allocation class, with the initial measurements included in the total shot budget. Furthermore, we use the same data to reconstruct the Hamiltonian and overlap moments jointly by fitting them to a common nonnegative spectral measure. For asymptotically Gaussian moment errors, we characterize precisely when this reconstruction lowers the leading energy MSE in the case where two linearly independent inequalities describe the feasible moment perturbations to first order. Numerical experiments on spin and Hubbard models show that learned allocation can improve Ritz energy estimates at fixed total shot cost. The experiments also illustrate that enforcing spectral consistency can further reduce the energy estimation error.

papers.title: Intent-Conditioned Argument Mediation for Tool-Using LLM Agents: Blocking Trusted-but-Unauthorized Arguments
papers.abstract: LLM agents turn a user's request and retrieved content into tool calls, and a call can reach the wrong recipient, endpoint, file or participant. Argument-level provenance blocks such values when they come from untrusted content, but accepts a trusted value that the user never requested. IntentFlow, a mediation layer between an unmodified planner and its tools, checks each authority-bearing argument against an intent contract and a provenance policy. On a synthetic benchmark of 200 attacks (oracle intent and injection labels, declared roles), attack success falls from 50.5% with provenance alone to 12.0% [8.2-17.2%]; every remaining success alters a content or payload field. IntentFlow wrongly blocks none of 200 paired benign tasks and 4 of 50 hard ones. On 50 trusted-but-unauthorized attacks, provenance-only mediation executes all 50 and IntentFlow none; a CaMeL-style check also blocks all 50 but rejects 16 of 50 benign tasks. On an offline AgentDojo-derived replay, IntentFlow blocks all 20 attacks at 75% benign success, as does a CaMeL-style check; a Progent-style allowlist blocks 19 and keeps all benign tasks. With one live planner and the same oracles, the mediator blocked all 17 corrupted calls proposed in 110 attacks.

papers.title: Geometric properties of concatenated geometric and holonomic quantum gates
papers.abstract: We investigate the geometric properties of concatenated quantum gates, focusing on the distinction between geometric and holonomic quantum computation. We show that, although individual gates may be purely geometric, their concatenation does not generally preserve this property, since the cyclic states of the composite operation can accumulate nontrivial dynamical phases over the course of the concatenated evolution. In contrast, we demonstrate that concatenations of arbitrary single-qubit holonomic gates remain holonomic, provided that the parallel-transport condition holds throughout the evolution and the computational subspace undergoes cyclic evolution. The preservation of geometric or holonomic character under concatenation is an important prerequisite for extending arguments underlying geometric protection from individual gates to complete quantum circuits.

papers.title: Comparison of 3D-DXA Measurements with QCT Software Solutions for Proximal Femur Bone Density Assessment
papers.abstract: 3D-Shaper reconstructs proximal femur shape and density in 3D from a standard hip dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) scan. In men and women aged 35-91 years, we compared 3D-Shaper integral volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD), trabecular vBMD, and cortical surface BMD (sBMD) with quantitative computed tomography (QCT) processed with three methods: an in-house pipeline, Stradview and QCTPro CTXA, which were used to derive bone measurements equivalent to those of 3D-Shaper. Agreement, including among QCT methods, was assessed with linear regression and Bland-Altman analysis (bias and limits of agreement, LoA). 3D-Shaper agreed strongly with the in-house pipeline and Stradview for integral vBMD (R=0.95-0.96; bias 1.5 to 4.2 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$39.7 to 41.4 mg/cm$^3$), trabecular vBMD (R=0.92-0.94; bias -11.8 to -7.8 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$33.3 to 39.4 mg/cm$^3$) and cortical sBMD (R=0.94; bias 5.6 to 38.2 mg/cm$^2$; LoA $\pm$23.6 to 26.4 mg/cm$^2$). The in-house pipeline and Stradview agreed for integral vBMD (R=1.00; bias -2.7 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$3.7 mg/cm$^3$), trabecular vBMD (R=0.96-1.00; bias -0.2 to 3.9 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$6.9 to 27.5 mg/cm$^3$) and cortical sBMD (R=0.98; bias 32.7 mg/cm$^2$; LoA $\pm$14.6 mg/cm$^2$). Compared with 3D-Shaper, QCTPro CTXA integral vBMD was systematically lower (R=0.90; bias -28.4 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$61.5 mg/cm$^3$) and trabecular vBMD showed a proportional bias (R=0.89; bias -44.1 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$61.3 mg/cm$^3$). The same pattern was observed against the other QCT methods, for integral vBMD (R=0.93; bias -32.6 to -29.9 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$49.6 to 50.0 mg/cm$^3$) and trabecular vBMD (R=0.94-0.96; bias -36.3 to -32.5 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$51.2 to 54.9 mg/cm$^3$). These findings support the agreement of 3D-Shaper with independent QCT approaches and show that 3D-Shaper-QCT differences must be interpreted in light of the QCT method used.

papers.title: Transport-Safe Evaluation of LLM Agents: Trajectory-Dependent Judge Error and Anytime-Valid Auditing
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are often ranked by an LLM judge whose error rates are measured once and reused for every agent. The corrected success rates can then be biased when the judge's errors depend on the trajectory and agents differ in the trajectories they produce for successes or failures. We derive the exact asymptotic bias and give a chain of checks from identification to simultaneous ranks. On a four-agent semi-synthetic benchmark, a scalar correction with oracle calibration has maximum bias 0.245 and mean pointwise coverage 0.016, and never recovers the full ranking (0/250 replications). Augmented inverse-probability weighting (AIPW) with a uniform or a design-aware random audit keeps the maximum bias below 0.003, with mean pointwise coverage of 0.939 and 0.950. In a 48-cell stress test, effective target support rises only from 0.209 to 0.805 as calibration grows from 600 to 4,800 labels, while audited AIPW keeps a mean absolute error of 0.018-0.020. Without calibration support, or with judge dependence within an externally justified bound, we report valid bounds or sensitivity sets and carry them into rank sets. An e-process confidence sequence stays valid, for a stable target, under predictable adaptive auditing and arbitrary stopping.

papers.title: Place-Revisit Consistency Evaluation of Reference Poses
papers.abstract: Reference trajectories are widely used to evaluate odometry and simultaneous localization and mapping systems. However, local inconsistencies in benchmark reference poses can bias such evaluations. This paper presents a place-revisit consistency evaluation method for reference poses in mobile sensing datasets. When a platform revisits a previously observed place after a sufficient temporal gap, the relative pose implied by the reference trajectory should agree with relative poses estimated directly from onboard sensors. We instantiate this idea with lidar scan registration and stereo-image pose estimation, and apply it to the KITTI Odometry and SNAIL Radar. The KITTI analysis identifies several revisit regions where the public reference poses disagree with sensor-derived relative poses, with median translation discrepancies up to 6.60 m. Representative point-cloud overlays further localize these discrepancies and support the use of place revisits as a benchmark-validation tool.

papers.title: All-in-one Spintronic Sensory Neurons for Magnetic Edge Intelligence
papers.abstract: Magnetic fields enable non-contact sensing through nonmagnetic materials, offering opportunities for magnetic edge intelligence in autonomous recognition, navigation, and control. However, directly converting magnetic stimuli into neural spikes for local neuromorphic processing remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate an all-in-one spintronic sensory neuron (SSN) based on spin-transfer-torque magnetic tunnel junctions (STT-MTJs) fabricated using a 40-nm magnetoresistive random-access memory (MRAM) process. By exploiting magnetic-field-modulated stochastic switching, the SSN enables probability-based sensing with an electrically tunable sensitive field window, allowing adaptive operation across different magnetic-field ranges without structural modification. This tunability alleviates the fixed sensitivity-range constraint of conventional tunneling magnetoresistance sensing, providing an accessible sensing range of +/-40 mT with an average probability sensitivity of 2.91%/mT. Importantly, the same stochastic switching process directly transduces magnetic stimuli into binary spike trains, integrating magnetic sensing, nonlinear rate encoding, and spike generation within a single nanoscale device. The resulting sigmoidal spike-rate response enables magnetic-field encoding, experimentally validated using the Neural Engineering Framework. Using experimentally characterized device responses, a simulated 10 x 10 SSN array achieves 90.7% accuracy in contactless magnetic-trajectory recognition with optimized encoding, approaching the software baseline. These results establish a scalable, MRAM-compatible approach to unifying programmable magnetic sensing and neural encoding for sensor-native edge intelligence.

papers.title: Coordinating Perception and Planning for Test-Time Adaptation in End-to-End Driving under Distribution Shifts
papers.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving has achieved significant milestones, yet its reliance on the i.i.d. assumption renders it vulnerable to real-world distribution shifts. While Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) offers a promising paradigm for on-the-fly enhancement, its application to driving is hindered by two barriers: (i) multi-task adaptation dependency, where updates to upstream perception also affect downstream planning, while perception confidence alone does not directly assess these downstream effects; and (ii) continuous adaptation instability, where recursive online updates over long horizons cause compounding parameter drift. To address these challenges, we propose P2-TTA, a plug-and-play TTA framework for the continual adaptation of end-to-end driving models.
