In contrast, the remaining two edges are antiferromagnetically coupled in the armchair triangular QDs, indicating an edge-asymmetric antiferromagnetic (AFM) ground state. We further identified the AFM ground states in hexagonal QDs, indicating that these types of asymmetric configurations are not unique to triangular QDs. Collectively, edge-asymmetric magnetism could create potential opportunities for future spintronics.

papers.title: Shift by Analogy for Compositional Zero-Shot Learning
papers.abstract: Compositional zero-shot learning recognizes attribute-object pairs absent from training. An unseen pair has a semantic description but lacks an observed visual reference. We propose Shift by Analogy (SBA) to make unseen compositions visually seen through a shift-then-match process. Its core add-subtract-add rule transfers an attribute change between two seen image-text residuals on a source object to a reference residual on the target object. This shifts the target's own text feature toward its visual center; learned refinement produces a proxy for matching query images. During training, each target is excluded from its supports, and recognition is learned using references constructed from other pairs. An analogy library and same-object attention extend this construction across candidates, while joint learning integrates proxy matching with semantic and primitive evidence. Visual-center analysis confirms substantially improved correspondence for unseen compositions. Experiments across three standard benchmarks show that SBA consistently outperforms strong CZSL baselines under both closed- and open-world evaluation.

papers.title: FMSNO: Scaling Surface Neural Operators by Learned Flow Matching Reparametrisation
papers.abstract: We propose the Flow Matching Surface Neural Operator (FMSNO), which combines learning a shared map from irregular surface meshes to a regular two-dimensional grid on the sphere and training a neural operator on the regular grid. Constructing a separate map for each new geometry can dominate inference time on large meshes. We initially pretrain the mapping by flow matching using precomputed optimal transport maps as targets and then continue its training using combined geometry and CFD objectives. We apply it to unseen geometries in a single forward pass. The learned flow deforms the surface points, and we project its endpoints onto the sphere. We then splat geometric features onto the spherical grid, apply a neural operator (we tested both Fourier and Spherical Fourier Neural Operators), and interpolate its output back to the surface. For a mesh with $N$ points, evaluating the map costs O(N), and the full prediction costs O(NlogN) with the FNO backbone. We evaluate surface pressure prediction on ShapeNet-Car, AhmedML, and DrivAerNet++, and drag coefficient prediction on DrivAerNet++. Across the three pressure benchmarks, our accuracy is on par with that of the most accurate baseline. On a surface with one million points, our method achieves a 354x end-to-end inference speedup over that baseline while keeping the same memory usage asymptotics of O(N).

papers.title: The Fourth-Power Formula for the Antipode in AS-Gorenstein Hopf Algebras
papers.abstract: AS-Gorenstein Hopf algebras, for which homological integrals are defined, form a broad class of (infinite-dimensional) Hopf algebras. We establish an $S^4$ formula for left AS-Gorenstein Hopf algebras, thereby generalizing Radford's $S^4$ formula for finite-dimensional Hopf algebras and refining the formula of Brown and Zhang by identifying a group-like conjugating element in the Hopf algebra $H$. Our approach is to endow the space of left homological integrals $\int^{\ell}_H$ with a canonical right $H^*$-module structure compatible with its natural right $H$-action. If the $H^*$-action is rational, then $\int^{\ell}_H$ carries a canonical $(\mathrm{id}_H,S^4)$-twisted right-left Yetter--Drinfeld module structure. The right $H$-action and left $H$-coaction on this one-dimensional space determine a character and a group-like element in $H$, respectively; the twisted Yetter--Drinfeld compatibility condition then yields the $S^4$ formula. The $H^*$-action on $\int^{\ell}_H$ is rational if either the coradical of $H$ is coreflexive or the trivial left module $\Bbbk$ admits a finitely generated projective resolution. In particular, the latter condition holds when $H$ is left noetherian. We also establish a corresponding result for right AS-co-Gorenstein Hopf algebras with coreflexive coradical. As applications, we use the $S^4$ formula to study the bijectivity of the antipode and derive explicit finite-order bounds when $H$ is module-finite and faithfully flat over a central right coideal subalgebra, or finitely cogenerated and faithfully coflat over a cocentral quotient.

papers.title: AirVT-15k: A Query-Diverse UAV Video-Text Dataset and Query-Adaptive Evidence Alignment Network for Retrieval
papers.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle video-text retrieval (UAV-TVR) requires matching language to both scene context and subtle object changes. A harbor-layout query relies on global scene context, whereas a departing-vessel query requires local functional cues and motion states. Existing benchmarks provide diverse aerial descriptions but give limited attention to distinct evidence needs within the same video. We introduce AirVT-15k, a benchmark of 15,504 UAV videos and 155,040 captions, with ten complementary bilingual captions per video describing scenes, object states, and temporal changes. We also propose AirFocus-CST, which selects query-relevant frames and patches, encodes temporal feature differences, and combines coarse-to-fine interaction (CFI) with optimal-transport alignment (OTA). Average mean recall reaches 63.67% on AirVT-15k and 24.41% on CapERA, improving over the strongest baselines by 2.96 and 1.91 percentage points, respectively. The dataset and code are available at https://chenxi000233.github.io/AirVT-15k-site/.

papers.title: Learning Teacher Output Preferences from Final Responses for Reasoning Distillation
papers.abstract: Many large language models (LLMs) use chain-of-thought (CoT) to solve complex problems, but hide their CoT traces to prevent reasoning capabilities from being distilled. While recent studies have shown that hidden CoTs can be reconstructed, existing methods typically require training a separate attacker for each target LLM. This paper studies model-agnostic CoT reconstruction, aiming to reconstruct hidden CoT traces from arbitrary target LLMs using only input prompts and visible final responses. We propose Final-Output Preference Learning (FOPL), which trains a single reconstruction model that generalizes to unseen LLMs without target-specific adaptation. To achieve this, the reconstruction model must learn which reasoning patterns match a given final response without knowing the target LLM's identity. We address this using preference optimization, training the reconstruction model to prefer native CoTs over synthetic alternatives for the same question and final response. By learning these preferences from LLMs with accessible CoTs, the reconstruction model learns to distinguish reasoning patterns based on visible responses. Experiments show that reconstructed CoTs capture distinct reasoning patterns across LLM families, including a family unseen during training. Moreover, students trained on reconstructed CoTs match or outperform those trained on native CoTs across several reasoning benchmarks.

papers.title: Rotating Black Holes from Scaling Transformations in Horava Gravity
papers.abstract: We study the scaling transformations that change the physical parameters of solutions in low-energy Horava gravity. In particular, we present a simple scaling transformation that generates rotating black-hole solutions in low-energy Horava gravity from known relativistic solutions. As explicit examples, we obtain "Doran-like" and "Kerr-Schild-like" rotating solutions in Horava gravity. We find that both solutions are horizon-penetrating, but their null horizons are not Killing horizons. We also find that, although their singularity structures differ from each other, chronology is protected in both solutions, as in the previously obtained Kerr-like solutions in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates.

papers.title: Impact of Topology and Sequence Length on the Pressure-Dependent Collapsibility of Proteins
papers.abstract: Several physical and evolutionary factors, including temperature, pressure, solvent quality, and natural selection, influence how amino acid sequences adopt their native structures. Although protein folding has been extensively studied, the physical determinants of protein collapse and their relationship to native-state folding remain less understood. In particular, "collapsibility", the intrinsic propensity of a protein sequence to form compact conformations, is distinct from but closely related to "foldability", the ability to reach the native structure. Previous theoretical studies suggested that collapsibility is encoded in native-state topology, potentially reflecting evolutionary selection. However, the roles of solvent-mediated interactions and hydrostatic pressure remain unclear. Here, we extend the theoretical framework of protein collapsibility by incorporating a pressure-dependent desolvation potential to investigate how hydrostatic pressure influences protein collapse. We find that increasing pressure destabilizes the fully folded native state, but can still favor the compact, water-mediated conformations. Furthermore, the magnitude and direction of pressure-induced changes in collapsibility depend strongly on native-state topology, including secondary and tertiary structures. Proteins and domains with a higher proportion of non-local native contacts generally exhibit greater pressure-induced water-mediated collapsibility. These findings highlight the role of native-state topology in determining the pressure sensitivity of protein collapse and provide insights into the interplay among protein structure, solvent-mediated interactions, and environmental perturbations.

papers.title: MH-RAG-DIVE: Dynamic and Cost-Efficient Multi-Hop RAG Evaluation via Tree-Cached Dialogue Simulation
papers.abstract: Quality assessment is essential for determining whether changes to a Retrieval-Augmented Generation system improve or maintain its performance. However, existing evaluation approaches often rely on single-turn or single-hop interactions and therefore do not capture the complexity of multi-hop, multi-turn conversations. We introduce MH-RAG-DIVE, a dynamic interactive user simulation framework designed to evaluate RAG systems in more complex multi-hop and multi-turn settings. The framework extends RAG-DIVE with a Context Discoverer, which identifies documents that can be combined to generate multi-hop questions within an ongoing conversation. To address the high computational cost of dynamic user simulation, we further introduce a Conversation Cacher, which reuses turns from previous evaluation runs while preserving the dynamic nature of the evaluation. We evaluate the framework across six distinct RAG configurations and compare its results with the original RAG-DIVE evaluation and the static, human-created CLAPNQ dataset. Our experiments show consistent performance trends across the evaluation approaches, while the more complex multi-hop and multi-turn setting exposes additional challenges for RAG systems. Furthermore, the Conversation Cacher substantially reduces token consumption, demonstrating its potential to make dynamic evaluation more cost-efficient. Finally, we apply MH-RAG-DIVE to an industrial RAG system with domain-specific data, demonstrating its applicability to real-world evaluation scenarios. Overall, our results show that the proposed approach provides a more complex and cost-efficient framework for evaluating RAG systems. All code and experimental data are publicly available in our GitHub repository (https://github.com/Daniel-Innsbruck/MH-RAG-DIVE).

papers.title: When Does Reasoning Help Entity Disambiguation? Small LLMs In-Domain and Under Shift
papers.abstract: Entity disambiguation (mapping ambiguous mentions in text to entities in a knowledge base) is a foundational step in tasks such as knowledge graph construction, question answering, and information extraction. Recent work has applied LLMs to this problem, achieving stateof-the-art performance. Notably, reasoning LLMs have been shown to perform entity disambiguation in a true zero-shot fashion, generalizing across knowledge bases and domains. However, it is unclear whether this capability survives, or remains competitive, with smaller LLMs, where entity disambiguation has typically relied on reranking rather than reasoning. We ask when reasoning is worth its cost at small scale. We compare pointwise, listwise, and reasoning-based candidate-selection components within a classical coarse-to-fine entity disambiguation pipeline, across the classical, few-shot and true zero-shot settings. The reasoning paradigm is trained with distillation and reinforcement learning recipes. The benefit of reasoning grows with domain shift: negligible in-domain, decisive in the true zero-shot setting. We show that two distinct factors are at work: the reranker's uncertainty over the candidates locates where the paradigms disagree, while shift governs which is right when they do.

papers.title: Alpha-points of a putative binary $q$-analog of the Fano plane
papers.abstract: A point $P$ of a putative $q$-analog $\mathcal{D}$ of the Fano plane is an $α$-point if the derived design of $\mathcal{D}$ in $P$ is a Desarguesian line spread. Kiermaier showed that for $q$ prime or even every hyperplane contains a point which is not an $α$-point. For $q=2$ we study the $45$ blocks of $\mathcal{D}$ inside a hyperplane $H$. Call a $5$-subspace of $H$ a $β$-flat if all its blocks pass through one point, its focal point. We show that at least $41$ points of $H$ are not focal points of $β$-flats. Consequently $\mathcal{D}$ has at least $85$ non-$α$-points, at most $42$ $α$-points, and at most $22$ $α$-points in every hyperplane.

papers.title: First-Order Entropic Sampling of Words with Prescribed Letter Counts in Linear Time
papers.abstract: We sample, exactly and uniformly, a word of length n over the alphabet {0, . . . , r} in which the letter j occurs a prescribed positive number k j of times, from a source of fair random bits. Every exact sampler reads on average at least H = log 2 (___ n k0,...,kr )___ bits. We give a sampler that reads on average at most H fresh bits, whatever r and the counts, and that performs O(n) bit operations on average over every fixed alphabet, in a bit-RAM in which a memory access costs O(1) while arithmetic is charged bit by bit. Both bounds are optimal: the first one to first order, the second one up to a constant factor, since writing the output already costs $Θ$(n). The sampler writes the word as a Huffman tree of independent binary words, and samples each of them in one of two ways. Binary words with few ones are generated by random insertions; the rank of each inserted letter among its copies, which the Fisher-Yates shuffle generates for nothing, is uniform and independent of the word, and is given back to a recycling source of uniform integers, where it pays for the next insertions. Binary words with many ones are generated by MergeShuffle driven by blocks of $Θ$(log n) bits of entropy; a block is decoded by locating only its ones when the minority letter is rare, and otherwise, its number of ones being concentrated, by a precomputed table of the blocks of typical type, of size O( $\sqrt$ n log 4 n), the rare atypical blocks being decoded slowly.

papers.title: Centimetre-sized meteoroids from the active asteroid (3200) Phaethon: lunar impact flashes during the 2018 and 2025 Geminids
papers.abstract: Centimetre-sized meteoroids released by the active asteroid (3200) Phaethon, parent of the Geminid meteor shower, probe the ejection of refractory material from a comet-asteroid transition object and the age of the stream; lunar impact flashes (LIFs) are the only ground-based technique that samples this size range. We determine the impact flux, mass and size distributions, and expected crater sizes of Geminid meteoroids on the Moon from campaigns at the 2018 and 2025 maxima, and test the stability of the centimetre-sized population over seven years. Both campaigns used the Nihon University 0.40 m "GUNDAM" telescope with CMOS video cameras at 60 fps, with candidates validated at independent stations; a common aperture-photometry pipeline calibrated in the Cousins R band gave peak magnitudes to 0.1-0.25 mag. Eleven LIFs were detected in 3.3 h in 2018 and nine in 2.2 h in 2025, all with Geminid probabilities of 0.87-0.96. With monitored areas measured on the video frames, the campaigns give consistent fluxes of $4.2\times10^{-7}$ and $5.2\times10^{-7}$ km$^{-2}$ h$^{-1}$ (merged: $4.6\times10^{-7}$ km$^{-2}$ h$^{-1}$). For a luminous efficiency of $1.4\times10^{-3}$ the impactors have masses of 10-320 g, diameters of 1.8-5.9 cm, and predicted crater rim diameters of 2-5 m. The combined sample gives a maximum-likelihood mass index $s=1.76\pm0.17$ and a population index $r=2.0\pm0.3$, markedly shallower than the NELIOTA all-flash values; a single power law with this slope connects the Global Meteor Network millimetre flux to the LIF centimetre flux. The Geminid stream delivers an excess of large particles relative to the sporadic background, consistent with an asteroidal origin, and its stable centimetre-sized flux over seven years constrains stream-formation models with ages of $2\times10^3$-$2\times10^4$ yr.

papers.title: Atomistic insight into defect-mediated boron redistribution and high-temperature strengthening in TiAl alloys
papers.abstract: Boron (B) microalloying can effectively refine microstructures of as-cast TiAl alloys and regulate their mechanical properties. Yet, how dilute B exists in TiAl and interacts with defects and how these interactions govern high-temperature deformation remain elusive. Here, we systematically elucidate defect-mediated B redistribution in TiAl alloys and its consequences for their deformation using hybrid grand-canonical Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics simulations augmented with a newly developed high-fidelity machine-learning potential. As a typical product of B microalloying, borides are markedly stiffer than the TiAl matrix and act as brittle reinforcing phases, while borides/matrix interfacial adhesion depends on surface termination and stacking sequence. In the bulk, interstitial B tends to be trapped at Ti-rich octahedral sites by high migration barriers but can kinetically evolve into substitutional dopants upon approaching Al vacancies. Increased tensile stress and vacancy concentration further promote B enrichment in the bulk. B is enriched at semi-coherent $γ/α_2$ boundaries and preferentially partitions into the $α_2$ phase. In polycrystalline TiAl, B accumulates primarily in disordered regions, raising the average flow stress by 9.4% at 1 at.% B and 900 K. This strengthening is accompanied by reduced shear strain accumulation. Simulated microstructural evolution and stacking-fault energetics indicate that B impedes dislocation glide via local pinning and suppresses deformation twinning, thereby increasing resistance to plastic deformation. By linking solute redistribution to defect interactions and deformation, these findings establish an atomistic framework for understanding and designing high-performance alloys based on interstitial solutes.

papers.title: The sharp mass threshold for the three-dimensional Riesz liquid-drop model near the Coulomb exponent
papers.abstract: We determine the exact mass threshold of the three-dimensional liquid-drop model with repulsive kernel $|x-y|^{-s}$ in a two-sided neighborhood of the Coulomb exponent $s=1$. The infimum is attained precisely for $0<m\le\mstar$, with balls as the unique minimizers up to translation and null sets. Here $\mstar$ is the mass at which one ball and two equal balls at infinite separation have the same energy. We compute the first-order variation of this threshold at $s=1$. For $s>1$, a diameter bound proportional to the mass supplies a lower bound on the averaged planar slicing integral and yields a uniform mass bound. The resulting compactness and a uniform quadratic energy gap for finite-perimeter sets close in measure to a ball allow us to transfer the Coulomb classification to nearby exponents. At $m=\mstar$, every minimizing sequence has a subsequence asymptotic in measure to single balls or pairs of equal balls with diverging separation, with both alternatives realized by minimizing sequences. For $\mstar<m\le3\mstar/2$, only the separated pair occurs and the infimum is twice the energy of a half-mass ball. We also obtain the first-order change in interaction energy with respect to the exponent along subsequences of near-minimizers as $s\to1$ and $m\to m_*(1)$.

papers.title: Draft Forcing: Target-guided Speculative Drafting and Learned Verifier for Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion models enable streaming synthesis chunk by chunk, yet invoking the large model for every chunk remains costly. While chunk-level speculative decoding can offload chunks to a lightweight draft model, existing approaches suffer from two limitations: (1) an off-the-shelf draft diverges from the target's trajectory, compounding errors in history; and (2) they either omit verification or rely on costly post-decode aesthetic scores rather than verifying consistency against the target. We address both with Draft Forcing, a framework coupling target-guided drafting with an on-policy trained verifier. Specifically, to align the draft for high acceptance, we opt for feature-level drafting, conditioning it on multi-layer target hidden states persisted from committed chunks, whose outputs are pushed to match target trajectories with multi-aspect losses. For verification, we propose an on-policy trained feature-space verifier predicting CDF-calibrated frame-wise relative RMSE against the target. It is trained on speculative rollouts as contexts anneal from random to inference-aligned mixtures, and gates proposals without VAE decoding. On the 14B Self-Forcing target, Draft Forcing achieves $1.63\times$ DiT and $1.57\times$ end-to-end speedups on VBench with minimal quality loss, and up to $1.93\times$ DiT ($1.82\times$ end-to-end) when combined with orthogonal KV compression. It generalizes to accelerate a streaming variant of MiniMax-H3, generating over $50\%$ draft frames with competitive quality.

papers.title: Tropical limits of holomorphic linking for toric hypersurfaces and points
papers.abstract: A holomorphic top form on a smooth hypersurface in a smooth projective toric variety has a unique meromorphic residue lift when the ambient dimension is at least two. Evaluating this lift at a point, relative to the logarithmic volume form, gives a complex linking number. For a one-parameter family of hypersurfaces and a normalised monomial residue, we prove that this function converges to the indicator of the corresponding tropical chamber. The convergence is uniform over compact sets disjoint from the tropical hypersurface, independently of the arguments of the point coordinates. When the chamber is nonempty and its index is an interior lattice point, the limit is the classical linking number of the oriented chamber boundary with the limiting logarithmic point. A plane cubic illustrates both this interpretation and its failure on a tropical wall.

papers.title: TAED: Trajectory-Aligned Encoder--Decoder Distillation for Detection Transformers
papers.abstract: Distilling localization knowledge into compact detection transformers (DETRs) requires consistent teacher-student query correspondence across decoder layers. However, in DETRs with encoder-based query selection, the teacher and student select top-K proposals independently. Same-rank queries can originate from different spatial locations and correspond to different objects, making rank-based layer-wise supervision unreliable. To address this problem, we propose Trajectory-Aligned Encoder-Decoder Distillation (TAED), a framework for knowledge transfer between DETRs of different capacities. Encoder feature distillation matches normalized multi-scale features to strengthen student representations and increase the number of teacher-student query pairs from the same encoder locations. Source-indexed query alignment pairs native queries from the same encoder locations and retains pairs associated with the same object for which the teacher provides reliable and more accurate final localization than the student. Trajectory-aligned localization distillation maintains these correspondences and uses teacher proposals and corresponding decoder-layer box predictions to guide student refinement, without introducing additional queries. On COCO, TAED improves DINO-R18 and two-stage Deformable DETR-R18 by 2.5 and 1.7 AP, respectively. Further gains on D-FINE and ECDet demonstrate applicability to recent real-time DETRs at no additional inference cost.

papers.title: Verifiable On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become a powerful approach for improving language-model reasoning, but its supervision is inherently sparse: a sequence-level verifier reward is propagated only through sampled trajectories and provides no direct signal for alternative actions. On-policy distillation (OPD) offers a complementary form of supervision by providing dense teacher feedback over the full next-token distribution, but this signal is not grounded in verified task outcomes. Simply co-optimizing the two objectives does not couple these signals: verifier feedback remains sparse and does not inform the dense teacher supervision. We introduce Verifiable On-Policy Distillation (VOPD), which transfers sparse verifier feedback into dense, verifier-grounded supervision. Our key observation is that the implicit-reward view of OPD places teacher supervision and verifier feedback in a common reward space while retaining a reward signal available for every next-token action. Under this view, VOPD projects verifier preference onto the teacher's implicit-reward direction and Rao--Blackwellizes the resulting signal over the full vocabulary, propagating verifier-grounded supervision to actions that were never sampled. The resulting objective can also be interpreted as adaptively extrapolating the distillation target according to teacher--verifier agreement. Across two teacher--student configurations and eight mathematical reasoning benchmarks, VOPD consistently improves both final performance and learning efficiency over vanilla OPD and other on-policy distillation baselines. Our code is available at https://github.com/juntongshi48/VOPD.

papers.title: Conservative Rupture Force Relating Co-seismic Rupture and Afterslip Process
papers.abstract: The post-seismic phase plays a crucial role in the earthquake cycle by releasing co-seismic stress and reshaping the fault-zone stress field. Traditionally, the relationship between afterslip and co-seismic slip is made by the ratio of their respective moment ($R_M$). However, in this study, we perform numerical and theoretical analyses to reveal that $R_M$ is inherently unstable. To quantify the afterslip, we first introduce an inter-seismic "equilibrium state" as a reference from which the pure afterslip is separated, while the afterslip releases the co-seismic stress loading over the velocity-strengthening region after correcting for this equilibrium state. To define the relationship between co- and afterslips, we propose a novel physical quantity termed the "conservative rupture force" (CRF), which is defined as the area integration of co-seismic stress drop. The CRF is equal to the area integration of stress loading over an infinite fault plane as well as the area integration of afterslip stress release over an infinite time and fault plane. This relationship holds for both full-space and half-space faults. We derive a dimensionless parameter as the ratio between afterslip and co-seismic CRFs as $R_F$. We also propose a strategy to derive such a factor with given co-seismic and afterslip models. We demonstrate that after correcting for the spatial partitioning of stress release, $R_F$ converges to one in an infinite time. This strategy is applied to the 2015 Mw 7.8 Gorkha earthquake, and we find that afterslips released 30% of coseismic stress loading over 5.5 years after the mainshock, while a large portion of the fault plane remained locked. The introduction of the equilibrium state and CRF offers a fresh quantitative view to understand relationships between inter-, co- and post-seismic fault slips.

papers.title: The $H^p$-Corona theorem on bounded pseudoconvex domains with $C^2$ boundary
papers.abstract: For $0<p\le2$, we solve the $H^p$-Corona problem on bounded pseudoconvex domains $Ω\Subset\mathbb C^n$ with $C^2$ boundary, obtaining the bound $C_Ωδ^{-q-1}|\logδ|$, where $q=\min\{n,m-1\}$ and $m$ is the number of generators. The range of $p$ is sharp even on a bounded smooth pseudoconvex domain admitting a smooth plurisubharmonic defining function and having only one weakly pseudoconvex boundary point.

papers.title: Free-boundary minimal varifolds I: zero boundary mass
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a $k$-varifold in a compact Riemannian manifold $M^n$ with smooth nonempty boundary, where $2 \le k < n$. Assume that $V$ is stationary with free boundary and almost minimizing modulo two in every sufficiently small relative annulus about each point of $M$. We prove that $V$ is integral and that the trace of the boundary second fundamental form on $T_x V$ vanishes at $\|V\|$-almost every boundary point. On all of $M$, the first variation is $δV = ν\,σ$, where $ν$ is the outward unit normal and $σ$ is a nonnegative measure on $\partial M$ singular with respect to $\|V\|$. A strict sign for the trace on all tangent $k$-planes at each boundary point forces zero boundary mass. For hypersurfaces in ambient dimensions three through seven, strict mean convexity gives smoothness and proper embeddedness. In every bounded smooth Euclidean domain $Ω$, we obtain $\|V\|(Ω) \ge c_{Ω,k}\|V\|(\overlineΩ)$ with $c_{Ω,k} > 0$. For smooth connected free-boundary minimal submanifolds in $\overlineΩ$, assuming a volume bound and a common annular almost minimizing condition at a fixed scale, then their first Dirichlet eigenvalues uniformly bounded above.

papers.title: Dark matter mass fraction in axion stars
papers.abstract: QCD axion dark matter is fragmented into small mass miniclusters of high density. With the natural parameters of miniclusters, the time for Bose-Einstein condensation is less than the age of the Universe, which leads to the formation of Bose stars inside these structures. Recently, the problem of the subsequent growth of Bose stars was solved analytically (Dmitriev et al, Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 091001 (2024)). We use this solution to determine present day mass fraction of dark matter in Bose stars and their mass function.

papers.title: Accuracy Is Not Evidence: Measuring and Training Evidence Dependence in Video Temporal Grounding
papers.abstract: In video temporal grounding, a correct interval can come from finding the event, answering blind or fitting one annotation style, and Recall at IoU scores them alike. We measure evidence dependence, how much the answer rests on the event's frames. Our fixed-answer audit edits either the frames inside the annotated interval or, as a placebo, as many frames elsewhere in the same video, and compares the two drops in the annotated answer's likelihood. Supervised fine-tuning and three public checkpoints trained with IoU-reward reinforcement learning raise the accuracy of Qwen2.5-VL-7B by 9 to 20 points, partly by answering blind and by fitting one annotation. Yet their answers rest on the event no more than the base model's, and the same holds for IoU-reward training on our data at the audit's frame rate. This comparison is a difference of the model's own likelihoods, so we can train on it. A placebo contrast and a bound on the placebo drop rule out learning to react to any edit. With them, evidence dependence rises in all five base models we train, and the weight on clean supervision controls how much. Added to IoU-reward training, the objective raises evidence dependence while keeping the accuracy gain. Masking the event's frames makes the trained models decline or miss the event more often than their base; masking as many other frames does not. The dependence moves to another event when the query names it, and holds on a second dataset and under patch scrambling, an edit never used in training.

papers.title: Weighted Flow Time Does Not Admit Constant-Competitive Randomized Algorithms
papers.abstract: We study online preemptive scheduling on a single machine with the objective of minimizing the total weighted flow time. Bansal and Chan (SODA 2009) showed that no deterministic online algorithm is $O(1)$-competitive for this problem. We show that no randomized online algorithm is $O(1)$-competitive against an oblivious adversary either. This settles the remaining case of the long-standing question whether the problem admits an $O(1)$-competitive online algorithm. Quantitatively, every randomized online algorithm has a competitive ratio in $Ω(\min\{\log\log W,\log\log\log\min\{P,D,n\}\})$, where $n$ is the number of jobs and $W$, $P$, and $D$ are the ratios of the largest to the smallest job weight, size, and density (weight divided by size), respectively. The lower bound also holds with high probability, with the same asymptotic dependence on the instance parameters. For every $ρ\ge1$ and every randomized online algorithm, there is an instance on which the cost of the algorithm is at least $ρ$ times the optimal cost with probability at least $1-2^{-2^ρ}$. Both lower bounds hold even if the algorithm knows in advance the size and weight of every job in release order and, for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, every interarrival time up to a factor of $1+\varepsilon$.

papers.title: Local limit theorem for the Kemperman's oscillating walk
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the local probabilities of the so-called oscillating walk on the latttice Z; this class of discrete time Markov chains was introduced by Kemperman. Our main result is a local counterpart of the convergence of a properly rescaled oscillating walk towards the corresponding skew Brownian motion. In particular, we show that the approximation of local probabilities by the density of the limiting distribution may fail in the points which are not far from zero.

papers.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures IV-2: Obstructed and unobstructed foliated deformations
papers.abstract: We study foliated deformations of compact complex manifolds with dimension 1-foliations and codimension 1-foliations, and unfoldings of compact complex manifolds with codimension 1-foliations in terms of deformations of sections with classical examples in deformation theory of complex structures.

papers.title: Video Generalized Category Discovery
papers.abstract: Generalized Category Discovery (GCD) aims to categorize unlabeled data from both known and unknown classes using labeled data from only the known classes. While recent GCD methods have shown promise on static images, their performance degrades in videos due to temporal dynamics, larger intra-class variation, and the lack of temporal consistency in existing approaches. We introduce VideoGCD, a framework tailored for video action recognition under the GCD setting. Our method integrates (i) a partitioned Mixture-of-Experts module that encourages specialization for known and novel categories, (ii) a novel-class balancing loss to reduce bias toward known classes, and (iii) a temporal optimal transport loss that promotes consistent routing across frames. Experiments on three video benchmarks demonstrate that VideoGCD significantly improves performance over existing GCD methods, particularly on novel categories. Our findings highlight the importance of combining temporal modeling and expert specialization for video GCD.

papers.title: Spin-controlled thermophase and noise-optimized thermometry in multiorbital quantum dots
papers.abstract: Converting temperature differences into electrical signals underlies both thermoelectric energy conversion and thermometry, which is essential for managing heat in cryogenic quantum technologies. Superconducting circuits typically show a weak thermoelectric response, since their quasiparticle spectrum is nearly particle-hole symmetric. In a Josephson junction, a temperature difference can instead be converted into a superconducting phase difference in an open circuit. We investigate this thermophase effect in a setup where the junction consists of a two-orbital quantum dot with Rashba spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and Zeeman splitting. A second orbital near the superconducting coherence peaks supports quasiparticle transport over a broad gate range. Zeeman splitting can enhance the thermophase by suppressing pair transport, while spin-orbit hybridization shifts the orbital resonances and can reverse the sign of the response. We assess the junction as a phase-based thermometer using a noise budget that includes readout and current noise together with fluctuations of the orbital energies and the magnetic field. The optimal operating points do not maximize the thermophase but balance a large quasiparticle response against sensitivity to parameter fluctuations. Under experimentally motivated noise assumptions, we obtain projected noise-equivalent temperatures of order $10\,μ\mathrm{K}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$ and determine the range over which a linear calibration remains accurate. Gate-tunable quantum-dot junctions thus offer a phase-based route to sensing temperature differences in superconducting circuits at sub-kelvin temperatures.

papers.title: SafeRank-ReID: Candidate-Conditioned Re-Ranking under Identity Conflicts for Multimodal Person Re-Identification
papers.abstract: Multimodal Person Re-Identification (ReID) exploits complementary identity cues from different sensing modalities to mitigate the performance degradation caused by challenging imaging conditions. Existing methods typically estimate Modality Reliability at the query level, making it difficult to identify conflicting inputs that retain normal visual quality but correspond to an incorrect identity. Such inputs may receive high confidence, promote irrelevant gallery candidates, and lead to negative fusion. To address this issue, we propose SafeRank-ReID, a candidate-conditioned safe re-ranking framework for Multimodal Person Re-Identification (ReID). To capture the varying support of the same modality for different candidates, we introduce a candidate-conditioned evidence arbitration mechanism that integrates unimodal retrieval evidence, input quality, and cross-modal consistency to estimate trust and conflict logits for each modality-candidate pair. Together, these logits contribute to the normalized modality weights, allowing support strength to vary across modalities and candidates while reducing the contribution of potentially unreliable evidence. A candidate-set refinement module subsequently applies self-attention to jointly model candidate representations and predicts residual scores from their competitive relations, thereby refining the initial fused ranking. For fusion results that remain uncertain after refinement, a query-level fallback gate estimates an interpolation coefficient from the overall conflict level and cross-modal uncertainty, adaptively combining the fused scores with those of the most reliable unimodal branch. Experiments on RGBNT201 and MSVR310 show that SafeRank-ReID maintains competitive clean-input retrieval while improving robustness to Identity Conflicts across person and vehicle benchmarks.

papers.title: Dark and bright solitons in a multimodal lithium tantalate microresonator
papers.abstract: Bright-soliton and dark-pulse microcombs provide complementary outputs. Integrating both states in a single resonator would expand the operating capabilities of an integrated coherent source, but requires opposite group-velocity-dispersion (GVD) channels while reconciling localized interfamily interaction for dark-pulse formation with spectral isolation for independent bright-soliton pumping. Wavelength-addressed access to both states is achieved in a LiTaO$_3$ microring through two TE-like transverse mode families. The higher-order TE$_{10}$ family fulfills two distinct roles in different spectral regions. Within localized avoided-mode-crossing regions, mode-resolved spectroscopy implicates TE$_{10}$ in perturbing the normal-GVD TE$_{00}$ resonance sequence. Away from these regions, TE$_{10}$ retains anomalous GVD and remains spectrally isolated as an independently pumpable bright-soliton channel; at representative pump resonances, the closest resonance of the non-addressed family is separated by 75--192 loaded cavity linewidths. With the input polarization held fixed, pumping TE$_{00}$ and TE$_{10}$ resonances generates dark-pulse and bright-soliton microcombs, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first experimental realization of a dark-pulse microcomb in an integrated LiTaO$_3$ microring. These results establish transverse-mode-family engineering as a route to combining localized modal interaction with independent spectral addressing in a single microresonator.

papers.title: One Policy, Many Bodies: Cooperative Human-Object Interaction with Heterogeneous Teams
papers.abstract: Physics-based human-object interaction (HOI) has enabled multiple characters to cooperatively transport objects, but existing cooperative controllers largely assume homogeneous embodiments and predefined interaction tasks. We ask whether a single physics-based policy can enable cooperation across diverse embodiments, team compositions, and interaction skills. We present MorphHOI, a decentralised framework built on a key insight: effective heterogeneous cooperation requires a unified representation across embodiments while accounting for differences in their physical capabilities. To realise this insight, we introduce a canonical body interface that unifies observation and action spaces, together with an embodiment-conditioned transformer that adapts cooperative decisions to the physical capabilities of each agent and its teammates. To extend cooperation to new interaction skills, we reuse the learned cooperative policy through task-specific tokens and lightweight adaptation, preserving its original capabilities. Our framework achieves success rates of up to 96.7\% on seen embodiments, 95.6\% on unseen embodiments, and 91.4\% on novel payloads. Furthermore, the learned cooperation extends to diverse interaction skills with high success rates, including box carrying, transport on stairs, and waypoint following, while preserving previously acquired cooperative capabilities.

papers.title: Scaling limits for equivariant Szegő kernels near a singular point of the moment map and applications to Kähler reduction
papers.abstract: Suppose that a compact and connected Lie group acts holomorphically on a Hodge manifold, and that the action linearises to the associated Hermitian ample line bundle. Assume that zero is a singular value of the associated moment map. The spaces of global holomorphic sections of powers of the line bundle decompose over the finite dimensional irreducible representations of the group. The main goal of this paper is to study the scaling limits for equivariant Szegő kernels near a singular point of the moment map. As an application, we discuss the quantization of the singular reduced space: the behaviour of invariant sections along the singular strata, the failure of the asymptotic unitarity of the Guillemin--Sternberg map near the singular strata, and the number of invariant sections concentrated near a singular orbit.

papers.title: Seeing Together, Acting Apart: Shared Environmental Understanding for Multi-Robot Navigation
papers.abstract: Multi-robot embodied systems are typically designed to collaborate by coordinating actions, sharing trajectories, or learning joint policies. We ask a complementary question: can collaboration emerge before decision-making, by first building a shared understanding of the environment? We introduce Shared Environmental Understanding, a policy-agnostic representation that aggregates partial egocentric observations from multiple robots into a shared latent world model. This shifts collaboration from the policy space to the representation space, enabling decentralized decision-making with shared environmental context. To this end, we propose Shared Environment Encoding and Retrieval (SEER), a framework that organizes multi-robot observations into a shared memory, retrieves relevant context via spatio-temporal similarity, and encodes it using a predictive latent world model. The resulting representations are injected into downstream navigation agents as tokens. Experimental results demonstrate that SEER captures action-relevant environmental structure and consistently improves navigation performance across both specialized VLN agents and general vision-language model agents, while preserving single-agent capabilities.

papers.title: Optimal quantitative stability near the Coulomb fission threshold
papers.abstract: We study the optimal quadratic stability constant for the three-dimensional Coulomb liquid-drop energy at fixed volume, measured by the squared Fraenkel asymmetry. Let $M$ be the critical mass at which the energy of one ball equals the limiting energy of two infinitely separated balls of equal volume. We prove that, as $m$ approaches $M$ from below, the optimal constant satisfies $Λ(m)=(36π)^{1/3}(2^{1/3}-1)(1-m/M)+o(1-m/M)$. We further show that every almost optimal sequence with masses $m_n\to M$ from below is asymptotic in measure to a union of two equal-volume balls whose centers diverge. We also identify the corresponding perimeter and Coulomb-energy limits and give a necessary and sufficient criterion for almost optimality after rescaling to mass $M$. The proof combines a strict binding inequality for mass partitions, a local spectral gap at the critical ball, and a BV truncation argument for critical minimizing sequences. All results hold for arbitrary finite-perimeter competitors, without connectedness or boundary regularity assumptions.

papers.title: ConsisX: Cross-View Consistency Thinking in 3D for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models integrate visual perception and language understanding from vision-language models (VLMs) with action prediction for robotic manipulation. Although multi-view observations provide complementary scene information, VLMs model cross-view interactions based on 2D feature similarity, which can lead to physical inconsistency in the form of cross-view incorrect association between distinct entities and cross-view information fragmentation about the same entity. To address these challenges, we propose ConsisX, a novel VLA framework that integrates cross-view association and entity coherence to enable cross-view consistency thinking in 3D for physically consistent robotic manipulation. Specifically, Cross-View Association Modeling (CAM) is proposed to introduce cross-view spatial proximity constraints in a shared 3D space to reduce cross-view incorrect association. Entity Coherence Organization (ECO) is designed to organize cross-view local information into coherent 3D entity evidence, thereby addressing cross-view information fragmentation. Consistent Action Conditioning (CAC) is introduced to condition action prediction on task-relevant 3D entity evidence for cross-view consistent action execution. Experiments on 3 real-world manipulation tasks and 4 simulation benchmarks establish ConsisX as an effective and competitive framework for robotic manipulation.

papers.title: Robust Lateral String Stability and Error Attenuation for Heterogeneous Vehicle Platoons
papers.abstract: Keeping an entire vehicle platoon close to its planned path is essential for navigating road boundaries and obstacles safely. Followers may rely on predecessor information for lateral guidance, which couples their lateral dynamics and allows errors to propagate downstream. This paper develops a robust lateral string stability framework to study this propagation and achieve downstream error attenuation in heterogeneous platoons under varying longitudinal motion and local perturbations. Arc-length-based feedback linearization gives each vehicle the same nominal lateral error dynamics, with parameter uncertainty and external disturbances represented as local perturbations. We define robust $\mathcal L_2$ lateral string stability in terms of platoon-length-uniform error bounds and derive a sufficient condition for achieving it. Furthermore, we show that the same condition guarantees platoon-length-uniform $\mathcal L_\infty$ error bounds. For the considered control formulations, predecessor tracking (PT) can accumulate lateral errors, whereas desired-path tracking (DT) prevents this accumulation. We propose a learn-from-predecessor (LFP) strategy with explicit gains for downstream error attenuation and characterize how intervehicle perturbation differences limit this attenuation. Simulations validate the theoretical findings under vehicle heterogeneity, varying longitudinal motion, and local perturbations.

papers.title: Spatial dimensionality affects the convective thawing of permafrost
papers.abstract: Permafrost thaw is one of the major consequences of ongoing climate change, with potentially far-reaching implications for high-latitude and high-altitude environments. Because permafrost degradation is a subsurface phenomenon, its dynamics and future evolution are primarily investigated through numerical models. Yet, the role of groundwater convection in permafrost thawing is an underrepresented process. Here, we explore how the spatial dimensionality affects the simulation of permafrost thaw and heat transport within the thawed layer, known as the active layer. Using two- and three-dimensional (2D and 3D) simulations, with realistic parameter sets that enable convection, we show that permafrost thawing rate and heat transport are systematically slower in 2D than in 3D simulations. The ice-water interface develops spatial patterns that coincides with the underlying convective structures, with rising cold plumes and descending warm plumes shaping its morphology. These findings reveal a coupling between convective flow structures and the evolving geometry of the permafrost boundary, and highlight the importance of three-dimensional representations of subsurface heat transport for accurately capturing permafrost thaw dynamics in land-surface models.

papers.title: SPECTRA-RCWA: A Spectral Propagation Engine for Coupled-Wave Theory with Recursive Admittance
papers.abstract: Rigorous coupled-wave analysis (RCWA) is the standard full-wave solver for periodic metasurfaces, but every solve diagonalises a dense nonsymmetric matrix for each layer. Inverse design repeats this step for every wavelength, angle and polarisation of an objective. On a graphics processor it is the slow step, and its derivative fails where eigenvalues coincide or a diffraction order reaches cutoff. Here we introduce SPECTRA-RCWA, an RCWA forward and adjoint solver that never diagonalises the layer matrix. Each layer step uses three entire functions of the half-size layer matrix, evaluated by matrix products alone, and an admittance recursion, or scattering-matrix doubling for thick layers, keeps the evanescent orders stable. One adjoint field gives the gradient for every design value without a computational graph, and all solves of an objective run as one batch. For 144 solves with 578 x 578 layer matrices, the value and the gradient take 0.25 s on one graphics card, 218 times less than with a differentiable eigendecomposition code. The truncated-series solver TorchRDIT loses accuracy beyond a few tenths of a micrometre unless the user slices the layer; SPECTRA-RCWA keeps single-precision accuracy in layers several wavelengths thick with no setting changed and is 47 to 65 times faster at matched accuracy. Its single-precision gradient stays within 4e-5 of a double-precision reference at a cutoff, where eigendecomposition gradients are wrong by order one. A freeform metagrating designed in 3.4 min on a desktop processor deflects both polarisations by 65 degrees with a band-averaged efficiency of 75%.

papers.title: PinGround: Pinning Queries to Points for Parallel Grounding in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can localize through their text interface, grounding open-vocabulary objects, complex referring expressions, text lines and layout regions with strong semantic understanding. They write the boxes one after another as a single sequence, although the instances of a query, unlike the words of a sentence, form an unordered set with no sequential dependence. The number of decoding steps therefore grows with the number of instances, which makes dense scenes the most expensive. Decoding the instances in parallel avoids this growth, but streams that cannot see each other duplicate some instances and miss others. We propose \method, which writes a single point into each query as a spatial anchor and asks for the matching instance nearest to that point within a local radius, or \none. Given the image, the anchored queries are independent, so they are decoded in parallel as leaves of a prefix tree that shares the image and the query, and the model is trained on the same tree. Coarse-to-fine anchors refine only the regions where instances are found, duplicate suppression keeps one box per instance, and set-level reinforcement learning optimizes the set F1. Only the prompt and the attention mask change, not the architecture. On three different VLMs and 12 benchmarks covering detection, OCR, layout and referring, \method is at most 5.5 F1 below sequential decoding trained on the same data, while its speedup grows with instance density and reaches 21.9$\times$ on dense scenes.

papers.title: Impact of structured noise on bosonic quantum error correction
papers.abstract: Bosonic quantum error correction relies on an accurate description of single-photon loss dissipation using an ideal annihilation operator, under which correctable loss errors act equivalently on different logical code states. In realistic weakly nonlinear bosonic modes, however, coupling to a structured environment can render photon loss Fock-state dependent, thereby modifying the effective dissipation operator and deforming the associated error space. Here, we experimentally investigate this effect in a three-dimensional circuit quantum electrodynamics system. By injecting spectrally engineered environmental noise into a weakly nonlinear oscillator, we observe pronounced frequency selectivity in the measured Fock-state dynamics. While the long-time transition rates converge to the Markovian limit, the transient dynamics display distinctly non-Markovian behavior, in quantitative agreement with a second-order time-convolutionless theory. By applying narrowband noise to a binomially encoded logical qubit, we further demonstrate Fock-state-dependent dissipation channels that drive logical states beyond the nominally correctable error space. These results establish structured environmental noise as a mechanism for deforming photon-loss errors in weakly nonlinear bosonic systems and highlight the need to incorporate realistic, state-dependent dissipation into the design and characterization of bosonic quantum error correction.

papers.title: Sharp global well-posedness for the defocusing nonlinear wave equation outside a ball with radial data
papers.abstract: Let $Ω=\mathbb{R}^3\setminus\overline{B(0,1)}$ and $3<p<5$. We prove sharp global well-posedness of the defocusing Dirichlet boundary value problem of nonlinear wave equation with radial data in the critical space $\dot H^{s_c}_{D,\mathrm{rad}}(Ω)\times \dot H^{s_c-1}_{D,\mathrm{rad}}(Ω)$, where $s_c=\frac32-\frac{2}{p-1}$, thereby improve the result in \cite{XuYangYou2025}. The proof combines the distorted Fourier transform in \cite{LiSZ:NLS,XuYang2024} with the energy--Morawetz estimate by Dodson in \cite{DodsonCubic2018,Dodson2018}.

papers.title: The Stigmergic Index: A Biomimetic Edge Centrality for Spatial Network Analysis
papers.abstract: Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) is a family of metaheuristics inspired by the pheromone-based navigation of real ants, a decentralized mechanism often associated with shortest-path discovery. Over the past two decades, research has primarily focused on optimization tasks such as vehicle routing within a network. In this paper, we shift this perspective by using swarm intelligence to gather diagnostic information about the underlying network structure itself. Through decentralized exploration, we harness stigmergic dynamics to introduce a novel topological and behavioural metric: the Stigmergic Index. While sharing baseline structural properties with traditional betweenness centrality on simple grids, our index accounts for path polarization effects that can diverge from shortest-path-based assumptions.

papers.title: Dynamic Channel Gain Map Reconstruction via Object-Attached Gaussian Propagation
papers.abstract: Channel gain maps describe location-dependent propagation, but moving vehicles can change reception beyond their physical footprints. Reconstructing these changes requires connecting local object states to regional power. We consider a fixed transmitter and predefined receiver areas, with historical static and dynamic radio supervision and continuing delayed, noisy vehicle-state messages. We propose OA-GS, an object-attached Gaussian propagation model with a shared area correction. Each vehicle carries anisotropic kernels whose effective attributes are supplied by offline-calibrated templates and affine condition generators. Closed-form Gaussian integrals along finite propagation segments evaluate an effective attenuation model, while directional scattering terms account for additional power. These interactions modulate a learned static reference and contribute to regional channel gain. A shared multilayer perceptron then uses object, propagation, and receiver-area features to predict a bounded path-loss residual that compensates for errors in the compact propagation model. All learned parameters remain fixed during deployment, and reconstruction uses arrived vehicle messages without current-traffic radio measurements. In a fixed-scene ray-tracing study over four development traffic sequences and three initializations, OA-GS reduces map and strong-event dynamic-response root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) from 2.503 to 1.272 dB and from 5.965 to 3.563 dB, respectively, relative to a task-adapted GS-CG baseline receiving eight initial radio reports. The shared correction reduces strong-event dynamic-response error from 3.962 to 3.563 dB under the same propagation backbone, demonstrating the benefit of combining explicit propagation structure with learned regional correction.

papers.title: Endomorphism algebras of Drinfeld modules in special characteristic
papers.abstract: We classify the division algebras that occur as endomorphism algebras of Drinfeld modules of a given rank in special characteristic which cannot be defined over a finite field. The classification is in terms of the center of the algebra and its local invariants. Together with the known results in generic characteristic and over finite fields, this gives a complete description of the endomorphism algebras of Drinfeld modules of a given rank.

papers.title: HEART: Hierarchical Expert Adaptive Refinement Transformer for ECG Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Learning robust representations from electrocardiograms (ECGs) is challenging because repeated cardiac cycles coexist with subtle and sparse diagnostic cues in local morphology and rhythm-level context. Existing ECG foundation models commonly rely on Transformerbased patch encoders with uniformly shared dense refinement pathways, limiting adaptive processing across heterogeneous ECG tokens. We propose HEART (Hierarchical Expert Adaptive Refinement Transformer), an ECG foundation model that introduces stage-specific conditional expert refinement during self-supervised pre-training. HEART places a local-level MoE over patch-level representations before temporal contextualization and a global-level MoE over context-integrated token representations after self-attention. Token-level Top-1 routing allows different patches or contextual tokens within the same ECG to follow different expert pathways. On public ECG benchmarks, HEART achieves strong performance under both linear probing and fine-tuning, with particularly large frozen-encoder gains on PTB-XL Form and Rhythm (+6.76 AUROC points each over the strongest protocol-reproduced baseline). Routing analyses provide qualitative evidence of complementary local and global expert specialization. We release our code and pretrained models at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/HEART-5E9F.

papers.title: Anatomy of orbital and spin responses in GaAs and Si: Hall, inverse Faraday, and magneto-optical Kerr effects
papers.abstract: Magneto-optical signals in nonmagnetic semiconductors entangle spin and orbital contributions, both in angular-momentum generation and magneto-optical detection. We calculate these contributions for electron-doped GaAs and Si using density-functional theory, linear-response theory, and a second-order density-matrix treatment of the inverse Faraday effect. At small electron doping, the intrinsic orbital Hall conductivity exceeds its spin counterpart in magnitude, while the orbital contribution to light-induced magnetization dominates over broad photon-energy ranges. We show that orbital- and spin-resolved optical Hall and polar Kerr coefficients exhibit stronger sensitivity to orbital moments than to equal spin moments. This contrast reflects direct electric-dipole coupling to orbital motion versus spin-orbit-mediated coupling to spin polarization. Consequently, Si maintains a substantial orbital magneto-optical response despite its weak spin-orbit interaction. At probe energies of 1.5 eV in GaAs and 3.0 eV in Si, the magnitude of the Kerr rotation per unit orbital moment is approximately 5 and 13 times larger than that per unit spin moment, respectively. Combining the calculated Hall conductivities and Kerr coefficients with a phenomenological drift-diffusion model yields predominantly orbital edge signals for the assumed diffusion constants and relaxation lengths. These results indicate that optical detection of induced magnetization in doped semiconductors such as GaAs and Si can be dominated by orbital signals, and therefore cannot be interpreted solely in terms of spin polarization.

papers.title: Matter-decorated trumpets in double-scaled SYK
papers.abstract: In sine-dilaton gravity, the double trumpet, the wormhole amplitude without matter, is obtained by gluing two trumpets along a closed geodesic of discrete length and summing over this length. When the wormhole carries the propagator of a matter field of dimension $Δ$, joining the two asymptotic boundaries and crossing the neck, such a gluing is known only in the Jackiw--Teitelboim (JT) limit. We construct the gluing beyond JT in double-scaled SYK (DSSYK), the proposed boundary dual of sine-dilaton gravity, whose disk amplitudes it reproduces. In this context, we adopt the definition of the matter-decorated wormhole in terms of the ETH two-matrix model with Gaussian matter. We build matter-decorated trumpets from an end-of-the-world brane trace with a matter insertion, and prove that the wormhole is glued from them exactly, sector by sector in the number of chords through the neck, with a positive weight that accounts for the twists and windings of these chords and for the closed loops around the neck. Trumpets and weight are obtained in closed form, the former as transforms of Rogers polynomials, and we discuss the uniqueness of the construction. In the JT limit, both reproduce the known gluing separately, and not only in combination. In the classical limit, each trumpet takes the form expected in the bulk: a pure-gravity sine-dilaton trumpet dressed by the factor that a probe matter geodesic contributes at its boundary.

papers.title: Degree 2 foliations on $\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ with only saddle-node and nilpotent singularities
papers.abstract: We classify all foliations of degree $2$ on $\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ having only saddle-node or nilpotent singularities up to projective equivalence. To do so, we use the bijection between such foliations and their polar configurations stated by Campillo and Olivares~\cite{CO}. We also show that three families of the found foliations admit no algebraic invariant curve.

papers.title: Periodic orbit asymptotics and dynamical zeta functions for smooth surface diffeomorphisms
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of a closed surface $M$, and let $H$ be a closed homoclinic class with topological entropy $h=h_{\mathrm{top}}(f|H)>0$ and homoclinic period $\ell$. We prove that \[ \forall\,0<χ<h,\qquad \lim_{\ell\mid n,\;n\to\infty} \frac{\#\mathrm{Per}_χ(n,H)}{e^{nh}}=\ell, \] where $\mathrm{Per}_χ(n,H)$ denotes the saddle points in $H$ of least period $n$ whose Lyapunov exponents lie outside $[-χ,χ]$. We also prove exponential remainders for the class and global counting formulas. As a result, for every $0<χ<h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$, the Artin--Mazur zeta function of all $χ$-hyperbolic periodic orbits, including sinks and sources, extends meromorphically beyond its disk of convergence. Its leading poles are determined by the periods of the ergodic maximal measures. This answers the meromorphic continuation question of Buzzi.

papers.title: Topology-Prior-Guided Regional Latent Dynamics for Transient Structural Response Prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting the transient nonlinear responses of complex engineering structures remains challenging due to large finite element meshes, heterogeneous structural components, and history-dependent mechanical behavior. This study proposes a topology-prior-guided regional latent dynamics (TPLD) surrogate model that combines physically structured regional representations with dynamics-aware latent learning for full-field time-history prediction. Based on mesh topology and engineering priors, structural responses are encoded into spatially coupled regional latent variables through region-aware feature extraction and topology-constrained interactions. An auxiliary one-step prediction task enhances latent-space dynamical predictability by introducing state-transition supervision. A load-conditioned spatiotemporal Mamba model then predicts regional latent trajectories by integrating temporal causal scanning and bidirectional spatial scanning, while a shared coordinate-conditioned decoder reconstructs full-field nodal responses. The framework is evaluated on three finite element datasets: a parametric stiffened panel, a partitioned pressure impact plate, and a Toyota Yaris full-vehicle crash model. The relative L2 errors for the three displacement components range from 4.00% to 8.21% on the stiffened panel and from 1.41% to 12.22% on the approximately 1.49-million-node vehicle model. On the BIW crash benchmark, TPLD achieves a relative L2 position error of 0.620%, representing a 30.7% reduction compared with the best-performing GeoTransolver configuration. Ablation studies demonstrate the advantages of topology-guided regional representations over global latent and learnable soft-slice alternatives, while auxiliary one-step prediction particularly improves the prediction of accumulated plastic strain.

papers.title: MirrorGuard: Defending LiDAR Perception against Passive Mirror Attacks
papers.abstract: Mirror-based LiDAR attacks passively redirect automotive LiDAR's beams to create phantom objects in the vehicle perception. Recent work has demonstrated that these attacks may cause vehicles to brake for a phantom where nothing stands. Every phantom return is a genuine time-of-flight measurement, so current spoofing defenses are not able to differentiate phantoms from real objects. We present MirrorGuard, a physics-informed defense that identifies and removes mirror-induced phantom returns before they affect downstream perception. MirrorGuard tests three consequences of the reflected path. Every phantom bearing crosses the mirror's finite aperture, its opaque surface blocks any direct return beyond it, and the two reflections off the mirror dim the phantom. MirrorGuard identifies a phantom by these cues over multiple scans and removes the reflected beams before it reaches any detector or occupancy grid. On real-world recordings of this attack, MirrorGuard removes 96.31% of the phantom's returns at 98.30% precision, with 99.99% of non-phantom returns untouched. In a closed loop with the CARLA driving simulator and the open-source stack (Autoware), a vehicle without the defense halts for an obstacle that is not present and a following car crashes into its rear. With MirrorGuard, no vehicle produces a halt or a crash. MirrorGuard runs at 59 ms mean per scan on a CPU and is a software-only solution that does not require new hardware or environmental training.

papers.title: Beyond Which: Where, How, and When in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models typically rely on vision-language model (VLM) features as the primary perceptual source for action prediction, showing strong generalization across diverse robotic manipulation tasks. Although VLM features can identify which entities are relevant to action prediction, precise manipulation also requires understanding where task-relevant entities are located within the spatial layout, how their geometric structure constrains physical interaction, and when spatial or geometric information should make a greater contribution to action prediction. To this end, we introduce {\mathcal{W}^{3}\mathcal{H}}-VLA to organize VLA perception and action prediction around which, where, how, and when. Specifically, {\mathcal{W}^{3}\mathcal{H}}-VLA retains VLM-based semantic entity perception which and further introduces spatial distance perception where and geometric structure perception how with adaptive spatial-geometric guidance when to enrich the perceptual information available for action prediction. Experiments across real-world settings and simulation benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and superior performance of {\mathcal{W}^{3}\mathcal{H}}-VLA.

papers.title: Uncovering Separable and Composable Skill Mechanisms in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Recent work has sought to localize the internal mechanisms underlying visual reasoning skills in vision-language models. These methods largely overlook separability and composability in both mechanism identification and evaluation. We propose separability and composability as two important desiderata for skill localization. Separability requires identified mechanisms to contribute primarily to their target skills while having limited effects on other skills, enabling precise diagnosis and targeted intervention. Composability requires skill mechanisms to be combinable to support complex tasks, allowing a small set of mechanisms to account for broader capabilities. In this work, we propose a multi-skill interpretability framework DISCO, built around these two properties. For identification, we propose Separable Head Selection, which selects skill-specific attention heads based on their contributions across skills. For evaluation, we are the first to design metrics for measuring separability and composability of identified heads. Extensive experiments on three VLMs and four fundamental visual reasoning skills demonstrate the effectiveness of DISCO. It achieves the highest separability, outperforming the strongest baseline by 24.80, 18.38, and 13.75 points across the three models, respectively, while also achieving the highest composability on all three models.

papers.title: Temporal Leakage Distorts the TGB Node Affinity Leaderboard: A Point-in-Time Audit
papers.abstract: Node affinity prediction in the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB) asks how a node's future interactions will be distributed over other nodes. On this task, methods that reuse past ground-truth labels often outperform temporal graph neural networks, and the state of the art builds on them. Such comparisons assume a point-in-time correct evaluation, in which a model receives only information available at prediction time. Drawing on as-of joins and bitemporal databases, we formalize this requirement by distinguishing when a label must be predicted, its query time, from when it is fully determined, its availability time, and we audit the four TGB node affinity datasets and their evaluation loop with model-agnostic tools. None of the four meets it. On three datasets, each label summarizes a single day about five days after its timestamp, not the documented following week, yet the loop feeds it back right after that timestamp; on the fourth, the loop processes the edges from which each label is computed before predicting it. Under a drop-in leakage-free protocol, every method whose inputs leak loses up to 17% of its NDCG@10, the advantage of past labels over the interaction stream nearly vanishes or reverses, and both the best configuration of the state of the art and the rankings change; a blend of training-free long-memory statistics, with weights fit on validation data, matches or exceeds the state of the art under both protocols. Point-in-time correctness should therefore be built into benchmarks, and our tools carry over to other benchmarks whose labels aggregate event streams over time windows.

papers.title: Face Is Not All You Need: MIME Benchmark for Incomplete Multimodal Emotion Recognition
papers.abstract: Multimodal Emotion Recognition (MER) is a fundamental task in multimedia understanding, where state-of-the-art methods have achieved prominent success relying on the assumption of complete, well-aligned multimodal inputs. However, real-world unconstrained scenarios often suffer from unpredictable modality degradation and information loss, leading to catastrophic performance collapse of existing MER models that heavily depend on facial cues as the core inference anchor. However, few systematic works evaluate model robustness under diverse, fine-grained incomplete settings, as prior works are limited to coarse-grained full-modality removal and neglect interpretable analysis of emotional reasoning. To bridge this gap, we formally define the Incomplete Multimodal Emotion Recognition (IMER) task, which benchmarks model generalization and robustness under multi-grained modality and emotional information loss. We further construct MIME, a dedicated IMER benchmark with 2,000 video segments covering realistic fine-grained facial-detail degradation, severe facial degradation, and extreme full-modality loss, surpassing the limited coarse-grained settings of prior works. We also propose the Chain of Emotion (CoE) analysis paradigm with tailored metrics to dissect the fine-grained emotional cue perception and reasoning process of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). Extensive experiments on seven mainstream MLLMs reveal that body language and scene context act as critical compensatory mechanisms under facial degradation, while a pronounced gap exists between models' basic visual perception ability and high-level cognitive reasoning. Our work provides a focused evaluation platform and actionable insights for advancing robust multimodal emotion recognition. Our dataset and code are public at https://yuxinokk.github.io/MIME.

papers.title: MMMem: Self-Improving Agents with Task-Aware Multimodal Experience Consolidation
papers.abstract: AI agents accumulate conversations, images, and documents through long-term interactions with users. Answering later questions often requires connecting evidence across these records, yet the resulting understanding is rarely retained, allowing mistakes to recur on related questions. Existing multimodal memory methods largely focus on storing and retrieving records, with limited mechanisms for learning from completed tasks and consolidating task-specific experience. We therefore propose MMMem, a task-aware multimodal memory framework that extracts and consolidates experience from completed tasks through four complementary strategies. First, source-linked multi-view memory organizes original text, images, and rendered pages alongside generated scene images that combine clues across records for retrieval. Second, source-generated tasks support knowledge alignment at two levels: warm-up consolidates source knowledge into task-relevant experiences in external memory, while self-training adapts the model's parametric knowledge to task demands. Third, the same vision-language model distills completed tasks into experiences that record the task context, conclusion, and support links. Finally, task-aware retrieval recalls source views and relevant experiences for answering and verification, while source-supported reuse guides long-term retention. Across three memory benchmarks and two vision-language readers, MMMem outperforms eight baselines. With Qwen3.5-9B, MMMem achieves relative gains of 36.9%, 17.6%, and 15.2% over the best-performing baselines on LoCoMo, Mem-Gallery, and LooGLE v2, respectively. Ablations show consistent gains from training and memory warm-up, while case studies illustrate how individual components work in practice.

papers.title: A statistical measure of trust in generative AI
papers.abstract: Trustworthiness is a crucial issue for generative AI, as modern models can produce convincing and confident responses even when their outputs are incomplete, unsupported, or wrong. The frequent absence of ground-truth knowledge or labels complicates verification of generative AI outputs. To address this issue, we propose a trustworthiness framework grounded in model-internal confidence calibrated against an external expert reference. We estimate per-token trustworthiness of a student generative model as the statistical typicality of each generated token relative to an expert model's distribution, where the expert is used as a distributional reference rather than as a source of factual verification labels. To this end, we introduce an AI ontology calibrator that leverages the student model's internal latent features and token-level output statistics to compute expert-reference acceptance scores. Combined with traditional token-level confidence, entropy, and perplexity statistics, calibrator scores yield a compact set of $15$ response-level indicators for correctness classification.
