Attribution concerns attackers who do not erase that fingerprint, which a random Pauli layer would do cheaply. Each result is stated within one of four verifier classes. For per-unit verifiers, which never couple two seal units and hold no untouched reference, the sample separation is asymptotically exponential, by reduction from a known lower bound for one parity of strength up to 1/3. On ten tampered cells it is proved to be at least \qnProvedUniformMin-fold against non-adaptive stabilizer probes and observed in simulation at \qnEoneRatioFine-fold. Against an implemented self-referencing strategy the simulated gain is about twice the inverse squared strength. The value also depends on the attack: destroying the untouched cells makes the reference necessary, whereas copying errors exposes the fingerprint to reference-free probes. We derive the vault's qubit inventory and simulate a seal requirement curve: ten times more seal noise lengthens the seal's lifetime \qnSealLifeGainFive-fold at \qnSealRhoFive{} times the attribution cost at $r=10$.

papers.title: Second Moment Penny Packings via Rolling Spaces
papers.abstract: We solve the unrestricted minimum second moment problem for six unit disks in the plane by proving that the minimum is \(29/3\) attained uniquely up to isometry and relabelling by one disk together with five of its six neighbours in the triangular lattice. The realised contacts themselves define the space of admissible motions, while the directions preserving those contacts to first order define the rolling space consisting of motions whose relative velocities have zero normal component at every realised contact. Together, these spaces lead to an exact tangent cone formula and to a criterion by which a strictly positive centroidal contact balance, combined with rolling rigidity, implies strict local minimality modulo Euclidean motions. Our method recovers the classical five disk minimum \(34/5\) of Graham and Sloane, previously the largest unrestricted case known exactly. Geometric reductions and a graph census reduce the global search to finitely many contact graph classes. Exact analysis and validated interval arithmetic then exclude competing configurations, establishing the global bounds and uniqueness. Our method allows us to pass from putative lattice extremisers to unrestricted optimality.

papers.title: The Temporal Residual: Fast and Effective Retrofitting of Latent Feedback into Pretrained Language Models
papers.abstract: A transformer language model computes a deep hidden state for every token but uses it only to sample that token. Existing latent-feedback designs, which feed hidden states back across tokens, are mostly built in during pretraining and gain little when added to a pretrained model. We introduce the temporal residual, a second residual stream that every sublayer reads and writes and that is carried from each token to the next. It adds 2,752 parameters to a 4.2B-parameter model and starts exactly at the pretrained network. Retrofitted onto Qwen3.5-4B-Base with 5B tokens of training, it beats a standard model trained on the same data by 7, 13 and 5 points on AIME 2024, AIME 2025 and AMC 2023, writes shorter solutions, and stays ahead at matched training compute. The separate stream matters: prior designs that feed state into the existing stream recover at most 40% of the gain when retrofitted. Validation loss can mislead: the recipe with the lowest loss gains nothing at decoding. Trained with filler tokens in place of reasoning, the model reasons in its hidden state: its GSM8K accuracy with no visible reasoning rises from 21% to 40%, and falls back when the carried state is zeroed.

papers.title: Construction of a Deployable Closure Model for the Transport of Turbulence Dissipation Rate with Hard-Constrained Physics-Informed Machine Learning
papers.abstract: We present a hard-constrained physics-informed machine learning (PIML) method for constructing a deployable closure model for the transport of turbulence dissipation rate. The framework is built from modules, each performing a single task. The closure module represents the closure with a small network, while the state module represents the flow state during training. The closure network is coupled to the state network through the governing equation residuals. This coupling allows us to learn the closure without using reference closure values as training targets. The coordinate module learns monotone input coordinates that help both networks resolve sharp changes. Within the network architecture, the boundary condition (BC) module imposes boundary values exactly using the Theory of Functional Connections, and the realizability module keeps the closure realizable. We study decaying homogeneous isotropic turbulence (HIT) and learn $ψ$, the closure function governing dissipation rate decay, from trajectories obtained in experiments and direct numerical simulations. Here, the state module is a Deep Operator Network (DeepONet), the BC module imposes the initial state and the closure's low and high Reynolds number limits, and the realizability module ensures growth of the Taylor microscale. The framework reduces the root mean square of the closure variation across ten random seeds by about 95\% relative to the unconstrained model over the training and held-out range. The deployed 18-parameter closure network requires only the Taylor scale Reynolds number $Re_{λ_g}$ and can be exported as a standalone C function.

papers.title: Lie-Poisson Formulation of Dissipative Spin Hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: Covariance and the second law cannot fix how fluid flow couples to spin, since reversible couplings produce no entropy. We show that the spin commutation relations and the Poincaré algebra fix these couplings. Reversibly, a flow exerts no torque on the spin: its magnitude per particle is conserved, its direction is Fermi--Walker transported, and spin--shear couplings reflect a deforming triad. The magnitude changes only through higher multipoles, as in spinor condensates, or dissipation, whose first-order spin--shear coupling reorients the spin away from the vorticity above a critical shear rate.

papers.title: PACT: Plan-Action Consistency Training by Preserving Correct Plans and Repairing Actions in GUI Agents
papers.abstract: GUI agents can formulate a correct immediate plan in their reasoning yet emit an action that fails to execute it, creating an execution gap. This recurring mismatch undermines reliable task completion, as a single execution error can derail a multi-step workflow. In outcome-supervised reinforcement learning, broadcasting a negative response-level advantage across all generated tokens risks penalizing valid planning together with erroneous execution. To address this credit-assignment conflict, we introduce PACT (Plan-Action Consistency Training), a training framework that combines reference-aligned plan protection and plan-aligned action repair without altering the original scalar action reward. Using annotated reference actions to identify execution gaps, PACT protects the verified plan by masking negative policy-gradient contributions across its token span. Keeping the generated reasoning unchanged as context, it then favors the reference action over the emitted erroneous action through a preference surrogate with stop-gradient pair weights. Compared with the outcome-only baseline, PACT raises AndroidWorld task success from 60.34% to 68.97% (+8.63 pp), while improving rule-based plan-action consistency on AndroidControl High from 83.71% to 89.74% (+6.03 pp). Adapting PACT to desktop agents also improves task success from 40.92% to 44.17% (+3.25 pp) on the full 369-task OSWorld benchmark. Together, these results establish PACT as an effective credit-assignment framework for bridging execution gaps and improving task completion across mobile and desktop GUI environments.

papers.title: As Student Rollouts Continue, Visual Backdoors Keep Growing
papers.abstract: Conventional knowledge distillation can facilitate the propagation of backdoors from teacher models to student models. However, how this risk manifests in On-Policy Distillation (OPD) remains insufficiently studied. OPD has recently emerged as an important post-training paradigm for Vision-Language Models (VLMs). Unlike traditional offline distillation, OPD does not require teacher-generated responses. Instead, it uses the teacher's probability distributions to supervise response trajectories generated online by the student. Since the initial student model typically generates benign responses and receives no explicit supervision from malicious target responses, OPD appears to offer some inherent resistance to backdoor propagation. In this paper, we challenge this intuition and reveal a more subtle risk of visual backdoor propagation in OPD. Through experiments across multiple model families and datasets, together with theoretical analysis, we identify three main findings. First, unlike the relatively gradual propagation observed in traditional offline distillation, backdoors rarely emerge in OPD at low poisoning ratios. However, the attack success rate rapidly approaches 100% once a critical threshold is exceeded. Second, backdoor propagation does not depend on explicit malicious responses. Instead, it is driven by the continuous accumulation of anomalous probability mass assigned by the teacher. Finally, based on these findings, we propose a novel trigger design that enables visual backdoor propagation with zero explicit trigger injection. These findings further reveal an overlooked mechanism of backdoor propagation in OPD and highlight its potential security risks.

papers.title: TeleChat to Xing4: Advancing Frontier Agentic Models on Domestic Chips and Frameworks
papers.abstract: We present Xing 4, a series of large language models that extends the TeleChat lineage through coordinated advances in model architecture and training infrastructure on Ascend. This report describes the design principles and systems engineering behind the series, spanning architecture selection, large-scale pretraining, and reasoning and agentic post-training. We study how sparse activation, attention design, model depth and width, and speculative decoding balance model capacity with computation, memory access, and execution overhead. Our pretraining infrastructure builds on MindSpore HyperParallel, combining topology-aware hybrid sharding, efficient distributed optimizer execution, and coordinated management of long-sequence workloads and activation memory. CPU affinity and core isolation further reduce host scheduling interference. Together, these mechanisms support the pretraining of a 285B-parameter model on 8,192 Ascend 910C cards, providing a concrete setting for the architectural and systems studies. For post-training, we introduce TeleGym, a unified agent execution platform that connects execution, evaluation, and trajectory construction to policy optimization. Disaggregated asynchronous execution, bounded oversampling, and partial rollout accommodate heterogeneous task durations while preserving trajectory continuity across policy updates. Together, these advances establish an Ascend-oriented training foundation for the continued development of Xing 4 across model scales and increasingly demanding reasoning and agent workloads.

papers.title: Boundedness of a Schur multiplier on the Schatten p-class, $1 < p \neq 2 < \infty$, does not imply complete boundedness
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a bounded Schur multiplier on the Schatten class $S_p(\ell_2)$ which is not completely bounded when $1<p\ne 2<\infty$, which confirms Pisier's conjecture (1998).

papers.title: Perturbative Recovery of Stabilizer-Subspace Correlations for Quantum Computational Chemistry
papers.abstract: Stabilizer-based subspace methods can substantially reduce the quantum resources required for electronic structure calculations, but the resulting projection neglects Hamiltonian couplings to configurations outside the retained subspace. In this work, we introduce Stabilizer-Subspace Perturbation Theory (SSPT) to recover the associated correlation contributions, using the Contextual Subspace Variational Quantum Eigensolver (CS-VQE) as a representative application. The central idea is to exploit the Pauli terms eliminated by stabilizer projection as perturbative operators that generate an external manifold from the optimized reference state. Their energetic contributions are evaluated using an Epstein-Nesbet-type second-order correction or a resolvent-based formulation that retains couplings within the external space. By exploiting the factorized structure of the stabilizer-constrained reference state, the required matrix elements can be evaluated through Pauli expectation values on the reduced contextual register without explicitly reconstructing the full-space wave function. Molecular benchmarks demonstrate substantial reductions in projection-induced energy errors, allowing chemical precision to be achieved with fewer contextual qubits in several cases. These results establish stabilizer-guided perturbation theory as a promising strategy for improving the accuracy of resource-efficient quantum chemistry calculations.

papers.title: SkillBuffBench: Measuring What Agent Skills Contribute across Harnesses, Models, Skill Access Modes and Memory
papers.abstract: Agent Skills, file-based packages of procedural knowledge that a coding agent can discover and load on demand, are now shipped by every major agent harness, yet the evidence for how much they help comes almost entirely from settings in which the right Skill is hand-picked for the task and the agent starts from a blank slate. Neither holds in deployment, where an agent chooses from whatever library happens to be installed and frequently carries memory from earlier work. We present SkillBuffBench, a benchmark and paired evaluation protocol that treats Skill access as a three-level factor (no Skill, a curated Skill, and automatic invocation from an installed library), crosses it with memory (off and on), with four agent harnesses and with multiple models (the state-of-the-art proprietary models from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI, and the state-of-the-art open-weight models from Chinese providers), every model being run under every harness, and evaluates the result on research tasks contributed by domain experts together with the Skills they use, currently in materials science and biology, with the suite extended on a rolling basis. Every run is marked by a deterministic verifier; uncertainty is reported with a paired, task-level bootstrap; and cost, agent rounds and wall-clock time are reported alongside the score rather than folded into it. This version of the paper describes the design of the benchmark, its evaluation protocol and its current tasks and Skills. The evaluation is in progress: results will be added once the runs are complete, and the task suite, results and analysis will continue to be updated on a rolling basis.

papers.title: Projector-Based Conic Formulations and Exact Decompositions for Distance-Based Assignment
papers.abstract: Given a set of fixed origin points and a set of variable target points in the same ambient metric space, we study distance-based assignment problems in which target placement and the assignment of origins to targets are determined simultaneously to minimize the overall distance-induced cost. We show that the assignment structure can be represented using orthogonal projection matrices. This observation leads to new mixed-projection conic formulations that avoid the big-$M$ envelopes used in standard mixed-integer models. Building on these formulations, we develop exact decomposition algorithms that separate the discrete selection of assignment projectors from the convex conic subproblems for target location. We also derive semidefinite relaxation bounds and primal procedures that provide warm starts for the exact methods. The proposed approach establishes new connections between distance-based assignment, orthogonal projectors, and low-rank semidefinite optimization, and applies to general conic-representable metrics.

papers.title: The BMM symmetrising trace conjecture holds for all complex reflection groups
papers.abstract: We prove the symmetrising trace conjecture of Broué, Malle and Michel for the generic Hecke algebras of all exceptional complex reflection groups, and we treat the remaining case of the infinite series, so that the conjecture now holds for all complex reflection groups. A key ingredient is a new family of bases, constructed via breadth-first search, which generalise the standard basis of an Iwahori-Hecke algebra; they provide a uniform proof of the freeness conjecture of Broué, Malle and Rouquier for these groups, and a model for computing in the Hecke algebras. The canonical trace is then obtained from other bases: generalisations of the $z$-bases of earlier work for the smaller groups, and bases built along towers of parabolic subgroups for the largest ones. The verification for each group reduces to a finite computation, carried out using programs developed with the assistance of a large language model.

papers.title: Virtually solvable groups with balanced presentations
papers.abstract: We show that if $G$ is a virtually solvable group with finite Hirsch length and such that $β_2(G;\mathbb{Q})\leqβ=β_1(G;\mathbb{Q})$ then $β\leq3$. This sharpens bounds on the Betti numbers of 3-manifolds which embed in $S^4$ with the fundamental groups of each complementary region virtually solvable and of finite Hirsch length.

papers.title: Jordan-Frame Dynamics of Curvature Inflation: A Derivative Expansion of the Friedmann Constraint
papers.abstract: We derive a slow-roll approximation for the Jordan-frame Hubble rate $H_J$ in metric $f(R)$ gravity. A derivative expansion of the vacuum Friedmann constraint to third order gives $\dot H_J$ as a function of $H_J$. In the Starobinsky model we also show that the difference in $\dot H_J$ between two expanding solutions decreases as they pass through successively lower values of $H_J$, and that a signed square root of $H_J$ evolves smoothly through the zeros that follow inflation. We test the approximation in a regularized inverse-logarithmic $R^2$ model and in $R+α^{p-1}R^p$, taking the pivot from the exact background 60 Einstein-frame e-folds before the end of inflation. For the inverse-logarithmic coupling $δ=3$, the third-order approximation reproduces $\dot H_J$ at the pivot with a relative error of $3\times10^{-8}$. Integrating the approximate branch between the pivot and exit values of $H_J$ taken from the exact background gives 59.98 e-folds, compared with 60 on the exact trajectory. At the six couplings $δ=0,1,\ldots,5$, the absolute difference from the numerical mode result is below $1.1\times10^{-5}$ in the scalar tilt $n_s$, and the relative difference is below $0.0052\%$ in the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$. Here the second-order spectral formulas account for nearly all of this difference. For $p=1.8$ the approximation itself adds to the error, which becomes $3.9\times10^{-5}$ in $n_s$ and $0.047\%$ in $r$. For $δ=3$, perturbative scalaron decay into a minimally coupled Higgs doublet places the pivot 51.59 e-folds before the end of inflation and gives $n_s=0.9690$ and $r=0.0067$. At fixed $αμ_0^2=0.006065$ and with the same decay rate prescription, $δ\simeq8.7$ gives the central $n_s$ value inferred from ACT DR6, Planck, CMB lensing and DESI baryon acoustic oscillations. This comparison uses the published one-dimensional constraint.

papers.title: Seen but Unsaid: Locating and Repairing Cross-Image Comparison in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) often fail to match a point or an object across two images, even when the match can be decoded from their hidden states. We trace where this information is lost in Qwen3-VL-2B/4B/8B/32B, InternVL3.5-8B, and Gemma-3-12B on synthetic shape matching, HPatches point correspondence, and SPair-71k semantic correspondence, comparing input-matched probes with calibrated outputs. The models fail at two distinct points. Exact copies are compared and the result reaches the answer position, but the output does not use it, whether or not the shapes have names. Semantic correspondences are present in the visual tokens but are only weakly compared and never reach the answer position. The comparison runs through 16 to 32 attention heads that let tokens of the second image attend to the first. Redistributing their attention at fixed mass removes up to 32 points of accuracy, against at most 7 for random or attention-matched heads, and their attention is gated by salience and weighted by content. Training only these heads (0.02% of the parameters) recovers 25 to 28 points on SPair-71k and transfers to HPatches and BLINK. Unconstrained LoRA adapters, which reach higher accuracy, converge on the same heads: inserting only these heads' attention into the base model recovers 21-51% of an adapter's gain, mostly through changed inputs to the heads. Across all 14 trained arms, the selectivity of this small head set tracks the accuracy they reach, and it is read directly from attention, without probes or retraining. The gain in selectivity is not a by-product of more attention to the first image: it comes mostly from the wrong options no longer being drawn to the marked reference.

papers.title: Sharp $L_p$-Regularity for Quantum Markov Semigroups
papers.abstract: We determine the sharp universal constants in positive-input $L_p$-regularity for finite-dimensional quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful invariant state. For $1<p<\infty$, they are $p\sin(π/p)/(2(p-1))$ under KMS symmetry and $\frac{p}{2(p-1)}\tan(\fracπ{2}\min\{1/p,1-1/p\})$ without a symmetry assumption, with the endpoint values at $p=1$ given by $π/2$ and $π/4$, respectively.

papers.title: Neural Marked Point Processes for Health Insurance Claims
papers.abstract: Health insurance claims exhibit temporal dependence, as previous claims may provide information about the timing, type and amount of subsequent claims. Such dependencies are difficult to capture with traditional actuarial models based on aggregated claim counts. We investigate a neural marked point process in which a causal Transformer represents individual claim histories and determines type-specific conditional intensities, allowing for self-excitation and interactions between claim types. The framework also incorporates conditional severity distributions, reporting delays and stochastic medical-cost inflation. We develop a likelihood-based calibration procedure that accounts for incomplete claim reporting and evaluate the model using both simulated and empirical data. A simulation study with 10,000 insurance contracts examines the recovery of known claim dynamics, while an application to MEPS-derived medical-event data assesses predictive performance. The fitted model reproduces the main patterns in claim frequencies and severities, although some discrepancies remain in the tails of the distributions. On the MEPS data, the neural model achieves better predictive performance than two generalized linear model benchmarks in terms of claim-count deviance and expenditure discrimination.

papers.title: Source-Free Domain Adaptation for Multi-Label Image Classification: A Framework, Baselines, and Benchmark
papers.abstract: Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) adapts a model trained on a labelled source domain to an unlabelled target domain without access to the source data. Almost the entire SFDA literature assumes mutually exclusive classes, yet many deployed settings are multi-label. This paper formulates SFDA for multi-label classification and establishes the first benchmark for it: five adaptation tasks over six datasets spanning remote sensing, natural, clipart-style and driving imagery, with four single-label SFDA methods extended to provide the first baselines and a published multi-label method run alongside them, over three seeds. The benchmark shows that extending a single-label method is unreliable rather than merely suboptimal: half of the extended baselines fail to improve on the unadapted source model at all, and on two of the five tasks none of them does. The failures are not incidental. Nearest-centroid pseudo-labelling, softmax-based confidence, the diversity term of information maximization and confidence-weighted prototype construction each rely on mutual exclusivity, and each fails differently without it, so replacing the softmax with per-class sigmoids is a valid but insufficient extension. Multi-label Prototype Alignment with Contrastive Teaching (MPACT) is proposed in response, a mean-teacher framework whose objective, prototype construction and alignment term are each reconsidered for overlapping label sets. It attains the best average on every reported metric and is the only method that improves on the unadapted source model on all five tasks. The analysis further introduces a prototype-agreement diagnostic separating feature-space alignment from self-reinforcing agreement with the classifier, and reports a negative result for confidence-based pseudo-label filtering.

papers.title: The Cybersecurity Dataset Observatory: Which Data for AI in Cybersecurity?
papers.abstract: AI is increasingly used for cybersecurity tasks such as intrusion and malware detection, in enterprise, industrial, vehicular and mobile networks. Its effectiveness depends on data: models need representative network traffic, both to be trained and to be evaluated realistically. Public datasets of cybersecurity network traffic, however, are scattered across laboratory pages, repositories and aggregators, and are continuously released, corrected and withdrawn: 92 of the 234 datasets we catalog were released in 2023 or later. At this pace, surveys that list them are outdated soon after publication, since they describe the field only as it was when they were written. We present the Cybersecurity dataset observatory, a public and continuously updated catalog of cybersecurity datasets based on network traffic. New datasets are added as they are found or submitted, every record is periodically re-checked against its original source, to which it links rather than hosting the data, and every change is recorded in a public change log. This paper documents the first release: we define a traffic-centered scope and a seven-axis taxonomy, and review 234 datasets (204 original captures and 30 derivatives) across 14 domains. The review shows a field that grows quickly but unevenly, where 91 datasets distribute only processed records, a few laboratories produce a large share of the data, and UAV, wireless and V2X networks have little public evidence, while 5G has few real captures. We then relate the catalog to common uses in AI research, outline a procedure for selecting datasets, and discuss benchmark pitfalls and open gaps.

papers.title: Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation with boundary in higher dimensions I
papers.abstract: We study isolated boundary singularities of positive solutions of the scalar-flat boundary Yamabe equation. We prove the critical upper bound for general smooth metrics in dimensions $3\le n\le17$ and for Euclidean domains with smooth boundary in dimensions $3\le n\le22$. For general metrics, this range extends to $n=18$ when the conformal metric is complete near the singularity. In every dimension, the critical upper bound implies removability or a matching lower bound and convergence to a unique flat Fowler solution with a positive power rate. Sharpness of these dimension ranges will be established in a subsequent paper.

papers.title: Convergence rate of periodic homogenization for Hamilton--Jacobi equations with supercritical viscosity
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to studying the convergence rate in periodic homogenization of the viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation (with supercritical viscosity index $σ>1$) \[ \partial_t u_\varepsilon+H(x/\varepsilon,\partial_xu_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^σΔu_\varepsilon,\quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}_+,\ \] subject to a given initial datum. For Tonelli Hamiltonians $H$, the solution $u_\varepsilon$ is proved to converge to a certain $u:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ (solving the effective problem) in the optimal rate $O(\varepsilon^{\min\{σ-1,1\}})$. We also obtain a rate for the case of non-convex Hamiltonians and discussed its optimality therein.

papers.title: Inferring accretion bursts in intermediate-mass protostars from asteroseismic imprints
papers.abstract: During star formation, objects may gain the majority of their final mass through regular and intense bursts of mass accretion. For bursts of the FU Orionis-type (FUor), accretion rates can climb to $10^{-3} \ \text{M}_\odot \text{yr}^{-1}$ during short windows of time, amounting to just a few percent of the main accretion phase. To study the occurrence of such events observationally, signatures of the current accretion bursts and tracers of recent bursts are crucial. We investigate the potential to identify accretion bursts in protostars and pre-main sequence stars of intermediate mass using asteroseismology. We use the stellar structure and evolution code MESA to evolve stellar models from the protostellar seed phase of $0.01 \ \text{M}_\odot$ and $1.5 \ \text{R}_\odot$ up to $4.0 \ \text{M}_\odot$ with a constant accretion rate of $10^{-6} \ \text{M}_\odot \text{yr}^{-1}$. A single accretion burst is initialized during the accretion phase. The stellar oscillation code GYRE is employed to compute the resulting asteroseismic properties of the models. Accretion bursts of up to $10^{-3} \ \text{M}_\odot \text{yr}^{-1}$ are sufficient to cause the convective cores of the models to recede, leaving behind a chemical trace which manifests itself in the form of quasi-periodic dips in the g-mode period spacing. This effect is strongest during the outburst, but also lingers for up to 475 years before the convective core is re-established and the dips are gone. Our experiment shows that a single accretion burst leaves an imprint in the deep interiors of protostars and pre-MS stars of intermediate mass, and that this imprint can be captured with asteroseismology. Our results are most conclusive for burst magnitudes greater than $1\times10^{-4} \ \text{M}_\odot \text{yr}^{-1}$, corresponding to FUor-type bursts.

papers.title: The Silent Cost of Conversation History in LLM Reasoning
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) in multi-turn information systems accumulate their own earlier replies and a growing task state. We asked whether this conversation history lowers accuracy, and whether process-level quality metrics warn before it does. Each analysis was fixed before its outcomes were computed. In Study 1, on 48 sharded math tasks, retaining its replies lowered final success by 0.21 for GPT-4o-mini and 0.29 for Mistral-7B (Holm-adjusted p = 0.026 and 0.004); Llama-4 Scout showed the same direction, not significant. Study 2 introduces CDR-Stream, 100-turn state-tracking dialogues with an exact answer per turn and per-model difficulty calibration. With the full history, accuracy fell from about 0.6 to 0.1 within twenty turns at matched difficulty, whereas a solver-verified state summary kept it 0.52-0.59 higher (Holm-adjusted p less than 0.001). Consistency and logical coherence fell far less than accuracy, and stability rose. None of these metrics, a paired readiness measure or calibrated single-stream drift detectors gave robust, model-general early warning, although in Study 2 the repeat-based metrics were complete only for GPT-4o-mini. In the monitors we tested, a single 100-turn stream had power only for very large drops. Systems built on LLMs should keep task state outside the transcript and monitor across sessions.

papers.title: Fractional integration with singularity on the light-cone
papers.abstract: In this paper, we solve a classical problem investigated by Gelfand and Shilov on a family of fractional integral operators whose kernels have singularity appeared on the light-cone in R^n+1. As an implication, we obtain a desired sharp estimate for the L^p to L^q-boundedness of cone multiplier operators having a negative order.

papers.title: Linearization and local controllability of nonautonomous differential inclusions
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the linearization of nonautonomous differential inclusions, whose right-hand side is integrably Lipschitz in the state variable and measurable in time. We establish measurability results for time-dependent graphs and identify the Clarke tangent cone to the set of their measurable selections in $L^\infty\times L^1$. Combining this characterization with a subtransversality argument, we obtain a lower estimate for the Clarke tangent cone to the set of all admissible trajectories starting from a fixed set. As an application, we give sufficient conditions for local controllability around a closed terminal set.

papers.title: An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant
papers.abstract: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. In 2004, Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$. We prove this conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$ and determine all subsets of maximum size in $C_n^2$ that contain no $n$ elements with sum zero.

papers.title: On-policy distillation as a Backdoor Propagation Channel
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) is emerging as an important paradigm for the post training of large language models, improving student models by leveraging supervision generated online by teacher models. However, whether this process also transfers latent security risks from teacher models to student models remains insufficiently studied. In this work, we reveal a new security risk in which an attacker first implants a conditional backdoor into the teacher model through supervised fine tuning (SFT), after which OPD can transfer the backdoor to the student model with only an extremely small proportion of trigger prompt exposure. More concerningly, we find that such backdoor transfer is substantially stronger under OPD than under conventional distillation methods, suggesting that OPD may provide an efficient channel for propagating backdoors across models. Our mechanistic analysis shows that the backdoor signal is primarily transmitted through anomalous differences in the conditional probabilities produced by the teacher model for triggered and clean inputs, and is gradually internalized into the internal representations of the student model during training. Furthermore, we investigate how to suppress such anomalous conditional probability signals at the source of distillation supervision and, based on this analysis, propose an OPD training method tailored to this conditional backdoor propagation setting to mitigate the risk of backdoor transfer induced by untrusted teacher supervision.

papers.title: PoRef-MIL: Plug-and-Play Posterior Refinement for Multiple Instance Learning in QSM-Based Brain Disease Classification
papers.abstract: Quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) is a novel quantitative MRI contrast for studying tissue susceptibility changes in brain disorders, including Parkinson's disease (PD) and multiple sclerosis (MS). However, small cohorts and the lack of local annotations make developing deep learning models for QSM-based diagnosis challenging. In this work, we propose PoRef-MIL, a weakly supervised multiple instance learning (MIL) framework combining iterative slice relabeling and network retraining with a plug-and-play posterior refinement module (PRM). During training, a 2D dual-branch diagnosis network and a subject-level classifier were alternately trained for five rounds. The classifier was used to update slice pseudo-labels for retraining the diagnosis network. The PRM was applied during inference to refine slice probabilities through bidirectional posterior inference and calculate entropy-derived confidence from the refined probabilities, which was then used in sliding-window scoring to obtain subject-level predictions. PoRef-MIL was evaluated on an in-house PD cohort of 287 participants and a public MS cohort of 150 participants. Compared with eight classification methods, PoRef-MIL achieved the highest mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.942 and 0.872, and accuracies of 0.926 and 0.833, for PD and MS classification, respectively. Ablation experiments were conducted to validate the effectiveness of iterative relabeling and PRM, and the plug-and-play feature of the proposed PRM was also evaluated using four state-of-the-art MIL models. Overall, PoRef-MIL offers a promising approach to QSM-based disease classification in small cohorts without manual slice annotations.

papers.title: On two-dimensional affine Springer fibres
papers.abstract: We extend results of Spaltenstein on irreducible components of two-dimensional usual Springer fibres in reductive groups of simply lace type to the case of two-dimensional affine Springer fibres associated to loop groups. One of our methods is to relate these affine Springer fibres with certain subsets of the affine Weyl group.

papers.title: Lasso: Towards Sustainable AI-Generated Media Detection with Intel QAT On-Chip Compression
papers.abstract: Synthetic text, images, and video are rising. Software-only detectors are power-hungry, too slow, and costly, and do not scale with demand. When software cannot scale, historically hardware often comes to the rescue. We perform the first reverse engineering of a compression accelerator, the Intel QuickAssist Technology (QAT), and find that its latency depends on how its input repeats, not on what the bytes are, a property we call repetition-structure dependence. Using this information, we then build Lasso, a low-cost, high-performance detector for AI-generated content that turns the accelerator into a measuring instrument. For text detection, Lasso achieves 100% accuracy on original DetectRL text and retains 92% average accuracy after paraphrasing, compared with 78% for Binoculars and 55% for DetectGPT. Across original, paraphrased, and lightly perturbed text, where perturbation inserts typos and substitutes words, it achieves 82% average accuracy, outperforming all five baselines. With topic, length, and formatting matched, accuracy reaches 95% for instruction-tuned generators, including when the tested generator is unseen. On the RAID benchmark of 11 text generators and eight writing domains, accuracy averages 82% when trained on one generator and tested on another, and 74% across eight held-out domains. Detection takes 197 $μ$s, at least 356$\times$ faster than each of the five baselines. At the same time, Lasso consumes over 99% less energy per check than both Binoculars and DetectGPT. Beyond text, Lasso detects AI-generated videos, software code, and images with 78%, 70% and 98% accuracy, respectively, with low latency and power opening avenues for practical real time and edge device detection of multimodality AI artifacts for the first time. No other compared technique supports detection across all four modalities: text, video, images, and code.

papers.title: Bring Back Language to Actions: Restoring VLM capabilities in VLA Models via Parameter Merging
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) are obtained by fine-tuning pre-trained Vision-Language Models (VLMs) on robot demonstration data, enabling action prediction from visual observations and language instructions. However, this fine-tuning induces catastrophic forgetting, substantially degrading the semantic and visual grounding capabilities of the original VLM. We address this by merging the parameters of a VLM and its VLA derivative without retraining either model. Concretely, we extract the task vector (the difference between VLA and VLM weights) and decompose it via Singular Value Decomposition. For each component, we learn a scalar mixing coefficient controlling how much of the VLA adaptation is retained, optimised to jointly preserve action prediction and vision-language capabilities. Experiments show that our merged model performs well on both axes simultaneously, consistently outperforming established merging baselines.

papers.title: A toric construction of the spectral Tate curve
papers.abstract: We develop toric geometry spectral algebraic geometry. In particular, we lift toric varieties to flat schemes over the sphere spectrum. Furthermore, we prove several rigidity and strictness results allowing us to define and produce strict group actions of flat algebraic tori. As an application, we give a construction of the Tate curve in spectral algebraic geometry. This approach lets us produce a lift of the Tate curve to $\mathbb{S}[[q]]$. We furthermore describe how to lift (arithmetic) toric stacks.

papers.title: Nonperturbative lattice simulation of the nucleation rate in thermal first-order phase transitions
papers.abstract: We present a nonperturbative lattice study of vacuum decay through bubble nucleation in a three-dimensional real scalar field theory at finite temperature. The vacuum decay rate is computed by combining an expanded-ensemble multicanonical hybrid Monte Carlo approach, which samples the critical bubble configurations, with real-time Langevin dynamics, which follows the subsequent bubble evolution. We extrapolate the nucleation rate to the continuum limit and compare it with the corresponding one-loop perturbative prediction, finding a discrepancy of about 6.6%.

papers.title: SCAR: Bridging Coarse Retrieval and Fine Localization through Candidate Reranking
papers.abstract: Natural-language point-cloud localization typically retrieves candidate map cells and then predicts a position inside each candidate, yet the final output is still determined by retrieval order. A retrieval score measures region-description relevance, not whether the coordinates a region yields are accurate: a relevant region may produce a displaced prediction, and a lower-ranked region may contain a successful one. We study the final selection problem after the candidate pool and Fine predictions are fixed---how to choose the coordinate most likely to localize successfully, and under which conditions the gain holds. We propose SCAR (Spatial Consistency-Aware Reranking). SCAR treats each cell--Fine-coordinate pair as a localization hypothesis, interprets directional relations as functions of position, and reads spatial support at the backbone's actual Fine point (Fine-conditioned Evidence Readout). It organizes this readout with center support, semantic presence, retrieval score, and geometric offsets into a 23-D representation, trains a shared scorer with localization-success labels, and at inference reranks existing hypotheses and returns their original coordinates. Experiments cover four public backbones and a corrected Des4Pos reimplementation across five domains. Excluding one protocol-reference configuration, exploratory TEST point estimates on the remaining 24 configurations show Top-1@5\,m above Original on 23 and Cell R@1 above Original on all 24. On development-set VAL, the Fine readout improves Top-1@5\,m by 5.77 percentage points (pp) over a center surrogate on corrected Des4Pos*KITTI, and the complete scoring scheme improves it by 13.98\,pp over FSR on MambaPlace$\times$nuScenesFull; the latter measures the complete scheme, not learned ranking alone.

papers.title: Separability of coupled gravitational perturbations in Plebański--Demiański spacetimes
papers.abstract: Recently, a major breakthrough in the separability of gravitational perturbations of the Kerr--Newman rotating charged black hole was achieved by Hintz [arxiv:2609.33661], and extended to non-zero cosmological constant Kerr--Newman-(A)dS black holes by Yoshida [arxiv:2610.20500] and Zhao [arxiv:2610.22274]. This method removes the need for the freezing approximation, wherein coupling to the electromagnetic degrees of freedom are ignored, at the price of a coupled set of equations in the gravitational radiative degrees of freedom. The key insight is to transform the coupled system of equations into a chiral form which is amenable to a modified matrix $R$-separation of variables. In this work we extend the construction to the most general type D electro-vacuum solution to the Einstein-Maxwell equations, with aligned matter and cosmological constant. The construction makes use of the conformal properties of the equations and we find a symmetry operator underlying the decoupling of the chiral system.

papers.title: Obaleth: Build Your Own GPU Communication Stack
papers.abstract: Machine learning systems specialize computation to the workload and hardware, but communication remains in generic libraries whose device code and transport decisions are not visible to high-level compilers. We present Obaleth, a compiler that makes GPU-initiated communication part of a kernel's intermediate representation, co-optimizes it alongside computation, and lowers it to specialized transport code. Obaleth plans completions around buffer lifetimes and optimizes memory ordering, synchronization, and batching across NVIDIA and AMD GPUs. On H100 GPUs, Obaleth sends small messages up to 3.3$\times$ faster, and on 256 GPUs runs all-to-all 1.25$\times$ and 2.3$\times$ faster than NVSHMEM and NCCL GIN, with much smaller memory and register use. In vLLM, it serves Qwen3-235B on 16 B200 GPUs and answers requests up to 1.29$\times$ faster than with DeepEP.

papers.title: TSGP-2: On the Non-Linearity of Symbolic Regression Problems and How to Exploit It with Model-based Semantic Genetic Programming
papers.abstract: Model-based variation operators such as the one used in Transformer Semantic Genetic Programming (TSGP) are affected by possible biases of their training data. TSGP is trained on programs generated by Genetic Programming (GP) runs on linear target functions, which leads to a bias toward linear offspring. This bias can hinder search performance on problems that require non-linear solutions. This work has two goals: first, we investigate the linearity of standard benchmark problems including the Feynman and real-world problems. While most of the structure of real-world problems can be well approximated by linear functions, the Feynman problems exhibit varying levels of non-linear structure. Thus, a proper variation operator of a search method should be able to create both types of programs, linear as well as non-linear ones. Second, we propose TSGP-2, which follows the functionality of TSGP but uses as training data programs from GP runs on both linear and non-linear target functions. As a result, the training data includes a lower share of programs that behave linearly. With a higher share of non-linear structures, TSGP-2 outperforms TSGP on problems with non-linear structure, while performing similarly on linear problems. In addition, TSGP-2 is less biased toward linear offspring and is able to propose a higher number of meaningful non-linear offspring earlier during search, which coincides with better solutions. The findings underscore the importance of training data for a learned variation operator and emphasize that the biases of search operators should be aligned with the problems they are applied to.

papers.title: Faster Deterministic All-Pairs Shortest Paths with Real Edge Weights
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic algorithm for exact all-pairs shortest paths (APSP), that is, all distances, in directed $n$-vertex graphs with arbitrary finite real edge weights and no negative cycles. Its worst-case running time is $O(n^{2.9929729})$ with the recent rectangular matrix multiplication bound $ω(1,\tfrac12,1)=2$, and $O(n^{2.99306273})$ with earlier rectangular bounds alone; both improve the deterministic bound $O(n^{2.9997})$ and the Las Vegas expected-time bound $O(n^{2.993805})$. The algorithm runs on a real RAM whose only real-number operations are exact addition, subtraction, and comparison, each at unit cost.

papers.title: AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics
papers.abstract: Neural surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD) are trained and ranked on single-family, fixed-domain datasets that cannot test the minimum bar for an aerodynamic foundation model: predicting CFD-quality incompressible flow in seconds for new shapes in new enclosures. On DrivAerML, larger models and longer training barely lower Transolver's error; doubling training cases cuts it by about 12% up to 400 cases, exhausting the dataset. We introduce AeroZoo, a benchmark and training corpus of 3,815 time-mean unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (URANS) solutions with a transition model across seven geometry families, eight enclosures, and Reynolds numbers from $10^3$ to $10^8$. Each sample poses a well-posed PDE problem as a solver receives it: boundary meshes grouped by condition type, prescribed values, and fluid properties. The 2,816 time-mean-stable samples form the canonical benchmark: two tasks, mean engineering metrics with an overall flow score $S_{\mathrm{flow}}$ (1.000 for uniform inlet flow), and 22 frozen geometry-disjoint splits holding out shapes, enclosures, boundary-condition layouts, and Reynolds ranges. On the random split, boundary-condition tokens cut GeoTransolver's mean velocity error from 89.8% to 15.2% of inlet speed (uniform flow: 44.0%; $S_{\mathrm{flow}} = 0.290$). ISLA, a boundary-driven transformer, reaches 8.2% ($S_{\mathrm{flow}} = 0.153$; 0.123 with boundary targets), about 6 times mesh-refinement sensitivity. On shared test samples, holding out a geometry family barely changes ISLA's mean velocity error, whereas holding out enclosures or boundary-condition layouts raises it 3.8 to 8.4 times. The dataset is public; the scoring code will be released.

papers.title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
papers.abstract: Symmetry is a foundational principle of physics: the behavior of a PDE-governed system does not depend on the coordinate frame, unit system, or mesh used to write it down, and neither should a surrogate model. Yet today's leading neural surrogates lack these invariances and fail under simple transformations of the same problem: for models trained on PDEs of cars in one pose (i.e., translation and rotation), rotating the full PDE raises the surface-pressure error from 4% to more than 100%, and re-sampling its boundary raises it to about 30%. We introduce ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention), a slice-attention transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs. Because the boundary determines the interior solution, ISLA encodes the posed boundary once into learned slices and evaluates arbitrary interior points independently through a tree-accelerated learned boundary kernel. Inputs are nondimensionalized in scales computed from the boundary, sums over boundary cells are area-weighted quadratures that converge under mesh refinement, and geometry enters only as distances and relative angles to equivariant slice anchors, making the model equivariant to rigid motions and reflections up to optional token subsampling and tree clustering. On AeroZoo, 2,816 3D flows spanning diverse geometries, poses, physical scales, and boundary conditions, ISLA's mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are 1.9 and 2.2 times lower than the best baseline's. On full AirfRANS, ISLA is second only to an explicit boundary-integral network (GLOBE), with errors 1.6 to 2.6 times lower than the better of Transolver's and GeoTransolver's in every field.

papers.title: Control Variates to reduce the variance of the empirical Moment Generating Function: an extreme value perspective
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of Moment Generating Functions is fundamental in many applications, but empirical estimators have high variances. Within a control variate setup, Extreme Value Theory is leveraged to identify how extreme values affect the variance reduction method's optimality.

papers.title: Anonymous in Name Only: A Critical Review and a Reidentification Exercise on the European Commission's Anonymization Measures for Google Search Data under Article 6(11) of the DMA
papers.abstract: In July 2026, the European Commission (EC) set out the anonymization measures Alphabet must implement to share Google Search data with competing search engines under Article 6(11) of the Digital Markets Act. As the first concrete illustration of how the EC operationalizes anonymization under the EU digital rulebook, this methodology could become a regulatory benchmark. In this paper, we show why it should not. We critically review the anonymization measures proposed by the EC, from the characterization of residual risk to the suppression thresholds and the reliance on contractual safeguards. For each of those issues, we highlight significant conceptual flaws, and, where applicable, we illustrate these flaws with empirical observations from real Google Search data provided by Alphabet and protected under the EC's measures. Importantly, we present examples of low-effort reidentification, record linkage, and confidential attribute inference achieved through straightforward and automatable attack patterns. Our findings show that the approach of the EC relies on unjustified heuristics rather than formal privacy guarantees, underestimates the risks inherent in free-text search queries, and sacrifices data utility without achieving meaningful protection. We also demonstrate that the proposed measures do not meet any of the three anonymization criteria established by the European Data Protection Board (EDPB): no record isolation, no linkage, and no inference. Practitioners and regulators are therefore cautioned against treating these measures as a sound anonymization practice.

papers.title: The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
papers.abstract: We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture. The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity. We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar. In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.

papers.title: Concentration of Quasimodes at Spherical Interface between 3D-Topological Insulators
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the edge states localized at a spherical interface between two $3\mathrm{D}$-topological insulators from a continuous model of the semiclassical Dirac equation. Using the dynamical and spectral properties of the semiclassical Dirac operator tangent to the interface and the Landau level stratification of the energy in the transverse variable, we describe several concentration and invariance properties of the semiclassical measures associated with quasimodes of the system localized at the interface. Moreover, we construct explicit quasimodes which fulfill some of these properties and concentrate on some particular single periodic geodesics of the sphere.

papers.title: Eventual Collisional Relaxation After Large Echo-Driven Amplification in a Weakly Collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck System
papers.abstract: We study the weakly collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system near a Maxwellian equilibrium and construct global classical solutions exhibiting large transient growth before eventual collisional relaxation. The main mechanism is a nonlinear plasma-echo cascade which remains effective up to the enhanced-dissipation time scale $t\simν^{-\frac13}$, producing norm inflation of size larger than $ν^{-1}$ from arbitrarily small $ν$-dependent perturbations. At the same time, the nonzero spatial modes decay at the enhanced-dissipation scale $e^{-\mathsf{r}ν^{\frac13}t}$, while the zero mode relaxes at the thermal scale $e^{-νt}$. The estimates also reveal a sharp contrast in the smoothing effects before and after the collisional time scale $t\sim ν^{-1}$. As a consequence, our construction gives explicit upper bounds on the Sobolev and Gevrey stability thresholds: perturbations of the corresponding $ν$-dependent sizes can still trigger severe echo-driven amplification before collisional dissipation becomes dominant at the critical time scale $t\simν^{-\frac13}$.

papers.title: Double Blandford: Resistive GRMHD simulations of accreting black holes simultaneously launch winds and jets
papers.abstract: Magnetic fields can launch outflows through the Blandford-Znajek (BZ) or the Blandford-Payne (BP) mechanism in accreting black hole systems. Despite the dominant launching mechanism still being unclear, the BP process has been insufficiently studied in general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations due to difficulties in generating and maintaining the required large-scale magnetic field geometry. Here, we set up six resistive GRMHD simulations of thin accretion disks with BHAC. The accretion disks in two simulations become magnetically arrested, while the others stay in the standard and normal evolution (SANE) regime. All simulations form jets and winds. The jets are parabolic and collimated by the outer sub-relativistic disk wind; a power law relating the jet width $x$ to the height $z$ as $x\propto z^\mathcal{K}$ yields exponents between 0.52 and 0.64. Among the SANE simulations, the setup with spin parameter $a_* = -0.9375$ has the most efficient jet. For a highly spinning black hole with $a_*=0.9375$, the BZ jet power is $\gtrsim3$ times greater than the disk wind power. The simulated wind regions consist of a highly magnetized region, where the magnetization parameter $σ\gg1$, and a less magnetized region. A fast outflow with the potential to reach Lorentz factors up to $Γ_\infty\approx25$ propagates in the former region, but because the Lorentz force acts against the disk, it cannot remove a measurable amount of mass from the disk. In the less-magnetized region, a centrifugally driven slower wind efficiently carries away disk material.

papers.title: Asymmetric Multimodal Learning: The Alignment Redundancy Bound and Decomposed JEPAs
papers.abstract: Cross-modal alignment is the default objective for multimodal representation learning, but it rests on an implicit assumption: that the two modalities are roughly symmetric views of the same underlying state. We show that this assumption fails on real multimodal data, and that alignment as a sole objective is provably lossy under informational asymmetry. We formalize the failure through Partial Information Decomposition, proving that cross-modal alignment retains at most the redundant information atom and annihilates the modality-unique and synergistic structure on which asymmetric tasks depend. We give the exact PID decomposition of the alignment information bottleneck, characterize its failure regime, and derive a sufficiency condition that any encoder objective must satisfy to preserve all four informational atoms. We then introduce Decomposed JEPA (D-JEPA), which realizes this condition by factorizing each modality's latent space into an aligned shared core and a private fiber anchored by contextual masked prediction. On compositional reasoning benchmarks, alignment-only training undergoes catastrophic semantic collapse on relational queries; D-JEPA prevents this collapse, recovering the referent structure alignment discards, restoring most of the mutual information available from a frozen backbone, and producing positive multimodal synergy where alignment inverts it. Information-theoretic and causal audits confirm that the recovered information is causally localized in the private fibers.

papers.title: Metadata for the Flux Density Calibration of the April 2021 and March 2022 Event Horizon Telescope Science Data
papers.abstract: The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) has been conducting science observations annually since 2021 after the initial campaigns in 2017 and 2018. In this memo, we report on the metadata associated to the observations from 2021 April and 2022 March at 1.3mm wavelengths. We follow a similar path for the collection, processing, and validation of the metadata used for the initial amplitude calibration of the 2018 EHT data. In this release, we introduce some differences regarding the treatment of sensitivities and gain curves for some stations. In addition, we describe the changes to the EHT array since 2018.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): Spacecraft performance in the L2 environment
papers.abstract: The Euclid mission was designed around the need for thermo-optical and mechanical stability, stray-light suppression, low outgassing, and precise guiding. After three years in space, a wealth of data is available to assess the performance in these areas. We review the L2 halo-orbit design and consumables budget. Solar stray-light gradually increases by 14% per year and is consistent with meteoroid puncturing, but remains low overall. Data loss from high solar activity has declined notably since the maximum of the 25th Solar cycle passed. The thermodynamical response of the optical elements to a thermal step impulse follows sigmoidal growth curves, entering the asymptotic equilibration regime after 21--46 hours. Water-ice contamination has affected data from both instruments and requires continued monitoring; we review detection and decontamination methods, and Euclid's contamination history. High-precision measurements of the zodiacal background reveal, at eight sigma significance, the subtle modulation caused by the changing perspective on the dust distribution due to the L2 halo-orbit libration. These data also show that conservative pre-launch estimates overestimated the out-of-field stray-light by factors of 4 (H band) to 27 (I band). Telemetry data demonstrate excellent guiding, and enable highly significant detections of solar radiation pressure and of thermal-emission recoil from Euclid's unilluminated dark sides. Lastly, we present a list of 34 meteoroid impacts, discuss their mechanical and optical signatures, and derive a minimum detectable impactor mass of 5e-7 g.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): Calibration strategy and observations
papers.abstract: This paper reviews how Euclid's top-level calibration requirements were translated into a calibration plan, how this plan is implemented and maintained during the survey, and how it performs in the current DR1 release. We show that DR1 already meets or exceeds most end-of-mission spectrophotometric calibration requirements. The construction of spectroscopically complete and pure samples relies on ongoing data acquisition for the Euclid Deep Survey, while point-spread-function modelling and shear calibration are still converging to their stringent accuracy requirements. With all DR1 data reprocessed with the DR1 pipeline configuration, more subtle effects have been detected and characterised, and correction strategies have been developed for DR2. These include improved absolute flux calibration, astrometry, charge-persistence correction, shutter effects, wavelength calibration, and spectrophotometric corrections for water-ice contamination. Finally, synthetic photometric transformations between Euclid and each of Roman, the James Webb Space Telescope, and the Chinese Space-station Survey Telescope, are presented.

papers.title: Strong and weak mean value sets for elliptic operators: uniqueness and counterexamples
papers.abstract: Classical theorems of Epstein--Schiffer and Kuran characterize balls by the mean value identity for integrable harmonic functions. In the Fermi Lectures, Caffarelli described an obstacle problem construction of analogous averaging sets for symmetric uniformly elliptic divergence-form operators. For such an operator with bounded measurable coefficients in dimension $n \ge 2,$ fix a center $x_0$ and a volume $V > 0,$ and let $E$ be the corresponding canonical set. We prove that a bounded open set $D$ of volume $V$ containing $x_0$ satisfies the mean value inequality at $x_0$ for every integrable subsolution on $D$ if and only if $E \subset D \subset \operatorname{int}\overline{E}.$ In particular, every such strong mean value set agrees with $E$ almost everywhere. The proof uses weak modified Schwarz potentials and an energy comparison. Additionally, we construct smooth symmetric uniformly elliptic operators for which the unit ball satisfies the mean value identity for all integrable solutions but fails the subsolution inequality, showing that there can be two distinct notions for what one can consider to be a ''mean value set.'' The canonical mean value set with the same center and volume contains the entire unit sphere and has a hole of positive measure inside the unit ball.

papers.title: Entropy and charge transport limit Mpemba preparation in holography
papers.abstract: We study Mpemba relaxation and its preparation cost in a holographic superconductor with full backreaction. At matched final energy and charge, boundary drives of finite duration can reverse the ordering of the remaining horizon entropy after source removal. In separate comparisons, some protocols reach a prescribed entropy tolerance earlier even when driving and waiting times are included. At criticality, a slow scalar field can persist even when little horizon entropy remains available for preparation and subsequent relaxation. Along the critical slow branch at fixed energy and charge, horizon displacement cancels the quadratic area response, leaving an entropy reserve of order $\varepsilon^4$ for an initial scalar amplitude $\varepsilon$. The same coefficient governs the entropy advantage of the nearby superconducting equilibrium and the entropy weight of the slow mode on the normal side. This weight vanishes in proportion to the mode's decay rate near the transition. Horizon area growth is quadratic in the covariant scalar flux. When the horizon remains smooth and its area growth uniformly controls the radial drift of the scalar field, the time needed to suppress the leading horizon field and exterior charge grows at least as $\varepsilon^{-2}$. Charge transfer fixes the signed area swept out by the time integral of this same flux, raising the minimum flux cost and strengthening the time bound.

papers.title: Dual Representation Enhanced Diffusion Policy for Flexible Job Shop Scheduling
papers.abstract: The Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling Problem (FJSP) is a fundamental and challenging optimization problem in smart manufacturing. Although recent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approaches can learn effective scheduling policies through interaction with the environment, their performance often degrades as problem scale and processing-time uncertainty increase. In this paper, we propose DredRL, a dual representation enhanced diffusion-policy reinforcement learning scheduler. DredRL first constructs enhanced dual representations of operations and machines through self- and cross-attention mechanisms to capture both intra-entity and inter-entity dependencies. A diffusion model is further employed as the policy network, generating scheduling decisions through iterative denoising conditioned on the encoded state to enhance policy expressiveness and robustness. Extensive experiments on synthetic, public, large-scale, and stochastic FJSP benchmarks demonstrate that DredRL outperforms state-of-the-art learning-based schedulers across most configurations. Compared with SOTA learning-based methods, DredRL reduces makespan by up to 5.44% on synthetic instances. It also achieves the best learning-based performance on three of four public benchmarks and outperforms the stochasticity-aware algorithms on stochastic benchmarks. These results demonstrate that combining enhanced dual representations with diffusion-based policies provides an effective and robust approach for large scale scalable FJSP scheduling in complicated environment.

papers.title: Quadratic Elements in Finite $p$-Groups and Applications to Oliver's $p$-Group Conjecture
papers.abstract: We establish a property of quadratic elements in faithful modules for finite $p$-groups. Let $p$ be an odd prime, and suppose that $a$ is a quadratic element of an abelian subgroup $L$ normalized by $b$. Writing $a_0=a$ and $a_i=[a_{i-1},b]$, we prove that if, for some $r$ with $2\leq r\leq(p+1)/2$, one has $a_{r-1}\neq1$ and $a_r=1$, then $a_{r-1}$ is quadratic. As an application, we verify the Weakly Closed Conjecture for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $p+2$, and hence establish the Quadratic Conjecture for these groups. Consequently, Oliver's $p$-group conjecture holds for a finite $p$-group $S$ whenever $S/\mathfrak X(S)$ has nilpotency class at most $p+2$.

papers.title: Probabilistic State Space Enumeration in Neural Network Computation
papers.abstract: Can we faithfully approximate the output of a dense Transformer multilayer perceptron (MLP) by enumerating only a small set of probable channel configurations? Our primary objective is to characterize and control approximation error under a fixed mask budget. Probabilistic state space enumeration (PSSE) links the selected masks to the residual in the MLP output. For a partition into channel groups, probability weighting makes the expectation over all possible masks equal to the dense output. We derive the exact residual for any retained set by weighting each group's output by the fraction of its inclusion probability outside the set. The omitted probability mass multiplied by the largest masked-output norm therefore bounds the absolute error. To select masks, NORDER-II adapts ORDER-II from network reliability. Under independent group inclusions, it computes an ordering once per layer from frozen weights and finds the $B$ masks with greatest total probability mass without listing all possibilities. With 32 groups, the mean number of masks needed to capture 95% of the mass ranges from 1,020 to 4,725 across models, out of more than four billion possibilities. Across 168 MLP layers in six language models, this approximation yields lower mean relative error than both ordinary and bias-corrected uniform sampling in all 1,008 equal-count comparisons. Our secondary objective is to improve inference efficiency through pruning. We count the distinct channels covered by each layer's retained masks and use those counts to allocate a fixed projection budget offline. The pruned models achieve lower held-out perplexity than both top-$k$ baselines in all 36 settings at matched MLP projection FLOPs. Target projection savings of 10%, 20%, and 30% yield mean decoder MLP speedups of $1.11\times$, $1.23\times$, and $1.36\times$ over dense MLPs, respectively.

papers.title: Robbing Peter to Pay Paul: Cross-Attribute Externalities of Fairness Interventions
papers.abstract: Fairness interventions often targets disparities associated with a single sensitive attribute in binary classification tasks. However, when multiple sensitive attributes are associated with a data subject, improving fairness with respect to one attribute does not necessarily improve it across all attributes: it may exacerbate disparities associated with other sensitive attributes, including those that are unavailable to the practitioner. We refer to these unintended effects as cross-attribute externalities of fairness. We study how fairness with respect to one sensitive attribute varies when an initially unfair classification or regression model is corrected with respect to another attribute. We characterize these externalities using Wasserstein barycentric disparities and develop a distributional framework that captures changes in both marginal and joint fairness measures. This highlights a limitation of conventional fairness evaluation, in which the success of an intervention is assessed mainly for the attribute it targets. In a jointly Gaussian model, we derive explicit trajectories for marginal and joint disparities and identify conditions under which an intervention eliminates disparities with respect to its target attribute while increasing disparities associated with another attribute. We also derive sharp partial-identification bounds on the resulting externalities when a sensitive attribute is unavailable and extend our results to categorical sensitive attributes. We illustrate these externalities using classification and regression real-data: in the classification experiments, interventions increase unfairness with respect to the hidden attribute in the majority of scenarios across more than half of the datasets considered; in the regression experiments on the ACSIncome dataset, correcting for race reduces sex disparities, whereas subsequently correcting for age increases them.

papers.title: Katz Kernel Based Stratification of Breast Cancer Patients
papers.abstract: The integration of mechanistic signaling networks into clinical research has become a cornerstone of precision oncology. By capturing the complex biochemical interactions within a cell, these networks provide a functional map of disease progression that goes beyond simple genomic mutations. Consequently, the development of specific signaling models of patients has significant relevance, allowing for a more granular representation of individual disease profiles. In this setting, there is a growing need for robust methodologies capable of comparing graph based pathway structures to identify similarities and differences across patient cohorts. Such comparisons are essential for the identification of clinically meaningful subgroups, and the discovery of novel biomarkers. Standard graph kernels, while mathematically rigorous, often remain too generic for this purpose. They frequently fail to capture features specific to gene signaling networks, resulting in suboptimal clustering performance. In this paper, we present a domain specific graph kernel designed for mechanistic signaling networks. Unlike generic approaches, our method explicitly incorporates biological constraints and gene interaction patterns into the kernel formulation, enabling a more accurate characterization of both topological structure and functional behavior. We assess its performance on breast cancer datasets, focusing on its ability to support disease subtyping. Our results suggest that our approach can effectively contribute to patient stratification.

papers.title: Artificial Currency and Separate Selling: A Constant Approximation for Consumer Surplus
papers.abstract: We study the allocation of indivisible items to buyers with submodular values generated by independent item signals. The objective is consumer surplus net of burnt payments. We compare two simple mechanisms. Separate selling applies money burning item by item: each item is sold in its own auction with burnt payments. Artificial-currency mechanisms give buyers personalized budgets of a currency worthless outside the mechanism, which they use to bid across items. The better of our separate-selling and artificial-currency mechanisms provides a 3.80-approximation to optimal consumer surplus. For additive buyers, the factor improves to 3. The artificial-currency guarantee holds at every Bayes--Nash equilibrium, without equilibrium selection. Either approach alone may capture only a vanishing share of the optimum. The proof decomposes benchmark surplus into a stable part captured by artificial currency and a variation bounded using separate selling.

papers.title: Stagewise and interpretable emergence of inside-outside computation in Transformer-based language models
papers.abstract: Variability in syntactic structure and parsing ambiguity are fundamental aspects of natural language which modern LLMs have to learn to deal with proficiently. Previous "post-mortem" studies have shown that fully trained Transformers indeed approximate canonical parsing algorithms such as inside-outside, but little is established theoretically about how this is actually learned. Here, we make a first step towards addressing this by studying the learning dynamics in synthetic context-free grammars with variable parse tree topology. The stagewise learning curves are fully interpretable, in the sense that all of the loss stages a) can be computed analytically, and b) can be clearly associated to the representation of a hidden latent tree variable, which allows to lift ambiguity and utilize information from wider contexts. By probing representations, we visualize the emergence of inside-outside computation across depth and during training: while during early stages local (bigram/trigram) information is used and involves only a few initial layers, gradually the Transformer develops an encoder-decoder structure where the most abstract latent information is encoded in the middle, and the latter half of the network is used to progressively refine the final token prediction. This organization of computation is reminiscent of findings in real-world LLMs, and importantly applies here to a synthetic model which allows full analytical control of the data statistics, thus opening the door to theoretical progress.

papers.title: Sable: A Small-Field Sumcheck Argument for Bit-Exact Inference of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: We present Sable, an argument system and single-GPU prover for the statement that a committed, integer-quantized transformer produced a given token sequence from a given prompt, bit for bit. Sable fixes an integer function F_O with no floating-point step, in which every rounding, normalization, softmax and sampling decision is determined by its inputs, and proves it with a constraint system whose relations provably never wrap modulo the 31-bit KoalaBear prime. The proof batches zerochecks and LogUp-GKR lookups into one sumcheck per domain, and commits to every witness tensor and weight in one multilinear commitment built from Reed-Solomon codes, BLAKE3 Merkle trees and a mixed-length BaseFold opening. The prover streams the model layer by layer on one GPU. On one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU, Sable proves all 64 layers of Qwen2.5-32B in 92.5 s for 4,096 tokens and 398 s for 16,384 tokens, and covers Qwen3-32B and the mixture-of-experts Qwen3-30B-A3B (4,096 tokens in 121.8 and 84.7 s). A proof costs 41 to 50 times the serving time, or 6.4 cents per 4,096-token request at public GPU prices, and 40 to 64 times less time per parameter and token than zkLLM.
