A paired subset asking the same questions of a synthesized and a human recording of each passage localises the effect in the ASR stage -- the end-to-end model's abstention behaviour does not move with the speaker, the cascade's goes from 11.1% to 65.9%. Reliance on synthesized speech has been named as a limitation of audio benchmarks but not quantified; we quantify it, and show it large enough to reverse a finding. Since no prompt we tested repairs the residual failure, we transfer pre-generation attention probing to the multimodal setting. A probe over frozen prompt representations reaches 0.773 AUROC at predicting which unanswerable questions the model will answer anyway, where semantic entropy over ten sampled generations is at chance: the model fabricates the same answer every time, so sample disagreement cannot see a failure it is confident about.

papers.title: Admissible balanced pairs over cleft extensions
papers.abstract: Let $(B, A, i, e, l)$ be a cleft extension of abelian categories such that $e$ has a right adjoint $r$. It is proved that $(C, D)$ is an admissible balanced pair in $B$ if and only if $(\operatorname{add}(lC), \operatorname{add}(rD))$ is an admissible balanced pair in $A$. When the extension is directed with respect to a finite product decomposition of $B$, the lifting of complete hereditary cotorsion pairs $(C, Y)$ and $(X, D)$ to $A$ is characterized by the vanishing of first derived functors. Under a compatibility condition, the pair of special classes $(Δ(C), \nabla(D))$ is then shown to be admissible balanced if and only if $(C, D)$ is. As an application, for rings $A, B$ and a $(B, A)$-bimodule $U$ of finite flat dimension over $A$ and finite projective dimension over $B$, the triangular matrix ring $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A & 0\\ U & B\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is left virtually Gorenstein if and only if $A$ and $B$ are.

papers.title: Stable-like Operators related to Bernstein Functions in weighted Lebesgue spaces: Boundedness, Regularity, Embedding, and Martingale Problem
papers.abstract: We study variable-coefficient nonlocal operators associated with a Bernstein function $ϕ$ satisfying global weak scaling conditions. Let $j_d^ϕ$ denote the radial Lévy density of the corresponding subordinate Brownian motion. The kernels may be nonsymmetric, and the coefficients are measurable in the jump variable and satisfy a prescribed uniform modulus of continuity in the spatial variable. In the critical scaling regime, we impose an annular cancellation condition. For jump profiles satisfying $0\le V(y)\le Cj_d^ϕ(|y|)$, we prove that the operator $\mathcal L_V^a$ is bounded from $H_p^{ϕ,2}(w)$ to $L_p(w)$ for every $1<p<\infty$ and $w\in A_p(\mathbb R^d)$. For $V(y)=j_d^ϕ(|y|)$ and uniformly positive real coefficients, we establish maximal regularity for parabolic equations in mixed-norm spaces with Muckenhoupt weights in space and time. The parabolic coefficients may be merely measurable in time. We also obtain elliptic resolvent estimates in weighted $L_p$ spaces for sufficiently large resolvent parameters. Under suitable integrability conditions, we prove a weighted Sobolev--Hölder embedding with an explicit local modulus of continuity in space and time. The modulus depends on $ϕ$, the integrability exponents, and the Muckenhoupt indices of the weights. Finally, we prove global well-posedness of the time-dependent martingale problem. For the resulting time-inhomogeneous strong Markov family, we derive a Krylov-type estimate in weighted mixed norms. Its local normalization involves the weighted measures of an intrinsic time interval and a spatial ball.

papers.title: A thermodynamically consistent variational formulation and structure-preserving finite element methods for non-isothermal liquid--vapor flows with moving contact lines
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a variational formulation and structure-preserving finite element methods for non-isothermal liquid--vapor flows with moving contact lines. Based on the dynamic van der Waals theory with gradient contributions and surface thermodynamics, the governing equations and hydrodynamic boundary conditions are derived from a generalized Hamilton's principle for nonequilibrium thermodynamics. Two equivalent variational formulations based on internal energy and Helmholtz free energy are developed, using entropy density and temperature, respectively, as the primary thermal variable. Using the resulting weak forms, compatible spatial operators and discrete thermodynamic chain rules, we construct two thermodynamically consistent fully discrete finite element schemes. We rigorously prove the following properties for both fully discrete schemes: mass conservation, bound preservation for the number density, positivity of the temperature, an exact total energy balance incorporating external work and heat exchange, and a temperature-weighted weak entropy inequality with nonnegative bulk and boundary entropy production. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions assess accuracy and structure preservation, with applications to non-isothermal droplet wetting, pool boiling and droplet ejection.

papers.title: PINE: Point, Instance and Normal Estimation in One-Step Diffusion Model
papers.abstract: Understanding a scene requires both geometry and semantics: geometry recovers its spatial structure, and semantics separates it into objects. Current models obtain the two from separate networks or separate passes. We present PINE, a one-step Omni Diffusion Transformer that predicts the point map, the surface normals, and the instance map of an image in one forward pass. PINE treats each map as a token stream, and a stream mask decides which streams interact. A camera-aware ray encoding positions every token by its camera ray rather than its pixel. Grounding attention adds the affinity of pretrained DINOv3 features to the attention logits. Trained on only 139K synthetic images for geometry, PINE achieves state-of-the-art point maps whether or not intrinsics are given and the best average rank on surface normals. It also exceeds SAM on large objects with less than 1 percent of its training images, and it predicts all three maps 5.7x faster than MoGe-3 with SAM.

papers.title: SpectralGS: Spectral Gaussian Splatting for Unsupervised Spectral Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: Unsupervised spectral super-resolution aims to recover spectral information from RGB images without paired hyperspectral data. However, the limited spectral information in RGB observations makes learning an effective spatial-spectral representation challenging, requiring the incorporation of structured spectral modeling with sensor imaging. In this paper, we propose SpectralGS, a spectral Gaussian splatting framework comprising two components: Shared Spectral Gaussian Representation and Spectral Response Projection Rendering. The representation module constructs a continuous spatial-spectral representation via shared spectral and local spatial Gaussian primitives, exploiting the low-rank spectral structure of hyperspectral images. The rendering module utilizes the spectral response function (SRF) to apply integral projection to the continuous representation, blending it to generate an RGB image. Consistency between the rendered and observed RGB images provides training supervision. Our main contribution is a Gaussian splatting framework that integrates structured continuous spatial-spectral representation with imaging response-based rendering, enabling unsupervised spectral reconstruction. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: A transitive $C^{1+α}$ surface diffeomorphism with positive entropy has at most one measure of maximal entropy
papers.abstract: Let $0<α\le 1$. On a closed surface, every topologically transitive $C^{1+α}$ diffeomorphism with positive topological entropy has at most one measure of maximal entropy.

papers.title: On the Number Theory of the Greeks. II. Gauss's Lemmas and Riesz Domains
papers.abstract: In the second part of our article on Euclid's four number theorem we start from the notion of incommensurability and take a closer look at irrationality proofs for algebraic numbers. Along the way we encounter Gauss's Lemma, integral closure and Dedekind's Prague theorem, and finally we arrive back at the four number theorem.

papers.title: Exploiting Queue Information for Quality of Services Routing in SDN Networks
papers.abstract: Routing costs determine how deterministic networks allocate feasible queue resources to successive flow requests. We propose a topology-aware cost that combines normalized network-calculus post-admission delay and backlog bounds with static path diversity and shortest-path load concentration. Their product weights the backlog premium above a delay baseline within a shared queue-level routing, LARAC, and admission-control framework. Across ten paired runs, the proposed cost admits 657.7, 478.9, and 168.2 more flows than Max-Risk on Polska, NSFNET, and COST266, respectively; the corresponding 95% confidence intervals exclude zero. Germany50 shows a smaller gain of 67.6 flows with an interval crossing zero. The proposed cost has the highest mean acceptance among five costs on three of the four topologies. Gains are accompanied by comparable or lower mean hop counts and cannot be explained simply by higher aggregate utilization. On 100-1000-node networks, risk-aware costs remain comparatively stable while delay-only acceptance declines. A centralized SDN realization reduces distributed control and protocol-state overhead, while large-scale results expose the associated routing-performance tradeoff.

papers.title: Optimizer or physics? Machine-learning surrogates for collision-based preparation of multipartite entangled quantum states
papers.abstract: Repeated partial-SWAP collisions can prepare symmetric Dicke states, including the $W$ state, without measurement or postselection. The collision sequence uses only two global collision angles, and its fidelity is evaluated after a final layer of local phase rotations is optimized numerically, so each candidate pair requires a many-qubit simulation and a phase fit. We study when learned surrogates reduce the number of such evaluations, and what limits the best-found fidelity, for 65 Dicke targets with 11--20 qubits in noiseless simulations. At 50 evaluations per target, Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization (GP-BO) exceeds fixed Sobol and grid designs by 0.088 and 0.063 in mean best-found fidelity. Bounded Nelder--Mead reaches 0.760 against 0.762 for GP-BO, and has the higher three-seed mean on 41 of the 61 targets with a reference value; in this two-parameter problem, adaptivity matters far more than the choice between the two methods. A neural-network ensemble pretrained on 750 observations from smaller systems needs 32\% fewer new evaluations per target than GP-BO at comparable fidelity, but the full neural search takes 1.6 times the wall time of GP-BO in our implementation. In a separate source-only test, the best of five neural proposals per target exceeds the best of five population-model proposals by 0.070 in mean fidelity. Exact symmetries and state diagnostics help explain why the leading adaptive methods reach similar family-mean fidelities. The collisions conserve the magnitude of the bare Dicke overlap and the total-spin weights, and for the best controls on a 12-target diagnostic panel, 79% of the infidelity is an amplitude deficit that a final phase layer cannot remove, which motivates interleaved phase control.

papers.title: Self-Refining VLA Sampling
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models typically use flow-based generative modeling to learn a rich, often multimodal, distribution of robot actions. Generating samples from flow-based methods involves iteratively updating random noise, and distinct noise samples from the same state can result in distinct trajectories and task outcomes. Existing test-time scaling methods improve action chunk generation via selection, aggregation, or correction, but commonly require the generation of large ensembles of candidates or the training of an external corrector. We adapt Predict-and-Perturb (P&P), a self-refinement procedure for flow-based models originally used for mode-seeking in video generation, to the robotics domain. We find that applying P&P to VLA models requires modifications to the refinement process used in video generation due to differences in the underlying structure of the data. Across 400 episodes of LIBERO evaluated using SmolVLA, P&P improves upon the stock baseline by 5.3 percentage points. Further, episode-level P\&P uncertainty correlates strongly with task failure (AUC 0.851).

papers.title: Turbulence Strength Estimation from Multiplexed Orbital Angular Momentum Beams Using Multimode Fibre Speckle
papers.abstract: The strength of atmospheric turbulence governs how much the modes of a free-space optical link mix together. It is usually measured with a separate instrument or with a Gaussian probe beam, neither of which uses the beams that a structured-light link already carries. Here we show that the turbulence strength, expressed as the Fried parameter, can be estimated directly from multiplexed orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams without knowing which modes are present. The beams pass through a passive multimode fibre that turns them into speckle on a camera, and a trained weighted sum of the camera pixels (known as an extreme learning machine), averaged over a few tens of frames, gives the Fried parameter. In the laboratory with emulated turbulence, superpositions of up to eleven OAM modes give an estimate as accurate as that from a Gaussian probe beam sent through the same fibre. In all but weak turbulence the estimate is also more accurate than an ideal Strehl meter or an ideal tip/tilt sensor, providing an efficient way to estimate turbulence strength in mode-division multiplexed systems.

papers.title: Gaussian Belief Propagation and Periodic Jacobi Matrices on Trees: Spectral Curve, Antibound Poles, and Fixed Points
papers.abstract: Diagonal Green functions of a periodic Jacobi operator on a universal covering tree satisfy the scalar Gaussian belief propagation covariance equations on the finite connected loopless base multigraph. At cycle rank at least two, the Green functions continue to simple antibound poles at both Perron values for arbitrary real potentials and nonzero real weights. This proves the conjecture of Christiansen, Simon and Zinchenko. For positive weights the pole result includes self-loops. On loopless graphs the lower pole is the walk-summability threshold. Each energy strictly between it and the spectral bottom has at least two fixed points with positive definite local beliefs. On a connected simple graph, some coefficients yield a compact component of positive solutions exactly when the graph contains two vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs of cycle rank at least two. The covariance curve is generically irreducible, with one sheet per edge subset with no vertex of degree one. For cycle rank at least two and generic real coefficients, the diagonal Green functions, infinite half-tree $m$-functions and the density-of-states Stieltjes transform all have this degree, answering a question of Avni, Breuer and Simon. Then all eigenvalues of the signed Jacobi matrices are antibound poles. Signed principal submatrices classify finite points with nonzero residue of $(\sum_i V_i) dz$, where $V_i$ are the vertex variances. We give a genus formula. Near zero potentials and unit weights on $K_4$, independently varying the coefficients leaves the cover spectrum an interval. This refutes Avni, Breuer and Simon's conjecture on the density of parameters with all gaps open. In block models, generic irreducibility and a uniqueness criterion extend, and at uniform dimension $p$ the degree can exceed $L^p$ for scalar degree $L$. Part of the scalar theory is formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

papers.title: On the number theory of the Greeks. I. The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
papers.abstract: In this article we present Euclid's fundamental theorem of number theory and give evidence for the claim that this theorem, which is largely unknown today, was as familiar to number theorists before Gauss as the Gaussian version of the fundamental theorem is to us.

papers.title: On mesh transfers and time error estimation in adaptive finite element methods for parabolic problems
papers.abstract: In space and time adaptive finite element methods, the discrete solution is transferred onto a different mesh whenever the spatial mesh changes. Refinement is commonly regarded as harmless, since nodal interpolation then reproduces the discrete solution exactly. However, we show that for the implicit Euler method applied to the heat equation, the transferred solution and time derivative, in general, violate the discrete equation on the new mesh. Unless the resulting transfer residual vanishes, the corresponding time error estimator overestimates the local error, for small time steps, by a factor inversely proportional to the time step size. To address this issue, we propose transfers based on the elliptic reconstruction, which significantly reduce the transfer residual or even remove it. In numerical experiments, we confirm the analysis and demonstrate the advantages of the proposed transfers in a space and time adaptive example.

papers.title: Dynamic Renewal for Hydrodynamic Coupling in Ciliary Mucus Transport
papers.abstract: Mucociliary clearance in large mammalian airways involves millimetric MUC5B-rich mucus strands that emerge from submucosal glands approximately aligned with the direction of transport. These strands are observed downstream in cross-flow networks. Recently, Bos et al. [PNAS Nexus 2, pgad388 (2023)] modeled single strand reorientation using a free-draining coupling for the flow induced by cilia. This leaves unresolved whether the strand's own disturbance of the surrounding liquid assists or frustrates the turning. Here, we develop the methodology to address this question. An immersed-boundary coupling is combined with a Fourier-space Stokes solver and a bespoke dynamic-renewal algorithm that exposes the strand to new ciliary domain without enlarging the simulation volume. This allows us to overcome one of the multiscale challenges posed by mucociliary clearance. We find that hydrodynamic interactions result in only a limited decrease in the rate of reorientation, which supports the use of the free-draining approximation. Future work can build on the methodological foundation introduced here to study collective strand dynamics.

papers.title: Contact Harness: Enabling VLM Agents to Perform Contact-Rich Manipulation
papers.abstract: Agents built on pretrained VLMs have demonstrated zero-shot control of real robots, but vision alone is often insufficient for reliable contact-state assessment in contact-rich manipulation. Force and tactile feedback provide complementary information, but their semantic ambiguity makes them difficult for agents to use directly. These signals must be interpreted according to their physical meaning, together with task phase and visual evidence. We propose Contact Harness, which uses reusable, optimized skills to guide a VLM agent in assessing contact states from multimodal feedback and selecting subsequent actions. A compliant execution mechanism regulates in-contact motions using real-time force feedback. The framework requires no model fine-tuning, task demonstrations, or simulation training. We conduct zero-shot real-robot evaluations using GPT-6 Astra on Rokae and Franka robots. With a single prompt skill, Contact Harness achieves a full-insertion rate of 90.7% across 15 connector types, with further evaluations on a real PC under variations in lighting, background, and position. Across four additional contact-rich tasks, including whiteboard wiping, writing, peeling, and pivoting, Contact Harness achieves an average success rate of 100%. On six simulated tasks, Contact Harness reaches 96.7% success, compared with at most 68.3% for pretrained VLA baselines fine-tuned on task demonstrations, showing the potential of agent-based manipulation for contact-rich real-world deployment.

papers.title: Chameleon: Exploring Risk Interpretation through Scene-Matched Textures in Virtual Reality
papers.abstract: Users in virtual reality need to judge contact risks around physical objects while remaining engaged in the virtual scene. Scene-matched textures give physical objects a place in virtual reality and provide visual cues for interaction. We examine how Chameleon's risk-aware textures are perceived during a reaching task. A study with 42 participants compared scanned appearances with red warnings, uniform environment textures, and risk-aware scene-matched textures. Participants rated the risk-aware condition more favorably on four aspects of perceived cue clarity than both alternatives. Interviews connected visible warnings with initial caution and linked confidence in physical interaction to material expectations and intended actions. Awareness of an object's location did not necessarily imply confidence in interacting with it. These findings motivate risk cues that connect depicted materials to the physical properties relevant to an intended action, and ways to support verification during interaction.

papers.title: MusicListenBench: Can Audio LLMs Hear the Difference Yet?
papers.abstract: Audio large language models (LLMs) are typically evaluated on song genre, mood, and instrumentation. A more basic skill is telling whether two short clips play the same melody, chord or instrument. We introduce MusicListenBench, a benchmark of paired listening tests for melody, harmony, timbre, and tempo. Each test item comes with two variants. A FLIP variant changes the music, so the answer must change. A STAY variant changes only the sound, such as room echo or hiss, so the answer must stay the same. The two variants have opposite answers, so a model that ignores the audio scores 50%, whatever letter it prefers. The benchmark has a training split and two test sets, one rendered from symbolic music with exact labels and one built from real recordings. On the rendered test, seven of eight open audio LLMs score within 4 points of this floor. Of four commercial models, both GPT-Audio models are at chance, and the best, Gemini 2.5 Pro, reaches 74.2%, 12.8 points below human listeners (87.0%). Post-training with GRPO on 10k rendered clean pairs raises Qwen2.5-Omni from 61.2% to 99.0% on held-out clean pairs, and the gain transfers to a task left out of training. On FLIP/STAY, however, it only reaches the level of our listeners (86.0%). It now misses almost no change (1.9%, against 24.7% for Gemini 2.5 Pro), yet when only the sound changes, it turns a correct answer into a wrong one 25.7\% of the time. More than half of its false flips come from a quiet background hiss. Models learn to hear a difference much faster than they learn which differences matter. On real recordings, open models again stay near chance, and the trained model calls 27 of 42 pairs of two strums of the same chord different. Adding sound-only pairs to training lowers false flips on both test sets, but no training run teaches relative pitch. We release the data, code, and an open leaderboard.

papers.title: Checking the Cumulative Exposure Model: Cumulative Chi-Squared Goodness-of-Fit Tests for Interval-Monitored Step-Stress Life Tests
papers.abstract: In an interval-monitored step-stress life test the data are the numbers of devices that fail between consecutive inspections. These cells are ordered in time, but the usual goodness-of-fit check, Pearson's statistic, ignores the order. We propose goodness-of-fit tests based on the cumulative residuals, the differences between the empirical and the fitted distribution functions at the inspection times, with the parameters estimated by the minimum density power divergence estimator. The two statistics are Taguchi's cumulative chi-squared statistic and its version with constant weights, the classical members of a family of cumulative divergences for ordered categories, with the null probabilities replaced by those of the fitted model. For the exponential cumulative exposure model with a log-linear link we prove the existence, uniqueness and consistency of the estimator under explicit conditions, and we derive the limit distribution of the statistics under the null hypothesis and under contiguous alternatives: a weighted chi-square distribution with $L-s$ terms, where $L$ is the number of inspection times and $s$ the number of parameters. The critical values are obtained by plugging the estimated weights into Imhof's formula, and the procedure has asymptotic size $α$. A local-power analysis and a simulation study show that the cumulative statistics are more powerful than Pearson's statistic against a wrong lifetime distribution, and that the limit distribution is accurate already with $50$ devices. An application to light bulbs tested under step voltage illustrates the method.

papers.title: Five-dimensional homogeneous Riemannian manifolds with harmonic curvature are Ricci-parallel
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that 5-dimensional homogeneous Riemannian manifolds with harmonic curvature are Ricci-parallel.

papers.title: Emotion-Aware and Context-Grounded Dialogue Agents for Personalized Video Game Interactions
papers.abstract: We present ChatNPC, a game companion that dynamically personalizes its responses in real time based on players' emotional shifts to enhance user immersion. The model integrates sequential data, leveraging the dynamic nature of streams to benefit from player information, spoken lines, and in-game context. We leverage recent progress in LLMs' tool-calling capabilities to extract vital information from memory and recognize potential constraints for accurate reasoning, thereby tackling the complexity of NPC conversation scenarios. The task is divided into a game sentinel-guided agent (SeGent), a memory capability, and a chat planning tool for reasoning instantiation. The approach uses a lightweight game template as an information framework, with relevant details and a thorough reasoning layout. We conduct extensive experiments on a newly developed game dataset for in-game context NPC dialogue and demonstrate that ChatNPC sequentially captures players' emotional shifts over time; responses are more naturalistic and human-like with appropriate conversational cues, pauses, and sighs; and utterances remain faithful to the dynamics of in-game context and player actions, supporting narrative continuity.

papers.title: Transient Impact Force and Spreading Dynamics of Droplets Impacting Spherical Surfaces
papers.abstract: Droplet impacts on spherical surfaces are encountered in processes such as spray cooling, anti-icing, and spray deposition. The curvature of the impact target changes the spreading path of the droplet and the impact force, leading to more complex kinematic and transient force dynamics. This study employs a numerical model utilizing the volume of fluid approach to investigate the spreading, retraction, rebound and deposition characteristics of droplets impinging on spherical surfaces. The roles of wall wettability, spherical curvature, Weber number, and Ohnesorge number on droplet spreading and wall impact force are analyzed. The results show that the wall impact force exhibits two peaks in the complete rebound and partial rebound modes, whereas the second peak disappears in the complete deposition mode. Further parametric analysis shows that increasing the contact angle, i.e., decreasing wettability, reduces both the maximum spreading length and the contact time, and significantly changes the second peak of the impact force. Under complete rebound mode, the relationship between the contact time and the contact angle can be expressed as ${{{t}_{\text{c}}}}/{{{t}_{σ}}}\;={{C}_{1}}\left[ {{\left( 1-\cos {{θ}_{\text{eq}}} \right)}^{{-1}/{2}\;}}-{1}/{\sqrt{2}} \right]+{{C}_{2}}$, where $C_1$ and $C_2$ are constants. Within the investigated curvature range, increasing the dimensionless curvature reduces the critical contact angle required for complete rebound. The dimensionless first peak of the impact force decreases with increasing the Weber number and finally approaches a constant, following a relationship of $F_{\text{t}1}^{*}={{β}_{1}}+{{β}_{2}}W{{e}^{-1}}$, where ${{β}_{1}}$ and ${{β}_{2}}$ are constants. Increasing the Ohnesorge number reduces the maximum spreading length, prolongs the contact time, and slightly increases the first peak of impact force.

papers.title: On linear MMSE receivers in the presence of data-like multiuser interference
papers.abstract: Linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) receivers have been of great interest for many decades for multi-user interference (MUI) mitigation in radiocommunications networks in particular. Despite the extensive literature on this subject, this topic remains relevant to several current and emerging applications. In this context, the paper presents a continuous-time approach showing that most of LMME receivers of the literature are suboptimal. In particular, they are typically implemented at the symbol rate following matched filtering to the pulse-shaping filter and require a prior knowledge of the MUI channels, which can be difficult and costly to acquire in practice. The main contribution of this paper is to address the key challenge of designing new LMMSE receivers that achieve the performance of the optimal receiver without requiring prior knowledge of the MUI channels. To this end, two novel receiver LMMSE structures are proposed and analyzed for linearly modulated signals impaired by data-like MUI: a two-input receiver and a three-input receiver. The proposed receivers are shown to be quasi-optimal over a broad range of scenarios. These results provide new perspectives for practical implementation of the optimal LMMSE receiver in the presence of data-like MUI, relying only on knowledge of the signal-of-interest (SOI) channel.

papers.title: ClothCast: Generative Cloth World Modeling under Partial Observability
papers.abstract: World models support robotic manipulation by predicting how the scene evolves under a planned action. For garments this prediction is notoriously difficult: deformations are complex, and self-occlusion leaves much of the cloth unobserved. Planned gripper trajectories provide a useful motion prior because cloth held by a gripper moves with it, while the remaining deformation must be predicted. We introduce ClothCast, a world model that applies this prior to the cloth's points and learns the residual motion. ClothCast takes one RGB-D observation, the camera pose, the robot's own model and the planned gripper trajectories, with no cloth mesh or material parameters. It lifts the observation to a layered point set that includes hypothesized occluded layers, carries the points with a blended rigid prior derived from the gripper poses, and predicts the residual motion with a video-diffusion point-flow model. Over entire 4- to 11-second episodes at 10 Hz, the moved points are rendered into depth, from which a geometry-conditioned completion model synthesizes RGB; after release, a hand-designed settling step replaces the learned motion. We further release ClothCastBench, 10,000 simulated dual-arm cloth-manipulation episodes with the ground-truth cloth mesh, including occluded layers, at every frame. On 492 held-out episodes, ClothCast achieves 2.5x lower sequence-averaged visible-surface Chamfer distance than Flex-π, the strongest baseline in geometry (14.0 mm vs. 35.6 mm), and 3.7 dB higher cloth-region PSNR than Cosmos-Predict2.5, the strongest baseline in cloth PSNR. On a 50-episode ablation subset, the rigid prior alone, applied to ClothCast's learned initial geometry with the same post-processing, already outperforms both geometry-capable baselines, and the learned residual lowers its error by about a third.

papers.title: SAE-Audit: Clinical-Trial Prediction via Inference-Time Optimization of Black-Box LLMs Audited by Sparse Autoencoder Evidence
papers.abstract: Clinical trials are costly and often take years to complete, making early outcome prediction valuable for trial planning. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to forecast clinical-trial outcomes, yet their predictions remain unreliable and their rationales may not faithfully reflect the evidence underlying their answers. On tasks such as predicting whether a registered clinical trial will complete or terminate early, frontier LLMs perform only modestly above chance in our experiments. We introduce SAE-Audit, which optimizes a black-box LLM at inference time with evidence obtained from a deployable open model. A frozen sparse autoencoder (SAE) on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is converted into a vocabulary of clinical concepts. Sparse probes fitted on past trials determine which concepts are associated with the outcome. For a new protocol, the concepts detected by the probe are written as evidence, each with the direction and strength of its association with the outcome, and the LLM being audited optimizes its answer in the light of this evidence. Without additional training, SAE-Audit raises balanced accuracy of deepseek-v4-flash by 9.6--12.0 points on five clinical-trial prediction tasks and raises GPT-5.6-terra by 8.0 points on trial completion, exceeding other agentic inference-time optimization methods by a large margin. As an auxiliary, SAE probes module within SAE-Audit is itself accurate and auditable, providing natural-language explanations directly derived from verified concept contributions and protocol evidence, without requiring additional LLMs at inference time. SAE-Audit provides verifiable, concept-level evidence for more accurate and auditable clinical-trial prediction. It can also be embedded into biomedical AI agents such as Biomni to optimize their performance.

papers.title: BenchMint: From Real-World Tasks to Executable Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) need evaluations of everyday reasoning and tool use, such as planning itineraries under user constraints and grounding numerical answers in evidence. We introduce BenchMint, an automated benchmark-construction workflow, and Daily-Life, its collection of 100 selected tasks across 11 real-world domains. BenchMint jointly constructs tasks and scoring criteria from the same source documents. Language-model judges assess possible answers against these criteria using tool traces and private evidence. We report 26 model/harness configurations, including GPT, Claude and Gemini families; 17 have complete domain profiles. These are descriptive configuration results, not a controlled model ranking. In one selected travel task, we corrected the reference total from 320 to 380 minutes while keeping both answers unchanged. The incorrect answer's arithmetic verdict switched from pass to fail; the correct answer's switched from fail to pass. With one ballot per cell, this exposes a reference error without establishing repeatability or collection-wide validity. Incomplete construction comparisons establish no general advantage of joint authoring or feedback-guided revision.

papers.title: Scenario Compliant Indoor Pedestrian Trajectory Reconstruction from Partial Observation
papers.abstract: Pedestrian trajectory reconstruction is vital for applications ranging from security surveillance to indoor navigation. While existing probabilistic and generative frameworks have shown success in outdoor GPS-based trajectory imputation, they often fail in indoor settings where movement is strictly governed by dense geometric constraints such as walls and corridors. Standard models typically treat trajectories as unconstrained coordinate sequences, leading to physically infeasible paths with high collision rates. To address this, we propose a map-conditioned generative framework based on conditional diffusion models. Our approach explicitly integrates dense scenario maps as structured spatial inputs via a CNN-based encoder, allowing environmental geometry to guide the iterative denoising process. Furthermore, we employ an endpoint-aware mechanism by embedding observations (start and end points) directly into the scenario map, providing critical spatial anchors through image-level features. Experiments on simulated indoor trajectories and the real-world Shopper trajectory dataset, with three training seeds, show that our method achieves the lowest errors among the compared generative methods. Scene conditioning reduces the collision and invalid rates by 19\% and 46\% on the simulated dataset, whereas on real shopper data the gains are consistent but small, mainly because the model rarely learns to route around obstacles between the endpoints. Compared with a shortest-path planner, which never collides, our method better captures the variability of real motion (31\% lower CRPS), but the timing of stops is reconstructed only partially. These results show that explicit environmental context improves physical consistency, while reconstructing realistic human motion in real indoor spaces remains challenging. Our code is available at https://github.com/dang-qi/trajectory_reconstruction

papers.title: Probabilistic Timed Automata with Multiple Sure and Threshold Objectives
papers.abstract: Probabilistic timed automata extend the classical timed automata formalism with discrete probabilistic choice over edges. We consider the case of the verification of a combination of multiple objectives of probabilistic timed automata, where the objectives can be non-probabilistic (referring to sure satisfaction of all behaviors) and probabilistic (referring to a probability threshold), and refer to reachability or $ω$-regular properties on executions expressed using parity conditions. We show that existing algorithms for multiple objectives for finite-state Markov decision processes can be applied, using the classical region-graph construction, to obtain algorithms for the corresponding objectives of probabilistic timed automata. In particular, the verification of a probabilistic timed automata against multiple probabilistic-threshold sink-reachability objectives subject to the almost-sure divergence of time is EXPTIME-complete, while verification against the combination of a sure property, including sure divergence of time, and a single probabilistic-threshold parity objective is in NEXPTIME $\cap$ coNEXPTIME.

papers.title: SleepXA: Composing Pretrained Neural and Cardiac Foundation Models for Sleep Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Physiological signals recorded during sleep provide synchronized views of neural, cardiac, respiratory, and other bodily systems, while preserving modality-specific information. Existing EEG and ECG foundation models already capture rich but distinct physiological structure, motivating an alternative to training a multimodal sleep model from scratch: composing existing pretrained models. We introduce SleepXA, a framework that uses synchronized polysomnography (PSG) to compose independently pretrained neural and cardiac foundation models. SleepXA combines pretrained EEG and ECG encoders with lightweight encoders for additional PSG modalities, and learns shared and modality-specific representations through sleep-guided alignment. We pretrain SleepXA on 9,230 overnight PSG recordings from three large cohorts and evaluate it on 27 downstream tasks spanning sleep representation, clinical and disease prediction, and daytime physiological transfer. SleepXA ranks among the top two methods on 22 of 27 tasks. Controlled experiments further show consistent benefits across sensor configurations and EEG-ECG backbone choices, while pretrained initialization outperforms architecture-matched training from scratch and SleepXA surpasses alternative multimodal composition strategies. These results suggest that synchronized multimodal physiology can serve as a natural interface for composing existing physiological foundation models, yielding reusable representations that extend beyond sleep to clinical and daytime physiological settings.

papers.title: Is the learner or the summary the limit? Auditing machine-learning energy reconstruction for air-shower arrays on KASCADE and GRAPES-3
papers.abstract: Machine-learning energy estimators for cosmic-ray arrays are usually trained on a few fitted shower parameters, not station signals. When their resolution stops improving, standard diagnostics cannot say whether a better model would help or the summary has run out of information. We use a five-step audit that compares trained models with a learner-independent estimate of the lowest error the summary allows (its squared-loss Bayes risk, or floor), tests which inputs add information and flags inputs merely computed from the fit. We apply it to public KASCADE simulations with three hadronic-interaction models (QGSJET-II-04, EPOS-LHC and SIBYLL-2.3d), to 13,848,509 measured KASCADE events and to simulated GRAPES-3 events. Within known energy decades below 10^16 eV, gradient boosting on nine reconstructed features is within 2.2% of the estimated floor under every estimator setting, so more capacity is not expected to gain more than about 2%. The floor is an estimate, accurate to about 1% in a semi-synthetic benchmark with intervals that under-cover, and not a bound on the true Bayes risk. Replacing reconstructed by true particle numbers removes 70 to 72% of the error variance below 10^15 eV and 24 to 26% between 10^16 and 10^17 eV on all three models, yet simulated station signals close about a tenth of that gap. On GRAPES-3, networks given images rendered from the fit do no better than the fit. In measured data, the mean muon size at fixed electron size lies within every model's proton-to-iron bracket and a label-free probe finds the muon channel used as in simulation; neither fixes the energy scale. Energy-labelled results are simulated.

papers.title: Renormalization-group analysis of two-dimensional long-range XY models with $p$-fold anisotropy: the $σ=2$ boundary
papers.abstract: The two-dimensional classical XY model with $1/r^{2+σ}$ interactions has recently been shown to undergo, at the marginal case $σ=2$, a continuous transition into a logarithmic quasi-long-range-ordered (log-QLRO) phase where the correlation decays as $C(r) \sim (\ln r)^{-η_\ell}$. We study how a $p$-fold field $h_p\cos(pθ)$ modifies this picture. Using the physical vortex and $p$-fold field fugacities, we construct a unified set of renormalization-group (RG) equations that interpolate between the short-range (SR) and long-range (LR) cases through an LR coupling parameter $κ$. For $p<4$, the small-$h_p$ perturbative treatment breaks down and the critical behavior lies beyond the present RG treatment. For $p>4$, the field is irrelevant at the pure fixed point, but at low temperature the LR enhancement drives the stiffness upward: log-QLRO appears only as a finite-scale crossover, and the only transition is the continuous one from the disordered into the $p$-fold-ordered phase. For $p=4$, the fixed line shifts from the SR Ashkin-Teller form, and the transition into the fourfold-ordered phase has a nonuniversal correlation-length exponent depending on both $κ$ and $h_4$. These results support the $σ_*=2$ boundary, in contrast to Sak's criterion.

papers.title: Beyond Attention Maps: Understanding and Improving Medical MLLMs via Visual Values
papers.abstract: Current MLLM methods largely focus on whether models attend to the right visual regions, implicitly treating spatial attention map as the primary key of effective visual perception. To examine this assumption, we introduce a medical VQA dataset with paired non-contrast (NC) and contrast-enhanced (CE) images that share corresponding anatomy while providing different cues. We show that this view is incomplete: across paired NC and CE medical images, MLLMs often exhibit similar attention patterns despite producing contrasting answers, while controlled bidirectional interventions induce substantially larger prediction changes on visual values than attention weights. These results identify the visual content retrieved through values as a critical factor in improving perception beyond spatial attention alone. Guided by this finding, we propose VIVID (VIsual Value Intervention Distillation), which uses enhanced visual values to identify and refine teacher corrections aligned with useful visual evidence to improve on-policy distillation from CE to NC images. Across six internal and external test sets, VIVID consistently outperforms existing on-policy distillation methods across different model scales and architectures, requires only NC images at inference, and maintains strong zero-shot performance on general-domain VQA benchmarks. The project page is available at https://qiuzyc.github.io/VIVID.

papers.title: Collineations of particles as a tool to study nucleation and crystallization processes in liquids
papers.abstract: We suggest several methods that can be used for identification of crystal nuclei in the studies of the nucleation and crystallization processes in multicomponent systems and in situations when the forming crystalline phase is different from the FCC, HCP or BCC lattices. We suggest several methods that can be used for identification of crystal nuclei in the studies of the nucleation and crystallization processes in multicomponent systems and in situations when the forming crystalline phase is different from the FCC, HCP or BCC lattices. The approaches are based on consideration of collineations of particles. They allow finding nuclei and separating them from each other. We demonstrate the methods by considering two systems. For a single-component system, we perform a comparison between the results derived from the collineations and those obtained using the coarse-grained bond-orientational order parameters. Further, we illustrate the methods by considering the crystallization process in a Wahnström binary $BA_2$ system forming a rather complex crystal structure.

papers.title: Approximation of Semigroups of Random Processes on a Hilbert Space
papers.abstract: This paper develops Chernoff-type approximation methods for strongly continuous and bi-continuous semigroups of operators arising in the stochastic dynamics of quantum systems. The main focus is on applying Chernoff iterations to Markov semigroups of multiplicative random processes on separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. The justification of the passage from discrete quantum measurements to continuous ones depends essentially on the choice of topology and function spaces. We propose conditions for convergence to bi-continuous semigroups on subspaces that weaken the classical requirements of the Chernoff theorem. The existence of the limiting bi-continuous semigroup is established in each of the three cases: commutation of the approximating operators, their asymptotic commutation, and uniform convergence of difference quotients over a family of approximating operators. For diffusive models with a generator having bounded coefficients, the derivative of the approximating function is computed explicitly on the subspace of test functions with rapidly decreasing second derivative; the limitations of applicability of this result are discussed. Applications to generalized models of continuous imprecise quantum measurement with unbounded observables, as well as to Poisson and diffusion processes, are outlined as directions for further research.

papers.title: Two Primes Suffice for Definable Graph Canonisation
papers.abstract: We study inflationary fixed-point logic on finite simple graphs with unordered vertices and an ordered number sort. For a prime $r$, the quantifier $M_r$ tests whether the number of relations satisfying a formula is nonzero modulo $r$. For any distinct primes $p$ and $q$, the logic with $M_p$ and $M_q$ defines the adjacency matrix of a canonical copy on the number sort. On labelled inputs this matrix is computable in deterministic polynomial time with an oracle that tests whether the number of satisfying assignments of a Boolean circuit is nonzero modulo $p$. For each prime $p$, the logic with $M_p$ alone cannot define a canonical copy on all graphs. The primes also differ on Boolean queries. There is a single first-order formula $β(S)$ on vertex sets such that $M_q S β(S)$ is undefinable with $M_p$ alone whenever $p \ne q$. For a positive integer-valued function $g$, consider the class of all graphs $G$ with at most $g(|V(G)|)$ automorphisms. For each fixed prime $p$, the logic with $M_p$ canonises this class exactly when $g$ is bounded.

papers.title: Realizability and tunability of synchronized optical soliton collision patterns
papers.abstract: Synchronizing the positions and phases of colliding optical solitons can maximize the amplitude at the collision center, producing a large-amplitude localized wave. We investigate whether multiple prescribed synchronized collisions can be jointly realized within a single multisoliton field and to what extent their relative retarded times and propagation distances can be varied continuously while preserving synchronization. Ideal optical fiber propagation is modeled here by the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation with zero boundary conditions. For distinct discrete eigenvalues, we derive an affine system of equations constraining the collision event positions to determine whether the synchronization conditions at different events can be satisfied simultaneously. Furthermore, for a fixed discrete spectrum and a realizable complete collision organization in which each soliton pair participates in exactly one event, continuous tuning of the relative event positions while preserving synchronization requires collinearity of the auxiliary spectral points constructed from the discrete eigenvalues. When these points are noncollinear, only uniform translations of all event centers are possible. Any three-soliton spectrum with distinct soliton velocities and noncollinear auxiliary spectral points supports both a collective collision and a rigid fully pairwise collision organization. A physically admissible four-soliton family with collinear auxiliary spectral points demonstrates continuous internal tunability.

papers.title: Automatic Construction of Persian E-Commerce Dialogue Datasets for Conversational Product Search
papers.abstract: Conversational product search lets users find products through a multi-turn dialogue instead of a single keyword query, but Persian lacks the large conversational datasets needed to train and evaluate such systems; existing Persian e-commerce dialogue resources cover few categories and small catalogs. We present a framework that builds such a dataset automatically from a real e-commerce catalog and release the resulting dataset. The framework crawls 12,926 products in seven categories of the Digikala marketplace, groups them into 170 semantically coherent clusters, and selects the question the assistant asks at every turn with the Regularized Partition Balance (RPB) score. The RPB score accounts for feature coverage, the probability that the user can answer and the number of values, and generalizes entropy-based question selection. An LLM then verbalizes each question plan into a natural Persian dialogue. In a simulation on the full catalog, the RPB score needs 0.11 fewer turns than the strongest entropy baseline when the difficulty of answering differs between features, and is practically equivalent to it when it does not. Using only a free LLM API, we generated 1,000 requirement-driven dialogues covering all 170 clusters, with turn-level feature annotations; automatic checks and an LLM judge confirm their consistency with the catalog, while their realism is lower than that of the first, GPT-4o-generated version. Code and data are publicly available.

papers.title: Polytropos: What Do Vision-Language Model Descriptions Make of a Cultural Object?
papers.abstract: Vision-language models have become a new kind of describer, writing about almost anything people see, and their descriptions now shape how cultures are known by people and by other models. Descriptions of cultures tend to turn particular things into types, and what a description loses shows what its describer lacks. We introduce Polytropos, a benchmark that measures what model descriptions of cultural objects keep of the particular object by turning each description back into an image and comparing it with the original photograph. On 374 objects from the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Getty, with 1,870 descriptions from five models and 230 written by curators, reconstructions are recognised as the recorded culture more often than the photographs, at 54.55% to 59.09% against 52.14%, yet 16% to 21% of objects change outcome and only 0.49% of reconstructions are identified as the specific object. On the same objects, models lose recorded cultures at a rate similar to curators but gain more. Model descriptions give each object many faces, each typical of its culture and almost none the object itself.

papers.title: Endpoint-Conditioned Process Value: What an Endpoint-Blind Process Score Adds Once Terminal Status and Cost Are Known
papers.abstract: Trajectory metrics promise information beyond final-answer accuracy, but no one has measured what a process score adds once an evaluation knows the outcome and the cost. We build that comparison: a sealed consequence needing an artifact neither agent nor judge ever sees, an operational baseline of terminal status and cost, and judge scale and evidence access as experimental factors. On 1,255 trajectories over 158 test-generation tasks in 7 Python repositories, the answer is gated on the judge. Four judges from 4B to 14B, one reasoning before scoring, add nothing an interval separates from zero; a Qwen3 32B judge on identical trajectories adds +0.050 AUC (95% CI [+0.020, +0.081]) and survives a refitting bootstrap ([+0.013, +0.095]). Most of what it adds is recoverable from eight behavioural counters, so a harness should log them (the judge adds +0.020 beyond them). What the judge is shown moves it further: disclosing the terminal verdict inflates its standalone discrimination by +0.103, while reference disclosure and tool-output redaction move it by nothing an interval separates from zero. A process metric reported without the judge's scale and evidence access does not identify a quantity. We release the protocol, the sealed-endpoint harness, and all trajectories.

papers.title: NPUFHE: An Efficient CKKS Execution System for Ascend NPUs
papers.abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables computation directly on encrypted data, but its substantial computational cost hinders adoption in privacy-preserving artificial intelligence (AI) applications. Neural processing units (NPUs) already deployed in AI infrastructure provide a practical platform for FHE acceleration. However, after mapping the number theoretic transform (NTT) to matrix multiplications on Ascend NPUs, modular arithmetic and representation conversion on the Vector backend still incur substantial overhead at stage boundaries. Evaluation-key material of key switching also increases storage and data-transfer costs, and whole-limb task assignment causes tail load imbalance. We present NPUFHE, an end-to-end CKKS execution system optimized for Ascend NPUs. To reduce modular recovery and twiddle costs in NTT, we propose Boundary-Optimized NTT, which eliminates intra-axis modular recovery, compiles intra-axis twiddle factors into matrix constants, and introduces two-level folded modular recovery at axis endpoints. To alleviate evaluation-key storage and transfer pressure, we design Compact Shoup encoding, which halves the key representation through local coefficient recovery. Finally, we propose Cost-Aware Parallel Tiling to mitigate tail load imbalance caused by whole-limb task assignment. It uses a cost model to adaptively partition tail tasks and smooth stepwise latency increases. We integrate the above designs into OpenFHE. On one Ascend 910B4, full-packing CKKS bootstrapping with real evaluation keys takes 0.95 s, encrypted CIFAR-10 ResNet-20 inference with bootstrapping requires 9.87 s per image, and encrypted MNIST inference achieves an amortized latency of 19.81 ms per image. The peak NTT throughput of NPUFHE reaches up to $184.22\times$, $2.04\times$, and $4.46\times$ that of OpenFHE on CPU, TensorFHE, and CROSS, respectively.

papers.title: A novel mechanism for coherent radio emission: particle-in-cell simulations
papers.abstract: It has been established that electron (phase-space) holes, i.e., EHs, can arise from the nonlinear relaxation of the electron beam instability. Excitation of electromagnetic waves related to the EHs is, however, still not fully understood. Using 2.5-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations, we systematically investigate the nonlinear evolution of the (moderately relativistic) electron bi-stream instability (a special case of the electron beam instability where the densities of the two counter-propagating energetic electron beams are equivalent) in charge- and current-neutralized plasmas under weak and strong magnetizations. This study provides new insights into the wave excitation, the nonlinear wave-particle interactions, the formation of non-Maxwellian features, and the anisotropic electron heating in magnetized plasmas, with potential implications for coherent radio emission in astrophysical plasmas (e.g., solar zebra-pattern bursts).

papers.title: A Novel Algebraic Approach to Medium-Range Solvable Models
papers.abstract: We extend Jones' Baxterisation, which produces solutions to the Yang-Baxter equation directly from the generators of an algebra, to quantum spin chains with medium-range interactions. The key ingredient is an extended Yang-Baxter equation for R matrices that are built from the generators attached to two neighbouring sites. Together with the accompanying Lax operator, it gives rise to transfer matrices that are in involution up to boundary terms, exactly as in Jones' construction. We find a solution to the extended Yang-Baxter equation, of non-difference form, in terms of the generators of the chromatic algebra of 3-colouring, and obtain from it two families of medium-range lattice Hamiltonians. Thus, each representation of the algebra provides a medium-range solvable model. Using the relation between the chromatic algebra of 3-colouring and the fusion category $\mathrm{Rep}(S_3)$, we construct four such representations. They reproduce the folded XXZ model and the hard-rod deformed XXZ model, and give new medium-range models of a three-state antiferromagnet and of a Rydberg-blockade ladder. Two of the four models possess non-invertible symmetries.

papers.title: DuetFHE: Compiling Dual-Lane Nonlinear Circuits for Complex-Packed CKKS Inference
papers.abstract: Complex packing in CKKS stores two real streams in the real and imaginary lanes of each slot. Direct squaring couples the lanes, while squaring them separately requires two ciphertext-ciphertext multiplications (HMults). DuetFHE is a GPU compiler that uses a phase transformation to square both lanes independently with one HMult. It reuses dual-lane squares in polynomial activations and the modular-reduction stage of CKKS bootstrapping. The compiler further plans ciphertext scales and reuses conjugates to sustain the complex-packed representation across stages. On a single RTX 5090, DuetFHE accelerates four polynomial activations by $1.60$--$1.79\times$ over direct evaluation on two real ciphertexts. For two-image AESPA ResNet-20 inference, it maintains packed execution across convolutions, square activations, and bootstrapping, achieving a $1.97\times$ end-to-end speedup over the fastest tested EasyFHE batched baseline on both the RTX 5090 and RTX PRO 6000.

papers.title: Graph Neural Networks for Accurate Quasiparticle Energy Levels in Large Supercells of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
papers.abstract: The GW method is the one of the main workhorses of the materials science community to accurately calculate the electronic bandgap of materials, as it overcomes the gap underestimation problem from Density Functional Theory (DFT). Despite its accuracy, its computational cost becomes prohibitive when calculations have more than 10-100 atoms, which makes more difficult its use for defects, surfaces and moiré systems that demand large supercells. To overcome this problem, we developed a Graph Neural Network trained with smaller GW calculations which can make accurate predictions on large supercells at a small fraction of the computational cost. Our model uses as features the projection of DFT wavefunctions into localized atomic orbitals, while graph nodes represent the atomic positions and edges represent atom to atom distances, which captures the system geometry. We explore how to do "small AI", providing a workflow of how to create a personal and convenient dataset of GW calculations to train the model that can be applied to different materials so that the final user does not need to rely on massive datasets. We define what must be included in the training dataset to capture the physics of our objective simulation, and perform a Bayesian optimization of hyperparameters. In the case of monolayer MoS$_2$ with a sulfur vacancy our GNN models achieve high accuracy (MAE ranging 10 to 50 meV) with a simplified workflow applicable to other materials, accelerating accurate large electronic structure calculations.

papers.title: A Multi-Criteria Evaluation of Color Normalization Methods in Histopathology: Nuclei Preservation, Artifact Sensitivity, Background Fidelity, and Downstream Performanc
papers.abstract: Deep learning models for nuclei detection and classification may generalize poorly across medical centers because of variations in staining and scanning. Although color normalization aims to reduce these variations, its effects on nuclear structure, background preservation, artifact sensitivity, and nuclei detection and classification performance have not been systematically evaluated. We present a procedure to benchmark 11 classical and deep learning normalization methods using 7 public and private nuclei datasets. Additionally, we investigate the effect of 7 input color spaces. The normalization methods differed in their effects on nuclear structure, background, and sensitivity to artifacts. However, detection and classification performance varied more across datasets than across normalization methods, and the input color space had limited influence. No single method performed best on all criteria, and image-level metrics did not reliably predict downstream performance, highlighting the need for nuclei- and structure-aware normalization methods. To support this work, we introduce WSI Quality Control and Normalization (WSI-QCN), a publicly available pipeline for robust whole-slide image quality assessment and color normalization; the source code is available on GitHub.

papers.title: Gorenstein and Ding injectivity over coherent rings
papers.abstract: For a commutative Ding--Chen ring $B$, we prove that Gorenstein and Ding injectivity coincide over $R=B[x,y]/(x,y)^2$ if and only if injective $B$-modules generate the unbounded derived category of $B$. We construct a commutative von Neumann regular ring $B$ whose unbounded derived category is not generated by its pure injective objects. For this $B$, the coherent ring $R$ admits a strongly Gorenstein injective module $G$ which is not Ding injective. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module $G_{\mathfrak p}$ has infinite Gorenstein injective dimension. The ring $R$ can be chosen to have cardinality $\aleph_ω$, the least possible among coherent rings over which Gorenstein and Ding injectivity differ.

papers.title: Specification-Aware Sparse Differentiation: Planning under Signal Temporal Logic with Sparsemax Robustness
papers.abstract: Gradient-based optimal control under a Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specification involves solving a nonlinear program whose constraints are smoothed robustness functions of the trajectory, and automatic differentiation without knowledge of sparsity computes the Jacobian and the Hessian that its solver needs in full. This often renders the problem computationally intractable. The dynamics and the specification prescribe a sparsity pattern through the STL syntax, the windows of the temporal operators and the variables that the predicates read. Standard tools such as CasADi recover this pattern by structural detection. In this work, we propose a method to prescribe such a pattern directly from the task specification. We show that our method allows us to exploit SparseMax, a recently proposed smooth robustness operator that is certifiably sparse and sound. Its derivative is exactly zero at every operand at or below a data-dependent threshold, which structural detection cannot see. We derive the patterns that expose this trajectory-dependent sparsity to sparse automatic differentiation, with a margin test for their reuse and Hessians confined to the variables of each constraint's support. We demonstrate the method on a dual-arm coordination task in which two arms share a hand-off zone divided into cells and one until constraint per scheduled visit keeps the other arm out of a cell until the visitor has left it. The two scenes are a zone of five cells and a circle of 64 cells, with single solves and closed-loop re-planning on a rigid-body simulation. Our exact-Hessian interior-point solves are up to 27 times faster than those with the sound log-sum-exp robustness in CasADi and IPOPT.

papers.title: The fundamental solution of the logarithmic Laplacian is a function in dimensions 1 and 2
papers.abstract: We show that the fundamental solution of the logarithmic Laplacian in dimensions $1$ and $2$ is a locally integrable function. Together with earlier work of the first author, this resolves a conjecture of Chen and Véron. The key step is that the inverse Fourier transform of the high-frequency part of $1/\log(|ξ|^2)$ behaves like $|x|^{-d}(\log(1/|x|))^{-2}$ near the origin.

papers.title: A new upper bound for the Erdős--Szekeres conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $\mathrm{ES}(n)$ denote the smallest integer such that every set of $\mathrm{ES}(n)$ points in the plane in general position contains $n$ points in convex position. In 1935, Erdős and Szekeres conjectured that $\mathrm{ES}(n)=2^{n-2}+1$, and in 1960, they established the corresponding lower bound. A breakthrough on the upper bound was achieved by Suk in 2017, who proved that \[ \mathrm{ES}(n)\leqslant2^{n+O(n^{2/3}\log n)}. \] In this article, we further improve the upper bound by showing that \[ \mathrm{ES}(n)\leqslant2^{n+O(n^{1/3})}. \]

papers.title: LIELLA: Private Edge Adaptation with Photonic Weight Streams
papers.abstract: Although photonic accelerators have shown promise for energy-efficient machine learning inference, privately personalizing large models across multiple edge clients remains difficult under tight memory, precision, and hardware constraints. We present LIELLA, a weight-streaming architecture that enables multiple edge clients to personalize a shared model through compact private adapters. The two proposed photonic adapter architectures accommodate both backpropagation and forward-only optimization while substantially reducing modeled client-side electrical energy consumption compared with electronic adapters. Under simulated hardware noise, clients sharing the same streamed backbone achieve nearly clean accuracy on QNLI and SST-2, even with attojoule-scale optical energy per MAC at each receiver. The architecture also enables hardware-aware adaptation among clients performing the same task, allowing their individual private adapters to achieve further accuracy improvements. For a gigabyte-scale TinyLlama backbone, LIELLA maintains a megabyte-scale inference memory footprint and kilobyte-scale persistent adapter storage per client, while achieving strong performance through forward-only adaptation. These findings further highlight hardware-driven opportunities to develop smaller yet more effective parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods and more accurate, noise-robust forward-only optimization algorithms.

papers.title: Community Detection in Fuzzy Social Networks through Fuzzy Co-Membership Relations over Alpha-Cut Realizations
papers.abstract: In fuzzy social networks the ties between actors are triangular fuzzy numbers, and community detection applied to their cores ignores how the partition depends on their vagueness. We propose a fuzzy co-membership relation obtained by running the Louvain algorithm on crisp networks compatible with the alpha-cuts of the ties and integrating the proportions of co-assignment over alpha. The relation is positive semidefinite; from it we derive a consensus partition, the number of groups, membership degrees and an assignment ambiguity index. In simulations from stochastic block models the relation does not yield better partitions than symmetric perturbations of the cores of the same size. Its ambiguity index is more closely associated with the structural position of the actors and identifies actors split between two groups when the vagueness is concentrated on them; when the asymmetry of the fuzzy ties points towards the latent tie strength, its co-membership degrees have a lower Brier score. The interval-weighted Louvain algorithm estimates the number of communities more accurately. In two departmental collaboration networks the observed ambiguity is lower than under permuted ratings, while the partitions depend on the symmetrization of directed ratings and on the coding of non-response.

papers.title: MIMORPHEUS: Rethinking Cross-Modal Supervision for Human Pose Estimation from Radar Signals
papers.abstract: Deep learning has shown promise for estimating human pose with multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar through walls. Building paired radar and pose datasets demands considerable time and manual effort, while large visual pose datasets provide no corresponding radar echoes. Physical simulation can supply synthetic signals, but requires expertise in scattering models and can leave a gap between simulated and real data. To address this challenge, we introduce MIMORPHEUS, a framework that generates radar echoes from 3D human poses through conditional diffusion. To prepare echo and pose representations, MIMO-VAE compresses the echoes according to their channel and fast time sample structure, while SkeleCoder learns pose features through contrastive alignment with echo features. These pose features then guide diffusion in the MIMO-VAE latent space, and the VAE decoder reconstructs echoes from the generated latents. Once trained, the generator augments radar data by producing different echoes for a recorded pose and supplies the radar modality for pose annotations in existing visual datasets. In data augmentation experiments, our method reduces MPJPE by 6.8%-11.2% across four radar pose estimators. Transfer experiments with three public pose datasets also show that visual pose annotations can supply useful radar training data. Code will be made publicly available on GitHub.

papers.title: DeciForm: Incorporating Task Structure into Decision Models
papers.abstract: Decision models unify candidate selection, Boolean judgment, and numerical scoring within a single model. Their answer spaces nevertheless carry different structures: classification candidates form an unordered set, while numerical scores have an intrinsic order and distance. We introduce Deciform, which incorporates these distinctions into computation and supervision. Candidate-free queries and isolated candidate branches support consistent classification under reordering. A log--spherical objective trains candidate probabilities, while a decimal-prefix readout combines individual-value and interval-weighted cumulative supervision for numerical scoring. Shared adapters, task-private residuals, and output-channel gains support joint adaptation. On a shared 15,000-request test set, Deciform improves all three decision metrics on Qwen and ModernBERT; source-normalized errors support the Score gains across the data mixture. Canonicalized joint encoding also eliminates tested order flips, while isolation further improves prediction metrics. Separate objective studies and main-configuration ablations examine the classification and numerical components. After one epoch of MIND-small adaptation, Deciform improves multi-positive news ranking on both backbones. These results support matching encoding and supervision to answer-space structure within a unified decision interface.

papers.title: More Than Picturing the Future: Motion-Oriented Latent Reasoning for Generalizable Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Latent reasoning lets Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models deliberate at a fraction of the cost of explicit chain-of-thought, increasingly through visual foresight, which we show to be indispensable for predicting actions. Yet this paradigm is inherited from Vision-Language Models, where it serves understanding rather than action: each latent is aligned with an isolated future frame, often enriched with further modalities of that frame. We find that this binds the policy to the appearance of its training scenes, so that it degrades sharply once the scene changes. We argue that visual latents for action should capture not what a future frame looks like, but how the scene evolves toward the goal. We therefore propose Motion-Oriented Latent Reasoning, which redirects visual latents from the whole frame to the interaction that the action must bring about. Semantic latents, following the stages of embodied chain-of-thought, first establish what to accomplish and how. Conditioned on them, motion-oriented latents anticipate each future step from coarse to fine: from the global scene, to the interaction region spanned by the manipulated object and its destination, to the robot state. Relative to the state-of-the-art latent VLA LaST$_0$, our method raises the mean success rate on SimplerEnv-WidowX from 37.5% to 55.2% in distribution and from 22.4% to 30.2% under out-of-distribution shifts, and on an AgileX Piper dual-arm platform from 60.8% to 90.8% in training scenes and from 6.7% to 37.5% under environmental changes.

papers.title: A Glimpse of Training VLMs as Foundation Models for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Recently, GPT-6 Astra demonstrates strong generalization in robot control, yet limited disclosure of its training leaves open how such capabilities can be reproduced. We introduce nanoAstra, an approach to training vision-language models (VLMs) for generalizable manipulation that combines semantic action modeling with capability-preserving supervised fine-tuning (CP-SFT). nanoAstra represents robot behavior as semantic steps composed of reusable, parameterized action primitives, guided by explicit progress descriptions. Meanwhile, CP-SFT uses an explicit robot-specific system prompt to constrain manipulation outputs to a structured action space, aiming to focus adaptation on robot-specific contexts and promote specialization while minimizing interference with broader pretrained capabilities. With this formulation, we train nanoAstra on more than 5,000 hours of robot data together with general VQA data. On RoboTwin 2.0's randomized benchmark, nanoAstra-9B achieves a 17.8% zero-shot success rate, substantially outperforming advanced VLA and WAM baselines as well as similarly sized VLMs. With inference faster than the corresponding motion execution on a single H20 GPU, our model supports action-chunk-like streaming execution that overlaps inference with motion, reducing the robot's idle time from 35.0% to 6.9%.

papers.title: Unstable Solidification
papers.abstract: We construct a solidification functor $\LH$ on condensed anima by localizing at the maps inverted by solid integral chains. A pointed connected nilpotent condensed anima is $\Hsol$-local precisely when its fundamental group admits a finite central series with solid abelian factors and its higher homotopy groups are solid. For simply connected condensed anima, we construct a natural strongly convergent spectral sequence \[ E^2_{p,q}=L_ps(π_qX)\Longrightarrowπ_{p+q}\LH X \] where $L_ps$ denotes the $p$-th derived functor of the abelian solidification.

papers.title: Probe Before You Learn: Allocating Prompts from Initial Gradients under Label Noise
papers.abstract: Prompt learning provides a parameter-efficient way to adapt pretrained vision--language models through text and visual prompts, but noisy labels prevalent in real-world data inevitably bias prompt updates and thereby undermine adaptation effectiveness. Prior work on robust prompt learning focuses on suppressing unreliable updates under noisy supervision. We uncover a pivotal yet overlooked aspect--prompt allocation: shifting the parameter budget between text and visual prompts can substantially enhance robustness while keeping the training objective and total budget fixed. However, suitable prompt allocations vary across tasks and are unknown a priori, rendering brute-force candidate training computationally prohibitive. We propose GPrompt, a training-free method that derives allocation between text and visual prompts using only loss gradients at initialization before prompt optimization. Using a small sample of images and generated pseudo-labels as shared supervision, GPrompt performs an initialization probe to extract paired text and visual loss gradients, and characterizes the geometry of their trace-normalized Gram matrices through both concentration within each modality and overlap between modalities. GPrompt then derives a closed-form allocation, and projects it onto feasible prompt counts under the exact parameter budget, enabling task-specific selection without training candidate configurations. Experiments across eleven datasets show that GPrompt outperforms the strongest baseline by up to 7.75% while selecting configurations close to the best allocation identified through exhaustive training. The average runtime of gradient probe across datasets is 99.9% lower than that of exhaustive candidate training.

papers.title: CXL Coherence Writes Back What Surviving Hosts See, Leaving Flushes Only for Ordering
papers.abstract: Hosts that share memory over Compute Express Link (CXL) cache its lines, and a host that crashes loses the lines it has modified and not written back. Designs for such memory stop every host when one crashes, assume stored energy, or flush after each operation. We show that when a crashing host's clients die with it, the flushes a host crash requires are those that keep one line from reaching the memory device before a line it depends on, and not those that make a finished operation durable. The reason is a property that CXL requires of the fabric: a modified line is written back before another host accesses it. Whatever a surviving host has seen is then on the device, and our crash condition lets a crash drop operations that only the crashed host observed. We prove the claim for operations that take effect in a single store, and test it on small instances of models of three published designs, whose operations store several times.
