We show that the anisotropic Hardy difference controls a weighted critical Sobolev norm when $1<p<n$, a weighted exponential integrability of Trudinger type when $p=n$, where the Hardy term is replaced by its Leray logarithmic correction, and a weighted Hölder seminorm when $p>n$, proving in each regime that the logarithmic weights appear with the optimal exponents. In the borderline case $p=n$ this extends to general functions the optimal exponent previously known only for $F_o$-radial functions. The proofs rely on a common ground-state reduction and, for $1<p\le n$, on a splitting of the transformed function into its $F_o$-spherical mean and a mean-free part. Since $F^2$ is not a quadratic form unless $F$ is induced by a scalar product, the reduction of the radial part through spherical harmonics, used in the Euclidean case, is not available; we control the radial part directly, through a convexity inequality for $F^p$ with a quadratic remainder and sharp one-dimensional estimates, and the mean-free part through a Poincaré inequality on the boundary of the Wulff shape. For $p>n$ we use an anisotropic Morrey representation formula.

papers.title: The Social World Model Evaluation Gap
papers.abstract: A negotiation assistant can reach a good deal without accurately predicting the other person's response. We ask whether evaluations of social world models test that prediction directly. We audit 113 works published from 1999 to 2026. 9 primary evaluations measure a real person's response to an action selected by the system or experimenter. Only 2 also compare an explicit response forecast with that response. Their predictors use information available when the action is chosen, and the evaluated responses were excluded from fitting; both randomize the intervention. A separate full-text check of 25 language-model works finds no experiment meeting these conditions. The other evaluations test current-state inference, task success, or prediction from recorded actions. We propose a 1-step negotiation experiment that separates these questions. The findings describe the audited sample, not the prevalence of this evaluation gap across the field.

papers.title: Pattern-dependent stability of binary exponential perturbations
papers.abstract: We study how the arrangement of binary frequency perturbations affects the stability of exponential systems on an interval of length one. For frequencies $λ_n=n+s_nδ$, with $s_n\in\{-1,+1\}$, we represent synthesis in Fourier coordinates by a shifted-sinc operator $N_{δ,s}$ and identify its Gram operator as $G_{δ,s}=N_{δ,s}^*N_{δ,s}$. The optimal squared synthesis bounds are $1\pmρ_{δ,s}$, where $ρ_{δ,s}=\|P_-T_{2δ}P_+\|$ measures the interaction between the two sign classes. Using the finite-matrix representation of periodic perturbations, we prove that, for each fixed $0\leqδ<1/2$, the minimum lower bound among $p$-periodic binary patterns converges to the worst binary lower bound as $p\to\infty$. At Kadec's critical amplitude $δ=1/4$, the alternating pattern has a positive lower bound, whereas a step pattern reduces to a half-shifted Hilbert matrix and has lower bound zero. Every fixed periodic pattern nevertheless remains a Riesz basis. We discuss the resulting periodic extremal questions and record a direct perturbation estimate giving explicit stability neighborhoods around stable reference patterns.

papers.title: Precision Coexistence: Angular-Spectral Region Constrained Waveform Design for MIMO-ISAC
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a dual-function waveform design framework for multiple-input multiple-output integrated sensing and communication (MIMO-ISAC) systems operating in congested electromagnetic environments. In such environments, the dual-function waveform must coexist with legacy systems, such as localized positioning sensors, maritime radar networks, and satellite communication links, that occupy specific frequency bands and angular sectors. To enable precision coexistence, we incorporate localized angular-spectral region constraints that suppress beamformed energy only within the angle-frequency regions occupied by each legacy system, while preserving the spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) available outside those regions. The resulting waveform design problem is formulated as a nonconvex optimization problem and solved using a low-complexity majorization--minimization alternating direction method of multipliers (MM--ADMM) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides precise legacy-system protection while maintaining robust radar sensing and multi-user communication performance.

papers.title: S$^2$-MAS: A Society-Scale Multi-Agent Simulation Framework with a 500-Million-Persona Resource
papers.abstract: Simulating economic responses at society scale requires decision rules that respond to household circumstances and accounting rules that track the consequences. We introduce S$^2$-MAS, a multi-agent simulation framework that combines 500 million synthetic household personas with trainable decision policies, reusable financial scenarios and explicit state transitions. After training on 2.93 million financial examples, YN-mini achieves 74.554% accuracy and 38.375% question-macro F1 in its MLX implementation on held-out consumer financial choices. These scores exceed the question-specific majority baseline by 2.783 and 6.206 percentage points, respectively. In a purchase-funding simulation, 12 million households each make a choice under two conditions. The 24 million choices generate 288 million monthly ledger states in 3 h 59 min on 14 GPUs. Jointly increasing purchase goals and approved credit limits produces heterogeneous changes in consumption, cash and repayments. Much of the variation in consumption arises from households switching between deferral and purchase. In a separate retrospective study of 1,060 households, standalone YN-master-9B reduces the mean absolute error in annual consumption by 3.42% relative to the deterministic fully rational benchmark. Its mean forecast is 19.7% below observed mean consumption. Further tests measure how year labels and information about later outcomes affect decisions. Together, these experiments establish an executable alternative for studying heterogeneous household behavior with learned policies and explicit financial accounting.

papers.title: How Wet-Biased Datasets Shape the Training and Mislead the Evaluation of Generative Precipitation Nowcasting
papers.abstract: Generative models for precipitation nowcasting are trained and evaluated predominantly on wet-biased datasets, which over-represent precipitation events to emphasize rare extremes. Selecting test cases based on target observations is known to favor forecasts that match the selected distribution rather than the intended deployment distribution. We show analytically that the same target-dependent selection, applied to the training set, tilts the conditional distribution learned by an ideal generative model by exactly the factor that such an evaluation rewards. We test both evaluation and training effects with a satellite-to-radar diffusion model in a controlled experiment that crosses wet-biased and uniform sampling of the training and of the test set. The evaluation effect appears in full: the same model looks under-predictive on a wet-biased test set but over-predicts light rain on a deployment-consistent one, whichever way it was trained. Inverse probability weighting recovers the deployment scores from the wet-biased set. The training effect is real but partial: the model trained on wet-biased data forecasts more rain than its uniformly trained counterpart, yet remains far from calibrated even on a test set drawn like its training set, and gains skill for rain at a modest cost in calibration. Wet-biased training is thus a trade-off, not an error. Using classifier-free guidance as an example of a tuned quantity, we show how this misdirects model development: most scores on the wet-biased test set favor the largest guidance scale, whereas calibration, frequency bias, and a threshold-weighted proper score on the deployment-consistent set favor the smallest.

papers.title: Local failure of disjoint additivity
papers.abstract: Local Gauss constraints can prevent commuting regional algebras from generating the full algebra assigned to their union. We investigate disjoint additivity on the full magnetic physical subspace of finite-group quantum-double models while keeping the original lattice edge supports fixed. Every finite non-Abelian group exhibits a counterexample on vertex-disjoint regions contained within a contractible disk on a regular square torus. For a fixed eight-edge loop and a specified peripheral contact family, additivity fails if and only if the group is non-Abelian and the selected contacts cover all four interior faces of the loop. Leaving an inner face uncovered restores additivity; for the same loop, so does any second region avoiding the specified testing neighborhood. A peripheral projector restricts the exterior tests on a loop transition, allowing their product to preserve the constraints even when the loop factor does not. We construct union observables that deterministically separate orthogonal relative-sign superpositions that yield identical outcome statistics under every measurement whose effects lie in the generated regional algebra. For a separate wrapping pair, we also determine the complete matrix-block inclusion, identifying missing center-orbit coherences, and construct an independent regular-torus counterexample for the eight-dimensional Kac-Paljutkin Hopf algebra.

papers.title: Learning to Discriminate Scene Structures Makes Self-Supervised Depth Learning Scalable
papers.abstract: Self-supervised monocular depth estimation is appealing for its potential to scale with unlabeled data, yet existing methods often degrade when trained on diverse scenes. This study finds that, under self-supervision, models tend to encode dataset-specific structural biases rather than transferable scene geometry, leading to cross-domain optimization conflicts. To address this issue, this study proposes the MaSS framework, aiming to make self-supervised depth learning scalable to diverse data. MaSS introduces a dedicated structural representation pathway explicitly decoupled from contextual features, which is guided by a novel scene-structure discrimination objective to learn generalized, layout-aware structural representations for depth decoding. Trained and evaluated on four diverse datasets, both individually and jointly, MaSS substantially outperforms prior self-supervised methods and is the first to consistently benefit from mixed-domain training. Zero-shot evaluation on eight additional datasets further demonstrates its remarkable generalizability, particularly on those entirely out-of-distribution scenes. The source code is publicly available at https://mias.group/MaSS.

papers.title: On the Complexity of Symmetric Boolean Functions in Multiparty Private Simultaneous Messages
papers.abstract: Multiparty Private Simultaneous Messages (PSM), also known as Decomposable Randomized Encoding (DRE) or information-theoretic garbling, is a model for non-interactive secure computation. Each party encodes its input using shared randomness and sends a message to an evaluator who must recover the function output without learning anything else about the inputs. Perfect privacy requires identical transcript distributions on inputs with the same output. We also study the weaker notion of support privacy, which requires only that these distributions have the same support. We study the communication complexity of symmetric Boolean functions when each of the n parties holds one input bit. Lower bounds. We prove a $(1-o(1))n\log n$ lower bound for support-private PSM protocols computing $OR_n$, which is known to be tight. As a consequence, we obtain the same lower bounds for $MAJ_n$ and $EMAJ_n$. We also prove an $Ω(n\log q)$ lower bound for $MOD_q$. An alternative proof technique recovers most of these bounds as well as the previously known approach based on Nechiporuk's method. Upper bounds. We construct perfectly private and support private PSM protocols of total communication $\widetilde{O}(n^{3/2})$ and $\widetilde{O}(n)$ respectively for every symmetric Boolean function, improving on the known quadratic bound. For $MAJ_n$, known branching-program constructions yield an upper bound of $O(n\log^3 n\log\log n)$. For $EMAJ_n$ and $MOD_q$ with prime $q$, the lower bounds are tight up to constant factors. Earlier lower-bound techniques of Ball et al. (ITCS 2020) yield only trivial linear bounds for symmetric Boolean functions. Concurrent and independent work by Holmgren and Wu proves a $ω(n)$ lower bound for $OR_n$ using the same approach as our alternative technique. Both works used substantial AI assistance.

papers.title: Speculative Sampling in Interactive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Interactive video generation commonly relies on small bidirectional chunks to reduce response latency. Yet our preliminary experiments show that larger chunks improve video quality and better utilize GPU parallelism, allowing more latents to be sampled with only a modest increase in sampling time. Motivated by these observations, we propose Speculative Sampling, a strategy that combines the modeling power of large bidirectional windows with the low-latency interaction of small ones. It expands the modeling window by appending noise latents as padding and caches the resulting predictions for reuse when the condition remains unchanged. Predictions are delivered incrementally, while the uncommitted suffix remains replaceable. Our latency analysis shows that this removes the waiting-time lower bound imposed by chunk boundaries, shifting the optimization focus from reducing chunk size to accelerating per-chunk generation. Bidirectional window size thus becomes a decision variable for jointly optimizing visual quality and generation time, rather than a necessary constraint on low-latency interaction. This opens a path to serving large bidirectional models in interactive streaming systems without complex streaming post-training.

papers.title: SkillScreen: High-Recall Screening of Malicious Agent Skills with Decision Models
papers.abstract: Agent skills turn natural-language instructions into actions, creating a security challenge: legitimate automation and malicious behaviour can look deceptively similar. A practical screen must catch nearly every attack while keeping the review load manageable. We present SkillScreen, a compact decision model trained to score skill maliciousness directly from SKILL$.$md in a single forward pass. On MaliciousSkillBench, SkillScreen flags 20-25% of benign skills at 99% recall on unseen attack families, substantially fewer than the word-level classifier and prompted LLM judges tested. Under the same training protocol, it also generalizes better than a fully fine-tuned encoder to unseen sources. Yet unfamiliar benign sources sharply increase false positives, showing that recognizing new attacks does not ensure reliable screening of new skill collections. Our results demonstrate the value of task-trained decision models for high-recall skill screening. Project page: https://jerroldh.github.io/SkillScreen-webpage/

papers.title: Analytic Brill wave initial data with trapped surfaces
papers.abstract: Since Brill's work of 1959, the conformal factor of finite-amplitude Brill waves, the axisymmetric and time-symmetric vacuum initial data on $\mathbb{R}^3$ that describe pure gravitational radiation, has been obtained only numerically, up to the most recent studies. Here an explicit one-parameter family of such data is constructed; the data are real analytic and asymptotically flat, with trivial topology and a single end. The free metric function is a closed-form combination of elementary functions and a dilogarithm. The data have the toroidal conformal symmetry of Beig and Husa, and a change of variable of Natanzon type reduces every mode equation to the Gauss hypergeometric equation, so that the conformal factor is a series with explicit Gamma-function coefficients. A ground-state identity gives a sharp existence criterion: complete, asymptotically flat data exist precisely for $k<k_c=0.80480168\ldots$, and the explicit series is identified with the unique variational solution. The ADM mass is an absolutely convergent digamma series, with $m/a=πk^2/10+O(k^3)$ for small amplitudes and an explicit residue at its critical divergence. Sufficiently strong waves contain trapped surfaces: it is proved that for $k$ close to $k_c$ the rescaled conformal factor converges to an explicit function and explicit tori and spheres become outer trapped, so that the data contain an apparent horizon. A numerical search, restricted to equatorially symmetric star-shaped surfaces, finds marginally trapped (minimal) spheres, which appear in a fold near $k=0.7670$. A scaling symmetry of the mode problem generates further solvable families, whose simplest member has the elementary seed function $q=\frac12\log[1+4a^2ρ^2/(ρ^2+z^2+a^2)^2]$. No thin-torus or weak-field approximation is used.

papers.title: Solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with small $x_3$: a spectral approach
papers.abstract: We count the integral solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with $|x_3|$ of size at most $M$, for $M$ smaller than $\sqrt D$, using a smooth weight $Φ(x_3/M)$. Such solutions correspond to binary quadratic forms of discriminant $D$, and hence to geodesics in the hyperbolic plane. Under this correspondence, $x_3$ is small exactly when the geodesic passes close to the point $i$. We count these geodesics by the spectral theory of automorphic forms. Throughout, $θ=7/64$ is the Kim-Sarnak exponent. For non-square $D=f^2D_0$, with $D_0$ a fundamental discriminant, the geodesics are closed. We obtain an asymptotic formula with error $O(D^{\varepsilon}f^{1+θ}D_0^{2/3}M^{-1/2})$. The main inputs are the formulas of Duke-Imamoglu-Toth and Baruch-Mao for cycle integrals, the cubic moment bounds of Young and of Andersen-Wu, and a Hecke relation which reduces everything to the fundamental discriminant $D_0$. For $D\equiv 5 \bmod 8$ this counts all solutions, and the range $M\ge D^{1/2-1/1332}$ of Friedlander and Iwaniec improves to $M\ge D^{4/9+\varepsilon}$. For square $D=n^2$ the geodesics run from cusp to cusp, and Hecke theory reduces them to the single geodesic from $0$ to $\infty$. For every $n$ and both parities of $x_3$ we obtain an asymptotic formula with error $O(n^{1+θ+\varepsilon}M^{-1/2})$, which is non-trivial for $M\ge n^{71/96+\varepsilon}$. This improves the range $n^{5/6+\varepsilon}$ of the elementary method and confirms the corrected main term of the author's earlier work. This paper was written in collaboration with Claude (Opus 5.5, High; Fable 5.2 in the final stage), an AI model developed by Anthropic.

papers.title: Verifying Autoware Controller Node by Combining Model Verification and Runtime Monitoring
papers.abstract: Formal modeling and verification of autonomous driving systems remain challenging due to the vast operational space and the complexity of the control logic. We propose a hybrid verification approach that combines formal model verification and runtime monitoring for the trajectory-following control node of Autoware, an open-source autonomous driving platform. We formalize the controller as a hybrid system in differential dynamic logic (dL), and introduce an abstract model that captures the essential control dynamics. We then prove safety and liveness properties of the model using the KeYmaera X proof assistant. Complementarily, we monitor the constraints that assure the compatibility between the model and the Autoware implementation across numerical simulation runs using the Autoware toolchain, quantifying to what extent the implementation's behavior is subsumed by the verified model. The experimental results confirmed that (i) monitoring provides a sound evaluation of target following with accuracy bounds, and (ii) the Autoware implementation reaches the target with an accuracy of approximately 0.2-0.4 (m) in position and 0.8 (m/s) in velocity.

papers.title: When Generative Models Act as Simulators
papers.abstract: A simulator summarizes an environment in a state that users can read and change. Generative models learn representations of the world without explicit specification, but offer no built-in way to edit that world's state. We investigate the conditions under which a generative model acts as a simulator through $\textit{editability}$: whether changing a model's latent representation produces the next-step outputs we get by editing a simulator's state. We test two kinds of state mappings, both fit from latent states paired with simulator states. In one, we train probes to decode the simulator state from the model, then steer along them. In the other, we learn the simulator-to-latent mapping directly with an inverse map, which can succeed even when steering fails. We study both in two contrasting environments: the discrete board game Othello, and Rayworld, our own continuous world of moving discs seen through partial renderings, closer to physical scenes and video. We find that which mapping succeeds depends strongly on the environment, in ways decodability does not predict. In Othello, each simplification of the rules lowers editability. In Rayworld, probes fail to steer along the simulator's continuous state, yet an inverse map sets the model from that state anyway. Editability across layers suggests that the Othello model compresses its history into a board partway through the network, while the Rayworld model shifts its recent frames and then refines a rendering of the next frame. The inverse map succeeds by approximating this partial rendering. We relate both outcomes to the causal state of computational mechanics, the minimal summary of its history a model must keep to predict optimally, which may not align with the simulator. Guided by this view, we change how the Rayworld model is trained and make its state more simulator-like.

papers.title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part I: Sion-Carathéodory Extension in Net Convergence Groups
papers.abstract: We study extension of additive measures when the range carries a prescribed separated Abelian net convergence. On a $σ$-complete, lattice-$σ$-continuous pseudo-D-lattice, we prove an uncontrolled modular extension theorem using finite-response reflection, closed countable summation and uniform closure. Completeness is imposed only on the limit-stable hull of the source values. No topology, lattice order or positive control is required in its range. Modular interval identities, an order-null separation argument and two uniform transfer arguments construct the extension before establishing its normality. A separate relative lifting theorem combines this modular construction with a nonmodular Sasaki argument. Its cone conditions are verified for positive lattice-group values, lattice-normed groups, products and limit-stable subgroups. These verifications give explicit positive, dominated lattice-normed and topological corollaries. Uniqueness holds among all sigma-additive extensions to the generated domain. Sion's inner and outer nets exist in the original convergence and recover the extension there. For Boolean domains we retain the stronger identification with the full regulated splitting class and the finite-variation and finite-semivariation results.

papers.title: Self-intersecting sections of polar actions on simply connected manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct a polar action of $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ on a closed simply connected $11$-manifold with a compact three-dimensional section that is not injectively immersed. The section is injective over the regular part and has two distinct local branches along a singular stratum. All isotropy groups are connected, and all orbits are simply connected. This gives a negative answer to the injectivity question raised by Grove and Ziller.

papers.title: Ambient Discrete Diffusion: Using the Wrong Data at the Right Time for Data Efficient Learning
papers.abstract: We introduce RefineMix, a framework for training discrete diffusion models under severe data scarcity, a common constraint in scientific applications. RefineMix uses out-of-distribution data at selected diffusion times to improve generalization without biasing the sampling distribution. Although this strategy has been explored in continuous diffusion, discrete diffusion presents a distinct challenge: unlike Gaussian noise, masking preserves domain information in surviving tokens, limiting the use of related data at high noise levels. At low noise levels, however, the domains effectively disjoint supports become an advantage, allowing the model to learn from both in-domain and out-of-distribution data without biasing the sampler. We formalize these intuitions and provide a theoretical analysis for the proposed method. Experimentally, across five domain-shift settings, RefineMix matches or outperforms in-domain finetuning and data mixing. For protein sequence generation, finetuning with just 197 in-domain examples nearly doubles the fraction of generated proteins that are simultaneously novel, foldable, and in-family compared to standard finetuning.

papers.title: Seeing Through the Glare: A Multi-Source Benchmark and Ocular-Adaptive Pixel MeanFlow for Eyeglass Reflection Removal
papers.abstract: Eyeglass reflection removal is important across smartphone imaging, video conferencing, and other face-centric visual applications. The task is challenging because reflections range from mild photometric contamination to severe ocular occlusion, requiring selective correction and plausible reconstruction without altering identity or natural appearance. Existing datasets cover limited reflection conditions, constraining generalization to complex real-world scenes and systematic evaluation. We introduce OcuBench, a multi-source benchmark comprising 10,280 controllable synthetic pairs, 732 real-input pseudo-pairs, and 458 independent real-world test images, supporting both paired evaluation and assessment beyond generated supervision. We further propose OcuFlow, an ocular-adaptive pixel MeanFlow (pMF) framework for efficient, detail-preserving restoration. It combines geometry-adaptive representation with one-step pMF to focus reconstruction on reflection-obscured ocular regions, together with native-resolution frequency-preserving synthesis to retain reliable observed details. Experiments across diverse reflection conditions demonstrate that OcuFlow achieves consistent advantages in reflection removal quality, ocular fidelity, and efficiency. In a blind user study, it receives $67.32\%$ of selections, $6.2\times$ the next-best share. The code and dataset will be released at https://github.com/NTU-AI4X/OcuFlow.

papers.title: Fully Deterministic Shallow Neural Networks with Localized Activations: Construction and Optimal Sobolev Approximation
papers.abstract: We construct fully deterministic finite-dimensional spaces for Sobolev approximation using shallow neural networks with a localized activation $σ$, either Gaussian or tanh-difference. For a bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, and a prescribed regularity index $s>0$, the approximation space at frequency resolution $M$ is\[ V_M^Ω=\operatorname{span}\left\{ σ\!\left(\frac{ω_i\cdot x-b_{j,M}}{\varepsilon_M}\right): 1\le i\le J_M,\quad 1\le j\le K_{i,M} \right\}. \]All parameters are prescribed explicitly and independently of the target function. The offset cutoff depends on the direction and the domain, with an exterior margin tending to zero. The feature count satisfies $N_M=\sum_{i=1}^{J_M}K_{i,M}\asymp M^d$. For sufficiently large $M$, we construct a bounded linear operator $\mathcal A_M^Ω:H^s(Ω)\to V_M^Ω$ that achieves the optimal approximation rate \[ \|u-\mathcal A_M^Ωu\|_{H^m(Ω)} \le C N_M^{-(s-m)/d}\|u\|_{H^s(Ω)} \] for every $u\in H^s(Ω)$ and every integer $0\le m<s$. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions illustrate the approximation behavior in $L^2$ and $H^1$.

papers.title: A Wasserstein Trust-Region Method for Smooth Potential-Interaction Energies
papers.abstract: Finding low-energy particle configurations and approximating probability distributions both lead to minimizing potential-interaction energies in Wasserstein space. Second-order information can speed up minimizing these possibly nonconvex energies, but a quadratic model is accurate only near the current measure. We introduce a Wasserstein trust-region (WTR) method for smooth, possibly nonconvex energies of this type. Each iteration transports the current measure $ρ$ along a displacement field $s$, producing $(\mathrm{Id}+s)_\#ρ$. The field approximately minimizes a quadratic model built from the second variation of the energy, subject to $\|s\|_{L^2(ρ)}\leΔ$, using a truncated conjugate-gradient method. The ratio of actual to predicted decrease determines step acceptance and updates the trust-region radius. Under a lower energy bound and globally bounded Hessians of the potential and interaction kernel, we prove that the objective is nonincreasing, the Wasserstein-gradient norms converge to zero, and an $\varepsilon$-stationary iterate is reached within $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ iterations, rejected ones included. If the potential is quadratically coercive, every weak accumulation point is stationary. For empirical measures, WTR is an ordinary trust-region method in the particle positions, and its complexity bound does not depend on the number of particles provided the initial energy exceeds its infimum by a bounded amount. For $2048$ and $4096$ particles with Gaussian pair repulsion in a two-dimensional harmonic trap, WTR reaches the gradient tolerance $2\times10^{-4}$ a median $1.40$ times faster than L-BFGS. For equal-weight integration rules on two non-Gaussian targets, WTR reaches an integration error of $10^{-4}$ about $1.8$ times faster than L-BFGS and $1.3$ times faster than a Krylov trust-region solver.

papers.title: Open problem: Computing Bayes-Nash equilibrium in simple security games
papers.abstract: This is an open problem originally posed during the program "Economics and Computation" held in the Fall 2015 semester at the Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing. It asks whether a (Bayes-)Nash equilibrium can be computed in polynomial time for Bayesian simple security games.

papers.title: Spectral Erdős--Gallai Theorems for the \(\mathcal A_α\)-Tensor of the \(s\)-Clique Hypergraph
papers.abstract: The generalized Erdős--Gallai theorem determines the maximum number of $s$-cliques in an $n$-vertex graph with no matching of $t$ edges. We study its spectral analogue for the $\mathcal A_α$-tensor of the $s$-uniform clique hypergraph. For $n\geq2t-1$, $3\leq s\leq2t-1$, and $0\leqα\leq1$, we determine the maximum $α$-$s$-clique spectral radius among $n$-vertex graphs with no matching of $t$ edges, and characterize all extremal graphs. When $t<s\leq 2t-1$, the unique extremal graph up to isomorphism is a $(2t-1)$-clique with isolated vertices. When $3\leq s\leq t$, the extremal graphs are selected from this graph and the join of a $(t-1)$-clique with an independent set. We give the exact order at which the join becomes extremal and determine when both graphs attain the maximum.

papers.title: A Study of Prior Case Retrieval Using Lexical, Semantic, and Rhetorical Role Information in Indian Legal Documents
papers.abstract: For retrieving prior cases in Indian legal judgments, the problem involves distinguishing relevant legal facts from mere lexical similarities because a prior case that shares a statute with the query judgment is not necessarily relevant. In this paper, we describe an empirical evaluation of three consecutive designs of retrieval systems for the IL PCR(Indian Legal Prior Case Retrieval) task. We demonstrate that the combination of the rhetorical roles (Fact, Ratio Of The Decision, Precedent, Argument, Statute) is better than either using individual roles or performing full text retrieval, that statute similarity is not discriminative, and that a legal entailment reranker with training data produced by an LLM is much worse in terms of official evaluation than its internal validation score. Two rankers, with excellent internal MRR up to 0.97, performed poorly in terms of official evaluation (MRR as low as 0.14). Thus, we propose a new design with query disjoint splitting and frozen validation fusion. The result is a four stage pipeline with Micro F1 0.2549, MRR 0.6081, and nDCG@10 0.4187.

papers.title: Four Ways to Stream: Exponential Separations from Random Order and Quantum Memory
papers.abstract: A streaming algorithm can keep classical or quantum memory, and its input arrives in adversarial or random order. Each resource alone is known to beat the basic model exponentially, but it was not known whether random order can help a quantum algorithm. We compare the four models by exponential space separations: every pair is separated on some problem and tied on another, and the two models with one resource each beat each other on different problems, one direction for random inputs, by concurrent work of Bouland, Ding, and Jain. The new phenomenon is that quantum memory and random order together can be exponentially stronger than each alone. We show this on a streaming version of Hidden Matching in which the bits of $x\in\{0,1\}^N$ arrive many times and $m\le\sqrt{N}$ matching requests must be answered on arrival. In random order a quantum algorithm uses $O(\log N\log m)$ space, while classical algorithms need $Ω(\sqrt{N})$, and quantum algorithms need $Ω(m)$ when all data comes before the requests. Two properties explain this. Consumability: answering a request destroys the quantum state. Replenishment: the state can be rebuilt from bits that keep arriving, which random order supplies and a data-first order does not. We prove that one quantum message answering $m$ Hidden Matching requests needs $Ω(m)$ qubits, a conjecture of Gilboa, Jain, and McClean, for $m\le N^{1/2-δ}$. The rest comes from Noisy Gap Cycle, a problem of Assadi and Sundaresan: tell whether a graph is a union of cycles of length $k$ or $2k$. With long cycles it needs linear space in all four models: we extend their random-order lower bound to quantum algorithms and obtain the first quantum random-order lower bounds for natural graph problems. With short cycles, $\mathrm{polylog}(n)$ classical bits suffice in random order, but adversarial order requires polynomial quantum space.

papers.title: Visual Foresight for Agentic Reasoning Before Action in Urban Navigation
papers.abstract: Urban navigation requires embodied agents to pursue long-horizon goals through local decisions based on egocentric observations. However, existing agentic navigation methods often struggle to translate distant goals into coherent local decisions. Their reliance on linguistic reasoning over transient observations or limited history constrains anticipation of action consequences, despite the importance of such foresight for navigating long and complex urban routes. To bridge this gap, we propose PreAct-Nav, a training-free agentic navigation framework that equips frozen policies with visual foresight for reasoning before action. Our central idea is to use predicted future views to assess proposed actions in the context of persistent medium-horizon subgoals and observed experience. At its core, a navigation memory module maintains the active subgoal and relevant experience across decisions, translating distant goals into actionable intermediate objectives. To enable visual foresight, a predictive world sandbox uses an action-conditioned world model (AC-WM) to generate future views of proposed movements, providing visual cues for reasoning about their consequences beyond the current observation. A vision-language model (VLM) reasoner interprets these predictions using the subgoal and accumulated experience to retain or revise actions. After execution, real observations are used to assess outcomes, correct inconsistent assumptions, and update memory to continue or reformulate the subgoal. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that the proposed PreAct-Nav improves action selection through memory updates and visual prediction, with more pronounced gains on longer routes and routes with more turns.

papers.title: Generalized eigenstate thermalization beyond leading order in 2D large $c$ CFTs
papers.abstract: We develop a Fock-space formulation that reduces expectation values of vacuum-family quasi-primaries in quantum Korteweg--de Vries (qKdV) eigenstates to a free-bosonic problem, and employ it to test the generalized eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (GETH) in 2D conformal field theories with a large central charge. We prove that the first two qKdV charges $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ lift all degeneracies except along at most countably many curves in the $(c,\,Δ)$ plane, where $c$ is the central charge and $Δ$ denotes the highest weight of the conformal family, so that the full-qKdV simultaneous eigenstates are unambiguously determined by $Q_1$ and $Q_3$. Based on this, a comprehensive toolkit for testing GETH within the scope of vacuum-family observables, i.e. equating qKdV eigenstates and thermal states of the generalized Gibbs ensemble in the sense of expectation values of vacuum-family local observables, is provided in this paper. We argue that GETH is satisfied when the infinite tower of qKdV charges is considered. A more restrictive form of the GETH, namely that all expectations of local observables of a definite level should be expressible in terms of the first few qKdV charges, is directly falsified at subleading order in the large-$c$ expansion. Specifically, at levels 6 and 8 in the vacuum family, expectation values of quasi-primaries in simultaneous eigenstates of the qKdV charges are not determined by any finite number of the lowest-index qKdV charges. The question of whether additional microscopic information about the eigenstate is required is left for future work.

papers.title: Optimal convergence rates in homogenization of Monge-Ampère equations with periodic measures
papers.abstract: We establish optimal convergence rates in periodic homogenization of Monge--Ampère equations, allowing the microscopic measure to be singular or degenerate. Let $μ$ be a nonnegative $\mathbb Z^n$-periodic Borel measure with $μ(\mathbb T^n)=1$, and set $μ_\varepsilon(E)=\varepsilon^nμ(E/\varepsilon)$. On a bounded convex domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, let $u^\varepsilon$ and $u$ be the convex solutions of \[ \det D^2u^\varepsilon=F(x,x/\varepsilon)\,μ_\varepsilon,\qquad\det D^2u=\overline{F}(x) \] with the same Dirichlet data, where the coefficient $F$ is bounded, uniformly positive, and periodic in its second variable, and $\overline F(x)=\int_{\mathbb T^n}F(x,y)\,dμ(y)$. For $m=0,1$ and $0<α\leq1$, we prove \[ \|u^\varepsilon-u\|_{L^\infty(Ω)}\leq C\varepsilon^{m+α},\qquad \forall\,0<\varepsilon\leq1, \] provided that $u\in C^{m+2,α}(\overlineΩ)$ and $F(\cdot,y)\in C^{m,α}(\overlineΩ)$ uniformly in $y$. These exponents are optimal in their respective regularity scales, and the constant $C$ is independent of the distribution of the microscopic measure. In particular, the estimates include the optimal quadratic rate for general periodic measures. Our proof of the lower-order estimate ($m=0$) relies on uniform Lipschitz estimates for periodic correctors. For the higher-order estimate ($m=1$), we introduce a constrained Monge--Ampère problem that produces convex approximations with prescribed cell averages. This construction captures the cancellation in the third-order corrector expansion without uniform Hessian bounds for the correctors.

papers.title: Quillen's finiteness conjecture for the cotangent complex in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Building on work of Turner, we propose a proof in positive characteristic of Quillen's conjecture on finiteness properties of the cotangent complex for homomorphisms between noetherian rings of possibly infinite flat dimension.

papers.title: Lithium Niobate Surface-Acoustic-Wave Resonator for Very-High-Frequency Isolated Power Conversion
papers.abstract: Piezoelectric devices offer a promising magnetic-free alternative for high-frequency power conversion. Here, we demonstrate a lithium niobate surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonator that is optimized for isolated power transfer and show advantages in operating frequency, power density, power handling, and electrical isolation. Our application-optimized 40-MHz SAW resonator, with two electrically isolated interdigital transducers (IDTs) and acoustic Bragg mirrors, achieves a 25.7 W output power at a temperature rise of about 15 °C with only passive cooling through the back mounting side. With a chip size of 0.095 cm$^3$ and an acoustic mode volume of 0.00255 cm$^3$, our device features a peak chip power density of 270.5 W/cm$^3$ and a mode-volume power density of 10,078 W/cm$^3$. Our device shows an isolation voltage of 2.17 kV. Driven by a GaN full-bridge inverter, our device can drive different load resistors with a calculated peak power transfer efficiency of 87.5%. Our results show the potential of SAW devices as a core component for next-generation power systems.

papers.title: From Redundancy to Minimality: Fixed-Point-Guided Hierarchical Reduction of Learned Piecewise-Linear Dynamics
papers.abstract: Understanding a nonlinear dynamical system from time series requires not only reproducing its trajectories, but also identifying a simple representation that preserves its essential dynamical structure. Almost-linear recurrent neural networks (AL-RNNs) are piecewise-linear RNNs in which only a subset of units use ReLU nonlinearities, so that nonlinear capacity is explicitly controlled by the number of ReLU units. Their activation patterns define linear regions, represented as symbols, whose observed transitions form a symbolic transition graph. However, directly training AL-RNNs with few ReLU units to realize minimal dynamical representations can be unreliable. We ask whether an AL-RNN with more ReLU units can instead be trained first and systematically reduced to a minimal dynamical representation. We introduce a fixed-point-guided hierarchical reduction procedure that progressively linearizes selected ReLU units, merging neighboring linear regions and graph nodes while preserving distinct symbols containing fixed points (FPs). The resulting reduction tree defines a hierarchy of progressively simpler candidates. Each reduced candidate is initialized from the parent parameters and retrained through gradual linearization with guidance from the parent dynamics. We also prove that, under certain assumptions, reproducing $Q$ distinct fixed points requires at least $Q$ FP-containing symbols, providing a certificate of symbol-level minimality when this bound is attained. Across six tasks spanning attractor reconstruction and flip-flop memory, our learn-reduce-retrain strategy substantially improves the recovery of minimal models, including settings where direct training rarely succeeds. These results show that redundant nonlinear capacity can serve as a scaffold for discovering and realizing minimal dynamical representations.

papers.title: Latent Information Sharing for Accelerating Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a communication-efficient distributed learning paradigm. However, client drift remains one of the most critical challenges, hindering the efficient training of a global model. In this study, we propose a novel latent information sharing scheme that directly mitigates data heterogeneity across clients. Our theoretical and empirical results show that sharing a small amount of hidden-layer activations significantly improves training efficiency while preserving convergence guarantees and data privacy. Furthermore, we compare our method with existing FL approaches designed to address client drift, including FedProx, SCAFFOLD, FedPVR, FedProto, and SplitFed, and demonstrate superior model accuracy under a fixed round budget without incurring excessive communication overhead. Overall, this work presents a promising new knowledge aggregation scheme and provides a comprehensive analysis of the impact of activation sharing on federated optimization.

papers.title: A Few Reveal Many: Constraint-Enhanced Learning of Many-Body Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Discovering properties of many-body quantum systems is challenging due to the large number of parameters involved. Here, we show that harnessing fundamental constraints among quantum observables improves quantum learning, enabling the inference of exponentially many quantities from a linear number of direct measurements. We leverage this result to design constraint-enhanced algorithms for evaluating key quantum features such as Entanglement and Magic in 100-qubit simulators. At a fixed number of measurement shots, they achieve up to an 83% reduction in relative error compared with protocols based on constructing "classical shadows" of quantum states. Quantum constraints themselves are therefore a resource for exploring large quantum systems, guiding the allocation of the measurement budget to highly informative observables.

papers.title: Asymptotic Throat as a Minimal Geometric Alternative to the Singularity in Schwarzschild Black Hole
papers.abstract: A basic question in the study of regular black holes is whether the Schwarzschild singularity can be replaced by a geodesically complete interior while retaining a single horizon. An asymptotic throat offers a minimal geometric realization of this possibility. The areal radius approaches a finite, nonzero limit at a future internal infinity, without requiring a change in spatial topology or a bounce. We extend the geometric analysis beyond monotone contraction to interiors in which the areal radius oscillates about its limit. For both null-type and spacelike-type inner ends, we derive a necessary and sufficient integral criterion for causal geodesic completeness and criteria for bounded curvature in parallel-propagated frames. Explicit examples of both types have complete inner ends and satisfy all four standard energy conditions at sufficiently large exterior radii. Applying these criteria to the oscillatory solution of the Böhmer--Vandersloot model of effective loop quantum gravity, we find a causally complete spacelike-type inner end. Its scalar curvature invariants converge to those of the limiting Nariai-type solution. Along each radial null geodesic, however, a parallel-propagated curvature component is unbounded along a sequence of turning points as the affine parameter tends to infinity.

papers.title: ArgGYM: A Procedural, Engine-Verified Benchmark for Structured Defeasible Reasoning
papers.abstract: Recent progress in large language model reasoning has been driven by benchmarks and reinforcement learning environments with automatically verifiable rewards, particularly in mathematics, code, and formal logic. These settings make model accuracy easier to evaluate and optimize, but it remains unclear how far success under fixed problem specifications and stable evaluation criteria transfers to reasoning outside such domains. Real-world reasoning often proceeds under incomplete and revisable information: conclusions may be supported provisionally, defeated by counter-evidence, reinstated by further arguments, or revised when stronger reasons become available. Reasoning of this kind is generally referred to as defeasible reasoning. We introduce ArgGYM, a procedural benchmark and RLVR-compatible training environment for structured defeasible reasoning. ArgGYM decomposes this reasoning into twelve tasks and grounds task-specific scoring in a symbolic argumentation engine that computes the formal states used to evaluate model outputs. It includes a frozen benchmark of 1,440 verified instances across fifteen curriculum configurations, two argument preference orderings, and two set orderings, while the same generators and verifiers can produce fresh instances, reducing dependence on static test sets, for both evaluation and verifiable-reward training. On the frozen benchmark, frontier and open-weight models show sharply different reasoning profiles: they can recover substantial parts of structured answers without solving the complete task, and performance declines in later curriculum configurations with longer dependencies and more interacting structures. Training Qwen3.5-4B with ArgGYM's verifiers as rewards more than doubles complete-task success on held-out instances, with the largest gains on constructive tasks.

papers.title: Distillation Defenses Easily Break After Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Distillation attacks copy the reasoning capabilities of closed-source large language models, allowing bad actors to replicate state-of-the-art performance at low cost. Attackers systematically collect a large volume of frontier model reasoning traces and then train (i.e., "distill") their own models on these traces. Existing defenses against distillation attacks are typically evaluated immediately after distillation, implicitly assuming attackers do not train their models any further. In this paper, we argue that a more realistic threat model includes further training with reinforcement learning after distillation. A misspecified threat model can give a false sense of security -- some defenses that seem effective after distillation can be broken after subsequent reinforcement learning. Practically, reinforcement learning lowers the bar for a distillation attack to be effective. We show that simple attacks can steal reasoning capabilities from existing closed-source language models using data easily obtainable from current APIs, yielding reasoning improvements equivalent to more sophisticated attacks that extract the full hidden traces. Results indicate that any distillation defense that leaks sufficient information to reconstruct approximate reasoning traces is likely ineffective. We conclude by discussing broader implications and batch-level distillation defenses which could be more effective.

papers.title: Contraction-Based Model Predictive Control using Bilinear Koopman Realizations with Proportional Error Bounds
papers.abstract: Data-driven model predictive control based on Koopman operator theory is a promising approach for constrained control of nonlinear systems with unknown dynamics. This paper proposes a robust model predictive control framework for such systems using bilinear Koopman realizations with state- and input-dependent proportional approximation-error bounds that vanish at the target equilibrium. Since prediction in lifted coordinates with a finite-dimensional Koopman realization need not remain on the manifold of valid lifted states, multi-step prediction may leave the region where one-step error certificates apply. We avoid this difficulty by reprojecting each predicted lifted state onto the original state coordinates and lifting it again, yielding an error-aware discrete-time control-affine predictor in the original state space without assuming invariance of the Koopman dictionary. For this predictor, we develop a homothetic tube construction based on a discrete-time robust control contraction metric whose radius explicitly accounts for the proportional approximation error bounds. The tube tightening handles arbitrary continuously differentiable nonlinear constraints, and the resulting model predictive control problem includes terminal ingredients and a tube-radius penalty that exploits the vanishing uncertainty near the target. We prove robust satisfaction of the original nonlinear constraints, recursive feasibility, and exponential stability of the sampled true closed-loop system with high probability over the training data without requiring a globally optimal solution to the model predictive control problem. Numerical examples, including nonlinear obstacle-avoidance constraints, demonstrate robust stabilization and higher performance of the proposed approach compared to existing Koopman-based model predictive control methods in terms of smaller closed-loop cost and flexibility.

papers.title: Breit interaction in elastic scattering of vortex electron on Hydrogen atomic target
papers.abstract: The interaction of electron vortex beams with atoms is fundamental to their applications, yet existing studies of elastic scattering have considered only the Coulomb interaction. The role of the Breit interaction, which represents the leading relativistic correction to the Coulomb potential between two electrons, has not been systematically examined. In this paper, we study the elastic scattering of a vortex electron by a hydrogen atomic target, with emphasis on the role of the Breit interaction. Comparisons are made between two situations: the pure Coulomb contribution and the pure Breit contribution. Our results show that the Breit interaction dominates the scattering process when the total angular momentum of the vortex electron is larger than a certain threshold, which challenges the conventional notion that the Breit interaction makes little contribution to electron scattering for low-$Z$ atoms. This phenomenon arises primarily because a vortex electron with large angular momentum possesses a substantial magnetic moment, and the Breit interaction precisely describes the interaction between magnetic moments. The threshold can be adjusted by changing the parameters of the initial vortex electron. Moreover, we further compare the single-atom, mesoscopic, and macroscopic target cases, and show that the target size significantly influences the observability of the Breit-induced effects, with a smaller target size being favorable for observing this phenomenon. Vortex electrons add a new tool to the well-established electron-atom scattering tool box. Our results are important for applications of vortex electrons: they show that, when large total angular momentum is involved, the Breit interaction must be taken into account in calculations.

papers.title: DecFlowEdit: Self-Localized Flow-based Image Editing via Guidance Decoupling
papers.abstract: Flow-based image editing (FlowEdit) enables inversion-free semantic changes through the difference between source and target velocities. In this paper, we observe that FlowEdit's default classifier-free guidance (CFG) configuration, with asymmetric source and target scales, causes substantial background leakage. Matching these guidance scales, for example by removing CFG, improves edit-relevant localization but severely degrades editability. To get the best of both worlds, we propose DecFlowEdit, which decouples the optimal guidance scales for localization and for editing in flow-based generative models. In particular, DecFlowEdit first extracts an edit-relevant prior by temporally aggregating velocity differences evaluated without CFG, and then uses this prior to reweight the original updates under default CFG. Our method remains training-free and inversion-free, requiring neither external spatial masks nor attention manipulation. Experiments on PIE-Bench across FLUX.1-dev, SD3, and SD3.5 show that DecFlowEdit improves background preservation, reducing structure distance by approximately 61-73% and background LPIPS by 68-80% relative to FlowEdit at comparable editing fidelity.

papers.title: GUITAR: Structured Failure Diagnosis of GUI Agents via State Transitions
papers.abstract: Understanding where and why Graphical User Interface (GUI) agents fail is essential for building more reliable systems, yet current evaluation relies on step accuracy, a metric that treats each screen independently and overlooks the underlying structure of GUI environments. This leads to two critical blind spots: (1) functionally equivalent screens are evaluated in isolation, obscuring systematic failure patterns across shared screens; and (2) the long-tailed GUI distribution renders failures on rare but critical screens invisible under standard metrics. To address these issues, we propose \textbf{GUITAR}, a state-centric diagnostic framework that performs structured failure analysis over both states and transitions, using a State Transition Graph (STG) by mapping visually diverse screens to shared functional states. Across 8 agents and 6 tasks from AndroidControl and Mind2Web, GUITAR reveals that 60.4\% of failures occur in 20\% of states, localizing errors to a small set of bottlenecks. Bottleneck-targeted guidance improves SR by 2.8\% and retains a 1.88\% average gain across 7 agents under three-fold trajectory-held-out evaluation with fully automatic STGs. These findings demonstrate the diagnostic and actionable value of structure-aware evaluation within the evaluated mobile and web tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/sqzhang-lazy/GUITAR

papers.title: Surprising Success, Repeated Failure: Entropy-Guided Credit Assignment for Exploration in LLM Reasoning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) enhances reasoning in large language models (LLMs) through outcome-level feedback, yet recent approaches to finer-grained credit assignment often require auxiliary models, additional sampling, or privileged information. Although policy entropy provides a readily available signal, prioritizing uncertain positions under both reinforcement and penalization concentrates penalties where failed responses still retain alternatives for recovery, which can suppress opportunities for exploration. To address this, we introduce Entropic Advantage Policy Optimization (EAPO), an entropy-guided credit assignment method that treats success and failure asymmetrically. Specifically, motivated by the observation that success under uncertainty is less repeatable while confident failures tend to recur, EAPO couples normalized policy entropy with the sign of the response advantage to reinforce surprising success and correct repeated failure. It assigns stronger reinforcement to high-entropy decisions in successful responses and stronger penalties to low-entropy decisions in failed responses, while attenuating penalties at uncertain positions to preserve opportunities for recovery. By redistributing the response advantage across tokens, EAPO derives token-level credit directly from existing rollout signals without additional supervision. We validate EAPO on a range of reasoning tasks across both base and reasoning backbones, demonstrating that it achieves the best overall performance. We further show that EAPO promotes more effective exploration, broadening problem coverage and diversifying successful reasoning strategies.

papers.title: ALDER: Discovering the Laws of a World by Acting in It
papers.abstract: Reliable world models should not only predict future states but express how actions change the world in an explicit, transparent and testable form, such as equations. Yet methods that rely on a fixed set of trajectories cannot distinguish equally good competing hypotheses, while searches over a fixed set of predefined candidates cannot discover equations outside the initial hypothesis space. We introduce ALDER (Action-guided Law Discovery, Evaluation, and Revision), a method that actively proposes novel experiments to test and revise models. Specifically, ALDER proposes parametric equations; a numerical optimizer fits their coefficients; an independent verifier tests these candidates on held-out data. To distinguish between competing valid hypotheses, a cost- and safety-aware selector queries interventions, in the form of novel experiments. The resulting counterexamples update the evidence ledger and guide the next structural revision, while incompatible laws are discarded. Across an in-house benchmark, ODE equation discovery tasks, and robotic experiments, ALDER discovers laws beyond its initial formula set, repairs failed model proposals, distinguishes fixed candidate models with fewer interactions, and improves out-of-distribution prediction. Furthermore, given a current state and a target, ALDER selects control actions by solving the inverse problem defined by its validated world model. Together, these results show that explicit equation-based world models can be tested and revised through interaction, then naturally used to guide goal-directed control.

papers.title: Learning response-aware patient dynamics for respiratory support
papers.abstract: Respiratory support can shape the short-term physiological trajectory of critically ill patients, but patients receiving the same intervention may follow different physiological trajectories. Clinical patient dynamics models typically predict future states from recent physiology and recorded interventions, while physiological change is mainly represented through the predicted future state. We propose a response-aware patient dynamics model that explicitly represents physiological change during autoregressive state updating. The model decomposes predicted physiological change into state-dependent baseline dynamics and respiratory-support-associated deviations, with room air providing a reference for the decomposition. We provide a formal analysis of this reference-anchored formulation. A response pathway encodes the predicted physiological change and uses it to update the latent patient state across the forecast horizon. Across ICU cohorts from two independent institutions, the proposed model achieves comparable overall trajectory prediction to patient dynamics baselines, with more consistent improvements when physiological states are changing.

papers.title: RIPE-MambaSpike: Resolution-Independent Spiking-State-Space Interfaces for Parameter-Efficient Event-Based Vision
papers.abstract: Spiking-Mamba hybrids reach strong accuracy on event-based vision, but existing designs often require tens of millions of parameters. In hybrids that flatten the spiking feature map and project it densely into the scan, much of that cost comes from this interface rather than from the hybrid architecture itself. In a representative model, a single resolution-dependent projection accounts for 33.55M of 36.25M parameters. To that end, we introduce RIPE-MambaSpike (Resolution-Independent, Parameter-Efficient), which replaces that projection with a hierarchical multi-resolution bridge of fixed channel width. Its deployed footprint is 0.870M parameters, constant at fixed time steps and widths across a 43x range of input areas. Reparameterized spiking stages, temporal decoupled modulation, and a dynamic convex-hull-bounded dual-stream membrane-potential attention preserve accuracy under this compact design. Result-wise, RIPE-MambaSpike is pareto-optimal on CIFAR10-DVS, N-Caltech101, and DailyDVS-200. Notably, on the 200-class DailyDVS-200, a scaled 8.04M configuration achieves 45.7% top-1 accuracy, the best reported spiking result on that benchmark, and outperforms prior spiking methods with 3.0-15.1x fewer parameters than dense ANNs. Overall, our findings demonstrate that competitive event-based recognition does not require resolution-dependent parameter growth. Code is available at https://github.com/MuhiminOsim/RIPE-MambaSpike.

papers.title: Can Circuit Alignment Predict OOD Generalization?
papers.abstract: Can out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization be predicted from a trained model's weights alone, without any target-domain data? Existing representational similarity metrics (CKA, SVCCA, RSA) compare activations rather than forecast generalization. We show they are provably insensitive to structural rerouting in the computational graph, the very change distribution shift induces. We close this gap with the Circuit Alignment Score (CAS), which compares class-specific circuits across domains via graph kernels, decomposed into same-class coherence and cross-class confusion. Casting CAS as a Lebesgue integral over the domain distribution, we prove its Monte Carlo estimate recovers the ground-truth ranking of learners by OOD accuracy, with pairwise inversion error vanishing at rate $O(1/M)$, where $M$ is the number of sampled domains. Across $48$ learners on PACS, CAS attains $0.88$ rank correlation with OOD accuracy, versus $0.58$ (CKA), $0.23$ (SVCCA), and $0.14$ (RSA), with similar trends on other benchmarks and even against data-dependent methods, making it the first provably consistent predictor of distributional robustness requiring neither target-domain data nor labels. The code is available at: https://github.com/ayanban011/ACE

papers.title: Tails, Trails, and Transients: Comets, NEOs, and Supernovae in Rubin Early Data Preview 2
papers.abstract: We identify effective single-visit imaging hidden within the deep coadded images of the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory Early Data Preview 2 (EDP2). We develop a workflow to locate known small Solar System bodies in these data, using our Ponder orchestrator with the Sorcha survey simulator to predict their positions and the Rubin Science Platform to identify shallow coadds and extract image cutouts. Because cometary activity and near-Earth object (NEO) trails produce extended morphologies, both remain identifiable in shallow coadds. From approximately 700 comet cutouts, we identify 59 activity detections spanning 32 objects. We discover activity in 2025 NC6, previously unknown to be active, and independently rediscover two comets through their activity. We recover 336 NEO cutouts, including 29 with predicted trails over 25 pixels. We demonstrate how the same provenance-driven methods can recover stationary transients in Rubin coadds, including ones predating the alert stream. Of 47 publicly-reported transients coinciding with EDP2, 36 occupy shallow coadds. We show Rubin photometry agrees with published lightcurves to within 0.2 mag. The imaging provides additional bands, host-galaxy context, and deeper supernova pre-discovery limits than discovery surveys could reach. We showcase seven transients, including SN 2025nbh, which we identify as lying in the outskirts of AGC 114905, an ultra-diffuse galaxy central to the dark-matter-free debate; the supernova offers an independent galaxy distance measurement. Shallow coadds are a relatively unexplored facet of Rubin data with applications beyond the examples presented here; regions with varying numbers of contributing visits will persist throughout the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST).

papers.title: Pauli Spectra as a Boundary Spectroscope in Quantum Spin Chains
papers.abstract: We show that Pauli spectra provide a boundary spectroscope in critical quantum spin chains, resolving microscopic boundary fingerprints and finite responses to physical boundary changes. Universal logarithmic corrections to stabilizer Renyi entropy can remain identical across distinct boundary configurations, while their finite contributions retain information about how the physical boundaries are related. Using critical Ising chains, we demonstrate that suitable combinations of Pauli moments isolate normalization-independent responses to boundary reversal and reveal nonadditive contributions associated with the joint boundary configuration. These responses become analytically accessible through an exact term-by-term correspondence that organizes individual Pauli magnitudes into classical-group statistical structures, with their moments represented by discrete Selberg sums associated with unitary, orthogonal, and symplectic ensembles. In particular, fixed-boundary reversal admits an exact symplectic-character representation, while the same framework provides access to boundary-sensitive behavior at the Rényi transition. Our results establish a new connection between nonstabilizerness and boundary criticality through the exact statistical structures of classical-group ensembles.

papers.title: The Uniqueness of Exponential Second-Order Expected Utility
papers.abstract: A decision-maker entertains several probability models of the state of the world, distrusts each of them, and is unsure which of them holds. She therefore carries two relative-entropy penalties: one on departures from a given model and one on departures from the reference she places on models. The literature that introduced this structure treats the equality of the two penalty parameters as a tractable special case. We show that it is in fact a necessary and sufficient condition: her criterion carries a single relative-entropy penalty if and only if the two parameters agree, that is, when she charges the same price for doubting a model as for doubting her weights on models. Under that one condition the two layers collapse: the criterion is an exponential second-order expected utility based at the Bayesian predictive distribution, for every compact model set and every prior, with no large-sample limit anywhere. When the condition fails, the caution she displays blends her two parameters, with a weight equal to the share of an act's predictive variance that comes from disagreement among the models; since that share varies across acts, no single parameter and baseline represent her, and the same variation identifies the two parameters separately. The exponential aggregator and relative entropy are each forced: no other continuous and strictly increasing aggregator delivers the collapse, and within the power-divergence family only relative entropy does.

papers.title: Interweaving Marginals into Multivariate Sample Paths: Training-Free Dependence Construction for Probabilistic Time Series Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Probabilistic time series foundation models (TSFMs) provide coordinate-wise predictive distributions, but these marginals do not determine a joint distribution over multivariate future trajectories. We study training-free coupling of frozen TSFM marginals into multivariate forecast sample paths. Our primary evaluation fixes the empirical marginal sample multiset at every channel--horizon coordinate across methods, isolating the effect of coupling alone. Historical temporal and channel relations substantially improve their corresponding dependence diagnostics. The same pattern persists when the fixed-marginal constraint is removed and paths are sampled directly, and remains present under native multivariate backbone inference. These results support treating dependence reconstruction as a distinct post-processing problem for probabilistic TSFMs.

papers.title: WorldCrafter: Consistent Video World Model with Implicit 3D-aware Memory
papers.abstract: Video world models enable interactive exploration of dynamic environments, yet struggle to respect prior observations over long horizons and across viewpoints. We present WorldCrafter, a video world model that learns a camera-queryable implicit 3D-aware memory for this purpose. The key insight is to let the requested viewpoint shape how multi-view evidence is compressed into the video generator's limited token budget. Trained jointly with the video generator, a memory encoder and pose-conditioned readout module integrate historical observations into a fixed set of target view-specific tokens before denoising, without explicit depth-based correspondences. By combining this memory with recent temporal context and few-step distillation, WorldCrafter enables streaming scene exploration from a single input image or text prompt. Experiments across static and dynamic scenes show substantial gains in long-horizon consistency and camera-control accuracy while preserving visual quality during minute-scale exploration.

papers.title: Preserving Geometric Integrity in Graph Prompting via Measure-Constrained Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Graph prompt learning enables parameter-efficient adaptation of frozen Graph Neural Networks to downstream tasks through lightweight prompt parameters. As routing becomes increasingly node-adaptive, however, independently optimized local decisions can collectively concentrate assignment mass on a small subset of a finite shared prompt bank, even when individual node--prompt matches remain locally meaningful. We propose MINT (Measure-INtegrity Transport), an entropically regularized optimal transport framework that formulates node-to-prompt adaptation as a globally coupled allocation problem. The transport cost favors local geometric compatibility, while a prescribed prompt-side marginal explicitly controls graph-wide prompt utilization. We further derive an exact variance decomposition that separates prompt-side geometric variance into retained prompt-update variation and within-node barycentric dispersion, together with a conditional stability bound for the frozen-encoder forward map. Across standard citation networks and additional heterophilic graphs, MINT remains competitive in few-shot adaptation. Controlled and end-to-end experiments further distinguish the roles of routing and topology: fixed-marginal routing controls graph-wide prompt utilization and has measurable end-to-end effects on citation networks, while topology augmentation provides a complementary, graph-dependent mechanism for addressing structural mismatch. Code is available at https://github.com/Ga1axy0051/MINT.

papers.title: Uniform Inference for Parameters Identified by Conditional Quantile Restrictions
papers.abstract: Many structural and dynamic economic models imply that key parameters are identified by conditional quantile restrictions. Building on the exponential weighting approach of Bierens (1990) and the penalized maximum statistics of Chen et al. (2025), we develop a uniform inference method for such parameters. We construct an adaptive $\ell_1$-penalized statistic from a process indexed by quantiles and weighting directions. The statistic aggregates evidence across quantiles and regularizes maximization over directions. A shifted bootstrap is used to estimate local power for penalty selection. Under the stated conditions, adaptive selection asymptotically preserves or improves worst case local power relative to the unpenalized test over a prespecified set of alternatives. The improvement is strict when a positive candidate penalty raises the population level criterion above its value at zero. We also extend the process and bootstrap theory to the setting with pre-estimated nuisance parameters. We characterize their contribution to the limiting process, correct the variance estimator, and establish Gaussian multiplier bootstrap validity for null inference. Monte Carlo experiments favor the CvM-KS method for size control under pre-estimation and show that adaptive penalization can improve empirical power relative to the unpenalized test.

papers.title: Do Personality-Tuned LLMs Make Better Social Agents?
papers.abstract: LLMs are increasingly used in social simulations for socially interactive agents and robots, offering more flexibility than rule-based systems. However, even though they mimic human behaviour very well, there is a persistent alienness to them. This work investigates whether personality-aware fine-tuning can reduce this gap by improving the consistency and controllability of personality-conditioned dialogue generation compared with instruction prompting alone. We fine-tune two small open-weight LLMs, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Ministral-8B-Instruct, using a corpus that combines personality-labelled social media posts and dialogues to create a personality-based dialogue engine for social simulation. The resulting models are evaluated across multiple social interaction scenarios using three independent LLM judges, which assess personality fidelity and provide evidence-based behavioral interpretations. We additionally quantify inter-rater agreement and lexical characteristics of the generated dialogue. Results indicate that fine-tuned models are not better at role-playing different personalities than their respective baseline models. However, low inter-rater agreement limits the confidence with which these results can be interpreted. Concerning the quality of generated texts, fine-tuned models are mostly comparable to the baselines, with fine-tuning improving the linguistic diversity of the Qwen models. While the results appear generally usable and the baseline models offer the best overall performance, future studies should place greater emphasis on the quality and domain alignment of training data for accurate personality role-playing.

papers.title: A Geodesic Route toward Holography beyond AdS: Tessellating the Schwarzschild Black Hole
papers.abstract: In vacuum anti-de Sitter (AdS) space, the geometry admits a perfect tessellation by a geodesic network. This tessellation characterizes the background exactly, and a partial entanglement entropy (PEE) tensor-network toy model of AdS/CFT can be defined on it. It has so far been unclear whether this construction can be extended beyond vacuum AdS. In this paper we take the first step in this direction. We show that the exterior region of the Schwarzschild black hole and its Einstein--Rosen bridge are perfectly tessellated by a specific geodesic gas emitted from the boundary, so that Crofton reconstruction holds in these regions. We then prove that such a geodesic tessellation and the Crofton reconstruction it defines extend to more generic Riemannian manifolds. This allows us to construct a PEE tensor-network model of holographic duality on more generic geometric backgrounds. In the case of the PEE tensor-network model for the Schwarzschild background, we can concretely realize the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy, the Ryu--Takayanagi formula and the ER=EPR proposal. Our approach opens a new route towards holographic toy models beyond AdS/CFT.

papers.title: Fixed point properties for random groups in the density model with $d > \frac{1}{4}$
papers.abstract: We prove that random groups in Gromov's density model have Kazhdan's property~\((T)\) asymptotically almost surely (a.a.s.) at every density \(d>\frac14\). Together with Ashcroft's theorem for \(d<\frac14\), this establishes \(\frac14\) as the sharp threshold and settles the long-standing problem of determining the threshold for property $(T)$ in the density model. More generally, for every fixed number of generators \(n\ge2\) and density \(d\in(\frac14,1)\), there exists \(C_{n,d}>0\) such that, a.a.s., every affine isometric action on a real \(L^p\)-space has a fixed point simultaneously for all \[ 1\le p\le C_{n,d}\sqrt{\frac{l}{\log l}}, \] where \(l\) is the relator length. In particular, \(\frac14\) is also the threshold for each fixed \(L^p\) fixed point property, \(1\le p<\infty\). We also establish a simultaneous fixed point theorem for a large class of uniformly smooth real Banach spaces with a common power-type convexity bound and a suitable common bound on their uniform curvature moduli. We further prove that, for each fixed real Banach space in a class that, to the best of our knowledge, contains all currently known examples of super-reflexive Banach spaces, random groups at density $d>1/4$ a.a.s.\ have the fixed point property for affine isometric actions. The proof combines a fixed point criterion based on harmonic cocycles with spectral estimates for random bipartite multigraphs arising from decompositions of relators into four consecutive subwords. All asymptotic conclusions hold as \(\RelLen\to\infty\) through all positive integers.

papers.title: When to Use Subagents
papers.abstract: When should a task be delegated to subagents? We answer this at the granularity of individual trajectories.
