We prove global well-posedness in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ and global regularity for data of arbitrary size in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$, with bounds uniform in $\varepsilon$ and in time. For data in $L^1\cap L^2$, the energy decays like $t^{-3/2}$, with a constant independent of $\varepsilon$; for data in $L^1\cap H^2$, the first two derivatives decay at the corresponding heat rates. We identify the leading asymptotic profile and show that $t^{3/2}\|u(t)\|_{L^2}^2\toγ_\varepsilon(8πν)^{-3/2}|m_\infty|^2$, where $m_\infty$ is an asymptotic momentum and the explicit factor $γ_\varepsilon\in(\frac23,1)$ measures the energy removed by the penalization. Consequently, the decay rates are optimal in $L^1\cap H^2$ under an explicit non-degeneracy condition. Finally, as $\varepsilon\to0$, the solutions converge globally in time to those of the incompressible hyperviscous Navier--Stokes equations at the rate $\sqrt\varepsilon$, up to an explicit initial layer, and $-\varepsilon^{-1}div\,u$ converges to the pressure.

papers.title: Harmonic weights in inverse central binomial series
papers.abstract: We study how the partial fraction coefficients of an inverse central binomial series change when the harmonic weight $H_{pn}$ is replaced by $H_{qn}$. For positive integers $p<q$, every coefficient increases. As the index $k$ grows, the increase tends to $2\log(q/p)$ uniformly over all angles $0<ϕ\leπ$, even when the angle approaches either endpoint. The increase is above the limit at every odd index and below it at every even index. We give the first correction, of order $k^{-2/q}$ for $q>2$ and of order $k^{-2}$ for $(p,q)=(1,2)$. For the normalized transforms, subtracting $c$ times the first from the second gives a Stieltjes function exactly when $c\le1$. We also determine which real dilations $0<p<q$ satisfy the same sign law. For $p\ge1$ it holds exactly when $q\ge2$. For $0<p<1$ it holds above a threshold $Q(p)$, and at the threshold it holds precisely on one interval $0<p<p_*$. Finally, we give angle identities at every odd weight from three onward and determine which Dirichlet $L$-terms cancel at angle $π/3$.

papers.title: Universal swelling of tangentially driven ring polymers in two dimensions
papers.abstract: The interplay of tangential activity and excluded-volume interactions in ring polymers adsorbed to a surface, consistently results in the overall swelling of the ring configurations. This is in strong contrast to the case for three dimensional linear and ring polymers, where activity induces frequently collapsed structures. By means of Brownian Dynamic simulations, we investigate how the scaling properties of such active rings can be universally characterized by an activity-dependent Flory exponent, as a generalization of the equilibrium behavior. At high activity, an effective persistence length characterizes the conformations of active flexible rings.

papers.title: Impact of Channel Dynamics on Higher-order Interactions of Oscillators
papers.abstract: Modeling higher-order interactions (HOIs) in nonlinear networks with static topologies is often physically restrictive. We demonstrate that standard 3-body Kuramoto couplings are mathematically equivalent to pairwise connections modulated by latent variables of transmission channels. While standard HOI topologies emerge in the adiabatic limit of these variables, relaxing this constraint reveals that latent channel timescales dictate collective macroscopic states. Specifically, transmission inertia drives bistability for symmetric interaction tensors and anti-phase cluster synchronization for antisymmetric ones. Furthermore, dynamically induced clustering in global topologies emerges as a finite-size effect of the dynamics of the local channels. Ultimately, we show that relying exclusively on static topologies restricts interaction modeling. Integrating latent variables captures the transient inertia and fundamental asymmetry of physical networks, bridging the analytical utility of higher-order functions with the reality of the underlying transmission medium.

papers.title: The Stability of the Backward Problem for Photoacoustic Imaging in Attenuating Media via Carleman Estimates
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the backward problem in time for photoacoustic tomography (PAT) in attenuating media. It is well-established that photoacoustic imaging in attenuating media can be accurately modeled by spatial fractional-order damping. This inverse problem is ill-posed in the sense of Hadamard. In this work, we construct a novel class of Carleman estimates independent of spatial variables, and by virtue of these estimates, we establish conditional stability estimates for this problem for the first time. Building upon this, we propose a Tikhonov-type regularization functional and derive its associated adjoint system. Furthermore, leveraging the established conditional stability results, we derive the convergence rate of the proposed regularization approach. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of our theoretical findings through extensive numerical experiments.

papers.title: Probing Extended Recognition Sites in Zn-Metalloproteins via Quantum Chemistry and Polarizable Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: Zn-metalloproteins play vital roles in numerous metabolic processes, making them high-value targets for structure-based drug design. To advance these efforts, it is useful to unravel the individual components of the intermolecular interaction energies ($ΔE$) that stabilize the Zn-binding cavity, both in the absence and presence of bound protein ligands. Here, we utilize quantum chemistry (QC) to decompose $ΔE$ into distinct physical contributions. The relative magnitudes of these components vary significantly depending on the coordination number (four to six) and the chemical nature ('hard' vs. 'soft') of the Zn-coordinating ligands. These high-level QC analyses serve to calibrate and validate polarizable molecular mechanics potentials, effectively extending the accurate description of electronic effects beyond the immediate Zn-binding cavity to enlarged recognition sites and, ultimately, entire protein systems over long molecular dynamics (MD) simulation timescales. We focus here on a QC-grounded molecular mechanics procedure, denoted as SIBFA. Following a concise overview of our QC methodology used for its calibration, we present validation studies on complexes containing up to 300 atoms and discuss the prospects of applying this framework to large-scale simulations of Zn-metalloprotein-ligand complexes. Finally, the structural and energetic roles of discrete, highly polarizable water molecules are highlighted.

papers.title: XRISM Reveals a Kinematically Coherent Core System of the Nearby Cool-Core Cluster Abell 2199
papers.abstract: We present the results of a deep 251 ks XRISM/Resolve observation of the cool core of the galaxy cluster Abell 2199. From the integrated spectrum of the central $3' \times 3'$ Resolve field of view ($104 \times 104 \mathrm{~kpc}^2$), we find that the intracluster medium (ICM) redshift is consistent with that of the brightest cluster galaxy, within the optical-redshift uncertainty. This indicates that they form a kinematically coherent core system, which is offset from the mean cluster redshift by $\sim200~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$. The observed velocity dispersion of $\sim100~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$ corresponds to a three-dimensional Mach number of $M_{\mathrm{3D}}=0.16$ and a non-thermal pressure fraction of $P_{\mathrm{NT}}/P_{\mathrm{tot}}=1.4\pm0.2$%. Abell 2199 is one of the most dynamically quiescent relaxed clusters observed with XRISM, despite the presence of radio jets and a plume-like structure possibly associated with sloshing motions. Order-of-magnitude estimates suggest that turbulent dissipation could offset a non-negligible fraction of the radiative cooling losses, with $Q_{\mathrm{turb}}/Q_{\mathrm{cool}}\approx0.1$ for a large-scale driver such as sloshing and larger values for smaller AGN-feedback scales. Finally, we detect a localized enhancement of the Fe XXV He$α$ $y$ line in the southeast region, which spatially coincides with a Chandra surface brightness discontinuity.

papers.title: Connecting Microseismicity to Lithology via a Model of Slip Avalanches
papers.abstract: Fluid injection into the earth's crust can induce small and frequent earthquakes in the subsurface. Predicting their sizes and temporal occurrences via statistical analysis is crucial for safe operations in unconventional oil and gas recovery, enhanced geothermal systems, and geologic carbon storage. Here we show that a simple micromechanical model of slip avalanches in slowly deforming solids predicts the slip statistics observed over drastically different spatial scales, namely meter-scale microseismic observations and nanometer- to micrometer-scale nanoindentation experiments can be described with this model. Microseismic catalogs extracted from high-pressure fluid injection operations into geological basins with various lithologies and nanoindentation experiments on shale across a wide range of temperatures and mineral compositions yield statistics consistent with model predictions. This universality across materials, temperatures, and scales is consistent with the prediction that the slip statistics result from only a few basic properties. Previously debated deviations of the statistics in layered sedimentary formations are explained by finite-size and stress-integrative effects resulting from mechanically weak bedding planes. The slip statistics therefore provide important information about the structure and scales of the bedding planes. Conversely, the basin structure can also be used to predict the probability distribution for the sizes of triggered microseismic events.

papers.title: Landau-type theorems for $K$-quasiregular harmonic mappings
papers.abstract: In this paper, our aim is to establish several Landau-type theorems for $K$-quasiregular harmonic mappings $f=h+\overline{g}$ in the unit disk $\Bbb{D} = \{z\in\Bbb{C}: |z|<1\}$. Under various boundedness assumptions on the analytic part $h$, we obtain explicit univalence radii and corresponding schlicht disk radii that improve upon existing estimates in the literature. We also establish new Landau-type theorems under novel hypotheses. We provide examples to illustrate our results, and comprehensive numerical tables present quantitative values of the radii for various parameter choices, demonstrating the effectiveness of our results.

papers.title: A Gallager-Type Redundancy Bound for Binary Fano Coding
papers.abstract: Binary Fano codes build a complete prefix code by repeatedly splitting the sorted list of symbol probabilities into two halves whose total probabilities are as close to each other as possible. Krajči, Liu, Mikeš, and Moser proved in 2015 that the redundancy $R$ of this code satisfies $R\le1-p_n$, where $p_n$ is the smallest symbol probability. We prove that $R<U(p_1)$, where $U$ is a piecewise function of the largest symbol probability $p_1$ with $U<1$. In particular, $R<p_1+4-\tfrac53\log_2 5$ for every source, and $R<\tfrac52-\tfrac56\log_2 5$ when $p_1<\tfrac12$. The bound equals the supremum of the redundancy for $p_1\ge\tfrac12$ and on an interval just below $\tfrac13$, and we give a lower bound for the other values of $p_1$. Unlike the bounds for Huffman codes, the proofs do not use the sibling property. They work directly with the Fano split rule, mainly through the facts that every split is nearly balanced and that the redundancy is a sum of one term per internal node of the tree.

papers.title: When Simpler Is Better: Evaluating Translation Pipelines for Medieval Latin Manuscripts
papers.abstract: Despite remarkable progress in machine translation, Vision Language Models (VLMs) struggle on historical manuscripts, a domain that stresses core Natural Language Processing (NLP) capabilities: low-resource transliteration, archaic vocabulary, and noisy input signals. We present a systematic framework for evaluating the full image-to-translation pipeline on medieval Latin manuscripts, a setting in which scribal shorthand, ligatures, and parchment degradation expose failure modes that are invisible in clean-text benchmarks. Benchmarking on the CATMuS Latin dataset reveals a specialization gap: domain-specific Optical Character Recognition (OCR) models reduce character error rate by up to 4.3$\times$ compared to general-purpose VLMs, despite operating at orders of magnitude fewer parameters. We introduce the Interpres-Parallel-Corpus (IPC), a novel dataset comprising 1,383 aligned manuscript image lines, transcriptions, and expert translations, to our knowledge the first of its kind for medieval Latin. Our experiments uncover a complexity paradox: the simplest pipeline, a specialized OCR model feeding directly into a VLM, outperforms all multi-component variants. Adding retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) or post-OCR correction introduces prompt saturation and error propagation that degrade aggregate translation quality. These findings offer both a new benchmark and practical guidance for deploying translation systems in low-resource historical settings.

papers.title: GameEngineBench: Full-Session Verification of Coding Agents in a Networked Game Engine
papers.abstract: Coding agents face new challenges in game development, where they must produce code that is not only syntactically correct but also consistent with engine-managed lifecycle, state, and networking behavior. Existing game-development benchmarks, however, do not combine assertions over engine-based runtime states with cross-client consistency, failing to evaluate how well generated code adheres to the desired behavioral specifications. To address these limitations, we present GameEngineBench, a benchmark of 110 C++ implementation tasks derived from 9 existing Unreal Engine 5 projects. Each task requires an agent to implement missing behavior within an established gameplay architecture. We also introduce Full-Session Verification, a testing framework that injects hidden tests after the agent finishes and evaluates the resulting implementation inside Play-in-Editor (PIE) sessions, with networked client worlds in 71 tasks. The tests evaluate Unreal's game loop, actor lifecycle, subsystems, and replication stack while directly inspecting runtime state. In 53 tasks, 119 tests additionally inspect a distinct client world to determine whether the authoritative server state is correctly replicated. To our knowledge, this is the first coding benchmark to evaluate cross-client replication. Across 11 model-harness configurations, the best-scoring configuration achieves 46.4% pass@1, while 43 tasks remain unsolved by every evaluated configuration. These results demonstrate that compilation and shallow verification overestimate agents' ability to implement behavior that remains correct during full engine execution.

papers.title: The structure of FAC posets and the Aharoni--Korman conjecture
papers.abstract: A poset $P$ is said to satisfy the finite antichain condition, or FAC for short, if it has no infinite antichain. Such posets exhibit rich and complex structure, and it was conjectured by Aharoni and Korman in 1992 that any FAC poset $P$ possesses a chain $C$ and a partition into antichains such that $C$ meets every antichain of the partition. While a counterexample to this conjecture was recently discovered, in this paper we prove that the conjecture does hold true for a broad class of countable posets. In particular, we prove that the Aharoni--Korman conjecture holds for countable FAC posets containing no saturated chain $D$ such that either $D$ or its reverse $D^*$ is of the form $\bigoplus_{x\inω} D_x$, where each $D_x$ is infinite and co-well-founded. The proof of this result rests on novel structural theory for countable FAC posets, which may be of independent interest. One result states that every countable FAC poset is either scattered (contains no copy of the rationals) or may be broken up into a dense collection of scattered posets which reflect the structure of the poset as a whole. This provides a general reduction from arbitrary countable FAC posets to the far more tractable scattered ones. We also develop an extension $H(P)$ of a poset $P$ which includes ``limit points'' of $P$ and allows for intricate arguments involving these points. Amongst other points, one way in which $H(P)$ differs from existing poset completions and extensions is that it is sensitive to the order-type of a chain. Finally, we highlight a number of intriguing problems in this area which remain open.

papers.title: Convergence of Large-Stepsize SGD for the Cross-entropy Loss via Stochastic Lyapunov Stability
papers.abstract: Modern deep learning has been shown to operate using learning rates far larger than those justified by classical optimization theory. Most prior analyses of this phenomenon focus on deterministic gradient descent, leaving the stochastic setting largely unexplored. In this work, we provide sharp convergence guarantees for Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) applied to the multiclass cross-entropy loss, for both linear classifiers and two-layer neural networks. We show that the stochasticity of SGD may cause the dynamics to alternate between an edge-of-stability regime that is dominated by curvature-driven oscillations, and a stable regime in which the expected loss decreases at a controlled rate. Despite that, we prove that SGD stabilizes the dynamics, ensuring that the iterates return to stability in a fixed number of iterations and allowing convergence in the best-iterate sense even with large learning rates. Experiments validate our theoretical findings and illustrate the benefits of SGD in the large-stepsize regime.

papers.title: PyMETA: Evaluating Student Code Diagnosis on and Beyond the First Execution Error
papers.abstract: Code-diagnosis evaluation depends on how error supervision is constructed and what that supervision treats as a correct diagnosis. We introduce PyMETA, a dataset of 48,646 Python submissions with execution-derived single-error labels, and a targeted subset of 97 submissions annotated by experts through repair and re-execution. Under the first-outcome protocol, four recent prompted models obtain 87.5-93.8% macro F1, all above the strongest finetuned baseline at 80.6%. This reverses the comparison obtained with the earlier set of prompted models. The expert subset gives a less favorable account of complete diagnosis: exact-set match ranges from 43.3% to 48.5%, although sample F1 is approximately 79-81%. The evaluation setup also changes which behavior is visible. On the same 45 audited submissions without an expert-annotated Logic Error, none of the four recent models predicts that label when restricted to one output, whereas 46.7-57.8% include it under multi-error prompting, usually after an explicit-error label. These findings show that model comparisons and error-bias claims depend on what the gold label represents, which outputs the model is allowed to return, and how those outputs are scored.

papers.title: Does Regime-Gated Attention Help Stock Return Prediction? A Leakage-Controlled, Pre-Registered Evaluation
papers.abstract: Regime-aware attention is an appealing inductive bias for stock-return prediction, but claims about it are rarely tested under leakage-controlled, out-of-sample conditions. We re-examine the Adaptive Financial Transformer (AFT), which biases self-attention with feature-group similarities weighted by gates that a market-regime encoder produces. First, on a single stock under a corrected protocol (aligned and purged windows, identical test dates for all models, cost-aware non-overlapping backtests, five seeds, Diebold-Mariano tests), no learned model beats the historical-mean forecast. The AFT's regime and context components are numerically inert: the learned gates have 0.9982 of maximal entropy, the context bias has 0.020 of the scale of the attention logits, and we show that the product of two simplex-normalised weightings attenuates it by a factor 1/G. Removing these components changes nothing. Second, we build a point-in-time S&P 500 panel (500 stocks, 1,390,254 stock-days) with 63 stationary features whose causality is verified exactly, and evaluate a model zoo and a layered meta-model with yearly walk-forward refits, a development period (2016-2022) and a sealed, pre-registered holdout (2023-2025). Cross-sectional breadth turns weak signals into detectable ones; the AFT is statistically indistinguishable from a vanilla Transformer and less stable than gradient boosting or ridge regression; six learned meta-learners fail to beat an equal-weight rank combination; and a hysteresis rule roughly halves turnover. On the holdout, the pre-registered primary system (21-day horizon) fails (rank IC 0.0003, one-sided p=0.49), whereas the same system at a 5-day horizon, a pre-registered secondary result, attains a rank IC of 0.0172 (one-sided p=0.038) and a net long-short Sharpe ratio of 0.34 at 5 bp per side. Code: https://github.com/Dishan18/FinancialTransformer

papers.title: Hierarchical Bayesian Estimation of Covariance Matrices
papers.abstract: We develop a hierarchical Bayesian framework for covariance matrix estimation built on a key observation: while equivariance under the full general linear group GL(p) is well known, it is an extremely restrictive property. Estimators equivariant to GL(p) are limited to scalar multiples of the sample covariance matrix and carry considerably larger risks than shrinkage estimators. By contrast, commonly used shrinkage estimators, including the Haff empirical Bayes estimator and the Ledoit-Wolf estimators, are all equivariant under the smaller orthogonal group O(p). Exploiting this structure, we establish that the Haar measure Bayes rule in an oracle eigenvalue model is the minimum risk estimator within the class of O(p)-equivariant estimators, and derive oracle Bayes rules for the covariance and precision matrices under the squared Frobenius, Stein, and squared Stein loss functions. These oracle rules serve as theoretical benchmarks for all O(p)-equivariant estimators. To approximate them when the true eigenvalues are unknown, we introduce a hierarchical Bayes model that places a finite Pólya tree prior on the eigenvalue distribution and uses Gibbs sampling to generate posterior draws, yielding both shrinkage estimates for the eigenvalues and approximations to the oracle Bayes rules. In simulations, the resulting estimators come close to the risk of the oracle rules and have smaller risk than commonly used estimators, particularly when p/n is large. In an application to monthly returns of 49 US industry portfolios, the proposed estimators had the highest out-of-sample likelihood of all the estimators we compared, and their minimum-variance portfolios had variance comparable to that of estimators designed specifically for portfolio selection.

papers.title: MSU-Bench: Towards Speaker-Centric Understanding in Conversational Multi-Speaker Scenarios
papers.abstract: Spoken Language Understanding (SLU) is moving from task-specific pipelines toward large audio language models (LALMs) that generate natural-language responses. However, existing speech benchmarks mainly focus on single-speaker settings or isolated subtasks, leaving speaker-centric understanding in realistic multi-speaker conversations insufficiently evaluated. We introduce MSU-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark for multi-speaker conversational understanding, covering 16 speaker-centric tasks and 2,300 QA instances in a two-tier framework from speaker grounding to dialogue reasoning. We build a Gemini-assisted annotation and QA generation pipeline with human-in-the-loop verification, achieving high QA validity and strong agreement between human answers and verified labels. We further analyze speaker-referencing schemes and diagnostic error types to reveal bottlenecks in speaker grounding and reasoning. Experiments reveal clear gaps across model families, with closed-source systems leading overall but all models still facing challenges in complex speaker grounding and multi-speaker reasoning. The benchmark annotations, metadata, and evaluation scripts will be available at the GitHub repository: https://github.com/ASLP-lab/MSU-Bench.

papers.title: Towards Understanding the Power and Limits of the Muon Optimizer: A River-Valley Perspective
papers.abstract: Momentum Orthogonalized by Newton-Schulz (Muon) has emerged as a promising optimizer for large language model (LLM) training, yet when and why it outperforms established alternatives such as AdamW remain insufficiently understood. This gap matters in practice, as a sub-optimal choice of optimizer or even hyper-parameters can slow progress throughout expensive pre-training and waste substantial computational resources. Existing theories largely adopt a local-improvement perspective, emphasizing singular-value flattening or implicit curvature adaptation, but they neither determine which optimizer is preferable nor explain why Muon is typically fast only during early training. To better explain Muon's complicated behavior over the entire training trajectory, we develop a trajectory-level characterization of Muon dynamics based on a new mixed-spectrum matrix sensing (MSMS) model motivated by the river-valley view of LLM loss landscapes. Under simplifying assumptions, our continuous-time analysis reveals a qualitatively different convergence mechanism: Muon advances piecewise linearly toward the solution, whereas gradient descent and Adam-like flows approach it asymptotically along curved paths. With finite step sizes, however, the same normalized update magnitude makes Muon prone to overshooting near the solution, so its admissible step size shrinks with the residual scale. This links Muon's early advantage and late-stage limitations to a common mechanism and explains its sensitivity to learning-rate scheduling. Language model pre-training experiments support our discovery and suggest that switching from Muon to AdamW can preserve rapid initial progress while improving late-stage refinement.

papers.title: Spectral Properties of Dense Barabási-Albert Graphs
papers.abstract: Preferential attachment graphs model networks whose growth produces highly uneven degree distributions, describing many real-world systems. Their adjacency spectra are important because they allow graph-theoretic questions to be studied through the eigenvalues of matrices. We analyze the adjacency matrix of a dense Barabási-Albert (B-A) multigraph, where the number of edges added at each step is proportional to the final number of vertices. First, we compute the large-$n$ limit of the expected adjacency matrix and show that it is described by a rank-one limiting kernel, viewed as a continuous analogue of the adjacency matrix. After centering and scaling, the fluctuations form a random matrix with a computable variance profile. Using the quadratic vector equation approach, we derive the limiting bulk spectral distribution. We also determine the asymptotic location of the leading eigenvalue generated by the rank-one mean component.

papers.title: Bipartite cuts in Ramsey-Turán style
papers.abstract: We prove that every $K_5$-free $n$-vertex graph with sublinear independence number can be made bipartite by removing at most $n^2(1/18+o(1))$ edges, where the constant $1/18$ is best possible. The proof method is related to extensions of Turán Theorem in edge-weighted settings, and part of the proof uses flag algebra. Using a similar flag algebra formulation, AI proved that every $K_6$-free and $K_7$-free $n$-vertex graph with sublinear independence number can be made bipartite by removing at most $n^2(1/12+o(1))$ and $n^2(1/9+o(1))$ edges, respectively. These constants are best possible.

papers.title: High-Power Laser Drives Motion in Ultra-thin Photonic Crystal Lightsails
papers.abstract: Laser-driven lightsails require reflectors that are ultralight, highly reflective and robust under intense illumination. These demands point to the thinnest reflectors that dielectric optics allows, photonic crystals, in which a perforated membrane thinner than the wavelength of light acts as a mirror. Such mirrors reflect by confining light inside the membrane, but this confinement also amplifies absorption, making ultralow-loss, tension-bearing materials essential. Stoichiometric high-stress silicon nitride uniquely meets both requirements, yet its ~1 GPa stress makes large, compliant structures difficult to release intact, and such sails have never been pushed by high-power lasers. Here we demonstrate millimeter-wide, 200-nm-thick photonic-crystal trampolines in this material, with 99% design reflectivity at 1070 nm and a static stiffness of 0.53 N/m. Radiation pressure displaces them by more than a micrometer within 50 microseconds. In air, they withstand several times the irradiance found at the Sun's surface, delivered as a coherent beam. Light reshapes the sail more than it pushes it, since modest temperature differences buckle the membrane and collapse its stiffness, so thermal deformation outpaces radiation pressure within milliseconds. The interaction and compliance that make lightsails movable also let light deform them. These results establish a testbed for high-power nanophotonics, directed-energy systems and light-driven propulsion.

papers.title: VERITAS: Verifier-Guided Proof Search for Zero-Shot Formal Theorem Proving
papers.abstract: LLM-based formal provers often collapse the verifier's output into a pass/fail bit. We present VERITAS, a zero-shot framework that feeds what Lean reports (error messages with their position, verified partial proofs, and remaining goals) back into proof search. Phase 1 samples N whole proofs; Phase 2 searches a tree of verified partial proofs with a Tactician, automated step repair, a Critic that ranks states and allocates the budget, and a Retriever. On miniF2F test, VERITAS solves 86.9% with Claude Haiku 5.5 and 82.8% with GPT-6 Luna, against 71.7% and 61.1% for Best-of-5 sampling, and solves more theorems than three re-implemented feedback baselines at a third to a half of their search cost. We also evaluate on 55 combinatorics problems of CombiBench and release code and run logs at https://github.com/CoderDoge1108/VERITAS.

papers.title: Formally-Verifiable and Human-Interpretable RTL Generation with LLM-Guided Stepwise Refinement
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are accelerating register-transfer level (RTL) development, but ensuring the correctness of generated designs remains a major challenge. Existing LLM-driven workflows rely heavily on simulation-based verification, which provides limited correctness guarantees, and often offer little insight into the design decisions behind the generated RTL. We present a framework for LLM-guided, correct-by-construction RTL generation that combines the generative capabilities of LLMs with the mathematical rigor of stepwise refinement. The framework translates natural-language requirements into a formal hardware contract and progressively refines the contract into an implementation. At each refinement step, the LLM proposes a design decision, while the refinement engine applies the corresponding transformation only after formally verifying its correctness. The resulting program is formally verified against the contract and then translated into synthesizable RTL. The recorded derivation allows every line of generated RTL to be traced back to the design decisions and requirements that motivated it. Beyond generating verified implementations, the framework provides reliable verification feedback and reusable design experience, laying the foundation for self-improving hardware generation.

papers.title: Contextualizing Biological Language Models across Modalities via Logit-Space Contrastive Alignment
papers.abstract: Pretrained biological language models encode rich probabilistic structure through native token distributions, but multimodal adaptation typically aligns hidden representations or replaces the native likelihood interface with task-specific heads. We introduce LOGICA (Logit-space Contrastive Alignment), whose central methodological change is to align the context-conditioned native token distributions themselves rather than pooled latent representations. Using native-head-preserving cross-modal adapters, LOGICA couples models with distinct vocabularies and tokenization schemes without requiring a shared tokenizer, decoder, or embedding space. Contrastive learning operates directly through each model's original token-likelihood interface, enabling mutation-local ranking, cross-modal dependency mapping, and context-guided sequence design without task-specific heads. Across protein-ligand, TCR-peptide, and drug-resistance tasks, LOGICA outperforms matched latent-contrastive and conditional-MLM baselines, particularly in low-homology, mutation-local, and data-scarce regimes. These results support native-logit alignment as a general strategy for making pretrained biological token distributions context-sensitive without sacrificing their probabilistic semantics.

papers.title: When the Next Step Is Not One Step: Distribution-Aware Execution Modeling for Concurrent Go Programs
papers.abstract: Predicting the next scheduler event of a concurrent program is ill-posed as single-label classification: repeated runs from the same trace prefix produce different, equally valid next events. We formulate next-event prediction for concurrent Go programs as estimating an empirical next-event distribution obtained from repeated executions, and release a benchmark with 945 training examples from hand-written and generated programs and 798 held-out predictions on 54 real-world GoKer bug kernels from systems such as CockroachDB, Kubernetes, gRPC and etcd. We fine-tune Qwen2.5-Coder-7B with low-rank adapters under a cross-entropy objective and a KL-to-empirical-distribution objective and compare them with zero-shot models and trivial baselines. The outcome is a neutral-to-negative result. The fine-tuned adapters (re-evaluated: 36.3% cross-entropy, 33.6% KL; originally reported 36.2% and 35.8%) are statistically indistinguishable from always predicting the majority event (35.5%), and an event n-gram model reaches 33-34%. Because each held-out prompt carries labels from about five runs, no deterministic predictor can exceed 58.9% top-1 accuracy, so we report macro-F1, balanced accuracy, per-class recall, program-clustered confidence intervals and binned calibration measured directly on both adapters. A sensitivity study with 100 runs per program shows that five-run targets are noisy (mean total-variation distance 0.24 from a 100-run reference), which plausibly limits what the KL objective can learn. Rare event types are essentially never predicted. A select-block goroutine-leak signature follows from scheduler semantics rather than learning. We release the data, adapters and tooling.

papers.title: Schubert cells for the super affine Grassmannian of $GL_{n|m}$
papers.abstract: We study Schubert cells in the affine Grassmannian of the general linear supergroup $GL_{n|m}$, focusing explicitly on the low-dimensional cases $n|m = 1|1$ and $2|1$. We define the affine super Grassmannian as an fpqc sheaf, describe its bounded-lattice filtration by finite-dimensional superschemes, and provide coordinate descriptions, equations, and morphisms for the cells that arise in low dimensions. For $GL_{2|1}$ the cells in the positive and negative chambers split as odd vector bundles over jet schemes of the projective line, and cyclic cells of $GL_{n|m}$ are jet schemes of projective superspaces. In the mixed-sign chamber the transition functions acquire nilpotent corrections in the even coordinate, and all cells except one are non-split. We also introduce decorations, which record the odd directions of the cells on the lattice graph.

papers.title: EMRI Dephasing from a Torsion-Inspired Near-Zone Kerr Deformation: Motivated by Spin-Polarized Dark Matter
papers.abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are sensitive probes of weak conservative perturbations in the strong-field region of massive black holes. We study a phenomenological EMRI model motivated by Einstein--Cartan gravity in which a spin-polarized dark-matter spike is described by a Weyssenhoff fluid. After torsion is eliminated algebraically, the local spin contribution contains a repulsive exterior source $U_{tt}^{\rm spin}\propto-σ_0^2/r^3$. Solving the corresponding static linearized field equation, however, does not produce a global $1/r^3$ metric perturbation; the response contains a mass renormalization, a logarithmic $r^{-1}$ tail, and an $M/r^2$ term. We therefore introduce $g_{μν}^{\rm eff}=g_{μν}^{\rm Kerr}+αh_{μν}^{\rm eff}$ only as a local near-zone matching ansatz, not as a complete rotating Einstein--Cartan black-hole solution. Within this torsion-inspired deformation we compute circular equatorial inspirals and analytic-kludge waveforms. The fiducial model can produce large phase shifts in an idealized adiabatic calculation, but the forecast is optimistic and does not include a full LISA/Taiji response, Teukolsky/self-force fluxes, eccentricity, inclination, or high-dimensional parameter degeneracies. The results should be read as constraints on an effective near-zone operator rather than as a prediction of minimally coupled Einstein--Cartan dark matter.

papers.title: Scalable Deep Unfolding of Conic Optimizers
papers.abstract: Deep unfolding (DU) accelerates iterative optimizers by training learnable components through unrolled iterations, but extending DU to the large-scale semidefinite programs (SDPs) common in robotics has remained limited. Unrolling a full-update conic solver such as COSMO exposes two obstacles: backpropagating through the per-iteration linear-system solve incurs memory quadratic in the problem size when the coefficient matrix is formed explicitly, and backpropagating through the positive semidefinite (PSD) cone projection is numerically unstable under repeated eigenvalues. We address the first with a matrix-free implicit differentiation rule that reduces memory from $O(n^2)$ to $O(n + \mathrm{nnz}(A))$, and the second with a stable backward rule based on the Dalečkii--Krein representation of the Fréchet derivative. Together, these enable learning lightweight hyperparameter policies and warm starts for COSMO. On standalone SDPs and second-order cone programs, ranging from max-cut and Lovász $\vartheta$ to robust estimation and control, the learned policies outperform tuned COSMO on every problem class, reducing iterations to tolerance by up to 60$\times$, and transfer without retraining to instances up to 10$\times$ larger in the size parameter while retaining 2--5$\times$ speedups. Our matrix-free solver implementation also batches naturally on the GPU, solving 64 Lovász $\vartheta$ SDPs 14$\times$ faster than sequential COSMO. When embedded in sequential convex programming for nonlinear covariance steering, our learned optimizers outperform the interior-point solver Clarabel in terms of both success rate and solve time.

papers.title: HierSVA: A Data Synthesis Pipeline, Dataset, and Benchmark for LLM-Driven Hierarchical Hardware Formal Verification
papers.abstract: We present HierSVA, an integrated suite that combines a pipeline, dataset, and benchmark for LLM-driven hierarchical hardware formal verification. HierSVA-SP pairs an RTL preprocessing toolchain with an LLM-in-the-loop formal verification flow to produce reference SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) on hierarchical RTL. Applying it to BaseJump STL yields HierSVA-DS, a dataset of 342 modules, with hierarchy metadata and depths 0--9, accompanied by a deep subset of 28 module-bug pairs with natural-language specifications and bug variants. HierSVA-B decomposes assertion quality into six metric axes: syntax correctness, assertion proof success rate, vacuity, specification faithfulness, mutation coverage, and formal core coverage. Applying HierSVA-B to twelve recent LLMs reveals three findings. First, the module-level compile rate is 67.1\%; among generated assertions in evaluable runs, 82.1\% prove non-vacuously, but the corresponding assertion sets detect only 70.2\% of eligible injected faults and cover 36.2\% of the formal core. Second, on 211 evaluable model--module entries in the deep subset, assertion sets flag buggy RTL with 0.87 recall, but 40\% of predicted-buggy outcomes are false positives on correct RTL, limiting precision to 0.60. Third, agentic mode improves S1-style provability and strength metrics, but gains plateau and oscillate. Codes and artifacts are available at \href{https://github.com/HierSVAAnon/HierSVACodeAndArtifacts}{https://github.com/HierSVAAnon/HierSVACodeAndArtifacts}. Dataset is available at \href{https://huggingface.co/datasets/AnonymousHierSVA/HierSVA}{https://huggingface.co/datasets/AnonymousHierSVA/HierSVA}.

papers.title: Dynamic Programming without Contractivity
papers.abstract: Optimality results in dynamic programming are usually derived from contraction arguments, which require discounting or uniform bounds on termination times. We show that, in many useful settings, contractivity can be replaced by a simple global stability condition that requires no rate or uniformity. Under this condition and mild order-theoretic assumptions, we obtain existence of optimal policies, uniqueness of the value function as a solution to the Bellman equation, and convergence of value function iteration and of Howard and optimistic policy iteration. Applications include optimal stopping without discounting, where contraction methods can fail, and Bayesian sequential analysis.

papers.title: Gelfand--Kirillov dimensions of highest weight modules for basic classical Lie superalgebras
papers.abstract: We obtain explicit formulas for the Gelfand--Kirillov (GK) dimensions of simple highest weight modules over basic classical Lie superalgebras. For the type II orthosymplectic superalgebras $D(m,n)$ and $B(m,n)$, we describe the associated varieties determined by highest weights relative to two Borel subalgebras. This gives algorithms valid for arbitrary complex highest weights, without integrality or typicality hypotheses. In type $B$, we further derive a formula for $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2n)$, distinguishing between integral and half-integral weights. For $G(3)$, $F(4)$ and $D(2,1;α)$, finite odd-reflection procedures give exact GK dimension formulas and finite-dimensionality criteria. We also describe the dependence on $α$ for $D(2,1;α)$. In type I, the GK dimension equals that of the simple even highest weight module for the distinguished Borel subalgebra. The computations rely on established ordinary Lie algebra formulas involving Lusztig's $\mathbf a$-function and Robinson--Schensted (RS) insertion.

papers.title: Non-Isomorphic Optimal Cayley Graphs
papers.abstract: We present eighty-nine optimal degree-diameter Cayley graphs that are non-isomorphic to previously known optimal Cayley graphs with the same degree and diameter. For each graph, we provide comprehensive data on its parameters and structural invariants. Comparison with known constructions reported by Marston Conder on the Combinatorics Wiki and in related works reveals significant differences in girth, algebraic connectivity, domination number, automorphism group structure, cycle distributions, distance-related properties, and other graph invariants. These findings show that optimal degree-diameter Cayley graphs are frequently non-unique. The new examples enlarge the catalogue of known optimal graphs and provide benchmarks for investigations in degree-diameter problems, algebraic graph theory, and extremal graph theory. Since some of the graphs were identified through randomized search techniques, the collection is not exhaustive.

papers.title: A Multimodal Domain-Adversarial Network for Fragmentation Background Suppression in AMS Heavy Nuclei Measurements
papers.abstract: The Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer (AMS) aboard the International Space Station provides high-precision measurements of cosmic-ray nuclei fluxes from charge Z=1 to Z=28 and beyond. With negligible charge confusion from non-interacting nuclei, the precision of nuclei flux measurements is primarily limited by fragmentation backgrounds originating from heavier cosmic rays interacting within detector materials, particularly between tracker Layers 1 and 2 (L1-L2). As AMS extends its measurements to heavier and rarer nuclei, these fragmentation backgrounds become increasingly dominant, necessitating advanced background suppression methods. To address this challenge, we introduce a Multimodal Domain-Adversarial (MDA) neural network designed to effectively suppress these interaction backgrounds. The MDA model fuses heterogeneous data from the silicon tracker and time-of-flight detectors using specialized sub-networks combined via multi-head attention. Crucially, a domain-adversarial training strategy is employed to learn invariant representations, enabling the model, which is trained on Monte Carlo simulations, to be reliably applied to flight data. Using phosphorus (P) as a benchmark, we demonstrate its background suppression capabilities. This approach provides a robust, generalizable framework applicable to the measurement of other rare cosmic-ray nuclei with AMS.

papers.title: Structured Adaptive Tensor Prediction for Streaming Data
papers.abstract: Matrix-valued time series arise in a wide range of applications, such as spatio-temporal data in medical imaging and geophysics. Existing forecasting methods are mainly designed for static settings, while adaptive filtering techniques have been largely limited to scalar- or vector-valued data. In this paper, we develop an adaptive tensor prediction framework for streaming matrix-valued data based on a Tensor-on-Matrix (ToM) regression model, in which the responses in a sliding window are lifted to a third-order tensor and the regression tensor is updated online by stochastic gradient descent (SGD). We derive the leading terms of the steady-state and tracking errors of SGD with overlapping windows, which show that the steady-state error is proportional to the step size and the noise variance, and that the step size governs a trade-off between noise and tracking. We further analyze the statistical accuracy of structured ToM regression within a single window. We establish a restricted isometry property, which holds when the window length is proportional to the input dimension, and derive recovery error bounds for sparse, low-rank and sparse plus low-rank regression tensors, which show that the recovery error scales with the intrinsic degrees of freedom rather than the ambient dimension. Simulations confirm the theoretical results, and the effectiveness of the structured adaptive updates is validated on the tracking of a drifting quantum gate, citywide crowd-flow prediction, and global total electron content (TEC) forecasting.

papers.title: Ohmic warm inflation
papers.abstract: We show that Warm Little Inflation is anomalous, lacks a suitable inflaton potential, and cannot sustain the thermal bath, as the quasi-static approximation over-estimated the dissipated power. To address these issues, we propose a new friction mechanism and new anomaly-free models based on one fermion charged under a U(1) gauge group in one extra dimension. The four-dimensional lattice version is a ring of $N$ U(1) groups with one fermion at each site, reducing to an anomaly-free version of the warm little inflaton model for $N=2$. The inflaton is a Wilson line, protected for $N\ge5$. Large $N$ allows a suitable monodromy inflaton potential. In the continuum limit, $N\to\infty$, the inflaton velocity becomes a five-dimensional electric field and friction becomes Ohmic dissipation, which seems able to sustain warm inflation compatibly with observations.

papers.title: Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?
papers.abstract: It is commonly stated in the literature that T violation is zero in neutrino disappearance channels. We show this claim is not general: it holds only for symmetric matter profiles or when the T/CP-violating phase ($δ$) is 0 or $π$, that is, when the Jarlskog invariant is zero. The $ν_μ$ and $ν_τ$, but not the $ν_e$, survival probabilities carry a $\sinδ$-dependent term that is non-zero in asymmetric matter and constitutes a genuine T asymmetry. The confusion arises from an improper T test that subtracts a probability from itself: a mathematical identity, not a physics result. In this paper, we clarify the distinctions between a proper and an improper T test as well as the proper and improper CP and CPT tests, for a general, arbitrary matter profile. For a toy model consisting of two different layers of constant density, we find that the maximum T-violation is obtained when one layer is close to the solar resonance, and the other is close to the atmospheric resonance. We address whether the matter asymmetry for DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande experiments is sufficiently large to allow the $\sinδ$ dependence to be probed in $ν_μ$ survival probability. We also discuss future experimental scenarios that could probe T/CP-violation in $ν_μ$ survival probability.

papers.title: On the non-uniqueness of solutions of the axi-symmetric swirl-free Navier-Stokes equations, II
papers.abstract: We prove optimal non-uniqueness of Leray solutions of the unforced incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in 3D within the class of axially symmetric swirl-free flows. More precisely, we construct two solutions $u_1,u_2$ that have the same initial data $u_1(0)=u_2(0)$, are smooth for every positive time, satisfy the energy identity, and satisfy \[ u_1,u_2\in C_tH_x^α\cap L_t^2H_x^{α+1}\,\,\text{ for every }\,\,0\leqα<1/2,\qquad u_1,u_2\in L_t^\infty L_x^{3,\infty}\cap L_t^{2,\infty}L_x^\infty. \] Thus non-uniqueness holds in optimal Sobolev spaces and critical Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin weak spaces, even in a symmetry class where smooth solutions are globally regular. The proof relies on a computer-assisted construction of a linearly unstable forward self-similar solution, starting from the numerical profiles identified in our preceding paper (arXiv:2606.07501). We combine explicit asymptotic expansions and global residual estimates with weak coercivity inequalities stabilized by finitely many functionals. Approximate solutions of auxiliary linear equations yield quantitative inverse bounds, allowing us to correct both the stationary profile and its unstable eigenpair by contraction arguments. The instability and localization theorem proved in arXiv:2606.07501 then produces the non-unique solutions.

papers.title: Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance
papers.abstract: We study high-probability linear regression in the infinite variance regime, wherecthe regression noise has only a finite conditional $α$-moment $ν$ for some unknown $α\in(1,2)$, and the covariates may only have finite moments up to a given order (e.g., 4th moment). We give a black-box reduction that converts finite-variance regression procedures into weak-moment procedures. The reduction is based on empirical residual pruning and is agnostic to the moment exponent, the noise scale, the covariance, and the design moment. Under a finite fourth-moment condition on the covariates, any finite-variance subroutine attaining the sub-Gaussian rate yields the following when the number of samples $n$ is above a suitably defined threshold: Without knowing $α$ or $ν$, we have with probability at least $1-δ$ that $ \|\widehatθ-θ^*\|_Σ \lesssim_α ν^{1/α} \big(\frac{d+\log(1/δ)}{n}\big)^{\frac{α-1}α}, $ where $d$ is the dimension, $Σ$ is the covariate covariance matrix, and $\|v\|_Σ:=(v^\topΣv)^{1/2}$. We further prove a matching minimax lower bound that holds under the same conditions. The reduction is computationally efficient whenever the finite-variance subroutine is. We also obtain a distribution-free prediction guarantee under a bounded raw $α$-moment assumption on the response, and give an analogous $α$-agnostic reduction for mean estimation.

papers.title: Quantum Many-Body Scars from Operator Size
papers.abstract: We present a general construction of approximate many-body scar states in two copies of a system using a bilocal size interaction that couples one site to its partner on the other copy. For an uncoupled two-sided Hamiltonian whose terms have fixed size in an operator basis, we identify polynomially many Krylov basis states that it annihilates and that, in the thermodynamic limit, become concentrated on a single size sector. The size operator splits them into a tower of equally spaced levels that gives rise to coherent revivals characterized by collective oscillations of energy across the two copies. We provide a concrete realization of this construction in two copies of a general $q$-body nearest-neighbor spin chain, and the SYK model.

papers.title: Thermopower overshoot from collinear scattering in two-dimensional Fermi liquids
papers.abstract: Electron transport is typically described in terms of relaxation times, which measure how quickly Fermi-surface deformations decay. We show here that the thermopower of a two-dimensional Fermi liquid instead probes the structure of these deformations in the form of their local temperature change, which we call the thermal dressing. This structure leads to an overshoot of the thermopower over its hydrodynamic value $- s/(ne)$ with increasing wave vector, before it falls to half that value in the ballistic limit. At low temperatures, the excess thermopower does not have the linear-in-temperature scaling expected of a Fermi liquid, but decreases only logarithmically as $1/\ln(T_F/T)$ at optimal wave vector. The overshoot is caused by collinear scattering, which redistributes energy over the Fermi surface and induces the thermal dressing, the strength of which grows with the angular harmonic index $m$ of the deformation. In contrast to tomographic effects in the charge conductivity, this overshoot does not rely on an odd-even effect in quasiparticle lifetimes and defines a distinct thermographic transport regime. The thermopower overshoot survives realistic disorder and should be detectable in a thermocouple with high-mobility samples.

papers.title: Structure and relaxation of long-lived odd-parity modes in two-dimensional Fermi liquids
papers.abstract: In two-dimensional Fermi liquids, odd-parity deformations of the Fermi surface relax anomalously slowly at a rate $\sim T^4$, where $T$ is the temperature. However, the leading-logarithmic prediction for the magnitude of this rate $\sim m^4 \ln m$, where $m$ is an angular harmonic index, exceeds exact-diagonalization results and the $\ln m$ scaling is not observed. We resolve this discrepancy by evaluating the 2D Fermi-liquid collision integral for general regular isotropic potentials to leading order in $T/T_F$, including the nonlogarithmic term beyond the $\ln(T_F/T)$ term. We find that the local temperature modulation of the odd mode, which we call the thermal dressing, suppresses relaxation by collinear scattering, with residual relaxation set by large-angle scattering. Such large-angle processes give corrections of order $\ln m/\ln(T_F/T)$ that are not small and must be resummed. We benchmark our results against exact-diagonalization calculations for constant interactions and find agreement over a range $m^2 T/T_F \lesssim 0.4$, and we provide closed-form results for the slowest odd-mode relaxation rate of a spin-polarized dipolar gas.

papers.title: A Methodologically Rigorous Benchmark of Linear Regression,RNN, and LSTM for S&P 500 Forecasting:Identifying Sources of Performance Inflation in Financial DeepLearning
papers.abstract: This study examines one-day-ahead forecasting of the S&P 500 closing level using a 2006-2025 dataset that includes fundamental price data, macroeconomic indicators, and engineered technical features. We benchmark three model families, namely linear regression, vanilla recurrent neural networks (RNN), and long short-term memory networks (LSTM), within a unified preprocessing and chronological evaluation pipeline. A central contribution of this work is a methodological audit of common practices in the deep-learning-for-stock-prediction literature. We identify three sources of result inflation that frequently appear in published methodologies: wavelet-denoised evaluation targets, the absence of a naive persistence baseline, and best-of-N replicate reporting. We then re-evaluate all model families under a corrected protocol that controls for each. Performance is reported using root mean squared error, mean absolute percentage error, and the Pearson correlation coefficient, averaged across N = 30 independent replicates per configuration. We compare models on accuracy, stability across replicates, and architectural depth sensitivity, using the naive persistence forecast (predicting today's close as tomorrow's close) as a primary baseline against which all candidate models must demonstrate improvement.

papers.title: No Polynomial-Time Algorithm For Tarski Fixed Points Unless Cryptographic Assumptions Fail
papers.abstract: We study the time complexity of finding a Tarski fixed point. We provide a subexponential-time reduction from the Unique End of Potential Line (UEOPL) problem to the problem of finding a Tarski fixed point. Using a range of known cryptographic lower bounds for UEOPL, our reduction implies a range of conditional lower bounds on the running time of any algorithm that finds a Tarski fixed point. The strongest of these give quasi-polynomial-time lower bounds for the problem. We also obtain a similar quasi-polynomial-time lower bound for Tarski based instead on a weak exponential-time type hypothesis for UEOPL. These running time lower bounds match the recently discovered quasi-polynomial query lower bounds for the problem.

papers.title: Observation of rotonic density enhancement at the boundary of a uniform dipolar superfluid
papers.abstract: The collective excitations of a quantum liquid lie at the heart of its emergent behaviour. In many systems, the variation of excitation energy ${\varepsilon}$ with wavevector $k$ exhibits a softening at a characteristic lengthscale, which plays a key role in thermodynamics and transport. These excitations, termed rotons, often reflect an underlying tendency of the liquid to crystallize into a competing symmetry-broken state, such as the solid state of helium or the Wigner crystal of electrons in a magnetic field. More than $50$ years ago, it was predicted that rotons should manifest as emergent density oscillations at the fluid's boundary, but this effect has not been observed. Here, we realize an ultracold dipolar superfluid confined in a homogeneous trapping potential and directly confirm the emergence of rotonic density enhancement at its edge. This is accompanied by rotonic density fluctuations across the bulk, which are linked to the static edge structure via the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. Increasing the dipolar character leads to an azimuthal density modulation of the fluid's boundary, which we show to be analogous to the behaviour of a quasi-one-dimensional fluid confined in an annular optical potential.

papers.title: Nonperturbative Bounds on the Ground-State Energy of Lattice QED
papers.abstract: We establish nonperturbative bounds on the ground-state energy of lattice quantum electrodynamics with naive fermions in Coulomb gauge, within the Gaussian photon approximation. Our central result is a spectral comparison theorem showing that, in the thermodynamic limit, the minimum fermionic energy density over all link configurations coincides with that of the trivial gauge configuration. The proof exploits a logarithmic determinant representation and dimensional reduction, without relying on reflection positivity, and applies to lattices of either parity. Combining this result with the positivity of the electromagnetic and Coulomb Hamiltonians, we derive an explicit lower bound on the interacting ground-state energy. Finite-lattice counterexamples show that the thermodynamic limit is essential.

papers.title: Hölder continuity of meromorphic functions and equisingularity
papers.abstract: For a complex analytic variety and an exponent between zero and one, we study the sheaf of meromorphic functions that are locally Hölder continuous with that exponent for the outer metric. It sits between the structure sheaves of the seminormalization and of the Lipschitz saturation of Pham and Teissier. We prove that these sheaves are coherent and that only finitely many of them are distinct, the exponents at which they change being rational numbers governed by the Rees valuations of the ideal of a certain diagonal. Each exponent defines a Hölder saturation of the variety. We show that a variety whose Hölder saturation is smooth for some exponent larger than one third is itself smooth and that one third is sharp. For reduced curve germs we compute the Hölder saturations from the characteristic exponents of the branches and give explicit thresholds, in terms of classical invariants, at which they become the seminormalization, the Lipschitz saturation, or a curve of the same multiplicity. We prove that homeomorphic curves are bi-Hölder homeomorphic for some positive exponent, whereas bi-Hölder homeomorphisms with exponent close enough to one preserve the multiplicity. We then introduce the relative Hölder saturation of a family and prove that it specializes to the saturations of the fibers over a dense Zariski-open subset of the base. This leads to two notions of equisingularity for families of complex analytic varieties, Hölder equisingularity, defined by a bi-Hölder trivialization, and the stronger Hölder equisaturation, defined by the triviality of the relative saturation. For families of reduced curve germs we show that they interpolate between topological, Whitney and Lipschitz equisingularity, with explicit exponents depending only on the invariants of the special fiber.

papers.title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Deploying large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon and continual interactions requires maintaining reusable memory states for future inference, posing challenges for existing architectures. Standard Transformers accumulate layer-wise, token-level KV caches, incurring linear GPU memory growth and quadratic computational complexity as the context expands. In contrast, linear-time architectures compress history into fixed-size states, but struggle to retain fine-grained details. We introduce MemOnce, a foundation architecture that learns scalable memory states for language models. MemOnce is based on two core designs: (a) Memory encoder-decoder: it caches only a small subset of final-layer hidden states as compact memory representations and dynamically decodes them back into KV caches for attention layers; (b) Memory sparse attention: for each continual input, MemOnce adaptively retrieves relevant memory representations, with the sparse indices computed only once across layers. Coupling these two designs enables efficient on-the-fly memory loading and KV cache decoding, drastically reducing the GPU memory footprint and achieving linear-time complexity. We conduct extensive experiments to show that MemOnce outperforms Transformers and other architectures across varying model sizes, context lengths, and training paradigms (pretraining and post-training adaptation). In particular, adapting Qwen3.5-4B with MemOnce reduces memory state cache by 1313$\times$ and prefill latency by 6.9$\times$ at 1M context, and improves throughput by 3.5$\times$ and overall memory performance by +5.77%. Finally, MemOnce generalizes zero-shot to downstream representation tasks, achieving competitive results against specialized models.

papers.title: Localization of weakly integral objects in braided fusion categories
papers.abstract: An object $X$ of a braided fusion category is called weakly integral if $\mathrm{FPdim}(X)^2$ is an integer. We prove that every nonzero weakly integral object admits a localization, that is, a Yang-Baxter operator $R$ on a finite-dimensional vector space $W$ such that, for every $n$, the algebra homomorphisms from the group algebra of the braid group $B_n$ to $\mathrm{End}(W^{\otimes n})$ and to $\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})$, defined by $R$ and by the braiding, have the same kernel. The operator $R$ can be chosen unitary when the braided fusion category is unitary. This proves the 'if' direction of a conjecture of Rowell and Wang, motivated by topological quantum computation, which states that a simple object admits a localization if and only if it is weakly integral. For a simple weakly integral object of a unitary braided fusion category, the operator $R$ that we construct has an enhancement in the sense of Turaev, and the resulting knot invariant is the Reshetikhin-Turaev invariant of knots colored by $X$.

papers.title: Soft--hard Bayesian inference in heavy-ion collisions
papers.abstract: Bayesian analyses of jet quenching commonly constrain jet--medium interaction parameters using a fixed quark-gluon plasma (QGP) background obtained from a soft-sector calibration. This approach neglects uncertainty in the medium and prevents hard observables from providing additional constraints on its properties. We investigate these effects in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.76$ TeV using sequential Bayesian inference in a reduced three-parameter space. We vary the initial normalization and nucleon width of the medium together with the jet--medium coupling, combining JETSCAPE medium evolution with MATTER+LBT calculations of high-$p_T$ hadron and inclusive-jet suppression. We first constrain all three parameters using the hard observables alone, then incorporate a projected soft-sector posterior through sequential inference. We find that the hard observables are sensitive to the medium properties and reveal substantial correlations with the jet--medium coupling, reflecting their compensating effects on jet quenching. Propagating the soft-sector information shifts the preferred coupling relative to a fixed-medium extraction, with the update driven primarily by hadron-suppression measurements. Despite substantial differences in the medium parameters and coupling favored by hard-observable-only and sequential inference, their suppression predictions remain similar over much of the measured range. These findings highlight the difficulty of distinguishing changes in the QGP medium from changes in microscopic jet--medium interaction strength using inclusive suppression measurements alone.

papers.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
papers.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is a neurodevelopmental condition that can affect attention, activity and impulse control. Electroencephalography (EEG) records brain activity as children and adolescents perform cognitive tasks. However, comparing features derived from these recordings requires consistent signal preparation, shared analysis windows and documented quality decisions. We curated 669 existing BALLADEER recordings from 156 participants across five task conditions so that researchers can compare seven EEG feature families on the same time intervals for each participant and task. The dataset links continuous signals to precomputed measurements from 115 feature definitions or templates and records the quality decisions made for each recording. Analyses must still account for repeated measurements within participants, residual artefacts and differences between acquisition systems. Technical validation covered signal integrity, numerical checks on feature estimators and completeness of the released files. In every task, the median proportion of recording time retained after preprocessing was 100%. To illustrate reuse, we report saved participant-held-out evaluations comparing XGBoost using all seven families on eight-second windows with a predictor based only on recruitment-group prevalence in the training fold. Recruitment-group discrimination was stronger in Robots than in the three Slackline conditions. These descriptive results from overlapping cohorts do not establish diagnostic validity. The dataset, curation software and aggregate results for the predictive example are publicly available.

papers.title: A proof of the polygonal Faber--Krahn inequality
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every integer $n\ge3$, the regular $n$-gon uniquely minimizes the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, up to congruence, among simple polygons of prescribed area with at most $n$ sides. We also obtain the optimal linear correction when fewer than $n$ sides are present. The proof combines a partition into convex cells with a mixed boundary comparison. Among convex polygons of fixed area and fixed sum of base angles less than $π$, the isosceles triangle minimizes the first eigenvalue with Dirichlet conditions on the base and Neumann conditions elsewhere. A comparison of Fourier transforms of conformal area densities proves this inequality and the corresponding upper bounds for inverse spectral moments of integer order at least two. We prove strict log-convexity of an interpolation of the eigenvalues of regular polygons of unit area for real parameters at least four. We then derive sharp hexagonal bounds for periodic convex polygonal tilings and asymptotic bounds for convex polygonal partitions of a fixed convex polygon, with an explicit correction for boundary junctions.

papers.title: Convergence of a finite element Chorin projection method for the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations
papers.abstract: We analyze a fully discrete finite element projection method for the stochastic incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and multiplicative noise. We show solvability and uniform moment estimates for the intermediate and the corrected velocity approximations under the assumption that the initial data is square-integrable and divergence free, and that the deterministic forcing term is bounded in $L^{q}(0,T;H^{-1}(D))$ for a sufficiently large $q$. Under standard stability and approximation assumptions on the finite element spaces and a coupling condition on the spatial and temporal discretization parameters, we prove convergence of a subsequence to a martingale solution of the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations. The analysis combines the complementary spatial and temporal estimates of the predicted and the corrected velocity approximations and uses the numerical dissipation to identify their common limit. We establish tightness of the piecewise constant temporal interpolations of the velocity field approximations using Aldous' criterion combined with the uniform discrete moment estimates. The convergence result holds in two and three space dimensions as it does not rely on any additional regularity of the limiting martingale solution beyond the one naturally available from the energy inequality. Finally, we demonstrate the performance of the scheme in numerical experiments in two space dimensions for smooth and vortex sheet initial data.

papers.title: Task2Hand: A Contact-Grounded Skill for Parametric Dexterous-Hand Morphology Design
papers.abstract: Dexterous hand design demands repeated expert work across geometry, robot-description code, collision debugging, grasp initialization, and policy training. We present Task2Hand, a Skill: a specification package that turns a functional manipulation brief into a parameterized hand model and routes every candidate through cost-ordered contact, dynamics, and learning gates. Each gate returns a status and an evidence record; on failure, the Skill records the earliest blocker, revises one bounded parameter group, and reruns the cheaper gates. The agent generates, validates, and trains autonomously within declared bounds, and escalates trade-offs, plateaus, and conflicting evidence to a human who sets the next design direction. An evidence-driven design trajectory for bidirectional in-hand manipulation yielded SAGE Hand (Skill-Aware Generative Embodiment): four fingers, 16 actuated DoF, an integrated guiding palm, compact roots, cylindrical tips, and a collision-cleared opposable thumb. Under a matched training protocol, SAGE Hand reaches 45.6% task success on a hexagonal prism against 37.3% for the LEAP hand, and 70.8% on a bicolor cylinder against 51.6%. Dense simulated tactile input more than halves the cylinder drop rate. In a controlled iteration study, the Skill path preserves capture at 164/165 trials while the path without the Skill degrades to 14/165, confirming that the gates act as a regression guard during refinement. Accepted candidates pack with URDF/MJCF, metrics, checkpoints, and a provenance manifest.

papers.title: All stable Schoen--Wolfson cones are minimizing
papers.abstract: In the late nineties, R.~Schoen and J.~Wolfson studied the problem of minimizing the area among Lagrangian surfaces in a Riemannian symplectic $4$-manifold. In their parametric approach, they showed that minimizers are smoothly branched-immersed away from a discrete set of points, where there exists a nonflat tangent cone minimizing the area among Lagrangian disk competitors. They also classified the stable singular cones into a family $C_{p,p+1}$ indexed by a positive integer $p$, but left open the question of which of them are globally minimizing. We settle this question by showing that for each $p \geq 1$, $C_{p,p+1} \cap B_1$ minimizes the area among Lagrangian disks spanning its boundary with degree one.

papers.title: Recognizing $k$-inducible Digraphs is NP-complete
papers.abstract: A digraph is k-inducible if its arcs correspond to the pairwise majority relation of a preference profile with k voters. By McGarvey's theorem, every asymmetric digraph is k-inducible for some k, but for every fixed k there are digraphs that are not k-inducible. Whether a digraph is 1-inducible or 2-inducible can easily be decided in polynomial time. The complexity of deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible for every fixed $k\geq 3$ has been a long-standing open problem. We prove that deciding whether a tournament is 3-inducible is NP-complete and then leverage this result to show that deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible is NP-complete for every fixed $k\geq 3$. Our results imply that, unless P=NP, k-inducible digraphs cannot be characterized by finitely many forbidden induced subdigraphs.

papers.title: Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata
papers.abstract: To prevent motion sensors from acting as covert microphones, Android 12+ caps SensorManager gyroscope and accelerometer rates at 200 Hz by default, requires HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS for higher rates, and throttles sensors back to 200 Hz when the microphone toggle is off. We show that Android's Camera2 subsystem bypasses these defenses. During an active Camera2 session, Camera HAL stabilization pipelines record high-rate gyroscope measurements and export them via vendor CaptureResult metadata. Loudspeaker speech excites chassis vibrations that couple into this path. Across 50 smartphones (2020-2026) from 10 vendors, 37 expose gyroscope metadata via Camera2, and 26 exceed 200 Hz--including six flagship models at 800-1000 Hz, double SensorManager's 400-500 Hz ceiling. This channel requires neither RECORD_AUDIO nor HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS and defeats privacy switches: turning off the microphone toggle does not throttle metadata, and turning off the camera toggle blanks only video frames while 800-1000 Hz metadata keeps streaming. To build a zero-profiling attack that generalizes to unseen phones, we introduce Source-to-Leakage Learning (S2L). Prior attacks train on real sensor traces, entangling speech with a specific phone's mechanical resonances and sampling rate. S2L decouples speech content from hardware acoustics using a physics-constrained forward simulator. Trained exclusively on simulated leakage without target-phone traces, our universal recognizer CamEar achieves 52.1% mean word accuracy (up to 61.8%) and 74.3% character accuracy (up to 80.7%) across the six 800-1000 Hz phones. In contrast, ISpyU models fine-tuned on real target-phone data drop to 25.9% word accuracy on unseen phones; CamEar improves cross-device accuracy by 101.4% and outperforms ISpyU's same-device models on every tested phone.

papers.title: Non-penetrating World Models
papers.abstract: We study a new problem of preventing object penetration in interactive video world models. To understand how existing models handle this, we introduce NoPeBench, a benchmark that evaluates how world models respond to physical obstacles. Our evaluation reveals that none of the open-source models can reliably prevent such failures. Surprisingly, however, these models already encode the information needed to predict such violations. We find that the hidden states of diffusion transformers (DiTs) can predict whether a candidate action will penetrate an obstacle. Building on this, we introduce NoPeWorld, a lightweight framework that detects and prevents penetration. Specifically, we train a small prediction head on top of a frozen DiT's hidden states to read out if a candidate action is safe or not. Unsafe actions are then replaced with safe ones that best preserve the original intent. Despite its simplicity, NoPeWorld substantially reduces the physical violation rate, averaged over six video world models, from 74% to 16%. Remarkably, our method shows zero-shot generalization to open-domain imagery, third-person viewpoints, and moving obstacles. We publicly release our code, the NoPeBench benchmark, and model weights. Project Page: https://nopeworld.github.io .

papers.title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology
papers.abstract: Machine learning has largely kept separate the choice of architecture and the process of training. A classic Transformer, for instance, trains a fixed set of attention and MLP sublayers at every layer, in the same order, and optimizes the weights within. This uniformity is a convention rather than a principled design choice, and it is likely suboptimal: the best architecture for a given task may be smaller, more efficient, and far from uniform. We believe that, ideally, training itself should shape the model's topology. To this end, we introduce Model Carving, which learns both a Transformer's weights and its architecture in a single run. By applying learnable, scalar gates to each sublayer, we allow the training loss to remove the model's own components during training -- freeing a smaller heterogeneous network inside. We evaluate Model Carving by pre-training standard Transformers from 140M to 2.7B parameters and looped Transformers from 140M to 1.3B. At equal training compute, carved models reach a lower validation loss than dense models trained with up to 1.7 times more compute. Furthermore, carved models also outperform size-matched models produced by pruning or distillation, suggesting that the best way to obtain small models for edge devices is to carve them during training, not to compress a large one afterwards. This advantage both grows with scale and carries over to downstream tasks such as few-shot evaluation and generation.
